for the price, it couldn't be better! my boyfriend and i stayed a night at the millenium hilton on a short stay in los angeles for the police concert at dodger stadium. i booked through expedia, and my rate for a saturday night was only $150 including taxes and fees. rare for an upscale hotel these days, especially in a large city. we recently paid the same price for a fleebag motel in monterey.pros:* amazing public spaces. i felt like i was transported to the glamour days of hollywood past. felt like a grand old new york style hotel.* great bar. not the sports bar, but the main bar attached to the lobby -- was gorgeous. drinks however, were expensive. my appletini was $14!! free nuts though.* room was charming. high ceilings, nice moulding, bed was comfortable and room was quiet. who cares that the tv was a bit small...we were not there to watch the tube.*easy to find.* neighborhood is not 'scary' like other people have reported. it's just in a business district so there's not a lot going on at night. you'll need to drive if you want nightlife, unless of course you walk over to the standard hotel's roof top bar / club which is great.cons:* sports bar: ech. dark, dingy, did not serve late night food. actually it was really difficult to find late night eats besides the room service menu.* expensive valet parking at $32 per stay. also it was very crowded and there was an air of confusion where you drive up. your car is whisked away before you even know what's going on. make sure you have all your things with you when you exit your vehicle, i heard it was very difficult to retrieve items after the car has been parked.**************************we didn't visit the pool which i would have liked to comment on but the pictures look amazing.all in all, very worth the money. we'll be back.oh...one more thing, expedia gives it a 3 and a half star rating (hotel class, i believe, not based on reviews) -- not 4 stars as reported on this website. i would have to agree with the 3.5 star rating as it could be use a little tlc.

it's a wonderful experience in everyway - not in kansas anymore to all of those who are insulting this hotel and the location i would have to disagree. i grew up in kansas so i am no city slicker but i don't see any homeless people around this hotel. the streets are clean and safe. i now live in san francisco and it is much more intimidating. the hotel is lovely and has good service. furthermore, what do you want for a 3 1/2 star? the rate is $129 per night and parking is what it is. i can't believe the way some people are so self serving that they'd ruin a great experience and price for an average income working american to see a great historic architectural place. it has great restaurants everywhere and i walked the streets last night a 11pm with no problems. it aint the four seasons but overall it is the best hotel in downtown la...

mixed reaction i believe the letter i sent the manager afteri checked out sums up my expierence at this hotel. i will preface this with a few things, i have had good expierences there in the past and i did get a response from the hotel manager and a phone call to follow up - so i do give high remarks for that; however the manager did not offer any compensation of any kind and just said to call him next time i stayed there. here is the letter: i checked out of this hotel today june 3, 2007 and i can honestly say that this was one of the worst hotel experiences i have had. i have stayed at your hotel before nd have had pleasant experiences, but after this last time - i will think twice before i reserve there or continue to recommend your hotel to friends and family. the room i was assigned was drab, walls were bare, and pieces of the room were wore very badly - it was rm 329. when asked if there were other rooms to switch to - there were no other rooms in the class i had reserved so i was stuck with the room, which overlook the industrial portion of your hotel, so needless to say i left my shutters shut because of the disgusting view. additionally, staff were very unfriendly and no one every smiled - at any point except for the maid staff who made it a point to say hello and good morning, everyone else in the hotel had some big chip on their shoulder. the valet attendants were lax and just hung around until one of them decided to get my car. at one point i waited 15 minutes to get my car and during that entire time there were no other guests dropping off or picking up there car. i saw a ticket come up for my car and a lien of guys standing around doing nothing for at least 5 minutes before one of them decided to pick up the slip and retrieve the car - and for this i pay $32 a day? lastly, when i checked out, i wasnéˆ¥??› even asked how my stay was, which is typical hospitality protocol and i was just given my bill and sent away. there wasn't even an opportunity to reviewthe bill before it charged to my credit card - it was just printed and handed to me. i am shocked at how horrible everything was for an establishment like yours and really greatly disappointed.

great to experience the biltmore this is a perfect hotel for those interested in the grandeur of the past. the housekeeping service was quick, clean and efficient. tea was lovely, except the server was not very engaged. on the other hand, the bartender in the lounge was outstanding. terrific stories of the past. if you are looking for flat screen tvs and sleek duvets with trendy touches-this is not the place. but if you love ambiance and garndeur in public spaces...time to check in.
4 stars!!! loved the location, history, service and grandeur of the biltmore ball room
millenium biltmore is a real treat hotel room

great, classic meeting space, classically outdated rooms the biltmore really feels like la of old. the common space, lobbies and meeting facilities are dramatic, beautiful and filled with history. book your meeting there and you'll be happy. the meeting rooms once hosted the academy awards and other star-filled functions and they look as good today as they must have 70 years ago.the rooms are another story. open your wardrobe and find what looks like a 20-year old small tv. sheets and blankets are thin and old. bathrooms are functional but small. the room itself is large and the bed moderately comfortable. food is just ok. as it's an old hotel, outlets are at a premium, especially if you have a laptop, blackberry, ipod, etc. to plug in.i got a good rate of $161 from expedia. that's fair for this hotel.
nice hotel, good service. but all it takes is one incident..... room 635--to the bathroom

excellent choice my wife and i stayed at the millennium biltmore over memorial day weekend. we initially went with the hotel based on a great deal on expedia and hoped for the best. right from our arrival, things went great. we were greeted warmly at check-in and we were informed we were being upgraded to a junior suite. the room was huge and, while not super modern, it was immaculate. we were also given vouchers for free breakfast for two mornings and a round of drinks at the hotel bar, to compensate for some minor remodeling going on that weekend (which didn't effect the quality of our stay one bit). the hotel itself is a gorgeous throwback to old l.a. the place has a ton of history and character, while still having all of the basic amentities needed in this modern world (i.e. high speed internet, business center, indoor pool, gym, etc.). it is centrally located and a good base for exploring los angeles. finally, i highly recommend the martinis on offer at the gallery bar.

would not stay here again i stayed at the millennium biltmore for a conference earlier this month. the location immediately presents a challenge. it is not an area in which i would feel comfortable and safe as a single female traveler walking around during the day, let alone at night.the common areas of the hotel are really quite beautiful, and reflect the grandeur of a more glamourous, old hollywood. the rooms, however, possess none of the same allure. worn, dingy sheets with questionable bedspreads to match, dismal views, the constant hum of busy, downtown traffic...i could go on and on. the banquet food, too, was on par with the rooms - dismal.a supreme staff could have bridged the gap to make the experience memorable. the staff fell short, however (with the notable exception of julio in the bar, who possessed a savvy service level beyond this property, and also the director of rooms, whose name escapes me). from misquoted room service delivery times to failure to deliver packages to a ridiculous $50 charge for chicken fingers in the bar. yikes. and, the worst part was the apathy and lack of ownership apparent everywhere. not my problem seemed to be the going mantra.all in all, not a place i would care to return.

okay at best i was at the biltmore millennium for a conference earlier this month, and i have to agree with the majority of the previous posters. i travel quite a bit for business, and at this hotel, i feel it's all about the lobby and public areas and the guest rooms are sadly overlooked.when i arrived, i was definitely impressed. the lobby and front desk areas are truly stunning. front desk clerk tried to upgrade me at check in (for a $50/night fee). i declined. however, i have to say my room was large when i stepped in - i was one of the lucky ones at my conference - other people's rooms were half the size of mine. no matter - as the pr/marketing person for the hotel stated, it's an old property - and i can definitely understand the room variations in older hotels.what i can't understand, however, is the lack of quality in everything *inside* those guest rooms - small or large. sheets were thin and paper-like, the pillows were like burlap sacks, the comforter was ratty, and bathroom amenities (shampoos, soaps, etc.) were never replaced during my entire stay even though i used them. in fact, one day the maid knocked a lampshade off the lamp when making the bed, and even though she was back to the room two additional nights - it was never fixed.what ticked me off though was the way the hotel nickel-and-dimed. i understand it's a high business hotel, and the thought process is that people are on expense accounts - and who cares what things cost?? wrong. those days are over - i have strict budgets i need to adhere to when i travel for business, and i don't appreciate a $6 charge to print out my boarding passes for my flight (grand total of time in the business center - 3 minutes). the hotel advertises hi speed internet in public areas and guest rooms - but be aware, it's certainly not *complimentary*..the food was very good at my conference, however, and the meeting rooms, while a little chilly (but what meeting rooms aren't?), were beautiful and the ballrooms extraordinary. staff was always pleasant and helpfuli do agree with other posters, however, that the hotel is not the best location-wise for tourists at all, and while i didn't feel *unsafe* in the neighborhood, it did get a little seedy at night.so once the renovations are complete, i think this would be a fine property for your event or for business meetings. tourists, however, reconsider.

grand hotel that has seen better days i spent four nights at this biltmore and have to say that the lobby and meeting rooms were impressive and opulent in the old world hollywood way. the staff was attentive, polite and professional, however the rooms are in serious need of an update. the beds and pillows were very hard. the comforter reminded me of something i have seen in budget hotels. the restaurant and room service was extremely overpriced! i ate at the restaurant three different times and the service was slow and the food exceptionally overpriced.if you enjoy being a part of a historic hotel, then i would suggest a night here, however if you are looking for comfort and luxury, look somewhere else.

nice staff, avg rooms, terrible neighbourhood the staff members were very helpful and the common areas were quite beautiful - lovely high ceilings and very well-kept.however, the room i stayed in (476) was quite small, tired looking and had a view of a brick wall. the linens were old and not luxurious by any means.the neighbourhood around the hotel is pretty sketchy and there's not much to do, particularly on the weekends. even the starbucks close to the hotel is closed on sundays. i would not stay in downtown la again. next time i have meetings in downtown la, i would stay in santa monica or beverly hills and rent a car.

beautiful hotel my husband and i recently stayed at the millennium biltmore in los angles while i was on a business trip. overall, i'd say we were pretty satisfied with our stay. the hotel is beautiful and has such a fascinating history. i had to be careful to watch where i was walking because i was so busy looking up at the beautiful walls and ceilings. i was lucky enough to get to see several of the ballrooms because of the conference i was attending and i was just as amazed with those as with the rest of the hotel. the room we had was small but sufficient. i had to keep reminding myself that older hotels didn't necessarily have big rooms. we were right by the elevators though and heard the dings from the elevators at all hours of the night. the air conditioner worked very well, but it made a awful banging noise when it turned on and off. we could even hear the banging of the air conditioner in the neighboring room. we also had trouble with the water draining in the bathtub. after probably less than 2 minutes in the shower, the water was over my ankles. for late night snacks, don't count on the vending machines. the floors alternated between vending and ice machines and a search of a couple of floors with the vending machines only turned up coke machines. the hotel staff was friendly so that was nice. the food at the hotel restaurants was expensive which i somewhat expected. the problem was that on saturday and sunday most of the other stores and restaurants in the city are closed, so we didn't have much of a choice but to eat the food at the hotel. it would have been nice to have some other options. also as an fyi, there is no information in the room as to what ammenities are offered at the hotel (i.e. restaurants with menus or at least highlights and price ranges, pool hours, fitness facility hours, city transportation information, etc.). we found that a bit odd.

not so much... i just returned from a 4-day stay at this hotel. the lobby and meeting rooms are quite lovely -- they have an old hollywood feel. however, the rooms are in need of a serious update. the rooms are large, but very dreary. the window overlooked a brick wall, so there was hardly a chance for any sunlight. the sheets were very low quality, the bedspread was dingy, the shower head had low water flow, the base of the vanity was some kind of painted plywood...i could go on and on. the location is good only if you have a business meeting in downtown. it's just not convenient to much else that tourists would like to see. also, i just didn't feel that safe walking around on the weekend or in the evening.
out of place, or what! the best coffee bar ever!

millenium biltmore - basic and overpriced! myself and my boyfriend stayed here for 5 nights in october 2006. on arrival, we were greeted in a friendly and efficient manner and directed to our room. the hotel lobby and all the public areas were fantastic. not exactly my style hotel, i'm more into contemporary decor but the public areas in this hotel looked fantastic with their traditional decor. once we entered the corridor from the lift though, we noticed that the standard had dropped dramatically. instead of looking fresh like the lobby, the corridor looked very dated and in need of some redecoration. once we entered the room, in this 4 star (?!) hotel, we were not too pleased at all. it was grubby in fact. i moved a chair towards the wall to make a bit more space and there were crumbs from the previous guests there which were obviously not cleaned properly. the room was dark, the bathroom was completely outdated, with dirty looking old tiles and the wooden panelling was painted white a long time ago but was now a dirty yellowy colour. nothing special about this bathroom at all. i wasn't impressed. i was going to complain and ask to change rooms but i decided maybe that i was just expecting too much and that if this room was like this then all of them probably would.later then we lay on the bed with the intention of watching telly for a while. there was a large mahogony television/drawers unit a few feet away from the end of the bed but with the side of it facing the bed. we pulled out the sliding tray with the television on it as far as we could and swivelled it as far as we could but we still could not comfortably see the television from the bed. this was a very bad set up altogether. mind you there was 2 chairs in front of the television unit so perhaps you're only meant to watch television from there?! the concierge though, was very helpful, he helped us to organise a rental car and a day trip to disneyland, he was a brilliant help to us i must say this.on our first morning, we went for breakfast in the hotels restaurant (we mistakenly thought it was included in the price - our fault). we walked in and it seemed to be a bit of a help yourself/we'll take your order at the table set up, so as the waiters were staring at us (but not approaching to explain the routine) we felt under pressure to just do something. so we took a seat at a free table. the waiter then approached and asked if he could take our order, i just wanted a bowl of frosties and a slice of toast and my boyfriend ordered an omlette. i got the feeling from the waiter that we must have been doing something wrong with the ordering, and caused him some inconvenience but he never took the time to explain what we were supposed to do therefore how could we rectify this? as a result of whatever we did wrong?? the waiter proceded to be quite rude and abrupt to us throughout serving us. he nearly cut me with a look when i asked for a 2nd glass of orange juice. next thing shock horror, the bill arrived for the breakfast! you won't believe the price. 7 dollars plus tax for a small bowl of frosties, 5 dollars plus tax for one slice of toast with butter, 3 dollars each for the small glasses of orange juice and 15 dollars for an omlette served with a few breakfast potatoes. when we queried the waiter politely as to whether or not breakfast was included he stomped off to check with reception, he came back and said that it wasn't so we didn't argue and took the bill. he left us momentarily while we organised the money. the total bill including tax was around 38 dollars so we put 40 dollars in the bill booklet and as we stood to leave the waiter practically ran over to our table and picked up the bill booklet, in front of us, he rudely opened the bill, acknowledged the 40 dollars and threw his eyes to heaven with a loud tut because clearly he didn't think that 2 dollars was enough of a tip for making people feel uncomfortable and being rude right throughout our service.the sports bar in the hotel was very dingy and really undesirable but we ate there the first night, the food was only ok and a homeless person managed to come in and hassle us for a tip while we were eating.location-wise, the hotel was only ok too. we rented a car for a day or two which was great and also the metro stop was only around the corner which brought you to most places easily enough but it was a bit of a trek out to hollywood and universal studios. the gym and swimming pool were very poor as well unfortunatlely and we didn't feel the urge to use these facilities once we saw them.unfortunately, for the price we paid for the grubby accomodation and especially the measly overpriced breakfast, and the rudeness of that waiter, the dirt of the sports bar, it was just enough for me to say that for your money you could probably get a better hotel in la in possibly a better location. i honestly wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone - especially tourists, maybe we had that look about us that they felt they could throw us in any old room and we'd be content because to be honest the hotel seems to hold a lot of business conferences etc during the day and the restaurant where we had breakfast seems to be a classy financial district type restaurant where professionals go for business meetings over dinner or something. they could do with concentrating on their accommodation though. unless there was a different set of rooms for business guests, then i don't understand how they would stay in this hotel over night?!

enjoyed the millenium! my husband i stayed two nights at the millenium biltmore in la while waiting to board a cruise ship. it was our first time in la and we thoroughly enjoyed both the hotel and the city. a car rental is a must though to get around and see everything. the hotel was so impressive - old and beautiful; very comfortable room and bed; wonderful restaurant; accomodating staff. highly recommend it!

biltmore a bit loud i spent four nights at this hotel at the end of april and must say i was really disappointed. i've stayed here before, but the room i had previously faced a courtyard and not the street. my room this trip was on the eigth floor, so you'd think street noise wouldn't be a factor, but unfortunately it is. this hotel is so old that it does not have a double pane windows, so you hear everything outside. since l.a. is always busy, there was always noise. also, my room did not have drapes, so the morning sunlight also was a problem and i woke up much earlier than i'd prefer. i had a huge corner suite, but there was only a small chair and desk, no couch to lounge on unfortunately. also, the ac in my room did not work half the time and when it did it sounded like a lawnmower was running in my closet. the valet here is also brutal if you have a car. it takes forever to pull in because their driveway is really small and can't accomodate a lot of traffic. the restaurants here aren't great either and they close really early and are overpriced. this hotel is in need of some serious upgrades or i won't be coming back.

nice lobby, horrible rooms i stayed one night ilast december with my family. the moment you arrive the hotel, yo see the beautiful lobby, but once you get the rooms, you want to leave the hotel. even the service is really good, the rooms are extremely old, but not the old charm they appear they are.try to find other hotel in downtown, this is not worth it.

beautiful, reasonably priced old hotel my husband and i stayed at the millenium biltmore for a long weekend,and we really enjoyed it. the common areas are breathtaking -- the carved ceilings especially -- and the location is great. the rooms are nothing terribly special, but they are clean and spacious. for thevery reasonable price, i think this hotel is a great choice.

classic hotel even if the rooms aren't truely a classic, grand hotel as the public areas demonstrate. rich wood, high ceilings and all of the flair and taste that does take you back to the early 20th century. but it is an old hotel with the rooms to match. we have stayed there 2x ... once in a standard room and then on the club level. both rooms were in need of a degree of freshening as the general furniture and decor was dated and worn. the club level (a bit more $) did provide a nice sized, corner suite with plenty of light. included with the level was an excellent breakfast offering ... juices, fresh fruit, yogart, assortments of fresh bakery goods, etc., which was well appreciated. they provided a similar happy hour of sorts early evening also. that was a nice touch. we much prefered the club level and would consider staying again. service overall, was acceptable, not superior nor terrible.there are several very good restaurants within close walking distance if you choose. if you're looking for luxurious rooms and boutique surroundings, stay across the street at checkers (have stayed there also) and visit the biltmore's lobby but expect to pay serious cash for the difference.

has class but also flaws arriving at the biltmore and entering the lobby is impressive indeed. it is spacious and rather grand. a long hallway runs behind the lobby and contains restaurants, shops and convention room. the hotel has a good business location and is near the dorothy chandler pavillion. when i went to check in, i had to wait for about 10 minutes because the entire computer system had crashed. however, after, that there way no wait and i was on my way to my room. it was unacceptable.first, the room looked like something out of the 1950s -- an older looking, low-level queen bed complete with a 1950s/1960s style cream bedspread and dust ruffle that didn't match, didn't fit, and was torn. there's good retro and bad retro; this was bad.the carpet was stained. the room was very, very small and very dark. the view was of a wall. the bathroom was tiny and poorly remodeled. there was one wing-back chair that looked incredibly uncomfortable. also, the room was so small that you couldn't possibly sit in the chair and watch tv. tv was on the dresser. there was a desk with a desk chair. however, the desk was the only table in the room. there was no nightstand -- some weird heavy box-like object (like an overturned computer box) was lying on the floor right next to the bed with various wires attached to it. not sure what it was or what it was for. but no bed light, no place to put anything if you lay in bed. i didn't see a clock. the only phone was on the desk -- not reachable from the bed.the worst part, however, was that there were huge stains on the cream-colored bedspread. at that point, i demanded a new room.i was upgraded to a junior suite. very large with separate sitting room, but the furniture was still somewhat dated and i couldn't fairly describe the suite as attractive or luxurious. the carpet was stained. tiles were missing from the dressing area counter. the tvs (there were 2) were only 19 at best. the bathroom was ok but small and also a bit dated. also, no mini-bar and no bottled water, coffee or tea. not sure if there were vending machines but, other than tap water, nothing in the room to drink. service was unremarkable -- neither great nor bad. concierge was helpful. checkout was slow -- there were 7 people in line and only one person to provide assistance. room service (breakfast) was fine -- prompt and tasty. had dinner in the japanese restaurant; it was good as was the service there. didn't make use of other hotel facilities.i get the impression that what room you end up with could mean the difference between a decent stay and an unsatisfactory one but am not sure what room or type of room you need to request. there is a club level -- didn't stay there but maybe it's better.overall, my experience was merely okay (once i was in the second room). i've stayed in many nicer hotels for the same price and thus will probably look elsewhere when i return.

nice restoration i stayed at the millenium biltmore hotel with an out of town guest so we could do some shopping in the jewelry district (very convenient.) i was not pleased to get dinged the $32.00 overnight parking charge (no mention of it when i booked the room) although i expect you'll pay a charge for parking in any big city. i had expected some attention with unloading our bags, checking in, etc. (we got some on the way out, but not the way in) and ended up just feeling fortunate that the valet finally parked the car. the hotel is beautifully restored and the common areas of the hotel were immaculately clean. we stayed on the concierge floor (11th) and we were very pleased with our room. the beds were comfortable and the room was very quiet. the fitness center was nice, fairly small but had a steam room which i loved they are generally hard to find. the concierge lounge was acceptable, not really anything special, and you need to get there early if you are interested in the snacks because when they run out, they aren't replenished! my friend experienced some poor service in the big hotel bar but went on to find the sports bar which she enjoyed very much. the service issues, although small, are what prevent me from giving this hotel maximum stars. overall, we really enjoyed our stay.

upscale common areas, average rooms, good price i have stayed at this hotel several times over the past year, and never been disappointed. first impression is the lobby, ballroom hall, and the bar are fantastic and reminiscent of old hollywood. it has a great gym also. the rooms are in need of an update of the bed linens to get them up to par with chains such as hilton. the room itself was nice, the bathrooms are a bit small and cramped, and the tv's are very small. no wireless internet. 30.00 to park for guest which i think is outrageous. but if you book far enough in advance, the rates are very very good for such a beautiful hotel and its ammenities. i have never paid more than 150.00 a night, and for downtown la that is a great rate. the hilton across the street is close to 400.00 a night. the sports bar has pretty good food, or you can walk a block to mccormick schmidts as well. i would certainly recommend this hotel for busienss travelers, or even tourists should stay here at least once to check out the place.

movie set hotel the biltmore is kept in a very traditional manner-it is full of history and in this respect a fascinating hotel-it has been used in many many films and tv shows and i have recognised it in a few since we stayed there. it staged the oscars in the 1930's, was jfk's campaign hq and has lots of other claims to fame.it is still a well appointed hotel, we had a nice large comfortable room which was clean and well appointed.the windows are old and therefore noise and cold can be a problem.the location is also a bit of a problem if you arein la as a tourist, it is quite a way to hollywood blvd fro example and the streets around the biltmore at night are virtually empty, this can lead to it feeling a bit intimidating when walking back from the metro etc.we were lucky enough to be able to watch filming of 'without a trace' being done in the hotel, it was in a room just off from the lifts that used to be the reception in days gone by-it was interesting to see.if staying here it is definately worth speaking with a member of staff about the history of the place, they all seemed well educated on their workplace-from al capone, the beatles to the victim of the black dahlia murder, they have all been there!

old school charm i stayed at the millenium biltmore for business. it has a great location downtown and it is easy to get in and out of the parking/valet area. the biltmore has old school charm. i have attended several conferences at this hotel and all have gone very smoothly. the ballroom is beautiful. you can look at all of the old pictures of past events and celebrities. the first room that i was given at the time of check in was not good. i walked in to a strong mildew smell and the bottom of the comforter was stained. it was also very drafty and loud. the window was not sealed and there was a 1 inch gap between the top and bottom window. i asked to be moved and they put me into another room that was smaller but very cute, comfortable, and clean. dinner room service was always prompt and the food was good (i didn't have breakfast at the hotel). the fitness center does not open until 6am, so for people that have to get going early that doesn't work. the fitness center does have a variety of weights and machines and a cool indoor lap pool. the front staff was friendly and efficient.

look, but don't stay. this hotel exudes the golden age of hollywood. the lobby and common areas are nothing short of spectacular. be sure to look at all the wonderful photographs and memorabilia. i strongly suggest a visit for a drink or a walk-through, but do not recommend an overnight stay. the elegance ends when you get to your room. the rooms are comparable to the cheapest motels -- cheap bedspreads and linens, bad furniture, terrible art, etc. there is no mini-bar and the coffe pot is a one cup, paper no less, model. the bathrooms are even worse. the attempts to bring them up to date failed miserably. instead of capturing the era, they are a pitiful mix of styles and a terrible use of space. add to that, that the shower had no water pressure and tepid water on both mornings of my stay. and the worst is that no one has made any attempt to soundproof or at least diminish the traffic noise. i was on the 7th floor and would have sworn my window was open. the old original windows are in place and the plantation shutters (with some broken pieces) did nothing to muffle the noise. neither did the drapes. while some older hotels have fans in the ac system that can be turned on high to muffle street sounds, this one did not, so you were stuck with noise far worse than any i have heard in nyc. after reading this, i changed my review to terrible, from okay. the lobby and beauty of the structure, just can't make up for the woeful inadequacies of a hotel that bills itself as a luxury property. there was nothing luxurious about the accommodations.

good, but... hotel is architectural and the public spaces are very nice. i understand the public spaces were re-done about five to seven years ago. in fact, a movie was being filmed during my stay at the hotel. the room - at least my room - was marginal. it was clean. everything was as it should have been, but it seemed empty. there was a large bookcase and a secretary desk with no books and no scratch paper, pens, etc. what astounded me was that i learned that the hotel management company changed about five to seven years ago. yet, items in the room with logo's on them (that is, hotel name) were still of the old management company.the hotel is located downtown. i had not been to la before. i learned that the downtown area essentially closes after about 6:00pm. i walked around within a block either direction to find a restaurant or deli to get something to eat on my arrival night. nothing was open. walking more than a block from the hotel, i found the areas rather seedy.i think this hotel is good if you attend a conference (which i did), but it would not be good to use as a base for a vacation.

beautiful lobby, ballrooms. rooms aren't that great unless your royalty. stayed during christmas 2006. hotel may be great to see on a historic tour of l.a. and if your an old hollywood buff and want too see where 1930s academy awards were held. rooms are lackluster and underkept in comparison to lobby and ballrooms. all ballrooms where locked up ( best part of hotel and they lock it up to guests!). i did sneal a peek one day at the biltmore bowl and the crystal ballroom, beautiful! i just got lucky that day. a film crew where in and they unlocked it all for them. the resturant were bothered that a asked for my a.m. coffee in a to go cup, they told me they don't do that. staff was cold, distant and security were plentiful and cold also. hard to get people to smile around there. we had a room with two queen beds. bathroom was the worst. mold, old broken cheap fixtures, bathtub was never cleaned while we were there. such a grand hotel but comes up very short on guestrooms. all the money must go to keeping lobby and ballrooms beautiful. so, it looks pretty online and the main entrance is, but if you like plush rooms and cleanliness this is not the hotel for you.
i spent christmas at the biltmore rendevous court stairway

great hotel, location not suitable for tourists we stayed here on 02 november 2006 for three nights.the hotel is beautiful in decor and the history of the place is interesting. worth getting up early from the jet lag and having a walk around. the rooms are fine for an old hotel, the size of the room was adequate and yes the bathrooms are small, but what do you expect from an old hotel? we have stayed in brand new hotels with smaller bathrooms! the rooms were clean and serviced every day. we were in room 840 which looked out the side of the hotel. noise was a bit of a problem with traffic but no more than stopping in a london hotel. if you are a light sleeper you might want to pack some earplugs.the reception staff were fine and the concierge was very helpful. the only problem with this hotel is its location. as we were only in la for three nights we wanted to see all the sights. by being downtown it took a long time to get anywhere, even with the metro. one option on the menu was a breakfast buffet for $20 + tax which is slightly steep compared to other hotels we stayed in, but there was plenty of choice. the service was fine though the waiters could have been a little friendlier. i would recommend anyone staying for business to stay here, but anyone going to la for leisure to pick the location of their hotel wisely that is unless you want to stay in a hotel that is beautifully decorated and has a bit of hollywood history and glamour.
fine hotel @ good price a basic, but neat tidy room on third floor

biltmore blues run, do not walk. do not house your events here. if this is your only down-town option, change the plan. they are a disorganized disaster. we heard that they are about to be sold which may account for the poor service that we had all weekend long. the front desk gave away the bridal and the hospitality suited though we had signed up for it six months ago and it was in the signed contract (they argued that no room is ever guaranteed). though they recovered the bridal suite (late in the day on friday) and found a hospitality room for my parents (located on a different floor from all of the guests rather than the one my mom had scheduled six months ago) they did so inefficiently and ineffectively. the crowning mis-management error came when they woke my sister and her new husband at 6 am on the dawn following her wedding saying the bill must be settled immediately; these villainous hoteliers actually came to the suite, pounded on the door and refused to leave when the staff already had an imprint of a credit card at the desk. please tell all your friends to stay away from this venue. they donéˆ¥??› have their act together. . .

grand old hotel we recently stayed at the biltmore for 3 nights. the staff were friendly when we arrived and the room clean and tidy with coffee and tea facilities. two double beds and a small table and chair.the foyer, reception and lobby areas were impressive.on arrival there was a demonstration in pershing park which created noise when the window was open but overall the room was quiet and you couldn't hear your neighbours.we were pleased with the service and cleanliness of the hotel and it was great to stay in a hotel with history. the hotel shop was full of interesting photos and facts about the hotel.we would stay again if in los angeles.
grand historic biltmore this is rendezvous court, where we could get drinks late and just relax. this was how...

a worldl of luxury what a wonderfull experience. this large, character hotel situated in downtown la. the atmosphere and ombience of this classic hotel has to be experienced to believe.i had to double check what i had paid as i was sure it was too exepensive for me. but no a great hotel in a great location with loads and loads of history.we visited hearst castle 2 days before and this was like going back to hearst castle.you must visit to believe

beautiful classy hotel please do not pay attention to those who would say negative things about the biltmore, they obviously were expecting a new hilton or something of the like.the biltmore is a lovingly restored hotel, originally built in 1923. decorative and classic, i enjoyed it from the moment i stepped foot inside. the staff is perfect, every need is quickly attended to.checkin was a breeze, and that is not always easy when there is a gigantic wedding going on!we wandered around and looked at the banquet rooms which were beautifully restored with mouldings, beams, murals, carvings and the like. absolutely beautiful works from the original muralist known as smeraldi whose paintings are also in the sistine chapel.the restaurants are simply breathtaking in their beauty and the food is unparallleled.the high tea in the rendezvous room is something you do not want to miss! very good tea with lovely scones and goodies, excellent service and ambience. they make you feel like royalty!we had a room on the 7th floor, and the room was furnished nicely and well-cared for. it is obvious the hotel is older, there are still remnants of dumbwaiters, and other little bygone-era touches.but we loved the place and can't wait to return!

great experience! love the new store! i come to la ca. and stay at biltmore in la. once every 6 months. i made my trip to california the last weekend of september . i must say it was a wonderful experience. from the lobby to the rooms i was impressed as i always am. i love the little shops there... one the older shops were replaced with a new shop ... i believe the store was named treasurer! beautiful store, great products, and very helpful service. its a great addition to the hotel and ideal for tourists like myself to go in and buy suveniers .. i will definitely be stopping in on my next trip.. i would definitely reccomend toursits and visitors to stay at biltmore it is an overall wonderful experience, no doubt!caroline~ r.

can't see what the problems are here??? i stayed at the millenuim biltmore in september, from the 4th until the 8th, and thoroughly enjoyed my stay.the lobbies and public areas are just beautiful, i felt like i was in old-world hollywood!my room was a great size - not at all small, we had two double beds and plenty of room to relax and spread out.the bathroom was more than adequate - large,even, and although was starting to show its age it was on the whole well maintained and clean.i found the staff to be pleasant and helpful, providing us with directions, and advice, and the valet staff were excellent.many complain about the price of parking - welcome to big city holidays! coming from sydney, australia - these prices are par for the course..as far as location went, for us it was great, easy to get to all the major attractions by car, and the train was two blocks away.

unimpressed with the biltmore the biltmore is an old beautiful hotel in downtown los angeles. however, the old portions of the hotel outweighed the beautiful parts. the lobby and accompanying area are quite well-done, it is interesting staying in a hotel that has hosted many 1950s award shows. it seems though that the rooms have not been redone since right before the 50s shows. we were surprised that the tv was color (the most modern feature in the room). i can appreciate historic hotels, but at some point the guest rooms need an update. the property is large and i figure this is the reason that the housekeeping did such a shabby job cleaning the room. overall, we were disppointed especially having come from another historic hotel in santa monica that had done everything right. if you don't need to be in downtown la for business, don't stay in downtown. however, if work brings you into the city look elsewhere for a quality hotel, the biltmore missed the mark.

if i could be there now! this is far more one of the best hotels i have stayed. i can not see how anyone was rate this bad. it is beautiful and everybody is so helpful. we only had one problem when the air stopped working in the room then we was upgraded for the same price. everytime i show the pictures everybody comment on the room and pool area and we recommend to everyone no matter what state it is to stay at the blitmore and you can not go wrong. yes there is a bit more homeless people than where i am from (ga) but they do not bother you and after stepping out of that hotel it just shows you just how blessed you are. all the attractions are good. great sate!

great stay! booked two rooms here for a concert overnight stay and was very impressed. the staff was friendly and helpful, was not put off in the least because of booking through priceline (which is sometimes the case.) our rooms were clean and charming, the lobby was all the glamour we expected at the original sight of the academy awards, and our breakfast there was outstanding. walking through the halls and taking in all of the historic photographs was as good as a visit to an entertainment history museum! we did not use the pool, but it is truly a work of deco art. i was somewhat worried about this booking after reading some negative ta reviews, but my stay was a positive one from start to finish. which just means that while not everyone is going to be pleased, not everyone is going to end up having a bad experience either. i would highly recommend this hotel for a lovely step away from the typical city high rise hotel.

beautiful lobby, friendly service the biltmore lobby is beautiful, the staff was very courteous and friendly. we were booked for a deluxe king, however, we were traveling with 2 preteen girls. we needed 2 beds. the first night, we received a room with two double beds, as there were no queens available, so it wasn't very comfortable. the room was older inside than anticipated, though clean. we were along the courtyard. we asked if we could change to a room with two queens the following day and they accommodated us at no extra charge. this room was much more what i expected. because the hotel was downtown the traffic was a bit noisy, but we were so tired from playing it didn't much matter.

mixed feelingas about the biltmore i have mixed feelings about the biltmore. lets start with the positve:the price - very good value especially if it includes breakfast.the buliding is very impressive - very grand and the rooms were clean and comfortable. the breakfast was excellent and attention from the waiters very good. we liked the location and used the nearby subway station at pershing square to get to univeral studios and hollywood. the public transport is very cheap and efficient. we even got the bus to santa monica !!however there are some negatives:we arrived at 4.30pm after a flight from the uk. at first we were told there were no rooms available(despite booking and paying well in advance with a very reputable company in the uk). the receptionist then offered us 1 upgraded room on the club floor (but not allowed to use the extra facilities on that floor) and were told to phone down at 8 pm to see if our other room was available. so 5 of us - 3 adults and 2 kids (aged 12 and 13) tried to get a bit of rest in a room with 2 double beds. we were lucky - a gentleman checking in at the same time was sent away despite having a reservation number. at 8pm we were advised that our room would not be available until 11pm!!! at this point we spoke to the manger and told him we were going for a meal and when we got back we wanted a room or another hotel. half an hour later we had our 2nd room - albeit 2 floors below the other one. because of this probem we did manage to get a late check out free of charge the day we left but only because we asked and it was given grudgingly. the receptionist seemed to think that 1 upgraded room was sufficient compensation. on that subject, the only difference i could see between the club rooms and the standard rooms was the decor, newspaper deliverd to the room and free bottled water!rooms were clean and comfortable but in need of a little tlc - a bit worn in places and in need of an upgrade. bath rooms are small even by british standards and definatley in need of an upgrade.pool - not in use as under repairlocation good but a lot of panhandlers about - no problems but may make some people uneasy.the probelms with check in didn't in the end spoil our stay but i would be wary about staying here again.

millenium biltmore - an unfriendly place we stayed at the biltmore from july 12th to the 15th 2006. as a family (my husband, myself and three children aged 4, 11 and 16) travelling from australia, we'd just had 3 days at disneyland staying at a hotel in anaheim. when we moved from anaheim to the biltmore i immediately felt we didn't fit in there. the ladies at reception were extremely unfriendly and when we asked them a question it was answered extremely reluctantly. my husband and i had a drink in the gallery bar (the children were in the room watching tv) and the barman was also not very friendly.the concierge, a wonderful man called james, made up for the unfriendly staff with his charming and friendly manner and he gave us all sorts of helpful tips, such as the location of a market nearby where we could purchase fruit for the children (we bought 5 bananas for us 80 cents! wow! in australia currently bananas cost about au$2.50 each!!!) and advice on what sort of tour of la we should go on.yes the biltmore is a beautiful and impressive hotel with a colourful history. however it's the first hotel i've stayed at where there was no bar fridge in the room - this costs an extra $10 per night! the pool, which the children were desperate to try out was not available the whole time we were there (!!! in the middle of summer!!!! grrr!!!) the room was spacious and comfortable but overall i would not stay there again.
glamour at the biltmore hotel exterior of the biltmore - classic architecture

i wouldn't pay to stay here i stayed here 2 nights for a meeting and am glad i didn't pay for it. the lobby and ballrooms are lovely, but it stops there. my room was small and dingy and the bathroom was gross. there was mold on the tiles and the bathtub didn't drain properly, so i ended up standing in a foot of water towards the end of my shower. i have to say the staff was not very good in regards to meeting logistics. there were av problems, the staff took forever to get there, and it took a long time to get things straightened out. they did not speak english very well and did not seem to fully understand what they were doing. i would visit this hotel again to admire the lobby beauty but never pay to stay.

enjoyed the milennium biltmore. location very convenient. was a little hard to find the milennium biltmore at night, but once we did, we found it to be lovely. feels like an old distinguished hotel. the lobby and other rooms are gorgeous, really. paid 150 per night (weekday rate), plus 30/night for parking (pretty much the standard for downtown).our room (called a king deluxe, i believe) was quite spacious. the decoration was a little spartan perhaps, but still nice. bathroom was fine, well-appointed, though a little on the small side. i think those that complain about the size, however, are maybe used to newer bigger hotels. we had more room than we needed overall. i guess it's possible that other four stars are nicer, but to us, it felt grand and stylish in an old school sort of way.we loved being right downtown, three blocks from the moma, disney concert hall, music center, mark taper, etc.would definitely stay there again.

ditto "false impressions" i agree completely with the previous author. i only wish i had the review before i booked the reservation. i ended up cutting my trip short by one day and spent my time hanging out at the bonaventure instead.
false impressions bathroom is the size of 10yr. old girl's closet. found a dead bug in the tub.
good stay to top it all off they shut off the water.

parking issues at biltmore millenium service was good, decor interesting for los angeles, friendly stuff, lots of events and weddings taking place downstairs, good restaurant...but someone already noted - parking (a couple of years ago) was over 30 dollars overnight! and for over two hours! including guests you invite over to dinner! i stayed in this hotel and invited some friends who live in town, and they got stuck with 33 dollar bills for parking their car in the hotel. nobody walks in la or uses public transportation, it is only driving. downtown la is not exactly a beautiful area, and not pedestrian friendly either. there is no place to park near by either... so... i think with the money this hotel charges for stay, parking for guests should be complimentary or reduced price, no more than 3 dollars. but 33!..hmm

nothing better, fantastic my wife and i and another couple were coming to la for a conference at the end of april. i reserved the biltmore before i started reading all the reviews. as you know the reviews are all over the map, from positive to negative. well let this very conservative canadian from edmonton describe the biltmore. first impression driving to the entrance was wow, they then let us check in at 12:00, 3 hours adhead of the posted check in time. service was great. both rooms were above average in size with great king size beds. who cares if the bathrooms were a little small. our rooms were in the 01-10 range and thus at the end of a very short hall, no noise what so ever. we were there for 6 nites and the staff became more than staff they became friends. the doormen and the bellmen were all fantastic. the champs sports bar was friendly and the food good. the pool area was above average. the history of the hotel was nothing but amazing and the public areas were like nothing i had ever seen. the neighborhood??? i felt comfortable going for walks at 6 in the morning or 10 at nite. as far as the homeless, they are far more polite than the homeless i have met in other cities. more importantly if you take the time to talk to them you will realize that they are just like the rest of us. they were great and no reason to be afraid of them. they are also polite enough to say hello every day and remember you. all in all the biltmore and the neighborhood were great. if some one wants to stay downtown this is the place to be, a nice easy 15 minute walk to the staples center or the convention center. the staff need to be commended for their positive attitudes and although i am not a world traveler, i would will out any hesitation at all recommend the biltmore. i will be back, and i will recommend to all the people that i know who are going to la. to the management and staff thanks for a wonderful experience.

shiny front - shabby back. good for smokers. the brochures and website photos all laud the grand ballrooms and lobby. these are indeed magnificent but belie the rooms behind them. you can stay somewhere better and just walk in and look. at $usd185 a night we didn't expect to find our bathroom door off its hinges or the continuing struggle with room staff for such trivialities as providing more coffee satchets. the guy that fixed the door was resigned to the fact that he and his colleagues had a real job on their hands and told us we were lucky that we didn't have plumbing problems.parking is very expensive and the valets (compulsory valet service) get surly if not tipped extravagantly.on the plus side - for all those smokers out there - the biltmore's fire escape lobbies are not alarmed or monitored and open on to little balconies. just perfect for that quiet smoke without having to get dressed and leave the hotel.

an enjoyable historical experience my wife and i stayed at the biltmore for one night as part of a much-longer trip to la and southern ca. a lot of tourists and business travelers go to the biltmore because of its high-class reputation and historical significance; we were there as part of a self-guided architectural history walking tour (which i highly recommend btw, check the la conservancy web site). the best feature of this hotel is its public areas ... make sure you allocate time to sit in the lobbies, have a look at the banquet rooms, have a drink at the martini bar (expensive but very romantic) and definitely swim in the beautiful italian-tile pool. i think the hotel is aware of the popularity of its public areas; after i got dressed i took several pictures of the pool and at some point a security person showed up and looked me over (but left when i smiled and waved at him). the rooms were small but very clean and the bed was wonderful. decor is classy but materials are somewhat old. the bathroom was very small but nicely tiled and worked well. we had a view of the interior air column of the hotel, but after walking around downtown la i can't say that we would have benefitted much by an exterior view! the staff are very nice and polite but very busy (i get the impression that there are a lot of people checking in and out all the time). internet is not free and parking is expensive. the neighborhood has improved a lot in the last decade-- we felt safe at night but there are a lot of disheveled, muttering people wandering about and occasionally panhandling in their polite, southern california style.overall, i'd comment that this hotel is worth a stay for historical reasons and to experience the hotel itself, but i personally wouldn't recommend it for kids or for a long tourism experience outside of the downtown la area.
why the complaining? ? its just beautiful!!! our room

bed was awesome @ biltmore! arrived to find out we were only getting a 2 double beds. i was told online company we used to book didn't have guaranteed king beds. after a slight nudge, they found a nice room w/ a king size bed.bed was extremely comfortable, pillow was nice and full shower pressure was awesome. first night was very pleasant.we asked for recommendations for vegetarian dinning and we were very pleased with the assistance we received.the second night was going as well as the first until @ 3:30pm the neighbor next door decided to turn on the tv full blast and pass out. after 1 hr of patiently waiting for the neighbor to find their common courtesy i finally called the front desk to have them take care of the issue. 30 minutes later i had to call the front desk again for status. they assured me they would take care of it immediately as they had thought security resolved the issue. finally, after the 2nd call and 1 hr 45 minutes later we heard security come to the room and after knocking numerous times and yelling through the door for the person to come to the door, they finally were able to reach the neighbor and we got to get a few minutes of additional nights sleep before we had to get up.on-site sushi restaurant was very pricey but the food was excellent.view was pretty nice as well.overall: 9 (if neighbor issue didn't happen.)overall: 8 (because it took 2 calls to get the issue resolved.)

great building - but !! we stayed at the biltmore, which is downtown, for 3 nights in april 2006 as part of our 25 th wedding anniversary 2 week trip to america. the biggest problem we encountered was the location. we were there over good friiday through to sunday and with all the business's closed it was like a ghost town. as soon as we walked out of the hotel we were constantly approached by homeless people morning and afternoon. we decided not to go out after 1800 and although we still managed to go were we wanted did not get to go the bars or restaurants in the evening. i would certainly stay in annother part of la. we did the city tour which was really what you have to do to see hollywood etc. we also went out to santa monica which was more suitable for staying in and then touring the city. conversations with locals backed up our view that downtown is not a good place to be after 1800, whereas santa monica was.getting back to the hotel, i can't see it surviving and attracting tourists, it has great history and they are doing their best to keep it up to scratch, but it feels like a hotel without any sole and the staff need an update on customer service. i wa hoping for some recognition that we were on our 25th anniversary trip, however despite their promises to 'let me know' they never responded and did seem to have some superior attitude that is not acceptable these days. my advice pick annother hotel

an overpriced relic i thought the hotel was a magnificent piece of history but some things should be confined to the past. the standard of the hotel in relation to the price was poor in comparison to other places i have stayed at in california. i found that the car parking charge was $24 per day. most hotel parking is free. this was a hidden cost i could have done without. oh, and it is only valet parking so be careful if you have a rental car. if you want to know where the nearest convenience store is - don't bother asking the receptionist! overall, it the hotel is clean but a bit of a relic and there is no heart to the place. service is polite but not necessarily efficient and some staff cannot speak english. it is certainly not a four-star hotel.

not a 4 star this hotel is not up to it's 3 or 4 star standard. it should be a 2 star.i will state my case:we checked in and was told that the room we reserved.. a king non-smoking..was not available. instead, we had to choose between a queen and a double.don't be fooled. the room is not luxuriously decorated. it does not match the ornate lobby. it is super tiny. beds are like motel 6. no extra nice duvets or covers.staff may not be paying attention to details.. such as hallway lights gone out.the ac was not working in our room.we complained about the room. the next night, we got our king sized bed and a room twice as big. with it, we had a little sitting area.. yet it just looked underfurnished.. and still w/ the same ugly furniture. you also get a vanity area, yet it's really just.. a cubby w/ a glued on mirror.parking is expensive.. about 25 a night.

parking everything about this hotel is fine, but the parking needs to be improved. the receptionists are great, but the hotel charges too much for the parking. overnight parking is about $30 additional. my friend lived there for 2 days and i left my car there end up spending about $60 for just 2 day parking. they dont have any free parking for the guests either living there or just dropping by for dinner.

beautiful hotel--a little spooky/noisey, but a good value the hotel has a rich history--the academy awards used to be held there. it was jfk's campaign headquarters in 1960. the beatles once landed on the rooftop there in a helicopter. although beautiful, remember it is an old building. i recently stayed there and experienced random unexplained noises in my room (haunted perhaps?) that kept my awake. bring earplugs. if that doesn't work, some holy water and an exorcism should do the trick.

a classic my wife and i spent three nights at the biltmore.we heap our praises upon the attentive staff, particularly the personnel in the hotel's dining rooms. they made our stay comfortable and pleasing.while we generally do not favor hotels of the size ofthe biltmore -- principally because we think thatthe service suffers -- we recommend this propertyfor its large rooms (with crown and base mouldingsand shutters), spectacular lobby (a wonderful settingfor the tea that the hotel offers each afternoon),surprisingly well-equipped gym (next to an art deco pool)and atmosphere of grace. we note that downtown la is not a whirl of activity. but the biltmore is near the freeway and (even better to our thinking) the metro and union station. should you wish to get out and explore we suggest taking a train to pasadena or to long beach. both are short trips and you will skip the socal traffic that we dread. when we next visit los angeles we will return to the biltmore.

a great experience! a few friends and i planned a spur of the moment, 4 night trip to los angeles. the pictures of the biltmore looked wonderful and we really liked the location so we made our reservations. i started to get a little worried after reading some reviews about the hotel and i just figured that i would have to find out for myself. i just want to say that my experience was absolutely perfect! everyone at the hotel, from the concierge to security to the valets and housekeeping, were incredibly friendly and accomodating. we wanted to check out the ballrooms on the lobby level (the crystal ballroom is where the academy awards used to be held) but some of them were locked. we happened to come across a security guard and just inquired about the history and he offered to take us through the locked ballrooms. the valet service was very convenient and not unreasonable (anyone from a large city would be used to paying for parking). we had a large corner room which had 3 huge windows that faced onto a courtyard - it was bright and extremely quiet, we didn't hear any traffic at all which was nice considering we were staying right in downtown la. this is a great location, very close to everything...took less than 30 minutes to get to santa monica beach on a beautiful friday afternoon. i would definitely stay here again!

great hotel with glitchy service i did not intend to waste time on writing reviews, but what i read below struck me as probably commissioned from the hotel management. it's true that this is a majesticly looking hotel at least at its lobby levels. the downtown location is really convenient and allows for some walk-arounds in the city. (still late night walks in la and sf are not recommended as those are laced with homeless people who cluster at dark for their rowdy drinking and may become agressive while panhandling, reminds me of new york in our pre-giuliani years)the club level rooms are bigger than the standard ones and ours came with breakfast and pre-evening snacks included.the service however varies from friendly to incompetent and downright hostile, depending on whom you get. we stayed 4 nights there over x-mas and came across at many employees asking for different things. we got confusing and contradicting answers like noone was truly aware what hotel's policies were. as in all us hotels the rooms in this one do not have ceiling lights-as one of the floor lamps in our room was missing a bulb i asked and left notes for a replacement for 2 days without much of an effect and ended up bying one for $0.99 from the nearby drugstore.when we left, my 9 year old daughter forgot a toy-cat in the room, we tried to call several times still from ca and got the telephone runaround to a department with a person who was always missing, left 3 or 4 mesages and sent 5 or 6 e-mails without having someone to answer whether at least they've found the toy. i don't even want to remember for the front desk guy who was refusing to let us into our room (with 2 young kids and weary of an 6 hour flight) because i've lost my aaa card (status verification from aaa is possible over the phone or online within 2 or 3 minutes) until someone higher intervened and left that verification issue for a more convenient time. ah, and also it took them 2 1/2 days and 4 calls on my part to deliver a fax to our room. yet we met some very helpful staffers during our stay and most of them balanced their poor english with an exuberant good will and after several explanations would finally understand what do you want from them.

i had always wanted to stay here... .. and i was not disappointed. this old hotel had always been on my wish list of places to stay. so when the oppurtunity came for me to visit my mother over the christmas holiday, i knew right where i wanted to stay.from the time i checked in, everyone was very very nice. please keep in mind i was traveling alone and am a 25 year old woman who looks 18. the took me very seriously and answered all my questions. the only thing i did not like that expedia did not tell me about when booking the room was that they needed a credit card where they could hold $50 a day for extra room charges (phone calls, room service, etc.) when i explained to the front desk clerk that i did not have that, she happily waived that fee and i had to use the phone in the lobby. i could still receive phone calls in my room for no charge and my cell phone worked just fine on the 4th floor. no problem for me.the location is wonderful. the dash service gets you almost anywhere downtown for a quarter and drops off right in front of the hotel. same goes for the bus and underground system, which is about 1 block away. the shopping at macy's plaza and the shops at 7th and fig. were only blocks away.as for food, the dinning at the hotel was a bit to pricey for me but there are tons of fast food and small places around the area. not to mention that domino's pizza delivers to the hotel. the concierge desk was so helpful with all information that i needed, from places to eat downtown, to museum hours during the holidays, to getting history on the hotel. the room was very comfortable and clean. there was no mini-bar but i was thankful not to have that temptation. i had just a regular room and was very happy with my choice.all in all i would recommend this for anyone. very pleasent place to stay within a piece of downtown los angeles history.
phantastic historic hotel - great value view from our room on pershing square

i love an old hotel just spent a long weekend at the biltmore. pluses: staff was friendly and helpful. room was surprisingly huge and quiet. valet parking efficient and quick. the afternoon tea a delight. the gym and indoor pool a time machine. great for exploring and people-watching. convenient to everything downtown. minuses: nonexistent water pressure in the shower. a lovely view of an airshaft. the price of the valet parking. overall: i couldn't recommend it more highly, and would definitely stay there again.

service is questionnable at the millenium biltmore... we expected more of the millenium biltmore and from the start, they totally and completely missed everything that is important to have a quality hotel.first, we arrived and there were some larger events (its 9:00 p.m.). it took us 30 minutes to even get close to the parking/valet area. ugh! we then checked in (knowing we had 9:30 p.m. reservations at their restaurant. it is published as being open till 10:00. the desk did call to say we would be late.)we then asked for our bags to be taken to the room so we could go to dinner. no can do - the bell hop said - you must be in the room and we cannot deliver for 15 minutes. we explained our dinner reservations and he said - too bad! he did relent and take them up about 5 minutes later.we then got to the restaurant at 9:40 p.m. ugh! we were basically blasted by the extremely unfriendly hostess - this lady should get a new job!!! she is one heck of an unpleasant person to deal with and said - you are bad people - you did not call to cancel your reservations - we are closing the restaurant now - we won't seat you. get out! ugh! here we are hotel guests - who have been mistreated by the hotel - and here we are getting yelled at.we then went upstairs to talk to the front desk. ugh! he suggested a couple of places we could have dinner....he said only a few blocks away. we arrived at 2 of them and they both were closing at 10 p.m.we then asked the last place - know of any places that stay open. luckily the standard does! and the standard hotel actually has great food and a fun bar area!we then went back to our room. the toilet was broken....we had to wait an hour for it to get fixed. we also found the bathroom extremely tight corners. ugh!for the price, its not worth staying here....we did find the room service menu to be good and enjoyed the room service japanese breakfast. of couse, when we got to use their in room check-out, it too was non functional. it took a bit to get the car to the front door by the valet - (note: the morning bell hop was wonderful and timely.)but in short----service here! only if you want to get yelled at; told wrong information; mistreated. (by the way we went to the bar and it stayed open till midnight - no munchies on the menu; and when they did not realize they had customers at the bar, we simply moved on up to the room.

impressive but dissappointing not worth the money as rooms are definitely not three star. staff are friendly enough and service is alright just not worth the money!getting around isn't as scary as it's made out to be in so many other reviews, as long as you don't walk about too late!! i live in glasgow so no big difference there!don't stay in this hotel because if you're just a tourist it's too far away from everything!!

good getaway stayed for thanksgiving and had the buffet. enjoyed some of the other hotel bars in the area especially the standard's rooftop lounge. nice old place parking was included in the club rate with a great breakfast bar the following day

pleasant stay we stayed at the biltmore on 09-23 for the first nite of our us journey. the atmosphere was very impressive, the room was okay and we loved the gym and pool/sauna area. very disappointing was the restaurant. i'm vegetarian and they have just one expensive dish to offer: penne pasta. this was made with soo much oil, that i later was afraid of getting sick. service was very poor as well - first they brought us an already used bread-basket...so, the hotel is beautiful-but the restaurant is expensive without being good - we can't recommend!

great weekend at the biltmore stayed at the biltmore the weekend of nov. 19th. my friend and i stayed overnight for a fresno state/usc football game at the coliseum. i had seen pictures of this historic hotel and had driven past it before so i thought i'd give it a chance. we opted for a millenium club room, which was a decent size and elegantly appointed. the bathroom was a bit small with hardly any counter space around the pedestal sink. other than that, the room was fine. our stay included complimentary drinks, which we took advantage of. i'm not much of a drinker and my martini was a bit strong - the bartender went out of his way to ask if it was ok and offered to water it down a bit, which was a pretty cool thing to offer for a novice drinker like me! we also received a complimentary breakfast brunch which was excellent. my friend and i enjoyed the little perks of a grand hotel - like having a turndown service for the beds at night and a newspaper at the foot of our door in the morning. i sound like a hotel broschure, but what can i say, i enjoyed my stay!

overall a good experience after reading so many mixed reviews online, my wife and i were a little anxious about staying at the millennium biltmore. while each guest's experience will be different, ours was overall good despite a few problems along the way. we arrived late at night and were assigned a room on the club level (even though we didn't pay extra). we were excited about this perk until we walked into our room and found 2 double beds instead of the king we had requested. we called the front desk and they agreed to move us to the next room. when we moved into the hallway to wait for our key to be delivered, we were greeted by a very unpleasant suprise--we could hear very loud music and other sounds coming from a room on our hall. the walls are apparently very thin! we called the front desk again and they agreed to move us to yet another room. they also sent security up promptly to take care of the noisy guests. our new room was very clean and nicely decorated (even mints on the pillows). however, don't be suprised by the very small bathroom. the bed was also very comfortable! the front desk and concierge were not very helpful at times, but occasionally provided good assistance. the valet (which is required) was slow and needs more workers. we made the mistake several times of trying to get our car at noon or 5:00 (when business meetings from hotel ballrooms were letting out) and eventually gave up on getting our car because of the long line. also, be sure to call well in advance of needing your vehicle, or you will be waiting a long time! the hotel is truly a classic beauty in the midst of a dingy downtown area. there is a ton of history (spend some time looking at the pictures of all of the academy awards held on premises) and the historic decor has been well maintained. we always felt very safe and taken care of. the hotel is also conveniently located to many different la destinations. despite all of the ups and downs of the stay, my wife and i both agreed that we would stay at the hotel again. it is a reasonably priced classy hotel with a convenient location.

millennium biltmore - beautiful hotel! we have just returned from la having stayed 5 nights at the millennium biltmore. it is a grand hotel -beautiful, spacious comfortable. we stayed in a standard room and as a treat, decided to upgrade to a club room on our last night. we were happy with both rooms. the standard room is adorned with oil paintings and beautiful furniture - the bed was very comfortable. it has a coffee maker. the club room is of course, bigger and more luxuriously furnished. it does not have a coffee maker but you can request one - i suppose the reason is that club room guests have access to the club lounge and are served complimentary beverages (including alcohol) and snacks from 5 - 8pm. there was no fridge in both rooms but ice is available on various floors. we throughly enjoyed our experience at the millennium biltmore. the service was great - we were pleased with the room service, bell service, concierge, front desk and housekeeping. we also enjoyed traditional afternoon tea at the rendevous court and were impressed by the spread of delightful sandwiches, tarts and cakes. the prices of food at the rendevous court are very reasonable and it has a wonderful ambience, casual yet stylish with a fountain in the centre of the room. we had breakfast at smeraldi's (another reaturant in the hotel) and the food was great. while we were there, two weddings were held in the ballroom. we had a peek through the entrance of the ballroom while they were getting the ballroom ready and it was just so beautiful!! the hotel is also a short walk to department stores such as macy's and robinson may's with a number of cafes and restaurants within its vicinity. as it's located in the financial district, it's in the nicer part of downtown la. in summary, this is a grand hotel with history - if you enjoy the splendour of grand old buildings, you will love the millennium biltmore!

great stay with a surprise! the millennium biltmore hotel is convienently located in downtown los angeles near freeway access, shops, and a plaza across the street. the lobby and public spaces are beautiful, full of classic moldings and decorations. if you like history, you would enjoy staying here! you feel like you are walking back in time as you walk through the halls and lobby. there is even a hall full of photos from the first academy awards ceremony held in the ballroom. we had no problems with the people who worked at the hotel, from the check-in clerk to the valet parking attendents. everyone was nice and friendly to us. our room, which we booked on priceline, was upgraded to a suite! what a pleasant surprise! there were four of us, my husband and i and our two young children, so the extra space was a wonderful bonus. the suite was the size of a small apartment, complete with a small entry hall, huge living room and dining room plus wet bar and refrigerator, and a separate spacious bedroom (with 2 double beds) and bathroom. there were two tvs, so the kids could watch their shows on one. the rooms were all clean and nicely furnished. the windows had shutters which blocked out the sunlight in the morning. our suite was located on a corner, so we could see across the street towards pershing plaza and over the roof top of a lower building. we felt very comfortable and safe staying here.i peeked into a standard room, and i can report that a standard room is just as spacious as an average hotel room. the same as the bedroom in our suite. i would not
