beats having to crawl into the closet to find the safe, which is where most hotels place them). just before leaving, we placed a call to the front desk lodging our tv repair request, and placed another in-person request with the concierge on our way downstairs to attend the pre-gala cocktail party (just in case). attendance at the cocktail party was great, but that also meant crowded, with lots of bodies in little space (the hallway outside the banquet room). it got really hot, really fast. we decided to take short leave of the festivities and head back up to our room to enjoy a glass of cold champagne and a chocolate-dipped berry or two, because (as it was upstairs in the club lounge) a glass of mediocre wine was $8.50. back at our rose petal festooned room, we found mr. maintenance carefully checking the plasma tv. he deduced that the tube was blown, and announced he was on the way downstairs to see if there was another tv around he could swap out. we advised him that we'd be there for about 20 minutes, so to come back after that, which he apparently did, as when we returned after 11:00 pm, the plasma was fixed. the last issue happened when we tried to access the thoughtfully-provided-and-easily-accessible-personal-safe containing our valuables, and found that no matter how many times we entered the carefully programmed personal code, the led display returned a error90 message. another call placed to the front desk requesting someone come by to fix obstinate electronic device resulted in yet another hotel staff member (this time from security) knocking on the door; this time at 11:45 pm, to reprogram the safe and rescue our belongings. while this seems like a lot of inconvenience...i can say the room itself was quite nice, the hor's douvres and the breakfast items were terrific - after we turned in the slight molded bagels in exchange for fresher, less green english muffins. recommend the management pay a bit of attention to quality checking the well-decorated and appointed rooms, and some time reviewing guest-preparation processes. this would go a long way toward making guest's stays more enjoyable.....by the way. if you've booked a club lounge access room, may i recommend requesting room 1125: most of the things that could go wrong in this room have already been fixed!

won't stay here again this was the third time i have stayed at this property, but this will be my last time. we have had problems each time. the last time they gave us a room that had been made up to look clean, but actually had dirty sheets and a bathroom that had been used.this time the lights did not work and the remote control had to be replaced. we stayed with a park n fly rate. even thought the rate was reasonable our car was so dirty we could barely see out the windshield. they said it would be parked in a garage, but i am not sure that happened. in the past they washed the car before they returned it to you. also after flying from montreal we had to wait 20 minutes to be picked up and after returning to the hotel had a wait another 15 minutes to get the car back and we were the only ones there at the time. oh yes my husband also loaded oour luggage. half way through someone came over to help since he was looking for a tip. i have also stayed at the sheraton lax and it was better. i will not be returning.

needed a hotel airport for a day flying into la to catch a cruise and needed a place to stay overnight. the hotel was as i expected for a marriott. no surprises and most important of all no disappointments. got a nice rate on a marriott weekend getaway promotion. ate dinner at the sports bar/restaurant at the airport marriott two blocks down, and breakfast at the hotel in between the two (whoéˆ¥??? name escapes me now) as we were not impressed with the restaurants at the renaissance. on the end of our trip, the room would have cost twice as much, so opted to stay at a different hotel for the last night in la, but only because of price.

very good airport hotel we stayed at the renaissance montura for 2 nights in a suite on the concierge level. the suite was a good size and was very clean and comfortable with all the little touches you would expect from a 4 star. the service from the reception, concierge and staff in the club lounge was excellent and the food was good too. we particularly enjoyed the chocolate covered strawberries in our room. the hotel also has a small pool, jacuzzi and fitness room, which we didn't use but they looked very well maintained. overall we were really pleased with our stay and everything about the hotel. for the price it is excellent value for money.

loved the renaissance montura i booked this hotel for $99 on the marriott website for a friday night. the hotel was beautiful with comfortable beds and nicely decorated rooms. the staff was friendly and helpful. there is a burger king across the street so you can save money on food. hertz, avis, and budget are nearby also if you need to return a rental car. there is a well stocked gift shop in the lobby and i was impressed with how many different items they offered. the bellman who carried our luggage up brought us 3 bottles of complimentary water. anytime we called down for extra towels or soap they were brought quickly. the hotel looks brand new and we really enjoyed staying there. i would definitely stay at this hotel again.

fab time! having just returned from a 3 week self planned tour of the west coast with my husband and 11 year old son i feel i must compliment the montura hotel. we stayed for the first 4 nights of our adventure and our only problem were noisy neighbours on the first night. the next morning we mentioned it to the concierge when asking for info on the area ( all of which we got plus maps etc - extremely helpful) - within seconds she said the 'noisy' guests were here for a while and she would upgrade us to a club room.the bedroom was a good size , comfortable with an attractive decor - bathroom was clean but not particularly stylish so could be updated to bring it more in line with the rest of the hotel, which had a luxurious feel with attractive artwork and sculptures.couldn't hear any airport noise although we could see the planes coming in to land which my son found exciting. we used the self parking which was a little cheaper than the valet parking and just used an interior lift to get to the appropriate parking floor - no hassle at all. we had breakfast included and it was one of the best things we did - staff were polite, attentive and the cook makes a mean omelette - lots of choice. well worth a visit. p.s. used trip advisor to assist in the planning of our holiday.

very nice airport hotel i bid on priceline.com and paid only $116 (including tax) for one night in this 4-star hotel. it was definitely worth it. it is a true 4-star hotel with all the style, comfort, and space. i asked for a room with double beds, but the hotel clerk told me that they ran out of such rooms and upgraded me to a room with a living area, and a pull-out sofa. it has plenty of desk and storage space, a large bathroom, two tvs, and a king-size bed. my mom and i had a very restful night between flights. though it was near the airport, we couldn't hear the airplanes at all when inside the room. it doesn't feel like an airport hotel at all. there is a burger king right across the street, so you can save money on food if you don't mind fast food for one day (we didn't.)

nice option in a central spot we chose to stay here even though we weren't flying in an out of lax. we got a nice rate for a great hotel, especially when comparing what the rates were going for with similar class hotels in other areas of l.a. staff were friendly and quick during check-in. self parking was included in our rate and was pretty easy breezy. the room was nicely appointed, with nice bed linens, marble counter-tops, and a flat screen tv. i was mostly impressed that we could not hear the airplanes at all. the room was nice and silent! we would not hesitate to say here again in the future.

good and bad stayed at the lax renaissance as a quick place to stay after arriving late into lax at the start of our trip. first, if you arrive late (after 11pm), their shuttle hardly ever shows up. we waited in the exhaust fumes for 30 mins before calling the hotel. all of the other hotel shuttles arrived - just not ours. when we called, they told us to book a cab and they would reimburse. cab fare was $20 with tip. i asked the cabbie when we got in if he took credit cards. he said yep. when we arrived, he told me he did not take credit cards, and pointed to the atm in the hotel lobby.lobby is nice and clean and updated. it's very close to the airport. hertz rentals is within walking distance (about two long blocks). the room is very small and has a musty smell. the a/c barely kept the room warmish-cool. the bathroom was worn out and old, but not dirty. the staff was generally nice and efficient though it took me a few calls to get extra pillows and towels.internet is available for a cost. it's generally pretty quiet. so i would recommend it for a no-frills, but expensive, one night stay after or before a flight at lax.

nice but not great recently stayed at this hotel after a 16 hour non-stop flight from asia. picked up a rental car so can not comment on the shuttle service but did notice that there seemed to be more shuttle buses for the hotels than some of the rental car companies.good sized room with a very comfortable bed. older style bathroom but certainly clean and plenty of towels. paid the extra for the club level but didn't use many of the extras as we got in late and left v early.low noise level given how close to lax the hotel is, allowing us to get a good nights sleep. room service food was excellent but huge serving sizes. corona's were expesnive even for us hotel prices, but you pay for the convenience of room delivery with a smile.the only downside was that the room rate supposedly included 8 bottles of water which would have been handy for the early morning drive. however, the check-out desk staff had no idea what i was talking about even though i'd called down 2 minutes earlier and i'd been told to collect them from the front desk by another staff member. given it was before 6am i couldn't be bothered arguing and tracking down whom i'd spoken with.... and hit the road.overall, i'd stay there again but could not say i loved it. however, it is a great airport hotel.

thoughtful staff, great food, loved it! my husband, mother-in-law, and i stayed at this hotel while traveling to ca to get married. we stayed four nights/ five days, and loved it! realistically, the shuttle was a little slow because of the sheer volume of people it had to pick up, and drop off, but the valet parking was awesome, and affordable at just $25/per day. once we arrived, the check-in was fast, and the ammentities were terrific. the bed was so comfortable! one night we were stuck in traffic for so long, that we were unable to get to any open restaurants, and decided to do room service. after a certain time, the hotel menu drops down to about 4 items, and i wanted some real food! i called the kitchen, and they told me to order whatever we wanted, and they'd fix it. they were so sweet. the hotel food is quite expensive but so good, and i'm a very picky eater. after getting married on the beach in santa barbara, we arrived back to our room to find fresh rose petals all over the floor and bed, as well as chilled champagne, 2 champagne flutes garnished with strawberries, and chocolate covered strawberries! it was such a nice surprise. the staff came in and cleaned at whatever time we specified, which were always really odd hours, and never interrupted our sleep. every night their was a turn down service when we returned from our destination, and it made our stay even more special.added suggestion: make sure to get the club level room package so that you have access to the conceirge lounge. they provide breakfast, hors d'eurves, dessert, soda, coffee, hot chocolate, and water that is completely complimentary. it's not open all day long, but it is open several hours at a time. it was fun to get to try different things. it's worth a little extra money per night.hope you have as good a time as we did!

the club floor ain't worth it!!! we stayed at this hotel for one night in preparation for our flight the next day out of lax. we stayed on the club floor at a tune of $259 per night. afternoon hor doeuvres were not plentiful. watch out for the seniors staying on the club floor; they ate everything in site making a meal with the hor doeuvres leaving nothing for simple folks like ourselves who are not used to fight for food in a club lounge. breakfast was the same chaotic manner with the seniors fighting for the club lounge food...it was a sight to see.nice beds, outdated bathroom with faucets the oldest that i have ever seen. free internet in the club lounge with free printing-nice!airport shuttle stops at the marriott first so if the bus is full it simply passes by the renaissance without picking anyone up and you have to wait again.suggestion for future travelers...simply try to avoid landing and taking off from lax...not too much choice for luxury hotels in the lax area.

great business hotel despite pratically being on the runway, the plane noise is not bad at all, and i am sensitive to noise. rooms were clean and the beds were very comfortable.staff was nice. food was good. great business hotel.

nice for airport hotel we stayed here for 6 nights while attending a conference at the hotel. the rooms were very nice and very clean. the furniture was pleasant and the bed was comfortable. the bathroom was typical for a hotel of this type. internet access was $12.95/day including local phone calls. it worked well. there was a flat panel tv with a decent selection of channels. the pool was nice, but needed heating. there is a nice fitness center and also a hot tub. check-in was easy and most employees were polite. the restaurant was very slow.
best hotel in lax area fitness center

this is well worth staying at this is a very professional hotel and of very good quality...there is simply nothing wrong with it..although for some people its location as an airport hotel and therefore some distance from eating locations might be viewed as a negative.we stayed there 4 nights and found that catching the shuttle ..which runs every 15 minutes..to lax ..enabled us then to hook onto the flyaway which for $8 return will take you to 3 significant destinations..union station, westwood and one other from which you can connect tolocal public transport..most notably the metro at union station..you can also get to santa monica by connecting on the blue bus.back to the hotel itself..the room was very clean and well cleaned each day..the facilities were of a level where any improvement would largely be a waste of money..we simply had no issues with the place other than to say we definitely enjoyed our stay

airport oasis i can highly recommend the renaissance montura. after the horrendous experience of lax airport i was in need of somewhere to relax and was so happy to get to the hotel. the renaissance is only a few minutes from the aiport and the shuttle service picks you up right outside the baggage claim area. the hotel is quiet (even though it is close to the airport) and classy. the rooms are large, clean and very tastefully furnished. the restaurant food was excellent with a great breakfast buffet. front desk staff were extremely professional, friendly and very helpful.

good lax hotel very nice hotel close to laxroom was very clean and comfortable.becareful of the nickel and dime expences (parking, internet, water, etc), we got a pkg with parking incl.one nice thing was an empty fridge (they will fill for you if you want) instead of a minibar.gym was small but functional and there was a small pool area.hotel staff was very helpful and friendly.

nice hotel in a terrible airport we have had great experiences staying at renaissance hotels , mostly in europe and when we searched for a hotel in the los angeles area very close to the beach cities and high wayaccesible , that also offered a nice week end rate we came to pick the montura hotel , we stay here for 3 nights and found a nice hotel quite impersonal quite comfortable (beds were very nice ) everythig seemed to work fine but it just felt like any first class hotel of middle age ,but still just to stay close to laxthe rooms were very quiet even they were just by the run ways , breakfast was good every morning but they offerd the same food , swiming pool and gym were quite small and un atractive , the bar at the lobby served a very smart wine selection but the attendants were quite slow and distant .we had a very late flight out of lax and the girl at front desk allowed us to stay till 4.00 pm (that was very nice )
great stop-over hotel montura flight path - room view

convenient place for a lay-over i stayed 1 night here on a lay-over from sin-lax and lax-mob to break up what would have been a totally unbearable journey.transport was free by courtesy shuttle from lax to the hotel. to catch it, you have to go out of the airport onto the curb following the signs for hotel courtesy shuttle and just wait around for the bus that flashes marriott/renaissance to pull up. it's a short 5 minutes journey from the airport to the hotel, dropping off at marriott first.room was large, comfortable beds with an over surplus of pillows. not that i am going to complain of course. although i booked for a breakfast to be included in the room rates, my next day flight was too early for me to consume it at a reasonable time so the front counter was kind enough to convert it to free internet access at no extra charge.the room only comes with a shower and no tub. a shower curtain prevents you from wetting the other parts of the bathroom but doesn't stop the water from flowing outwards especially if you have it running at speed for a while.the room was very well sound proofed and although you can see planes landing about a kilometer away, you can't hear them.i spoted a burger king next to the hotel. there are restaurants on the ground but i did not avail my self to them, choosing instead to turn in early for the next day flight.next morning was a breezy check out followed by the same easy shuttle ride to my connecting flight. it happens that the bus pulled up immediately when i got to the lobby so there was no waiting time needed at all!all in, plenty good hotel. will stay here again.

would definitely return we were moving from the u.s. (texas) to australia and wanted to overnight in los angeles the night before our long flight to australia. we selected the renaissance montura based on price and revues, plus i'm a marriott member. we couldn't have made a better choice. the hotel is only a few minutes from los angeles airport, and provides a free shuttle. the hotel interior is beautiful, as was our room. we had dinner, and lunch the following day, in the lobby bar. the halibut we had for dinner and the duck quesadillas we had for lunch the next day were both delicious and beautifully presented. the quesadillas had a hint of banana in them - sounds funny, but it made for a wonderful taste combination. we sat around the hotel lobby from a late checkout time of 3 pm until about 7 pm when we left for the airport , reading and chatting, and thoroughly enjoying our time there. the staff and everything about the hotel was great.

heaven after a sleepless trans-pacific flight! we checked in at the renaissance after a sleepless trans-pacific flight from sydney to la. though we arrived at 11:00 am, early check-in was no problem. our room was really comfortable, very attractively decorated, extremely quiet, and moderately spacious. we even had a very large lcd flat panel tv. everyone was super friendly and efficient from the moment we arrived. we forgot to ask for a portacot for our toddler; the smiling bellman arrived within two minutes. not enough towels, another smiling bellman arrived within five minutes. the bed was incredibly comfortable and we all immediately fell into bed for 3-1/2 hours of a blissful nap after the aforementioned sleepless flight. we heard absolutely no airport noise, though my toddler daughter was delighted to be able to watch the planes come and go out of our window.the food in the cafe was excellent (though just a bit pricey) and the staff there were exceedingly kind and efficient there as well. seeing our toddler they made sure to bring out our food quickly, which we greatly appreciated. they even brought us complimentary chocolate covered strawberries for dessert.we booked our stay through my corporate travel agent for $118 per night plus tax and would stay here again in a heartbeat. an excellent experience all around.

pity about the shuttle ... i used this an overnight airport hotel, arriving late evening and leaving very early in the morning so experience was limited. i just missed the shuttle leaving lax - i saw it drive off as i exited the terminal building - and had a rather long wait for the next one. probably about 20-25 minutes. i wish i had just taken a taxi. on arrival all was put right as i found that despite being a mere marriott silver card holder i had been upgraded to a suite. loads of space, adequately furnished but in the typical marriott style (i.e. i would not choose this for my own residence!). great soft comfy bed though, just what i needed after a tatl flight. triple glazing worked well to insulate the airport noise. or at least, until the air-con switched itself on, damaged motor, sounded like a bus starting up. it was not hot so i just turned it off: i was in the wrong timezone to bother making a complaint to the front desk.i didn't bother with breakfast the next day and the shuttle back to lax was prompt.my late late surprise was an email survey i received from the hotel after the visit, i filled it in and mentioned the air-con problem. shall we just say that the hotel delighted me with an excellent service recovery.

only a quick stay, but one of the best parts of my trip i stayed at the renaissance for just one night, after a flight delay. my stay there was fantastic though and made up for terrible travel issues earlier in the day. i checked in late at night and the staff was very fast and friendly. the room was beautiful and very comfortable. the bed was excellent, although the towels could have been a bit shofter. great shower and water pressure. for the price i paid ($129 including taxes) it was great. i was on the club level so a free breakfast was included. i'd definitely recommend this hotel for anyone looking for a nice, reasonably-priced hotel near the airport. the one thing to keep in mind is that the hotel shuttle doesn't run very frequently at night...if you're coming in super late (i landed after midnight) you may want to think about taking a cab for the brief ride instead of waiting forever for a shuttle to show up.

good stay near lax after staying at the sheraton gateway lax, i was looking for a hotel property in the lax area but with a little less of the airport noise and a little more updated. the rennaissance was just that.the room was great, the customer service at the front desk and at the hotel restaurant was exceptional and the food was good too. my only issue was that i couldn't get hot water out of my shower. maybe my room was too far away - it was at the end of the hall - or maybe they took dateline's advice and turned down the overall temp - but either way, it was a little chilly.other than that, i will be back here again.
worth the stay duck that we got in our tub

good choice for lax travelers and hertz nice rooms with nice furnishings. much less noise than most of the properties on century blvd near lax, and also avoids some of the traffic issues being off the main drag (but just as close to the airport). the bedding and towels were average and room service was okay. the gyms was nice too. alas, the neighborhood isn't great so there was a little noise from the nearby police activity. but the hotel itself is safe. there is a burger king across the street, and hertz is walking distance - great way to avoid parking fees. on the minus side, the pool was too small, the convenience store is mediocre, and hotel failed to assign us to a marriott elite floor.

great for 24h stopover we wanted an airport hotel for our mid-evening arrival and departure 24 hours later.i chose this hotel for our young family (3yrs and 11months) based on the reviews and free manhattan beach bus and we were very happy with our stay and the exceptional service we received.we had a 15 minute wait (at 6.30pm on a sunday night) for the shuttle pickup which was empty when we boarded at southwest. checkin was easy and quiet.we had a club room with 2 queen beds a cot/crib. it was a little tight all round but clean and pleasant enough. we got the kids into the bath straightaway, with their yelps of delight and play. as we were ordering room service (about 7.30pm) the customer service manager came onto the line and very pleasantly told us that he'd had a complaint about the noise from the kids. we explained we had had them in the bath and were rushing them to bed after a bite, so it would be quiet soon (they are pretty good kids and seasoned travellers). he offered us complimentary cookies and milk for the kids (and our own drinks with the meal were complimentary) to entice them to bed. how many places can you go where you get complimentary drinks for a complaint against you??? anyway it was a hit with us all.room service dinner was good all around, my crabcakes were yummy and memorable and the kids meals were good too. we all had a good nights sleep - great blackout curtains, no noise from the airport (we were facing), comfy beds.club breakfast was okay and the kids were thrilled to see the low-flying planes in front of the club lounge! snacks through the day consisted of fruit and sweets. the club lounge is always a great place to escape from kids in a hotel room.we organised an extra 4 hours accomodation (50% rate i think to 6pm) and all headed out to manhattan beach - the main reason i chose the hotel was for its proximity to the free bus (that'd i read about on trip advisor). dh and the kids spent the best part of the day at the beach and i spent time and money at the manhattan beach mall. concierge was very helpful with directions and what to do in manhattan beach.check out and transfers were easy. we checked our emails (at a small cost) before the quick and easy transfer to the virgin terminal.overall it was a really good choice for the airport area and the service was exemplary. we didn't get a ultracheap deal on the room as we would have liked at last minute (it wasn't much cheaper than the deal at the sofitel la), but the service more than compensated.

excellent value stayed here in transit heading back to oz. as per their website, picked up the blue bus at the airport. the room was a little larger than we expected; we were on the 8th floor over looking burger king and the airport. there is no mini bar fridge, however there is an ice machine and soft drinks machine is on every floor. the ice is free. the room was excellent value for money, and a bus stop for the number 3 big blue bus is nearby, which goes to santa monica. the room was soundproofed, so we were not distracted by airplane noise as long as we kept the windows shut.

nice enough, as long as you don't want to check email i attended a conference at this hotel and my significant other and i took advantage of the conference rate to spend two extra nights. i agree with other reviewers that this hotel is very, very nice. the rooms are comfortable, the lobby is handsome, and the breakfast buffet is excellent and an outstanding value. travelers should be warned, however, that this really is an airport hotel. every night we saw hordes of pilots and flight attendants checking in, and the property sits in the middle of a maze of highway ramps. you'd hardly know that you're less than a mile from marina del rey. it's designed for business travelers, not tourists.we were also puzzled by some of the small ways that this hotel nickels-and-dimes its customers. though we booked a room for two, we were supplied with only three bath towels. assuming this was just an oversight, on our first night we got a fourth towel from housekeeping. after our room was made up the next day, however, lo and behold! we once again had only three bath towels. we requested another, and this too disappeared after the next day's housekeeping. evidently towel-rationing is hotel policy. also, the glasses in the room were those nasty plastic cellophane-wrapped cups, and they gave us only two at a time--evidently you can either brush your teeth or enjoy a drink, but not both! finally, there is no free internet access in this hotel. there's a daily charge to use the in-room wireless or ethernet, and perhaps that's not surprising, given that business travelers might spend quite a bit of time online. but we were a bit dismayed to find that the internet access in the business center was also not free--you had to enter a credit card number and pay by the minute.even motel 6 these days has free internet, to say nothing of four bath towels per room. what's up, marriott?

nice for an airport hotel i stayed at this property 3 nights for an in-house conference. check-in was relatively quick and painless. i stayed in a junior suite on the third floor and was more than pleased with the room. there was not a single fault with the cleanliness of the room-- so this is the most important thing in considering this hotel! the bed was very comfortable and was dressed in nice linens and a fluffy duvet.you cannot hear a lot of airport noise, which is a plus at this type of hotel, but there were some other noises that were unidentifiable that did awake me the first night.the major problem i found with the hotel was that my room did not have truly hot water. at any time, it did not rise above tepid. in fact, one morning, i could not get it even warm enough to take a navy-style soap-and-rinse shower. maintenance was quick on the draw, but the problem was not fixed. it seems odd that no one else would have complained about this, but this was the only major problem for which i could fault my stay.

big disappointment i would never stay at this hotel again. we booked the club level and our first room was small that our suitcases (2 of therm) could not fit. when we changed rooms, it was larger but the air conditioner kept us up all night. it would cycle on and off all night making lous noises. we couldn't sleep.

excellent deal in los angeles! i do my homework and it usually takes me a full month to search out the very best deal wherever we travel to. it was labor day weekend when most if not all hotels raise their rates sky high. i kept coming back to the airport area for lower rates and the renaissance montura lax had the best deal going - about $95 per night! and to make it even better - the hotel honored their guarantee that if you find a cheaper price on any other travel site they will give you a lower price. i found it for less on expedia and the room rate was lowered to about $68 per night! now the renaissance chain is a marriott hotel so they have a fabulous bed which is wonderful. we got in late friday night from san francisco and were received with excellent hospitality, smiling faces and easy check in. we were even upgraded to a higher floor and more expensive room with a 'club' to go to for snacks, breakfast bar if wanted and a quiet place to relax with coffee or a glass of wine in the early evening. the room was clean, had a great view and flat screen t. v. which was great. good shower and super clean bathroom! i am exceedingly fussy about a clean bathroom in hotels. the restaurant has fabulous food and wonderful breakfast. so, watch this hotel for a great price for high quality. you do have to pay for parking and internet connection daily - so remember to add that extra $27.95 in when you budget your travel plans. it is also is right at the airport with a free shuttle which is so helpful as well.

great for transit i stayed at this hotel overnight after flying in from montreal, with a single overnight stay before flying back home to sydney australia. my expectations were delivered exactly after reading the reviews here. i successfully caught the free shuttle from lax, check-in was easy...the clerk even changed my room to one a little bigger, and even gave me a late check-out as my flight next day was not until 10pm. dinner in the bar was ok, and i was even entertained by the conversation boucing back and forth among the patrons. this is a well used hotel, and used almost exclusively for over night stays between flights. it's best to expect no more than that, but this hotel delivers a little better than most. my room only cost $99 and i was very well satisfied. given the friendships i struck at the bar, i was sorry to leave the next day.the free shuttle back to lax arrived as expected, although i do tend to leave for the airport very early to ensure no delays. i would stay here again for transit convenience, but it's not a hotel to stay in as a base for seeing la.

just okay! my husband stayed here for one night to be close to lax for a morning flight. we checked in and arrived in our room, which was clean and located on a higher floor. we had dinner in the bar, which service was slow but, we didn't have a lot of choise since we wer advised not to walk around the area, it was too dangerous. we expected some noise from outside the hotel due to the proximity to the airport, however we were very surprised at the internal noise. all night we heard the running water, and other noises we couldn't identify. we inquired after dinner with the concerige about checking-in at lax and checking bags when to leave the hotel in the morning. we were advised to check-in online and bag drop at the airport with no waiting in line. we left for lax approx. 1.5 hr prior to departure, and discovered the shuttle was delayed 15-20 minuets and the hotel began to use taxis to transport people to the airport. upon arrival to lax, we has to wait in line and almost missed out flight. i would not recommend this hotel due to the noise factor, and the shuttle problem.

huge room, plush bed, excellent stay my husband and i booked the renaissance for the last night of our honeymoon, as our flight from jamaica came in too late to book a connecting flight back to seattle. for $99, our expectations were definitely exceeded, and we would recommend this hotel to anyone!we arrived after 11 p.m., exhausted, and were pleasantly surprised to find out we'd been upgraded to a suite. the suite was huge and shaped like a rectangle. the separate sitting area, desk and old school tv were on one end, but that area was the farther from the window so rather dark. the restroom was in the middle of the suite, along with an empty fridge (no minibar but the sign said they could stock it for you) and a big mirror, good for getting ready while the husband was in the shower the next day. the king size bed was luxurious, and we appreciated the huge flat screen tv in that area of the room. we had a view of the airport and burger king from our 6th floor room. one odd thing, the room had one bathrobe and one bottle of water, as if it was set up for one traveller even though we'd noted there were two of us on the reservation...but no big deal.the only slight drawback was speed of service in the lounge. we went down at 11:20 p.m. for a quick bite as we hadn't eaten since 4 p.m., and it took our food (an average club sandwich) 45 minutes to come. there were maybe eight people in the lounge so i'm not sure what the problem was, but the server apologized.overall, for the incredible value we would definitely stay here again if we have to fly in/out of lax. one nice perk, we are marriott silver elite members and they recognized us with a coupon for a free latte in the morning. this was definitely one of the nicer marriott brand hotels we've stayed in.

expectations far exceeded! loved it! we stayed at this hotel for 5 days (joining my wife who had already been there for 3 days). the hotel is very conveniently located for travelers, about half a mile from the airport. it includes free transportation from/to the airport to/from the hotel. be prepared to pay for parking - about $10 per day. the valet parking is definitely not worth it - unless you like to be pampered. i didn't even check the price.the location of the hotel was surprisingly good. the airport's proximity had to be seen to be believed - the planes could not be heard at all. the check-in process was smooth. we had arrived by a late night flight that turned into a very early morning flight - around 2 am. the staff were courteous, helped get the luggage to our room and we settled in.the room itself was spacious. it was *not* the suite and yet we could place a rollaway bed in the room and have space left for walking around. the rollaway beds were nice too - not the folfing variety, but a stand-on-end variety that meant that the mattress was no too soft or springy. the bed itself (important for people with delicate backs) was not the best. i have slept on better beds. the bed (king size) was too springy. i would (almost) gladly have slept on the floor. the rooms were surprisingly well sound proofed.my wife liked the 2nd floor exercise space - i myself worked out in the room itself (5bx requires surprisingly less space - look it up on wikipedia), and my kids liked the swimming pool which they used once and even then it was too cold.on the whole, we had a great time and liked the hotel as a place to access the best things in la.

loved the renaissance! wow, what a hotel. when we made this reservations we figured that an airport hotel would be noisy and dirty... this was neither! this hotel was far enough away from the airport that you didn't realize you were next to it.the room was fantastic! what a bed! bathroom was clean and bath products were lovely. coffee in the room, no breakfast included.on-site restaruant was expensive, but the food was good.concierge give us a great recommendation for breakfast in manhattan beach called ??front desk staff needs a lot of work. i called to arrange an early check in prior to noon and they were nasty about it being a first come first serve basis. when i called to cancel the request due to a snow storm, the reiterated that there was no request made and it was first come, first served anyway.parking - be prepared to pay $20 to park!if this is what all marriott renaissance are like, we would stay at more! this is a luxury airport hotel!

best lax hotel this hotel was very surprising. i've stayed at other hotels in the area for a next day, early morning flight, but this was the best. the room was beautiful, lobby was very inviting. but most surprising, the food at the restaurant was the best food we had during our entire l.a. stay! turns out that the restaurant actually holds very high ranking among all restaurants in l.a.! beautiful presentation of the food and an interesting menu. i just wish that we had dressed up a bit more as this was not the typical hotel restaurant dining room. finally, in response to the other reviews, we had no problems with the hotel shuttle getting us to the airport in the morning, but clearly it is still a problem as the front desk clerk was very aware of the issue when we inquired as to the status. (she recommends phoning the hotel when you get to the pick up location to make the driver aware that you are waiting).

still one of only two lax hotels for me! iéˆ¥???e had a couple of stays here, and the montura continues to delight.rooms sparkle, with marriott revive bedding. toiletries are by lather. high speed internet is at 100meg, although i had a couple of signal drops that were irritating on this visit.front desk upgraded me to club floor (silver marriott status), which i was pleased with. when i got to the lounge (around 8:00p) most of the hot food was gone, but i had a couple of serviceable buffalo wings and a glass of nice wine. wine in the lounge is priced similarly to the restaurant at $8 to 12 per glass.i ate dinner in the restaurant, which was unusually busy. service suffered a bit from slowness (it was a saturday night), but the food was as good as always. the menu seems to have slimmed down a bitéˆ¥?br/>breakfast in the lounge was nice. plenty of breads and fruits, hot egg somethingorothers. coffee available in go cups. there was a free access pc in the lounge for printing boarding passes.lounge hint: they put out room temperature bottled water on the counter, but if you ask, they can produce well chilled sparkling water!when i transit lax (usually en route to asia) i only have my travel agent check the montura and the westin. this time, i got a $119 rate, so was really pleased. plus, it may be the only airport hotel in the world with a substantive collection of artwork, nicely placed around the lobby and the buildingéˆ¥?you donéˆ¥??› find that at the lax marriott!iéˆ¥??’l be back!

the bedbugs enjoyed their stay more than we did we decided to break up a trip with a stay in la following an overnight flight. while we appreciated the ability to get into our room when we arrived at the hotel, once we woke from our nap, we found that bedbugs were also guests in our room. when we notified the staff, the manager informed us that the marriott rewards points used for our stay would be recredited to our account. he also assured us that the exterminator would be called to rectify the situation. since we have yet to receive our point credit (it has now been 2 months), i can only assume that the bedbugs are still feasting on weary renaissance guests.

exceptional one night stay i was booked at a compeitor's hotel a block away, but ran into quite a few problems there. i called the renaissance, and they had just what we needed. having stayed, and enjoyed, the renaissance montura before, i should have not chanced another hotel, but i thought the competitor would be better for my family. i was wrong.the reservations agent was very helpful, and the front desk staff, concierge, and bell staff couldn't have been more accomodating.we were given an upgrade to concierge level, which had a very nice selection of hors d'oeuvres in the evening and breakfast items.the lobby and bar area is bright, cheery, and inviting, just what was needed after a long flight across the country.rooms were clean and inviting, with flat panel tvs and very comfortable beds.the food (we ordered room service, and it arrived very hot in a nice warming unit) was very, very good. the menu is quite extensive, something for everyone.if you are flying in or out of lax, i would recommend this hotel highly. it would be our first, and only, choice if we were to need accomodations in the lax area again.

great airport hotel over the years it has almost become tradition to stay one night at the start and end of a trip at this excellent property. it is quite amazing really that this hotel has been very consistent in service and quality for donkey's years.i never ever had problems at this property. staff always nice and helpful, high housekeeping standards, pretty good food quality. i suppose they could start on updating rooms and give it that modern design renaissance touch but having said that i am still pretty happy with the rooms.it also helps that this inn does not feel that much like a airport hotel. yes i said airport location apparently some reviewers expect it also to be close to tourist locations (???).parking is the usual la rates but one can circumvent this by parking on the street as long as one is aware of street sweeping days. saved me $ 18.40 including tax.i certainly recommend this hotel.

great airport accomodations just got back from a three night stay at this hotel. the room was spacious, quiet and easily accessible. the staff is great! should be able to book for about $100 a nite. this does not include parking which is an additional $17 per day.beware of the free airport shuttle. it's not a problem leaving the hotel to get back to the airport, if you try and catch it when you first arrive they sometimes get crowded and will pass you. i arrived at the united airlines arrival area and two shuttles to the hotel passed me because they were full. ended up catching a cab. evidently united is at the end of the run.

very nice hotel nice hotel, nice decoration,good service,expensive parking,above average hotel, yes i will go back on my next trip,good transportation service to the airport, and very good rate $99 dlls.

renaissance lax = nice i recently stayed at this hotel on a return trip to los angeles. i needed to stay near lax for a quick overnight trip. in october i stayed at the nearby marriott lax which was very expensive and they didn't have their act together. this hotel, on the other hand, is very nice and much cheaper too. it also seemed much more relaxed and less convention like. the lobby wasn't noisy or too busy. the restaurant had a well above average wine list - much to my surprise. the hotel is a little gem at lax. my stay was over a friday night so i had a $99 (the marriott was $119) weekend rate which is very reasonable price. the room was very spacious and had a large bathroom and the new-marriott beds. the room also offered a ipod radio as well as cd player, plus free bottles of water. very nice touch. being a marriott rewards member i was granted access to the concierge lounge which, i must say, was fantastic. this place offered well above the average appetizers including poached salmon, various cheeses, meatballs, etc. the hotel also has a cute-little gift shop and great gym (also outdoor pool if you have the time). i was on the 5:30 am airport shuttle and the shuttle (which also picks up people at the marriott) was right on time and was a short 10 minute ride to my airline at lax. this hotel is very nice an i highly recommend it if you need to stay near lax airport.
good for overnight layover room - chair/desk area

poor service, terrible location well, the renaissance montura was our last stop on or honeymoon this summer. we had booked the hotel through a friend and had choose amongst five different marriott hotels. based on the reviews at tripadvisor, we chose renaissance montura.we shouldn't have done that. we had planned to drive around in los angeles but due to the humungous cost of rentning a car - which really surprised us - the amount that was stated on the web site of the rental car company was more than doubled when we actually got to the rental company - and for a european who is not used to driving in 10 or 12 lane freeways the traffic was terrible. we ended up returning the rented car and got by using taxis and the metro railway instead. to get to - for instance universal studios - you had to take the tranist bus to lax, then take the lax transit bus to the metro to the green line. take the green line and change for the red line all in all making it a two and a half hour trip to get from the hotel to universal with public transportation. be advised that the red line runs through south central and watts - and it is not a pretty neighborhood.now it comes down to location. the hotel is located far, far away from the attractive parts of la. there is a burger king right next to the hotel but that's about it when it comes to eating opportunities. when it comes to the hotel a lot of problems occured. first of all, our room wasn't really prepared for us. half a bottle of bottled water left from the last occupant of the room were still in the room when we arrived. it took five - 5 - days for the maid to remove it, though we told the reception about a lot of times. the windows were all greased up as if a small child had been playing there. the pool is nothing special.the biggest problem though was the personal which was rather rude. one of the employees asked us to show id before we could enter the elevator at one occassion and we were dressed rather nicely. a tv repairman which had to fine tune are flat screen tv after they changed the television set didn't speak a word of english and couldn't fix the tv.for at four star hotel there were far to many problems at the renaissance montura.

a superb deal for lax just a one-night stay, but we were very impressed with the all-round quality of this airport hotel. despite a bargain rate, we were given a junior suite - which had had a stylish recent makeover. and the restaurant, although rather lacking in atmosphere on a saturday night, served up remarkably good, innovative food.

nice stay in the city of angels my sis and i stayed here 3 nights for a long weekend, returning home yesterday. after doing much research, i chose the package with this hotel because i liked the fact it was close to the airport.we had no problems! some of the reviews were horrible, and we were a little freaked. but i think those reviews really boiled down to the fact that some people like to complain about everything. sure, the bathroom sinks and showers are a little worn around the drains. big deal! water runs there on a regular basis. our room was clean and comfortable. housekeeping left plenty of towels everyday (more than we could use), obviously cleaned the shower everyday (our bottles were always moved), and even folded the facial tissue into a rose every time they came to service the room. the large flat-screen tvs, updated carpeting, and tasteful furniture did not even hint at what some people referred to as a éˆ¥?¸„atedéˆ¥?hotel. the bar/restaurant staff was excellent both nights we were thereéˆ¥?”…fficient and very friendly. the $15 steak sandwich was gross and left a lot to be desired but that was the only negative. even though the valet is contracted out, the staff was friendly there as well. we were in town for a writing workshop, but still drove all around melrose, santa monica, sunset, hollywood, wilshire, etc. the complaints that the hotel wasnéˆ¥??› close to anything didnéˆ¥??› seem to affect us either, as most places we went were no more than 20 minutes away (assuming there wasnéˆ¥??› a great deal of traffic). iéˆ¥???e traveled all over the world, staying in 5 star resorts where the service is impeccable so i have high standards. i have no complaints about the renaissance monturaéˆ¥?”?uch nicer than i would expect for an airport hotel.

deserved my return i had to have meeting near lax. after reading the reviews and client suggestions. i booked into the club level room for two nights end of nov. a reception staff named kia almost spoiled my trust in the marriott group which i used to stay throughout my travel in asia , europe and n. america. this female staff had a lot of screw-ups when i called directly to the hotel to made changes to my online reservation. she was extremely impatient and caused me time by calling the la regional reservation center to reconfirm the wrong info she told me.the system. to my surprise, she misled my niece that the ratei booked was not on club level and wasn't entitled to club lounge facilities when my niece checked in- who arrived one day earlier than i did.. i went to meeting right after i arrived at lax from an international flight. i didn't return to the hotel late after 9pm to get to enquire about the discrepancy against my reservations. i was delighted the renaissance montura has a capable front desdk manger - peter choi. mr choi upon checking on my reservation and instantly offered apology to the mishandling of my reservation. he made adjustment to the room rate for the first night which my niece didn't have the club level facilities. he rectified our key card to ensure we had the club level facilities even we were not on the club level which i was still willing to pay for the club room rate instead of moving. i was impressed with the professionalism of mr. choi.apart from this flaw, the rest of the hotel staff are hospital and helpful. the hotel shuttle runs aroiund lax every 15-20 mins. witha friendly bux driver. the hotel is closed to car rental base, and the shuttle stop to manhattan beach mall which is the closest quality mall in the area. four point sheraton is right next door, don't drive into the wrong hotel =)some review commented the hotel is dated. i was apparently not in a recently reburbished room. but it was spacious, clean and well maintained. the lobby is not as dated as some reviews. however, the lobby physical setting is a bit unorthodox, the reception desk in in the far left corner, with a lounge area right at the entrance. for an airport hotel, one can't expect a granduer spacious lobby with marble columns, it is still above average.i will return for the genunine marriott hospitality extended by the duty front desk manager- mr p. choi.

enjoyable stay at the renaissance we stayed at the renassaince montura lax for 2 nights enroute from london to nz. we had a uniformly positive experience through out our stay, and i would recommend this property to others who have a similar length stopover in the la area particularly between long haul flights.i can only imagine that some of the negative reviews of this hotel were down to one off poor circumstances ie: particular room defects, however comments on the the lobby and rooms being run down certainly in our experience of this hotel thankfully proved untrue.the shuttle bus runs 15 min intervals from lax to hotel (light blue van with screen on side saying renaissance marriot) located just outside baggage claim under a sign that says hotel transfers. it is only 5 mins to hotel which after a lengthy flight wait at customs is divine!the lobby area is modern and classy, check in was a breeze and staff were friendly and accommodating from the concierge, porter to domestic staff.our room was better than we anticipated, with a huge comfy bed, large flat screen tv, nice bathroom amenities (even quality miniature bath products). our room looked out over lax whose proximity initially worried me with noise, however we didnt hear a thing!a check out time of 1 pm was handy too as our flight was later that day - express check out via the tv system was easy saved time.burger king is located accross the road - and judging by the foot traffic i would say that it does a lot of patronage from renaissance guests ! ha! okay so it is located in lax and away from major attractions, but la itself is a sprawling area, so you are never going to stay in one place that has everything. it is close to santa monica - the bus transit centre is a 5 minute walk (75 cents to santa monica $1.25 to downtown la via bus). and if you want to venture further many of the tours available pick up from the lax area.if you are perplexed with accommodation options in la, and are coming off a long haul flight and want just a taste of la, and to stay in a clean, reliable and fairly modern hotel then i would recommend this property.
montura madness.......... what is that smell?....i refuse to stay in a vomit room!

that 70's hotel after reading the reviews for this hotel, i happily reserved one night before we travelled to san diego from thailand. upon entering the hotel, i knew that i would be disappointed. it was so old fashioned and tired as one reviewer pointed out. the lobby, lobby bar and restaurant was something from the 80s or perhaps 70s! i knew that the room itself wouldn't give any surprises... and i was right. how this hotel ever got to no. 1 position for lax is completely beyond me. it just goes to show that you really cannot trust everything you read on tripadvisor. everyone has different standards and after living in asia for many years, you really come to expect a certain standard and this hotel does not deserve no. 1 spot in my opinion. i also noticed that the thai air staff also reside at this hotel during there stopovers... i feel sorry for them! one thing i have to add at this point is that the staff are really really nice and friendly and this review is not based on them at all. the entire hotel needs basically knocking down and starting again. too tired, too old, too musty and too expensive. i would never ever stay here again even if they offered me a room for free.....

exceeded expectations exceeded expectations. unless this was a fluke, everything went incredibly smoothly from catching the complimentary shuttle bus to a personal welcome greeting from the hotel manager as i entered the lobby. check-in staff eagerly anticipated my approach way before i made my way to the counter and made sure i knew exactly where i could find the elevators.plus, if you are here on business, nothing beat the $9.95 (from noon to noon unlimited high speed internet access, with free local and long distance calling! i could sit at the desk with my lap top, check emails and make/return phone calls from the same desk with no worries about cell phone issues. it was a sheer delight.i would definitely consider this hotel again when i return to lax.

i thought it was great and will be staying there again! i was reading the last review on this hotel and i didn't agree at all. that is why i am writing this review. first of all, i am an experienced traveler and have stayed in many different places.my friend and i stayed here last december as an after christmas getaway. i booked it on the marriott website since i am a marriott points member. i did not find the property tired at all. our room was gorgeous. maybe we got a newly remodeled room but the lobby area was beautiful as well. is it in a great location to l.a beside wanting to be near lax? no, of course not. it is an airport hotel. the pool is okay and the exercise room was actually pretty nice. please keep in mind this is an airport hotel. however, it is very close to santa monica and marina del rey where we went to dinner both nights. i loved it and will be going back again next month. i used to be an la resident for 4 years and would highly recommend this hotel but if you know nothing about l.a it isn't near disneyland or universal studios. if you want to be close to disney, you need to stay in anaheim and if you want to be near universal you will have to stay in the valley some where. you are out closer to the beach areas with this hotel.

great airport location, tired property i recently stayed here for a two night business trip as i needed close proximity to lax. the hotel proximity to lax is great. the facility is an older property that has lost some of it's shine. our room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. both the housekeepong and front desk staffs were efficent. while we found it to be a decent place to stay for a short trip, i would not recomend it as a base to explore the la area. the pool area is dismal at best. use it for business and early morning flights.

great hotel i booked through priceline and got this hotel for $100 per night. what a steal! i found the staff to be incredibly helpfull. the day i arrived i wanted to send a box back home and the concierge came up with a box and tape and got me to the post office. the food was excellent (albeit pricey, but hey, it's an airport hotel). the beds were oh-so-comfortable. one thing i didn't like was the lack of a shuttle to area attractions. it was advertised in the hotel guest book (the one your room), but when i tried to get to venice beach i was told there was no shuttle and a taxi or city bus were my only options. also, the internet was $9.99 per day, which i think is too high. for the most part this hotel is a great deal.

wife loved it moved from la to alaska, had to go back and work on our home while it was being rented. my wonderful wife didnéˆ¥??› like that i picked the hotel (off the internet!!!!!), since she lived in la for 20 years, but i used alaska airlines hotel reservation service and paid in advance. we checked in and she was surprised how nice the hotel was inside, outside was ok. well, i never write reviews, a waste of time, but this hotel was great. we stayed on the club level, had continental breakfast and evening h'orderves at the concierges lounge. while walking by the maids we noticed, a of couple times, that they were scrubbing down the tile walls of the shower and taking out the down comforters and replacing them, these rooms were clean. all in all, my 5-star hotel loving wife really liked this place and for only $99.93 per night not including tax. as the governator says, we will baaaack.

good quality lax hotel we stayed at the hotel for one night on july 28th. the transfer bus from the airport was punctual.on arrival the reception desk member of staff was very friendly and told me they'd honoured my request for a high floor room. very unusual that hotels even notice a request on an internet booking.i had booked the club lounge rate which provided us with snacks and breakfast. breakfast was nice with a good view of the landing aircraft!hotel is conveniently located for car rental compounds. we rented from avis which is within walking distance.the pool and sauna were also good. having stayed at the hilton howard johnson at lax this is definitely the nicest and best value.

consistent quality, complimentary upgrade to club level i stayed here for one night after my flight plans were changed. i've stayed here a couple of times before and each time the facilities have been excellent. i was even upgraded for free to the club level due to my flight change as well as my marriott rewards elite privileges.

terrible don't stay here. staff totally disinterested. room shabby - light bulbs broken, power points hanging off wall. room service got order wrong twice, and both times when told of error failed to deliver missing order. almost impossible to rouse staff on the phone. cold shower. shabby bathroom. airconditioning noisiest i have ever encountered. stay away.

do not stay here i made reservations, but never received the promised confirmation email. i called a week later to confirm and still did not receive an email - though i requested one. i arrived and sure enough, they could not find my reservation. the staff and managers were rude, and uninterested in my predicament. i was offered a rate twice the price of my original reservation. after giving my confirmation and membership number they found my reservation - at another marriott property! i was treated as if i had done something wrong.parking was over $30. there was no hot water for the shower. i received multiple bug bites as i slept. the a/c unit was loud and abrupt and disruptive during the night.nice bedding doesn't make up for a miserable experience and a $250 rate.

impressive hotel - slow shuttle service my wife and i stayed at this hotel for one evening during a recent trip to the area. we stayed the night here as we had an early flight out the next morning and wanted a place close to lax.the pro's:this is a very impressive hotel, especially for being in the lax area. the lobby is very modern and impressive and the rooms were very nice (flat screen tv's, large size, etc). if i had to stay in the lax area, i would chose this hotel.the con's:my only negative experience (which is why i gave the hotel 4 stars instead of 5) was with the shuttle service. we dropped our rental car off in the evening and took the hertz shuttle back to the airport. we previously confirmed with the hotel their shuttle ran the airport route every 15-20 minutes. after 30 minutes, no shuttle. we called the hotel and the front desk insisted the shuttle ran every 15-20 minutes. after about 45 minutes standing by the curb waiting, the shuttle arrived. we were to the hotel in 5 minutes, but the wait at the airport dampened the moment. to give their credit, our wait in the morning to the airport was only about 10 minutes.

king bed for family of four??? first of all, let me say that we had no complaints with the hotel except for the fact that we were given a king bed for a family of four!!!!! i followed all the instructions perfectly to assure our needs would be met. i booked the hotel online and although i stated 2 adults 2 children (ages 14 17) the online confirmation read: 1 room king or 2 queens. it also said that i was to call 2 days in advance if we were arriving late. i called the hotel directly 2 days in advance and advised that our flight was scheduled in at 10 pm and so we would be late arrivals. at that time i said we were a family of four with 2 teenage daughters and would need 2 queen beds. i was told no problem, that information would be noted on our reservation. after a long day of travel across country and arriving at the hotel (close to 2 am on our body clocks) we were checked in and sent up to our room. mind you, we were all standing at the check-in desk and my 17 year old daughter is 5'11'' and my husband 6'1. we got up to our room with all our luggage to find one king size bed. we dragged all our luggage back downstairs and the clerk went to get her manager who explained that legally thay did not have to honor our request for two beds and that was the last room in the hotel. a childsize cot was put in the small room which meant we couldn't even walk around to get ready in the morning and that was that. won't be staying there again!!!!

excellent stay my family stayed at the montura on the last night of our los angeles vacation primarily so we could quickly get to the airport the next day. overall, our stay was excellent. for only $99, we were upgraded to a suite which was large, well decorated, immaculate, and very comfortable. in hindsight, i'm sorry we didn't stay at this hotel longer. i highly recommend this property for anyone traveling to la.

excellent overnight stop in la we needed to overnight at a hotel near lax on the way back to florida from a lengthy stay in australia and new zealand. we booked the renaissance montura on the basis of its location (convenient to lax by free shuttle) good price and favorable reviews. we were not disappointed. we arrived in early afternoon after a 10 hour overnight flight and were checked in in no more than 30 seconds. after an afternoon nap and swim, we had a light meal in the restaurant where the service was friendly and efficient. the room was clean and the elevator service speedy, even though the hotel was full.i would definitely stay here again. the renaissance montura provided a hassle free experience which was just what we needed after an exhausting overnight flight.

renaissance really does = "excellance" just piggy-backing on the review that convinced us to stay here (renaissance = excellance). :)i never think too highly of airport hotels for some reason, but this one was killer (in a good way).awesome experiences in chronological order:1. registration/check-in quick easy.2. lobby is elegant comfortable.3. room is simple, but nice.4. flatscreen tv is winner.5. room service delivery was professional nice.6. food from room service was surprisingly delicious - specifically the steak fajitas, steak sandwich, veggie sandwich, portabella basil chicken flatbread.7. breakfast buffet was tasty had a good variety of food. (chocolate pancakes anyone?)8. check-out room close-out straightforward fast.in conclusion, stay here.

great place the renaissance lax was a fantastic hotel. i arrived early from the east coast and requested early checking. the hotel staff was more than accomidating in helping me with this request. i found the property to be urban chic with great artwork, decor, photos, and lighting. the bed was great and the room was quite clean. i do get a bit annoyed with paying $17 for parking when most of the airport lots in the area have lower daily rates. they really ought to lower the rate for a guest. i ordered room service one morning and found the food to be delivered hot and fast. the menu was good for all diets and had a nice selection. overall i found this place to be a fine choice for your airport hotel needs. it's also great for early morning departures from lax. give the place a try, you will not be disappointed. it's usually a few bucks cheaper than the marriott that is a quarter mile down the road on century blvd.

loved it, very nice! this hotel is very nice. the staff were all friendly and very helpful. our room was decorated beautifully. the beds were absolutely the best, extremely comfortable. we never once heard the airplanes, despite the 3 minute drive to the airport. the only thing we did not like, was during the weekdays, when the business people would leave thier rooms, we could hear them in the hallways and slamming their doors. parking was a bit expensive $18/day. the location was great, close to the 405 and near gas stations, rental cars and shopping. we will definately return, especially because the room price was so reasonable.

top notch hotel beautifully renovated hotel. our rooms were very clean and the beds were so plush. nice touches such as a rubber duckie in the shower, a rain showerhead and a curved shower curtain rod offering more shower room. our room had a large flat screen tv and an ipod docking station. very quiet in spite of being close to airport. the club level offered a nice continental breakfast, happy hour appetizers and an evening dessert. roomy and light filled fitness center with 4 treadmills, a bike or two, an elliptical and separate weight room. the only feature missing from this hotel would be an on-site spa center offering massages, pedicures and facials.

close to airport since we were arriving late in the evening from reno, nevada, thought it would be good to stay close to the airport to have a good nights rest. found this hotel from trip advisors reviews. we did have some problems due to the a/c not working, though it was beyond the hotels control. after we arrived at 9:30pm, we caught the marriott hotel shuttle to the hotel. it was crowded, so had to stand for the ride. the driver was very nice, but didn't understand english very well. we got out at the wrong marriott hotel, but a passenger informed us that we weren't at the correct hotel, so hopped back on.check in was a breeze, however they did not have a roll away bed as requested, but gave us an aero bed instead. it was great substitute. they gave us a high floor, as well as 2 full size beds which were requested. the problem was that the air conditioning was not working in the rooms so it was very difficult to sleep with the windows open and the planes taking off. at check out, i told them that we didn't have a very good night. they were apologetic, and when i asked for some sort of compensation, they gave a discount on the room, so we were appeased.the room was small, but efficient. the beds were very comfortable, and room was clean.

renaissance = excellance !! after a long search on the tripadvisor website i chose the renaissance montura for an overnight stay at the beginning and end of my trip to hawaii in june 2007. it was a perfect choice. the hotel is close to lax and provides a free shuttle to and from the airport. the shuttle runs every 15 minutes and the valet offers free coffee while you wait. the room was very clean and the beds were heavenly. fluffy comforters and many pillows on top of a wonderful pillowtop matress. very soundproof. you forget you are a half mile from lax. the entire staff was very friendly and courteous. excellent breakfast. you could order from the menu or enjoy their fabulous buffet that included made to order omelets. awesome service in the restaurant by the staff. i highly recomment this hotel.

superclose to lax, but not noisy!! we found this hotel after immediately checking out of the santa monica doubletree due to dissatisfaction. the renaissance was much nicer, and less than half the price!rooms were above average and included a refrigerator. front desk staff recommended a good mexican restaurant (cozumel's) and was very efficient. would absolutely stay here again if we needed to stay around lax (5 mins to airport). surprisingly, we were watching planes land all night and no one was awakened by the noise (windows must be extra-soundproof because we couldn't hear a thing!). head south on hwy 1 about 5 miles for great shopping, dining, and groceries (whole foods).

best option for airport stopover having an overnight stay from my long flight to hong kong, i always try to be careful where i stay when near lax. for most part the hotels there are sub-par. since i got a great special rate ($110) and read some good reviews here, i booked one night. the shuttle was excellent, coming every 15 minutes to lax. the ride is only 10 minutes, check-in staff was really polite and helpful. the room was really nice, beds were excellent. my only problem was the decorative pillow had mysterious brown/ashy looking globs on it. apparently they arent changed between guest stays. the video check out didnt work but was no big deal. the restaurant had some great food, try the onion soup at night its a masterpiece. the shuttle back was flawless, the drivers lugged the luggage on board without disgusted looks. the staff seems like a good bunch. 5 stars but i subtract a star for the pillow globs. id stay there again.

ok stay i stayed here for one night as i had an early flight the next morning and needed something close to the airport. this property was disappointing for the 4.5 rating it earned on this site. room 752 was a surprisingly small king room (maybe 3-4 ft between the end of the bed and the entrance door), hairs in the tub and the complimentary shampoo was missing (i had to call housekeeping to get some--the person to whom i spoke seemed bothered that i had called). this maybe ok for a short layover but i do not recommend it for the business traveler or family of 5. as a former hotel g.m. and frequent traveler i expected more out of a 4-star renaissance. the hampton inn in cypress, ca, was less expensive, much cleaner, more spacious, more accomodating (free wireless and breakfast), and the staff seemed more genuinely interested in making sure my stay was satisfying.

great hotel for everyone stayed one night based on the trip advisor reviews. was not dissapointed. great service and very close to the airport. ask the conceirge for a list of nearby restaurants...they gave us a name of an italian place that was one of the best we have eaten at!

it's the people in my experience, this is the best of the lax hotels. everything works. the building, which looks non-descript from the outside, is elegant within, with a handsome marble and art-filled lobby, speedy elevators, and recently renovated (though relatively small) rooms. the lounge is an inviting place to eat and drink a glass of excellent wine; it's large enough to afford privacy, if that's what you wish, but also arranged to make it easy to watch sports on the big-screen tv. my aaa rate provided a club-level room, plus free valet parking, and was actually cheaper than the regular rate at some of the other airport hotels. the club level here is a real pleasure, with good complimentary food at breakfast and in the evening. what really makes this hotel special, however, is its people. absolutely everyone -- at the door, the front desk, in the lounge, the club room, and at the concierge's desk -- was welcoming, helpful, and very competent. it's a real pleasure to deal with such positive people. i'd return for this reason above all.this is not a luxury hotel, the art work notwithstanding, and the view from the rooms is primarily one of airport parking lots. so i would not recommend the hotel to someone principally interested in vacationing. but whenever i need to stay near the airport in la, this is my choice.

excellent choice this was a last minute booking after i had just arrived into lax, it was an overall excellent choice of a hotel. the location is great it near car rental (beware the parking per day is approx. 18usd); the hotel offers a complimentary shuttle. although, i didnt dine in at the hotel there is a restaurant and a burger king directly across the street. the bed slept very comfortable so at that rate i have no major complaints. no leaks,runs, or anything out of the ordinary. i have to say i was pleased and will probably stay there again.

perfect for a lax stopover stayed there for one night when connecting at lax (marc 31 st to april 1st 2007).efficient and fast shuttle service from and to airport. quick check-in and check-out. comfortable room. very good breakfast buffet. good value for money. only downside is pool (very small and located in an unpleasant courtyard).eric beylon

excellent food,problems with room temp i stayed at montura renaissance for a professional meeting during a week-end (april 12-16, 2007). all ran really smooth, having a super cordial check-in process from a guy just transfered from a marriott hotel in ny. hotel room big enough for 1 guest, really comfortable bed...but, problems with the room temp adjustment, made me call front desk for a table heater, since it was pretty cold in , as it was out, since i came from puerto rico not too used to those temps. the hair dryer in the bathroom was not working, but i did not reported anyway. another thing was that i had found in other web sites better deals for the same nights, having us a special corporate rate, it was not really a special rate, it appears as the regular offered rates for these sites. well i got 2 free nights -of 4- using my marriott rewards points, so it was not that bad..... food in the hotel and during meetings was excellent, international menus done really great , and the breakfast buffet excelent also, waiters super cordial people and 'bilingual', a lot of them speak spanish. bad that room serv after midnight was limited to certain menu -soups salads-. overall will stay again if i have too, but far from everything, just 5 min from lax...............

elegant oasis by a busy airport we spent a night here prior to a flight to hawaii on march 18th. i read the reviews at tripadvisor and compared it to other nearby hotels. we are marriott rewards members and this hotel, based on reviews at this website, sounded perfect for us. after collecting our bags, we picked up the free marriott shuttle outside baggage claim. the hotel is the 2nd stop on the route....about 2 blocks from lax and a block from the marriott lax, which does not have the same charm as this hotel.the hotel feels intimate, elegant and very clean. it is nicer than the other marriott nearby.the staff was very accomodating. i asked for a room on an upper floor, facing the runway and got it. the bed was amazing....lots of pillows and crisp white linens...nicely appointed bathroom too. we had a wonderful meal in the diningroom and then sat in the roof top jacuzzi on the 2nd level and watched the planes overhead.. it was a very nice little rooftop garden with pool as well, and fitness center. the breakfast buffet was also very nice. i did go across the street to the burger king once to get something for my husband but i do not recommend it. it was smokey and did not feel clean. there were alot of people there who seemed a little rough. even though the hotel is upscale, it is surrounded by rental car parking lots and an industrtial area. i still recommend this hotel to anyone waiting for a connection. it is really a great place to rest. just don't venture out on the sidewalk at night. one great thing we saw...the landing of the new airbus which came in from france. lots of media and police escort. it was quite a sight to see it land from our hotel window. by the way, the hotel is completely soundproof.
