should not be top rated! i accompanied my husband for an over night mid-week business trip and was disappointed because it has such a high trip advisor rating. while the public areas are tastfully decorated and spacious, the room was quite small and you could hear conversations and tv from adjoining rooms. the bathroom floor was dirty and the floor safe was difficult to reach and impossible to read the instructions. we ate twice in the resturant...$6 for coffee and poor service at breakfast, better at lunch. all in all, i expect more from marriott.

class a+ all the way. my credentials: have collection of 100+ different hotel soaps with wide ranging qualities.my stays: longest here was 3 consecutive work weeks except for weekends. all business related.price: paid 100-118, corporate rate.property: not outwardly impressive. enter and that changes forthwith. it's beautiful with original art throughout entire hotel. and the most important attribute; clean. staff: uber-dressed, groomed, polite and ready to serve. no whining or attitudes here. there's even a full-time concierge which you wouldn't expect for the price. room: small, but the top-of-the-line linen and granite comfort makes up for that. never found a hair or an odor, or heard any loud, unacceptable noises in here.food: i don't believe in paying hotel prices for food so i didn't sample it but it smelled gourmet wonderful. negatives: low-key cyclic noise from landing planes. have to pay for internet. could not make reservations from the front desk. tv channels minimal.summary: i've stayed at the other high end hotels around lax and this place is more comfortable. i have not encountered a single problem here. and the airport noise thing is actually a non-issue because the other places were on the main street into the terminal and the car noise was worse than the planes. and besides that, the way it's set up, you can observe the airplane activity which is really quite interesting.

above average when i checked this site, the hotel was rated #5 in la, with a base price around $100 less than the other hotels in the top 10. so from that perspective it was an easy choice. ultimately, though, i think the rating reflects this hotel's convenience as an airport hotel, and the across-the-board quality which limits any really negative reviews. it was a nice stay, clean room, all the amenities that you'd expect-- but certainly nothing to write home about. the hotel is just a few blocks from the airport, right across the street from the budget rentacar lot (a nice tip is to use budget and then return the car the night before you leave, avoiding the extra night rental fee and the extra night parking fee). there's a burger king across the street, but nothing else of note within sight in any direction in terms of shopping or eating. the hotel charges $17 per night for parking (unlimited in/out priveleges), which seemed extreme, and maybe that's one reason why the room rate is so competetive. no complaints about the room-- i found the heater/ac system to be much better than average, and the bed was very comfy. while the windows are reinforced to keep out most of the airport noise, there was a lot of noise bleeding in from the hallway (our room was close to the elevators), and i was awakened by what sounded like someone using a saw one morning. don't expect anything spectacular, but rest assured you'll have a comfortable stay.

great stay at the renaissance we stayed at the renaissance montura hotel for two nights while visiting la. we were very pleased with the hotel and the staff. we had a problem with a coffee pot that wouldn't work and within 5 minutes of advising the front desk of this problem someone was at our room with a new coffee pot. the beds at this hotel were incredible! they really made you wish that you hade more time to sleep. budget rental car is directly across the street from this hotel and free street parking can be found on both sides of the budget rental car lot. we found this hotel to be clean, comfortable and accomodating. we will definitely stay at this hotel again if we travel to la.

excellent lax hotel stayed for 3 nights and was very impressed overall. was upgraded to the club floor (mr gold). the club lounge was one of the few in the us that is open on the weekend! breakfast, evening snacks, and dessert were all outstanding, different each day, and amazingly free of any fried food typical of lounge snacks. room was quiet, large, and clean. the temperature, however, was difficult to control--either too hot or too cold, and the ac was noisy. excercise room had good equipment and individual tv's. the lax transit center is a five minute walk to the hotel; from there, you can catch public transit to downtown. for in-and-out burger fans, there is one within a 15 min walk on sepulveda. hotel shuttle runs continuously to and from lax and was very efficient. would definitely stay at the montura again.
not bad for an airport hotel

good stay spent the president's day weekend at the montura. got a very reasonable rate of $119 from their website. the hotel is above average in most respects. the valet was quick and courteous. front desk check-in was smooth. the room was spic and span. i requested and got a high floor with a view of the lax runways. the room was very quiet even with planes taking off and landing most of the day. i would not hesitate staying at this property again.

nice hotel near lax my husband and i recently stayed at the rennaissance after a quick trip from to boston to visit our daughter who goes to college in ca. we needed a hotel to stay at near the airport as our flight out was leaving at 7 am. i read the reviews of all the hotels near lax in tripadvisor and chose the renaissance based on the feedback. we were not disappointed. the hotel was convenient, clean, and very, very quiet. we felt like the only guests in our part of the hotel. it might even have been a bit creepy, if i was traveling alone on business. but that does not take away from the well-appointed room, and the absolutely divine bed and linens. the pillow-top bed with the soft cotton sheets and duvet were bliss. i dreaded having to get up early to leave as i wanted to luxuriate in the linens all day! the windowpanes must have been tripled-paned, as we could watch the planes land, but did not hear even a slight engine noise. the registration staff was competent, but not overly friendly. the early morning (5 am) coffee and continental staff were kind, given the early hour. it was nice to be able to grab a cup of peet's coffee before having to face lax. the shuttle was on time and one can track its progress with their touch screen kiosk in the lobby. it certainly eased our getting to the airport on time anxieties. once you are on the shuttle the automated voice even tells you how long it will be until you get to the airport. nice touch.all in all, i would highly recommend the rennaissance for overnight travelers who need quick access to the airport. i am not sure i would make it my first destination option if it was my first trip to la. the area around the hotel is asphalt, car rental agencies, and industrial complexes. pretty grim. but for an overnight, it is ideal.

perfect for airport layover we stayed at this hotel for 1 night as a layover before a connecting flight to tahiti.booked the room on the hotel website; $159+tax for a club level room- and well worth it. the staff were very pleasant and helpful when i called to add our marriot rewards number to the reservation, and to ask some questions.i received an email before our arrival to pre-request extra pillows, towels, etc.the airport shuttle was prompt. the front desk staff were courteous and check in was very fast.the room was spacious, nicely appointed and clean. typical business hotel room. the toiletries were lather brand, also provided by delta in business class, and included more items than the standard soap, shampoo, conditioner, and moisturizer. the extra towels requested were in the bathroom. there were 2 robes in the closet.the bed and pillows were comfortable, and the sheets were high quality (600+count).there is a free trolley shuttle to manhatten beach (and the mall) - we took the shuttle and had a lovely lunch in a restaurant overlooking the ocean. saved us the cost of renting a car and provided just enough activity after the long flight from boston.with a club level room, there are free appetizers (hot cold) in the evenings and a continental breakfast in the morning.after a large meal at lunch, we went to the club lounge and had very tasty snacks for a light meal, including seared tuna sashimi. -note- coffee is free but you must pay for anything from the bar.in the morning we went to the lounge and were surprised to find a hot entree (eggs benedict) available, along with fresh fruit, sliced meats, cheese, pastries, juices, and coffee.checkout was quick easy. there were no surprises or hidden fees on the bill.it was not a long wait for the hotel shuttle to whisk us back to the airport when we were ready to leave.the money we saved on dinner, breakfast, and car rental more than compensated for the extra $30 for the club level room.we would stay here again if we had a layover. this is not a place to stay on vacation.

great lax location we stayed here for 1 night before an early departure from lax. the hotel is easy to find and less than 5 minutes from departure terminals at lax. it is part of the marriott chain which i like to use whenever possible. it is a beautiful hotel, very nicely appointed. the check-in desk clerk was very hasty and not overly friendly, but the concierge made up for it. they were very helpful with questions etc.the rooms were average size, the beds were wonderful pillow tops and very comfortable. the bathroom was good size with nice amenities. there was a small fridge in the room as well.the airport shuttle was very convenient, it runs continuously 24 hours every 15minutes. no reservations are required, just proceed outside and catch the next bus.would certainly stay here again for the convenience to the airport. it is also very close to the rental car drop-off locations.

perfect flight recovery! we stayed here on our first night in the usa, as we didn't want to venture far in the rental car on our first night. the location was perfect, very close to the airport, and just one block from the dollar rent a car site where we had just picked up our car.as we were tired on arrival (it was early evening, but felt like the early hours to us due to the time zone change), we decided to remain in the hotel, and found the facilities very good, enjoying both the gym and swimming pool, before retiring to the huge bed in our room, watching the 747's landing at lax with the sunset over the pacific in the background! beautiful! the front desk staff were very good both on arrival and when checking out, recommending a good local diner for breakfast as we wanted to try a traditional us style pancakes breakfast! the room was very comfortable, and the only slight issue we had was a whistling noise which we found was air coming under the room door. we didn't complain as we found throwing a cushion in front of the door stopped the noise!

great value for the price found a great deal (less than $100/night) on the marriott website for the montura. much more intimate than full-line marriott and one block away. great bar, great service for the price. very nice rooms in good condition and immaculate. club floor rooms are better equipped than other floors. friendly staff. no wifi and was never able to get cable internet to work. self-park was pricey ($17/night). i'd defintely stay again for the price.

the best hotel bed i've ever slept in! this is a sweet little hotel located close (but not too close) to lax. the airplanes can be seen but not so much heard. the staff were warm and always made it a point to greet us when we passed by. the lobby was beautiful and the hallways and other common areas were kept up nicely. the swimming pool, while nothing special, was clean and the spa offered a nice way to end the day. the fitness center looked close to brand-new and had everything you could possibly need including individual tv's and complimentary bottled water. the only complaint i have is that the guest rooms were a bit cramped. we would often bump into one another because there was limited space between the end of the bed and the dresser. however, the beds themselves more than made up for it. they featured duvets and other european-style appointments as well as enormous pillows which made it especially comfortable when sitting up against the headboard.the location of this property is central to everything. it's closest to the south bay area which includes redondo and manhattan beaches. hollywood is about a 30-minute drive as long as you stay off the freeways. all in all, i would recommend this property, especially to business travelers or people who only have a few days to spend in l.a.

awesome! what a lovely property! this hotel is not new like a normally select, however it is very well taken care of, beautifully furnished and definitely an upper class hotel. i paid $119 and stayed one night. the airport location worked out great since we were leaving lax the next morning. the beds were wonderful....probably close to the best i've slept on in a hotel. the few downsides of the hotel is that the rooms are quite small and there is not very good lighting in the room. two of us were trying to get ready in the morning and the lighting in the living/sleeping area was very dark. the concierge was very helpful. they directed us to the promenade shopping center where we had a great meal and saw a movie....beware, the movie prices on a saturday night were $15.50 per adult! overall, if i needed to be near the airport, i'd definitely stay again and recommend it to friends. my husband stays here for business and he loves the location.....it is also close to the rental car return places.

nice place to stay great place to stay, a j october 17th, 2006, pawe stayed here one night after a long flight home from fiji. our check in went smoothly. our room was very clean. bed was a pillowtop, rooms are sound proof smoke free hotel. after we showered and changed the concierge, sergio gave us some good advise on where to go for dinner a map. they also went out and hailed us a cab right away. after we returned we had cocktails over looking la in their club house and talking with the friendly staff. in the morning we woke up to a newspaper delicious breakfast in the hotel. the airport shuttle came right away and took us to our terminal free of charge. this is a nice place to stay if even for 1 night.

fine stay at the renaissance we stayed here for 3 nights and were satisfied with the stay; the rooms were a bit small for more than an overnight stay (or perhaps the furniture was too large for the room as noted in some of the other reviews). overall property was clean, well appointed, and convient to major freeway(s), beaches, and the airport. we did not take advantage of any of the restaurants or other facilities the hotel offered since we spent our days sightseeing. we requested additional pillows and towels (the room was set up with only 2 of each), and they arrived promptly and with a smile. valet parking always had car ready after calling from room and heading downstairs within 5 minutes or so. would stay here again.

good location and very nicely done rooms near lax we booked here thru a marriott promotional rate ($89/night) for a layover at lax. the shuttle was prompt. rooms were surprisingly pleasant for an airport hotel. our room faced the runways (evidently that was a prime location for the nightime view) and the windows were so well sealed, we didn't hear a thing. we didn't have a car and the concierge helpfully directed us to a free shuttle a block away that went to manhattan beach (the beach and to a mall there). it was a great way to pass a long afternoon. the hotel restaurant (we ate in the coffee shop) was very pretty, had a decent selection and the food was done nicely (not amazing but good for being at the airport). yuo got the feeling that the hotel staff really did want you to enjoy your stay, even if it was a short one. we would definitely stay here again.

great start! my family and i stayed here at the start of our holiday! we only stayed for two nights while we got over any jet lag.its a really nice clean hotel and a very short drive from the airport. we stayed for 2 nights, which due to the hotels location, is about enough really, as there are nicer areas to stay for a holiday. we had to pay for parking our hire car, which was something we hadn't really thought about.

very comfy bed we stayed in this hotel for 2 nights. very close to lax just a short taxi journey. we had booked a non smoking twin room but on arrival this was not available so we were offered an up grade to a king size suite. as i was travelling with a friend we didnéˆ¥??› mind crashing in the same bed but might be a different story if you are away on business! the bed was huge and so comfy and the room was sound proof from the noise of the road and airport. there were complimentary bottles of water in the room and luxurious toiletries, which was a nice touch. the hotel runs a shuttle bus (which looks like a red tram) runs down to manhattan beach and to a local shopping mall which we would have never had known was so close by. the driver of the bus was very helpful and friendly. the bus runs every hour after 10.30. this hotel is fine for a short stay. we did not use the pool, go to the beach instead. there is a fantastic place for breakfast near the shore called uncle bills pancake house. well worth a visit.

far better then i ever expected! highly recommend my family am i stayed here two nights for a reunion of sorts in torrence. at first the the appearance of the hotel from the out side looked alot like any nearby hotel, fairly ordinary, but once you have checked-in and checked out the place it was very comfortable, very clean and very friendly. the room we had (9th floor) was well organized, very clean and very quiet. i loved the bed and wished i could have taken it home with me, it was that comfortable; and the linen was incredably soft and warm. our room rate ($119) included breakfast for two adults and children under 12 free. i was expecting a basic continental but it turned out to be a fairly comprehensive buffet style with white table clothes and full service. they do have a menu if you choose. we also ate dinner one night and again i was very impressed. the sword fish with lobster sauce was increadable. take your time though, it's not a fast service restaurant during dinner time, but if you are in a hurry, there is a burger king accross the street , which you never see unless driving by to get to the hotel parking garage ($13.00 per night by the way). there appears to alot of convetion space here if needed, excersize room, pool (small / 4ft deep max), and a well appointed lobby to just hang and watch the world go by. the freeway (i-405) is minutes away with good signes to direct you where to go. i will defintely stay there again when in town.

loved this hotel! we stayed here when we needed a hotel for one night near lax. it was really a surprisingly nice hotel. very comfortable. very quiet. nice facilities (but tiny pool). i would definitely recommend this to anyone needing a first class hotel near lax, and i would definitely stay here again.

good as an airport hotel, less good for long stays1 i guess the key thing that i need to remember when reviewing this renaissance hotel is that it is an airport hotel, and i have been staying at the hotel for extended periods of sometimes up to 10 days. the hotel is really designed to give people in transit staying, i suspect, for an average of one or maybe two nights. that is why i tend to rate the hotel as fine and may other people on tripadvisor.com would rave about the hotel. the hotel has been going through a process of staggered renovation and there has been a real improvement in the quality and state of the bedrooms. one improvement, in my view, being the beds! these are definitely soft, comfortable and have piles of pillows to snuggle down into at night. the rooms are a good size, both the normal rooms and the suites although the latter tend to be fairly dark. there is usually good space to do work, good internet access and fairly good bathrooms with great water pressure.the one thing that is a pity they have not addressed is the air conditioning which is very boisterous and noisy, and i have found that i need to leave it off when going to bed at night and so in summer the rooms get hot and bit uncomfortable over night.the other area that is not great is the bar and dining facilities. the bar is small and not that exciting and the food is pretty average and limited. so while this is fine when there for a night or maybe two, if you stay any longer then you tire of the food. the problem being that as this is a hotel airport there is nowhere to pop out and walk to for an alterative meal.there is a small outdoor pool that is very popular, with small hot tub. the gym is pretty good with a range of cardio equipment to keep most people happy with tvs above each. the weights area is very limited but fine again for a work out.the hotel has a large parking garage with self parking or valet parking. the view from rooms in the front of the hotel are over the airport and worth asking for when you check in - or you get the view of the multi story car park (which you will see i always have had!)so this is a good hotel for an airport hotel, probably good for a conference as is so handy for the airport but not a hotel to spend longer in.one thing as an aside is although planes come really close to the hotel the hotel is very sound proof and even between rooms is very well insulated!a tips is that you can get amazing rates for club room access at the weekend (from a thursday to a monday check-out) off their website.you can see videos i made of 2 of the rooms at this link: http://blog.myspace.com/index.cfm?fuseaction=blog.viewfriendid=89511767blogid=159775462

surprisingly very nice!!! highly recommended hotel. across the street from lax and around the corner from various car rental agencies. comfy rooms, very clean, superb service. the only negative is the parking garage unless you valet.

no great deal! the renaissance montura was ok for the price i paid ($99 per night). the room was quite small and the ac was not working when i arrived. the hotel did send someone up right away to fix the problem. then my keys never worked and i was locked out of my room twice. the pool area was small and the water was very dirty. the hotel does have 24 hour shuttle service to lax airport. plus there was no airplane noise heard from your hotel room.

convenient for lax i stayed here twice recently - for 2 days at the start of my vacation and for 2 days at the end of it. no complaints either time.anytime we needed directions anywhere, the hotel staff were only too happy to help. we received printouts with all the information we needed.rooms were clean, comfortable and quiet considering the planes fly so close to the hotel.it was easy to get the shuttle bus to and from the hotel.would stay here again no problem.

excellence! very recently my grandmother and i visited los angeles for the funeral of her sister. unfortunately, the family friend we were staying with in la, was hospitalized. our plans were to arrive on friday, participate in the funeral on saturday and leave on the red-eye sunday evening. when we were unable to secure a standby flight out of los angeles, we were left with the need for hotel accomodations. i called every area hotel and there were no rooms available. believing that the renaissance was far out of our price range, i called as a last resort. i spoke to the most delightful man, mario. after explaining the situation to him about the flight, he encouraged us to take the next shuttle to him and he will have a room ready. i was skeptical, because no one else had room for us, regardless of our situation. sure enough when we got off the shuttle, mario was there waiting for us, with a welcoming smile and a ready room. the service was superb. the staff was extraordinary. their service made our situation more tolerable. and the shower is to die for. thank you for making our stay pleasurable and for delivering the service that was promised, and then some.

superb service! i booked two rooms here during my daughter's graduation from ucla last weekend (6/16 6/17). my daughter and son-in-law and their two babies (under 2yrs) didn't arrive until well after midnight, very tired and frustrated from driving for nine hours. when they got to their room, they found a snack tray waiting for them - with grapes, apple slices, peanut butter-and-jelly sandwiches - and a handwritten note saying there was milk in the refrigerator below. i didn't request the tray and don't know who put it there for them, but it was beyond wonderful for them to have it there. someone mentioned the elevator arrangement. there is a separate elevator for the parking garage and you do have to then go through the lobby to reach the elevators to the floors, but we considered this to be a good security measure as there is then no outside access to the floors. we also had reservations for dinner for our family after my daughter's graduation, in the conservatory. i have to say that the waiters were wonderful - put up with everyone straggling in half-an-hour late and numerous special requests for the kids. this was a wonderful hotel and spotlessly clean. it is gorgeous inside as they are doing a big renovation. we will stay there again every time we go down to los angeles.
good hotel for lax access but not near much bathroom
a good spot stayed overnight in early may last. convenient to lax. nice bar with efficient staff. breakfast buffet was excellent. would recommend.

renaissance montura-doubtful we stayed at this hotel for 3 days, arriving on a friday evening at about midnight. we expected room service to be limited. when i called, i was told limited service selections meant pre-made sandwiches (two to choose from) and a pre-made salad. very disappointing, especially since the hotel is across from the airport and people are arriving at all hours. i was directed to denny's, ihop, or carl's jr. there were no other choices. for the most part, the room itself was clean. the cabinet door housing the mini refrigerator was a little askew. the refrigerator itself did not reach a very cold temp, despite the fact that we turned it all the way to the coldest setting. upon entering the room, you will see two bottles of imported water. don't open them unless you want to spend $3.50 and $4.50 each and they are not worth it at all.when we checked in, the garage elevator was out of order. there is only one elevator for the garage, which is a seperate structure adjacent to the hotel. this meant we needed to walk down four flights of stairs with our luggage, walk across the corridor to the hotel elevator and go up to our room, only to take the same route again to go out for a meal that the hotel room service could not provide.the desk gave excellent driving directions, however. it is doubtful that we will stay here again.

would be great at even twice the price a terrific hotel overall. very close to lax, walking distance to the hertz and avis lots, excellent service from the welcoming and competent staff (one of the fastest check-ins i've ever had at any hotel), fantastic bed, extremely clean bathroom, excellent food in the concierge lounge, marble top furniture, live plant in the guest room, beautiful artwork throughout the property. i still can't believe i only paid $109 per night. my only complaint was the airport shuttle, which is shared with a number of other hotels and makes a number of stops before getting to the renaissance.

not a pleasent stay!!!! the hotel itself left a lot to be desired! before i booked the hotel, i glanced over its website and figured that this is a great hotel due to those misleading photos on the hotel's website. all in all, i have to say that this is a terrible hotel. the lobby is appointed in dark colors. this made the whole enviroment looked gloomy. the rooms were ok, however i expect more from a renaissance hotel! the bed was hard and the beddings were below average! on the other hand, since the hotel is nearby the airport, is is very noisy 24 hours a day!

my favorite hotel in the lax area i travel to la twice a month and always stay at the renaissance. i used to stay at the lax marriott but the property has gotten so run down that i personally feel unsafe. not at the renaissance though. the rooms, the bar, the lobby, the staff, the food, the gym are all exceptional. i really like how quiet the hotel is at all times. i work late in the evening and so i sleep in until around 9:00am. i am never waken by the maid service in other rooms or hallway. the only recommendation would be to upgrade the breakfast in the concierge lounge. it is usually just ok. frankly, residence inns have been breakfast choices. other than that small detail, this hotel is home away from home. thank you marriott.

beautiful hotel, great service we stayed at the renaissance montura on saturday, march 25, 2006. there was four of us and with the senior rate we paid $98.00/night...$111.86 with all the taxes. excellent price for a beautiful hotel, close to the airport with no noise, seemed like a safe part of town.-check in was very quick and the staff was very nice.-free shuttle bus to and from lax runs 24 hours.-clean, beautiful rooms (furniture was a bit large for these smaller rooms)-we had a light breakfast in the hotel restaurant and it was delicious, service was excellent and when the food came to the table, it was on beautiful dishes and garnished with fresh fruit etc., looked like a picture out of a magazine. my toast was made with thick homemade bread and my daughter's french toast was garnished with fresh strawberries and she said that it was the best french toast that she has ever had.-burger king is across the street.-budget car rental across the street, i rented from alamo which is about 1 mile away. to save on taxi fees, i took the shuttle back to the airport and walked downstairs and caught the alamo shuttle. i highly recommend this hotel. i was in california for about a week and stayed at other hotels if you would like to look at those reviews. area/hotels:north hollywood - holiday inn, beverly garlandanaheim (near disneyland) - holiday inn expresshuntington beach - best western huntington beach innlong beach - the coast long beach hotel

if you have to stay near the airport this is a great hotel we stayed at this hotel for one night on our way back from ny to sydney. we had also stayed at the radisson lax the night before, but the renaissance wins hands down. the room was some 30% cheaper, the night we stayed, the beds more comfortable, the room a little larger, but what really stood out was the service. they have something called delighted to serve which i thought would be some cheesy corporate service standard that they just put up to say they have good service. but they actually all seemed to be genuinely delighted to serve you. everyone staff member we ran into or dealt with was extremely courteous, pleasant and nothing was too much trouble. a rarity in american hotels.if we have to stay near lax, we will stay here.

beautiful hotel - excellent experience based on this web site, we stayed at this hotel at the beginning and end of our trip to california. what a beautiful hotel! the staff was friendly, the concierge service was efficient and knowledgable, the breakfast was great! a bonus was the proximity to the rental car places - an easy walk to pick up and drop off our car, saving us a day's car rental fees!what a great hotel at any price, but the value was amazing!!

wonderful airport hotel! we stayed last week on our way to palm springs. the flight landed late and we made our way over to the renaissance. the front desk personnel were delightful and our club level room was fantastic. we'd booked the romance package and they had already layed out the rose petals when we got into the room. our champagne and strawberries arrived shortly thereafter. breakfast the next morning was delicious. it was a first class experience!

nice stay, convenient very nice hotel with a great location. close to car rentals and lax (1-2 miles). closest car rental is budget across the street. we rented from hertz which is one block from hotel, extremely convenient, can walk there.hotel staff are very friendly and helpful. room is very clean and decent size. furniture is a little big for the room but there was still plenty of room for two people. for women - bring your own blow dryer if you need to use it for more than five minutes. i have long hair and it kept shutting off to cool down after about 2 minutes of use on medium heat, what a nuisance.parking was $13 per day in the garage. did not use valet service. never heard the airplanes and our stay was very quiet and restful. would gladly stay again.

a remarkable experience as a meetings planning coordinator for my employer, we held a four day meeting at the renaissance montura. there were 140 employees in attendance. i was very impressed with the professionalism i encountered with the hotel management and banquet staff. the customer service was outstanding. they all exceeded my expectations.the sleeping rooms were clean and neat, and the beds were comfortable. the meeting space was very accomodating to our needs. food and beverage service was great.most importantly, the meeting attendees had positive comments about the hotel staff and the hotel property.with all this said, as the opportunities present, i will hold more meetings at the renaissance montura.for many years i have planned business meetings with many chain hotels throughout southern california. the renaissance montura is a 5-star hotel in many respects.

good, some improvements needed. this hotel is definitely a nice, safe place to stay. the lobby, bar and rooms are lovely and seem newly renovated. the concierge staff were helpful and friendly. the room we stayed in was very cramped with furniture and made it a little claustrophobic for a 3 night stay. (we were attending a conference in the hotel). if your only staying one night though, this shouldn't cause a problem. bed was comfortable. shower had very poor water pressure and didn't get very hot. (i hate that!)our room was tucked away in a corner by the stairwell, which i thought would work to our advantage noise-wise. however the housekeeping staff must use the stairs pretty regularly because there were doors slamming and talking all morning. couldn't sleep in! meanwhile you don't even hear the jets flying right outside!all in all, it was a pretty good stay. parking is expensive, and i wish more hotels would get on the ball with free wi-fi. it's really not that expensive to offer for free. this hotel wanted to charge $10/day. i think that's a scam. small little chains like microtel offer it for free! oh well.

best hotel near lax i stay overnight near los angeles int'l airport (lax) at least several times per year and this is easily the best hotel in the area. - beautifully appointed hotel and rooms- execllent location: 1 block off century blvd. near lax- free shuttle to airport- competetive parking rates incl. valet- club level provides breakfast and hors d'è‰™uvresthe only negative experience for me has been the clueless valet parking staff which always screws up the parking fees, car wash (included w/ some packages) etc... not a deal breaker by any means.

great airport hotel i stayed at the renaissance montura lax hotel during october 2005 for three nights. i booked this hotel as i was attending a conference held in the international room. the rooms are nicely decorated and the views range from la carparks to the runway at lax. surprisingly, there is zero noise from the jets, the rooms are very well insulated. i had a good amount of time to explore the lax area by foot and in the immediate area there is absolutely nothing aside from a burger king across the road. however, if you walk left and follow the main road right down (20 mins) you'll find many restaurants (mexican/ chinese/ american) and commercial blocks. otherwise there are many other hotels in the area to visit! in the lax area, it is the finest hotel, it has many european style touches including a prized art collection. the restaurant in the hotel serves very good food, though it is a little pricey! snacks and essential items are available in a store in the lobby and a pool/spa on the lower level. the staff are very friendly and provided items i requested free of charge such as toothpaste (!) and a late check-out at 3pm. if you're considering staying around lax to save on la hotel costs, the taxi downtown is $40, alternatively take the free shuttle back to lax and a super shuttle into town- $19 per person or the bus which is a few dollars but takes 2 hours. staying in the lax area you are really confined to the hotel itself to provide all necessary comforts. the renaissance montura hotel does this and more!

marriott does it again being a fan of the marriott chain, it is my first choice in hotels. recently visiting the tut exhibit, we chose the renaissance montura hotel los angeles that recently underwent a major remodel. my compliments to this fine hotel for a job well done. beautiful furnishings artwork throughout. close and easy to get to from lax and the freeway. airplane noise was minimal and not an issue. comfortable room beds.newspaper at your door in the am. staff pleasant and helpful with maps directions. food resturants excellant. the berry crepes were fabulous. small pool gym with lots of equipment. non valet parking in their garage was $14.00 pd. a little steep. i would absolutly stay again.

an excellent stay!! i stayed here on 09/23/05 and enjoyed the stay. i wasnéˆ¥??› impressed with the exterior, but the hotel was gorgeous inside and the rooms were in great shape. the bed was also very comfortable. parking at the hotel was $13.99 a day and included in-and-out privileges. we had one problem with room service; when we ordered at 1:30am the kitchen was having problems. the menu was inaccurate, the order took 45 minutes to get to us, and i didnéˆ¥??› get what i asked for. to their creditéˆ¥?”–hey gave the food to us for free and apologized. i was impressed. it was easily $30 worth of food. the hotel bar was great and i enjoyed the stay here

very good airport hotel i stayed at the renaissance montura about two weeks ago (in late august) for several nights, while visiting relatives in la. the hotel, while fairly close to the la airport, is quieter than many other hotels both near the airport and farther away-- for instance, on one of the many busy la streets--because of the excellent soundproofing. another advantage of staying here is that the shuttle picks you up and take you back to the airport, which spares my relatives the trouble of dealing with lax. i've stayed here a couple of other times for these reasons, even though i don't have a burning desire to stay near the airport. yet, freeway access is nearby and it's easy to get to other parts of la (usually west la for me). on this visit, the shuttle came by the airport within a few minutes. (however, the shuttle wouldn't take me to a local car rental place about 6-8 blocks away a couple of days later, but luckily enterprise picked me up, since i have some leg trouble.) the room at the renaissance was nicely furnished and of good size, with fairly comfortable beds, but not as comfy as at the westin, although the lax airport westin--which i've stayed at a couple of times because of my starwood membership--is noisier and less well maintained than the renaissance. i keep wondering, though, when most hotels--even quite upscale ones--will decide to use fitted mattress pads and bottom sheets so the bed doesn't keep unmaking itself during the night? the bathroom and desk had lovely granite countertops, although i found both much too high for an average-height woman. at least the desk should have an adjustable chair. i felt like i needed a child's booster seat to be able to write at the desk (and instead had to sit on two pillows). like most hotels, this one seems designed by and for (tall) men. the bathroom had a lot of counter space, so it was a little surprising that the coffeemaker was in the bedroom, near the tv, which made things a little more difficult than if it had been on the bathroom counter, near the water, as at most hotels. there was actually a nice small (and empty) refrigerator rather than a mini-bar, so i could keep my bottled water and a few other things in there without having to take the hotel's stuff out, as i usually do. the hotel provides fresh apples for guests, by the way, and has decent coffee replenished daily in the room with real half and half (although not much of it or of sugar). the staff i met all seemed very nice and helpful. my room was exactly as i'd requested--non-smoking (and this sometimes is true in name only), quiet, on a high floor, and away from the elevator and ice machine. i actually was able to sleep in a quiet environment for the most part. the a/c was a little noisy, however, so i turned it off when i was sleeping, even though it was fairly hot in la while i was there. i'd get up in the middle of the night and turn the a/c back on for a little while to cool off the room a bit. all things considered, and speaking as someone who oftens has bad hotel luck, i felt like my stay went smoothly. the hotel is nicely designed, both in its public spaces and guest rooms. i got a good rate on the marriott/renaissance website (about $100/night), and would stay here again if i could get a similar or lower rate. the parking charge of $13/day for self-parking is much lower than in some parts of la and in many other cities. i didn't use the restaurant or room service, so can't comment on those. but if you're looking for a quiet, understated, well-decorated hotel in this general part of la, the renaissance is a good choice.

great renovation! this hotel was lovely and the service (front desk, restaurant, valet) was excellent. the rooms were very clean, updated, smelled good. bed was very comfortable. ate twice in the restaurant. food was very good and very reasonably priced. i was worried there would be a lot of airport noise, but didn't hear any. i am going back out to la in a few weeks and am staying at this hotel again (i usually stay at the beach, but the renovation is so nice at this hotel, i'll give up the ocean for a much nicer hotel).

best airport hotel i've been in i stayed on the airport side and didn't hear a jet at all. i also turned of the airconditioner as i always do in hotels rooms. i was in club level though but that shouldn't make a difference. the marriot hotel around the corner is no where near as nice as i stayed at the marriot the week before and decided that i didn't want to stay there unless i was desperate. old dingy rooms with such skinny bathroom doors you almost had to turn sideways to get in. the montura rooms seem overly luxurious in comparison. service was fine, i signed up for the park and fly $199 and got club level, a private town car to the airport and free breakfast. that was very nice. didn't bring a car to park but they did call me to ask me if i wanted my car washed when i was gone (complimentary)! the food at club level is pretty much the same at most hotels club level floors -acceptable. didn't go downstairs for my breakfast as i was pressed for time so i can't say how the food is. i will definitely stay here again while passing through.

as good as lax get... the renaissance montura's web site (and some of the reviews on this page) would have you believe that this is a first-rate hotel experience, but that's just not the case. the hotel has a veneer of luxury, but it's inch-deep. basically this is a next-to-the-airport hotel that draws groups just off planes and business travelers who want to get an early start the next morning. so you'll have to expect kids running down the hallways, a jammed parking lot, and other signs of high volume usage from time to time. the hotel is also a paradox: it's huge from the outside, but corridors and general spaces inside are narrow if not cramped. in short: space at this hotel, wherever you are, is a commodity. having said all that, rooms on the back side are surprisingly quiet for the hotel's being so close to one run-way, the beds are comfortable, bathrooms are marble and well-lit, and room service is faultlessly polite (with filtered coffee, no less, as the standard). you could make this your lax-adjacent default hotel and be none the worse for wear...

better than most but nothing to write home about! wow the hotels must be pretty poor at lax for this to have received so much acclaim. generally i found the service poor especially at restaurant(s). we ended up just leaving the resturant to go to the bar area and then left that to go upstairs to order room service. yes the hotel is clean and comfortable but it is still just an airport hotel. not in our mind being worthy of anything but above average for airport hotels.

worked for us! we live about an hour north of los angeles and decided to spend one night at the renaissance montura before an early morning flight to maui. i booked a room online through marriott's website and got their 'aaa park fly' special. for about $215 (including tax), we got the room, 7 days of free valet parking, a car wash and a town-car ride to the airport the morning of our flight! we also stayed on the club level and enjoyed that thoroughly. the lounge (only accessible to people staying on the club levels) was great for appetizers/drinks in the evening and then breakfast the day of our departure. our room was very nice - beautifully appointed and not terribly cramped even with 4 people, golf clubs and luggage in it. we had a great view of the airport from our window - our 5 and 6 year old children loved watching the planes land every few minutes and we were amazed that there was no noise from the jets whatsoever! our children would've been perfectly happy with dinner at burger king (directly across the street!) but, instead, we enjoyed a wonderful dinner at the conservatory restaurant just off the lobby. the hotel is gorgeous - decorated beautifully and very clean. the orchids everywhere are just incredible!

very nice clean place to stay the hotel was extremely clean as if it were new. the beds were the most comfortable i have slept in in a long time. the maid service was great; anything asked for was given with no hesitations. we had total control over the air conditioning which worked great. staff was friendly and helful. the lobby was always spotless. the hotel was literally 2 minutes from the airport which can be a plus and a negative. if you are just stopping over it's a great location but may not be a great location if vacationing throughout the l.a. area (too much traveling). i was very happy with this hotel.

one of the better hotels in the lax area we staid at the renaissance montural for one night in june 2005 after an 11 h flight from frankfurt, germany. this is a relatively small hotel (compared to the other airport hotels) that offers more charme, privacy and personality than most of the surrounding chain hotels. the standard rooms are well equipped but not very spacious---however, since we only staid for one night (as most people do), room size was not so important to us ... staff was friendly and responded quickly to our needs. all in all it was a good value (since we got the aaa rate), and we would probably stay there again.

excellent hotel! i stayed here on business for one night. the primary factor in choosing this hotel was its proximity to lax since i had an early morning flight the following day. however, when i arrived, i was very pleasantly surprised by the size, quality and cleanliness of the room. the hotel was very quiet and i heard no noise from the hallway, other rooms or outside the hotel. airplane noise was not an issue at all (at least during my stay). the hotel has a complimentary shuttle to the airport, which is a great perk. i stayed on one of the floors that allow guests access to a complimentary buffet breakfast in the morning. it was a continental style buffet, with a somewhat limited selection, but excellent quality. overall, a very good experience. not your typical airport hotel by any means. i would definitely stay here again.

great airport hotel we stayed at the renaissance in june when my husband was attending a conference there. i was very pleasantly surprised by the quality of the hotel! it definitely was above the standard marriott hotel in terms of the bedding and its comfort; the bathroom linens were a little more plush, also.the hotel was very quiet. even though it is in the approach route for several runways, there was no airplane noise at any time.my only complaint? there is no direct subway or bus into downtown la from the hotel. i went back to the airport to get a shuttle into la.

great experiance we stayed at the renaissance hotel @lax july7,2005 we had a one day lay over on the way to maui. we had the room with a jaguaur to drive a special i got off their website we went to king tut in our jag came back and enjoyed our suite had pizza delivered we had a great lay over in the best airport hotel i have ever been to it was a really nice place. i also never heard the jets. stay on the top floors they serve brekfast up there and it was excellent. the whole hotel is upscale without the upscale pricetag!

excellent park and fly solution we picked this hotel for it's convenience since we drove in from the central coast and had an early morning flight. the service was great. the evening appetizers were enough to make a light meal. the rooms were clean, quiet and comfortable. we stayed on the club level which was included in the aaa park and fly promotion. from the dining room on the 11th floor there was a great view of the planes arriving and departing. the soundproofing was really good, couldn't hear the planes at all. we had two kids with us so we used the pool which is definitely small, but not crowded. the gym was well equipped. the front desk were very helpful arranging the shuttle since we couldn't use the towncar they offered for free with the two kids and no car seats. they also arranged an early room service for breakfast, complimentary, since we had to leave before 6am. also included in the aaa deal was 7 days of free parking and they washed the car while we were gone. the staff were all very professional and friendly. i would not hesitate to stay here again.

the best breakfast room at lax stayed here for 4 nights late may to attend a convention next door..used seniors rate of $us 84 plus tax. the room was above average although the bed was not up to new starwood standard.the breakfast room buffet(including omlette station that delivered to your table) was exceptional although when taken to dinner by a transiting fellow australian and his daughter on saturday night it was a disaster..but then it seems all lax hotel restaurants seem to have problems on saturday night.. back to breakfast buffet;staff were discreet and courteous-highly recommended...outdoor pool was small for a 500 room hotel and the spa/whirlpool positivly minimalist (2 comfortable or 4 in a squeeze) the room maids always had a smile and pleasantries as you passed them and the front of house staff were exceptional although the hold mail system needs centralisation as there appears to be 3 seperate security locations to be checked...would recommend this 4 star hotel for the quality of its staff at all levels....

good airport hotel the renaissance was very plush for the ?‹¢65 per room per night we paid. the lobby and public spaces were very elaborate and the breakfast included in our price was second to none. a huge buffet and a made to order counter too. the staff were helpful and the pool was nice and particularly quiet while we were there. the rooms were clean tidy and overall a 4* hotel. excellent airport hotel.

would visit again in a heartbeat. i just checked out of the renaissance this morning, may 21st. i got this hotel for 55 a night via priceline for 3 nights, may 18-21st. i was in town for e3, a convention in downtown la. i was so impressed by this hotel. the lobby was beautiful. their art collection alone was worth 14 million dollars, according to the brochure that described all of the pieces on the property. the staff was always wonderful, and the rooms..my god they were amazing. one of the most comfortable beds i've ever slept on. pillowtop and everything. the sheets were soft and luxurious and exceptionally clean. i'm a big pillow person and i never had to request more pillows. the room featured granite countertops in the bathroom, and granite on the dresser. the room also had a large armchair and a leather ottoman. the complimentary toiletries in the bathroom smelled wonderful and were all from bath and body works. maid service was always prompt and whenever we passed them in the hall, they greeted us with a smile and a 'good morning'. you could always tell when they had entered your room, because you were assaulted with a wonderful smell as soon as you opened the door.the only thing i felt that could be improved upon, was the pool area. it was very nice and kept clean, but it was small. the food was outstanding, even though it was a bit pricey. we ended up spending 60.00 on 1 dinner which included a delicious burger and fries, and a traditional club sandwich, 1 breakfast of yummy french toast with strawberries and powdered sugar, a bagel and cream cheese, a glass of orange juice and whole milk, and a bowl of soup. all of that included a nice tip. my last night there i was feeling ill and i called room service for soup and they brought up bread and a wonderful turkey vegetable soup, along with a wish to 'feel better'. my soup took a little longer than expected, but they were very aplogetic and explained they were quite busy.the hotel parking was expensive (13 for self, 16 for valet), but well lit and safe. the staff was very courteous and never hesitated to help us with directions to the nearest movie theatre, downtown la, food (subway),and the 405. as we were leaving, they wished us a safe drive, hoped that we would come back, and asked if we needed any help with directions. i would stay here again in a heartbeat. as a cost-effective college student, i couldn't find a better hotel to spend my 55 a night in. their regular rates aren't bad either (109 a night) and perhaps i might even be willing to stay there at that rate.yes, they're that good.i love the renaissance!

ok-but some glitches ok stay-bathroom is very small and basic for the nice furnishings throughout the rest of the hotel.bed wes comfy-air conditioning very old and noisy, and since the thermostat is right next to the vent it kept turning off and on all night.restaurant was ok.room service b'fast was horrid! and they were late in delivering it.bigguyinpasadena

best hotel in lax area! i stayed at the renaissance los angeles hotel (lax location) on march 19 - 21. after a fight with a traveling companion, i moved to the renaissance from the los angeles marriott downtown - what an upgrade! this is a lovely hotel, especially for an airport location. much nicer and bigger room than the marriott downtown and for a much lower rate ($109 at the renaissance versus $159 at the marriott). lobby, bar, and room itself were very clean, spotless in fact. staff was very helpful courtous. the gym is really nice, altough i didn't get to use it. the only area of this hotel that needs work is the pool, sorta small and not kept as neat as the rest of the property. i have stayed at other hotels in the lax area (crowne plaza and westin specifically) and was most impressed by the lax renaissance. great value and great service - definitely recommended.

not worth the price i have booked for 2 rooms and when i arrive, the rooms are on different floors. i expected for interconnecting rooms or at least 2 rooms not too far one from the other. i ask for a change and they can find me 2 rooms separated by 2 other rooms. this hotel is very close to lax airport and has a shuttle to the airport every 10 mn. the room are clean but not well maintained. in the bathroom, you cannot close the drain of the sink. in the tub, you cannot have full water for the shower. half is lost in the tub. some lamps are not working because they are unplugged. and this hotel charge double than the other others in the lax airport area. not worth it.

better than i thought just spent one night there after the flight in from london.can parking good but i had to pay which was a surprise for the states.check in staff and room service staff vey good and helpful.our deal included breakfast which was very good in deed.rooms good. all in all nice hotel.

very comfortable positives- spacious, clean rooms. close to the airport yet very quiet. short waits at the long front desk. helpful bellhops. burger king across street with mainly tourist clientelle (not inglewood riffraff like down on century blvd.) great gym with tvs. jacuzzi. negs- pool is too small, and there was some strange debris floating around (toilet paper?). internet hookup in lobby too expensive. late night bartender was a dullard. conclusion- highly recommended, but the doubletree el segundo is better.

nice, convenient airport hotel we stayed at this hotel twice on a recent trip, one night arriving in la and one night before our flight back. the shuttle is very frequent, so minimal waiting. the public areas are lovely, nice service (plenty of bellhops to take your luggage). the room is standard size, superior furnishings and accessories (very comfortable beds!), and very nice bathrooms. our only problem was trying to get synthetic pillows instead of feather - apparently when they remodeled, they threw out all the foam pillows! finally were able to rustle up a few, but took some doing (both times...). great view of the planes landing at lax. nice, if pricey, restaurant, although a good option is the burger king right across the street! many airport car rental facilities within walking distance (national, avis, hertz), so don't have to go back to the airport to pick up a rental car.

reasonble hotel reasonable hotel, room was small on club floor (floor 10) for extra rate. beds are comfortable. the airport shuttle is a bit of a gamble, comes every 15 - 18 minutes (they say) but not on a set schedule. not an exciting area there at lax but near the avis rental car return if you happen to do them, you can walk to the hotel. would i go again? perhaps if i were flying out early, but probably would just do the hotel where i was really staying and just get up early to get there at lax.

this is not the hollywood renaissance this is a nice hotel with a great staff, but some of the reviews submitted here are actually for the hollywood renaissance, not the lax renaissance. huge difference! when you're reading through the reviews, if you see anything about the hollywood sign, the hollywood walk of fame, the connected mall, the kodak theatre, mann's chinese theater... these are all in hollywood, not at the l.a. airport. this hotel is much cheaper than in hollywood, and not nearly as nice, but if you need to be next to the airport and you want a nice, clean, quiet, well-staffed place to stay, this is a great choice. just don't expect any l.a. sightseeing nearby!

paid for parking!?? the hotel is almost right next doors to la international airport (lax) with a free shuttle and that is why we chose it. we were flabbergasted that we had to pay for parking. about $12 for self parking which is about 3-4 minutes away from the front or $24 for valet parking. never paid for parking while staying at any hotel before. wish we were informed in advance. room was ok. had to pay for internet. front desk was mostly indifferent, but not rude. elevators were very slow but are being renovated. would not recommend other than proximity and convenience for the airport.

sheraton gateway lax stayed four nights on business/pleasure in dec. weekend rates were great...$109/night. they ended up giving me those rates during the week too. probably because the pool was down and they were rennovating a set of elevators so had to use service elevators...not becoming of a 4 star hotel.they do have a 4 star restaurant...shula's. not quite kid friendly or budget friendly but the wait staff was great to look at!they had a breakfast/lunch restaurant on premisis but did not frequent.requested and got a room close to elevators which is always nice at a hotel this size. saved my walking for what really counted...hollywood!nice clean place, helpful staff. great for the money! their shuttle was very timely both to and from airport. parking expensive and a few blocks from hotel so i just rented a car for one day and returned it that night...to a nearby enterprise location that is very near this hotel. the enterprise shuttle actually dropped me off at the hotel because they went past it, which saved me shuttle time from the airport.probably wouldn't have stayed at this place if the business portion of the trip wasn't held there. i really wanted to stay at eco lodge because i heard there were more restaurants over there plus i could get a smoking room, but this worked out.

great for the price, make sure to get it cheap we booked our room through priceline for $60 a night on priceline, had i paid more i would have been disapointed but for that price it was worth saving the extra money in these tough times. valet parking was $25 but well worth it if you are going to be in and out a bunch. the rooms were older and we had to move rooms due to the heat not working and the sink being clogged in our first room. in the second room everything worked fine but the shower seemed to have mildew or soap scum in both rooms. the hotel staff was extremely friendly and that alone with the starbucks in the lobby were the highlights of this hotel. if you are looking for someplace cheap to crash for the night, this place is it, if you are looking for more i would stay somewhere else.

convenient for overnight lay-over at lax we stayed at this hotel during a lay-over from seattle to puerto vallarta. we landed in lax at 11:00p and caught the hotel's shuttle to the hotel. the hotel's shuttle automatically runs outside the baggage claim areas every 15 minutes 24 hours per day, so need to call anyone to get picked up. the ride to the hotel is about 5 minutes, so super convenient especially when arriving late or leaving early. we didn't try any of the hotel services since we arrived so late and left so early. the room was comfortable, as expected at a sheraton. there is a starbuck's in the lobby of the hotel, which is also convenient for an early morning start.

mixed feelings it is not the first time i have stayed there. i am a starwood preferred guest. sheraton is normally synonymous with quality and comfort. still, i was disappointed this time with my overnight stay. half of the elevators did not work and the room clearly needed upgrading and refurbishing.more, the buffet breakfast is not up to one's expectations.compared to other hotels of the same category in the vicinity,- the westin in particular-the sheraton gateway has obviously lost part of its gloss and therefore become too expensive for what it actually offers.

best airport hotel bar none this is the best airport hotel property i have ever stayed at. there is almost nothing to do around lax, very few restaurants, bars, fun things to do. so if you have to be there for a nite before you leave town, this is the best hotel to stay at. by far!the vibe feels almost european, maybe b/c several of the front desk people are, maybe because of the very sleek feeling of the hotel. i feel more like i am in the downtown of a fun city than at an airport area with nothing going on.front desk is always helpful, and the lobby is always abuzz. always, and in a good way. there are some very hip, cool chairs in the lobby bar area, and they are always full. the rooms are nicely updated. try and get a room where you are facing the runways. it is pretty cool. by the way there are often very good prices at this location. do not bother with staying at the westin, which often is a more upscale starwood brand. this is a much better overall hotel.

not the greatest experience i was there over the weekend for a conference for my job. had i payed my own money, i would have been very disappointed. for starters there was very little hot water in the morning. so having to get up to a cold shower every morning was not that pleasant. next, the public elevators were not working so you had to ride the service elevators with the employees. also the service elevators were only running one at a time; so most of the time you were waiting anywhere from 3-5 minutes to get on an elevator that wasn't packed with patrons as well as employees. that was very uncomfortable considering that there were sometimes where i had to ride the elevator with the wait staff who had just cleared off tables of dirty dishes or the cleaning staff who had loads of soiled linens; not cool. furthermore, the bathroom in my room was extemely small. if i was there with my wife and child we would have had a hard time making it work. the rooms are not family friendly at all, and the bathtub was pealing. however,the beds and pillows were great, they were the best things about the room itself. the cleaning staff was exellent as well as the wait staff when we had our meals. i like the access that the hotel gives you to the trolley so that you can go down to manhattan beach. also, the los angeles by night tour was awesome!!!!

los angeles by night i stayed for three nights over the weekend for a conference. had my company not paid for the room, i would have had major issues. it was also my first trip to la so the excitement allowed me to overlook some inconveniences.first, i would avoid this hotel until the elevators are updated. the main elevators are not working and the hotel suggests the service elevators. so we rode for four days with the soiled linen cart and the guy who cleans up after room service. sloooooow elevators. next, the room did not have hot water in the mornings. hot was not a problem in the evening, but the early morning hours produced room temperature at best. the bathrooms should certainly be updated. on a positive note, the housekeeping and hotel wait staff were outstanding. concierge were invaluable. make sure you take the la by night tour. the concierge will book you for $55. they'll pick you up/drop you off at the hotel. if possible, go on a sunday evening, as the traffic is almost non-existent.also, take the $3 trolley from the hotel to manhattan beach. awesome. eat fish tacos at wahoos.

decent hotel near airport so its right next to the airport so you can hear the planes obviously. i'm not quite sure how to describe the style of the hotel..its like it was on the cutting edge in the early 90s and the decorating is still ok but some things have fallen into disrepair like the textured wallpaper in the bathroom etc. it was a good change though from a traditional boring looking room. valet parking was quick...i think it was $25/night for me. didn't eat there but i noticed they had a nice open bar. if you have to return a rental car, there are plenty of places nearby to fillup gas. leaving the hotel you can't just take a left, you have to go down the street and somehow figure out how to turn around...i never found a place so i had to go through the airport to get back to century blvd going the opposite way..still it only took me 5 mins to get to hertz. i would stay there again but i'd prefer a new or newly renovated property first.

convenient airport hotel the sheraton park n' fly is the reason i stay here (lax marriott has the same program), that and my spg points. i like the hotel, it is convenient for the airport, the pool is nice and shula's is good, but overpriced. the rooms are nice and the beds comfortable and they have good business services.all good so far.the negatives are the parking and the elevators. you have to valet unless you want a half mile walk for self parking. the elevators have been messed up for a while now. they are so bad you have to use the staff elevators more often than not and it has been this way for a while.will i stay here again? yes. it has some good positives. it is a great hotel for someone looking for an overnight stay or maybe two days. if you have to been in l.a. more than two days there are a lot better places to stay and better locations.

red light hotel we stayed twice within 2 weeks at this hotel and had 2 complete different experience. we book thru hotwire and paid $99 taxes in. the rooms were clean and the location is great for people coming in and out of the airport. there is also a trolley that can take you to manhanttan beach or some shopping malls for $3 round trip. pretty decent. our first experience was decent, professional staff, clean rooms.. however, our second experience.. what a nightmare. they had a covention of rough riders bikers. they almost fill the entire hotel. people were yelling and partying all night.. apparently, we were the only one on our floor not invited to the party. people knocked on our door all night (litterally we had to get up at 4:30 am to catch our flight and there were 4 people sitting in the hallway envoying another drink next to our room door.) we should have thought it would turned out this way when we saw police cars parked in front of the hotel when we checked in.. when we checked out, there was only 1 employee in the lobby and clearly he looked at uncomfortable as us... we saw prostitute in the lobby (it was not hidden - remember - we were intrudes into their convention), people driking from their vodka bottles... really, we could not get our of there fast enough... beware... if that is the kind of group they want to rent their hotel too... they should let other customers know uo front what is to be expected for the week... the poor clerk at the lobby wanted to leave with us.. nothing in this hotel was under control.

ok for a transit stop hotel is showing its age, which is why reviews are mixed. our room was ok, clean - though seemed a bit musty. the usual comfy sheraton bed, important in a transit stop. quiet, curtains darkened the room effectively. a/c not very efficient. limited toiletries supplied, nice orange fragrance though. no safe. usual coffeemaker, ironing board. slow elevators, cigarette smell in corridors. pool looked pleasant. limited restaurant options on site. we ate at shula's which was average - very slow service, waiter forgot part of our order, my beef tips sandwich was cold (but my husband liked his steak). left early so cannot comment on breakfast options. wouldn't stay here for sightseeing, but does the job for a transit stop.

great value we stayed at this hotel for one night. it is close to the airport and easy to find. the room was excellent value for less than $100 with a large comfortable room. staff were freindly and very efficient. we would stay at this hotel again.

convenient spot based on previous reviews i made a mental checklist on things to look for:isolated location? i didn't see any convenient places within walking distance. if you're going elsewhere to eat, be prepared to drive or make a substantial walk. it also seems like there are no other people around unless they're in their cars. parking ? yes, $13 out back, $24 valet. thanks for the warning. i can understand why someone might be uncomfortable walking from the back lot (see above). i felt okay, but i'm sure my wife would have reservations if she were alone.staff? check in and out was quick and convenient, the front desk staff i dealt with was friendly and informative and even the cleaning people acknowledged us and were friendly.elevator problems? we didn't have any problems, but we were amused at the warning signs and the printed explanation in the hotel information packet. yes, it's a long term problem.chipped bathtub? sure, there they are. it didn't affect the operation, but with the repairs and old tiles, it almost felt like you stepped into a different level of room to shower.hair in the drain? none, but i have a headful of my own, if needed. the bathroom, as well as the rest of the room, was very clean.the location was convenient for us because it was just a few blocks from the rental car center and our plans to explore the coast to the north of town (santa barbara) as well as south (orange coast). we had a late arrival and early departure, so being near the airport helped with time. we got back fairly late one night and had appetizers in shula's, which were very good. also, our package included the breakfast buffet. since it was included, i forgot to note the price, but we were very pleased with the quality, selection and attention of the staff.the pool area was very nice and there were families using it most of the time that we were there. i didn't have a chance to check out the exercise facility. we were pleased with our experience as everything went off without a glitch. based on this stay and, for a reasonable price, we'd stay here again and not discourage anyone from trying it.

solid sheraton i stayed at this hotel out of convenience for a work trip (and because i'm a spg member). i travel quite a bit and stay in mostly ws and an occasional westin or sheraton. it's completely on par with other sheratons i've stayed at in the past...everything pretty standard, clean, decent service, etc. it's also far better than most airport hotels (i normally won't stay in airport hotels as they tend to be yucky) the pool area is nice with a decent sized pool and nice furniture (like you'd normally find in a resort-type hotel). check in was quick and friendly. my room (an executive suite) was large, nice and clean...it faced the street/runway and contrary to some of the other reviews, you could barely hear a thing. i ordered room service for dinner and was pleasantly surprised by the quality.to those knocking this place (or to those wondering if you should stay here), please remember that it is (a) a sheraton, so you should know what to expect (b) an airport hotel, and (c) very reasonably priced for what you're getting...and you generally get what you pay for. if you want luxury resort/ritz type experience (which by some of the reviews is what i assume people honestly expected by their commentary), pay the money and stay at the ritz.

not impressed i got a good rate on priceline which was just as well because the rack rate would have been extortionate for the state of the bathroom and services. the bathroom was dirty; far more water came out of the tap than out of the showerhead on the shower setting; the water did not drain from the tub. yuk. the pinstripe dark decor is depressing. the pool was nice early in the morning but in the afternoon there was a corporate function going on and since it's a small pool area it wasn't really inviting for an informal swim. most of the lifts didn't work -- it took about 15 minutes to get down. the concierge sighed when i wanted to buy a stamp. the room service food was, as expected, overpriced and ridiculously salty. i wouldn't stay again.

mixed experience we got a good deal through hotwire. very nice hotel - nice rooms, good breakfast, decent outdoor pool, handy for airport. we did however encounter a few problems 1) the free shuttle bus from the airport dropped us at the far end of the airport parking lot - a few minutes walk from the lobby - with 2 young children and 4 large cases this was not a good start! 2) the room we were assigned had not been serviced - beds not made, plate of food thrown across the floor, dirty bathroom - you get the picture. 3) elevators slow, as some of them were out of order so getting back to reception after getting the unserviced room took a while 4) - and this was my biggest problem - the attitude of the front desk staff when reporting the unserviced bedroom - not a word of apology and no manners. don't get me wrong - we enjoyed our stay and feel that we were just unlucky with the room, but i feel the front desk staff let the hotel down - i would have been very disappointed if we had paid the full rate.

convenient to lax perfect hotel near lax. it's reasonably priced (through hotwire), comfortable, clean and most of all convenient with a 24hr shuttle running every 15-20mn to/from lax. would stay there anytime we need to catch a plane

great stay we stayed the last night before flying home because we wanted to be close to airport to avoid any potential traffic problems getting to the airport on time. the price at hotwire was amazing. even after paying for valet parking, it was still cheaper than going even slightly further away for a courtyard, embassy, etc. not sure what's up with the elevator problem. they have a laminated sign by the elevator banks apologizing and offering the service elevators as alternates. this sounds like a near permanent issue vs a slight fix. didn't cause us any issues. room was very nice on the 11th floor. airport noise was not like being at the end of the runway with your windows open. subtle and you almost had to be listening for it. did not interfere with conversation, tv, and most importantly, sleep. friendly efficient staff. in room coffee was single cup starbucks. if you have two people and both drink regular, check to see what you have. we had one regular, one decaf.

not what i have come to expect from a "sheraton" this hotel is not quite up to the standards of what i would expect from a sheraton hotel. lobby was open and spacious, but elevators were not working properly. room had old furniture, mildew in the bathtub, and the tub did not drain properly (constantly stood in ankle-deep water during a shower). close proximity to lax is only plus. for $185 per night + tax at the aaa rate, i will look for another hotel in the future. probably rate this a 2.5 star hotel.

mixed experience at sheraton gateway lax first let me say, for the price i paid via hotwire.com, this was an excellent deal! for the level of hotel, the price was hard to beat. also, the decor of the hotel fits my personal style and so i loved the feel of the place. the bar was awesome and shula's 347 restaurant inside the hotel was amazing (pricey, but amazing)! the beds are super comfy and the pool area was very nice too, the location was great since our vacation had us traveling all over the la area. that being said there are some definite problems with this hotel, in fact, if i was someone who could afford their normal room rates, i would absolutely think this hotel was the pits! first, there is no free parking whatsoever. that's pretty normal for los angeles but the valet at the sheraton is the biggest rip off i've ever heard of in my entire life! it's around $25.00 if you valet over 15 minutes!!!!
