if you elect to self park, it's $13.20 per night. make sure you add that on top of your room rate when budgeting your vacation. the hotel messed up my bill which added insult to injury, they failed to charge me for my hotel bar tab but then charged me for a week of valet parking i didn't use. when i tried to fix the issue and was honest about not being charged for the bar tab, they blamed me and i had to deal with three different people to get it fixed. the bathrooms are a bit scuzzy considering the rest of the hotel and the tv's need to be updated. also, it appears they have been having elevator issues for a long time now with only 2 of the 6 working so you have to take the service elevator. the brasserie for breakfast is overpriced and the service is super slow, i was shocked how bad it was in comparison to shula's the night before. i recommend avoiding a handicapped accessable room as well. i would probably stay here again but it would have to be an even better deal than the one i got. it left our vacation on a sour note due to the billing issues and the price gouging parking issues. just be prepared for what you're getting into.

very good airport hotel this is a very good airport hotel. there are 3 negative issues that are consistently mentioned in reviews here. everything else seems random and subject to personal preferences. 1. elevators: are a real problem. consistently did not stop at the 12th floor to pick me up on the way down. had to get on any elevator that was heading up since it would not stop again on the way down. very long waits at times. housekeeping staff kindly let us use their elevator a couple times.2. parking: $24 for valet, $12 for self-park. self-park lot is behind the hotel across the street. this is a 5-10 minute walk in relative dark at night. shuttle to parking lot is inconsistent. can park on street behind hotel but you might get a ticket during day.3. internet fees: $10.95 per day. true that internet is free in the lobby area (which is quite large). otherwise, the hotel is fine. beds are comfortable and room was clean. i can't figure out how anyone can stay at an airport hotel and then complain about hearing airplanes?! bring earplugs or noise machine. color scheme? yes, kind of dark but this shouldn't ruin your stay! long check-in line? i checked in very quickly. i noticed going through the lobby that there usually was no waiting at the desk, but a couple of times there was a line; that seems normal to me. this hotel is about as close as you can get to the airport. would stay there again but would check to see if there is improvement with the elevators first.

definitely not a 4-star. 3 stars is pushing it. overall, this was not a 4-star hotel as reported by hotwire.com. first, when you walk in, you just feel like there's just something wrong with this hotel. the lobby was dark, uninviting, and had uncomfortable furniture all around with bad loungy techno music playing. the hallways leading the rooms didn't match the motif of the lobby and rooms, which was definitely jarring. the rooms were small, the bathrooms were old and the tub was cracking and peeling, and the tiles were moldy. water was not complimentary (as it should be for a 4-star) and the in-room coffee was horrid (maxwell house!). the elevators weren't working either, 3 of 5 main elevators were out of service and we had to ride the service elevators along with the dirty linens and room service leftovers. some guests even reported up to 30-minute wait times for the main elevators, as only some of the staff were notifying people about the elevator problem. obviously, the hotel knew about the problem as there was a letter in the service elevator apologizing for the inconvenience. i would definitely not stay at this hotel again for what i paid for it.

sheraton does good at lax it's a good hotel. period. i don't critique the front desk, bell-hops, porters, valet etc. at hotels because i typically don't interact with them for more than a few minutes during my entire stay so i don't let them affect my review of the room. if they go above and beyond, then i usually make a note to say something (to them and in these reviews). my reviews usually deal with the nuts and bolts. the gateway is what you would expect a large chain hotel near a major airport to be - busy. the lobby has been re-modeled with mod furniture and is a comfortable place to lounge/work/meet for drinks. and, do not fear, it has it's own starbucks. the rooms are for the most part spacious but the bath rooms are a little small. speaking of the bathrooms, mine (on the 14th floor) could use a little updating and a new tub (it had some missing paint), however, i'm only in there to shower and get moving, so it didn't really bother me. back to the rooms - comfortable bed, good work desk, average t.v. (it's 2008, let's make with the flat screen already!). i couldn't tell you about wi-fi costs or speed as i have my own card. and i sure can't tell you about eating at the hotel, because i have a car and there are plenty of decent places to eat within a 5 mile radius. the hotel is close to a cpk and their in house choices are shula's steakhouse - think ruth chris - and the brasserie (continental?). don't forget, i mentioned the on-premise starbucks. if you book this room through priceline, you're getting a steal, if you book it through sheraton for $250 or under you should be happy (higher tier chain in a large city) and you better be a spg member so you can get the points. one last reminder - this hotel is basically at the airport and situated close to the north side runway so you will hear planes taking off and landing day and night. it's not too noisy, but you can hear them. earplugs can easily solve the noise situation.

beware of animal friendly hotels... just had a one night stopover at sheraton lax. hotel is good quality with good lobby, gym and pool facilities and right by the airport for a 24 hr layover. however after arriving and having a quick snooze in the afternoon, i awoke with bites all over me. we pretty quickly realised that there were fleas everywhere in the room. staff were helpful and straight away moved us to a suite, but we now have to wash everything in our bags as they got right into our baggage and i had a rather uncomfortable 15 hour flight with flea bites itching all over me. reception informed me whilst apologising that they are a pet friendly hotel and that this would be how the fleas got into the room. fleas and bugs can turn up anywhere but i would hope a sheraton does more to check its rooms if a guest has had animals in there in future.

good clean quality safe stay near the airport just what you would expect from sheraton. a nice clean hotel with plenty of room. the room was very nice and super comfortable bed. the only thing i could find that wasn't top notch was the bathroom tile and shower head could use a clean or replacement. but that is honestly the worse that i can say and it wan't a big deal at all! i just love a clean bathroom! the amenities were nice and there was a free shuttle to and from the airport and free wi fi. breakfast wasn't a total rip off and had a large selection of premade stuff. i was perfect for a night to get over the jetlag!

great stay i stayed here for 3 nights as a single traveller. i checked in at 2am and it was really quick and easy, my room was on the 14th floor and had two double beds, tv writing desk and a coffee maker with starbucks coffee, i found it quite spacious. i didn't have breakfast in the lounge but did take full advantage of the starbucks in the lobby and there's a small shop onsite for snacks too. in the evening i ate in the bar area which seemed understaffed but the waitress kept acknowledging me and the food was good. really nice pool area. during the day i travelled by getting collected by a tour bus and one day i got a taxi to santa monica, it cost 50dollars, i discovered the blue bus could take me straight back for 75cents so i did that. the walk from the bus station (10mins) was pretty isolated and there were quite a few homeless people around though but i felt safe enough.the only criticism is there really is nothing around the hotel area to do but all in all i had a great stay at teh sheraton.

good location because we booked through hotwire we thought we were getting only one bed. the person on the phone for sheraton was rude but the people at the gateway were really nice and getting two beds was no problem. getting to and from the airport was great and getting the metro or santa monica buses near the hotel was easy.the beds were a bit hard and there was something up with the bathtub but overall a very nice hotel with great food.

good enough if you are in town to see several different areas of la, this location is relatively convenient. however, there is nowhere to walk from here for dining or entertainment purposes. the room was clean and spacious enough for our needs. the main restaurant serves a decent buffet breakfast but the items ordered off the menu leave a bit to be desired. staff was friendly but overall they seemed a bit short staffed. our key stopped working an hour and a half before check-out. this, in addition to the parking (an airport surface lot located behind the building where the nearest space you can find is sure to be the last one, approx. $13.00 per day) was the only complaint.

not very good at the kor. i was told kor, the cool and hip company behind the viceroy and tides, runs this behemoth of a hotel on century boulevard, so when business dictated a stay at lax, i booked the sheraton gateway.sadly, the kor style did not translate well to the sheraton factory. the hotel has a cool front desk (where none of the employees seem to know what kor is, by the way), but that's where it stops. the rest of the hotel is more herman munster than chic, with black and flannel gray making an already dark hotel positively lifeless. there are cavernous expanses without a single stick of furniture to break the monotony. the rooms are equally dark and the bathrooms very rundown. my bathtub had been chipped and painted over in at least 10 places. the bathroom tile was equally disgusting, as was the ubiquitous hair i found all over the sink and floor.shula's was a bit disappointing, although the burger was excellent as was the undercooked apple crisp, but the bar/lounge was very bad and had surly service. but all of these seemed excellent compared to the lousy breakfast restaurant where the buffet seemed like left-overs. i wouldn't stay here again.

thumping still in my head my wife and i stayed here over the 4th of july weekend. when we arrived on the 4th, music was blaring at the swimming pool and could be heard across the lobby. when we got to our room on the 8th floor, the room was facing the pool and we were dismayed to find that we could heard the music from up there. given that it was 4th of july, we thought...oh well, maybe this was a rare event and the manager had indicated that it'd be over at 8pm. the music kept going past 8pm and into 9pm. we didn't complain.sunday afternoon comes around and they threw another party at the pool and the music was just blaring again. when i asked, the manager said it'd be over at 7pm. at 7:15pm, the thumping was just too much, so i called the front desk to ask when the music would be over, the front desk said 8pm. i decided enough was enough and went down to change our room. the manager said, oh it'll be over by 7:30pm. i said you can't entertain partygoers at the expense of disrupting an entire side of the hotel! finally i got a new room facing the other way. i could hear the roar of the airplanes, but that was expected and i'd take that over the constant thumping any day.room wise, it was ok. the bed slumped in the center and the shower/tub is in need of a renewal. the caulking were moldy and the stainless steel bars had rust streaks running down into the tub.

convenient stayed here one night (from nh) before a cruise. very comfortable bed. restaurant was nice not too pricey (for la). rented a car to see some of la, definitely need one. no place close to walk here. use the valet parking. it's worth it.

nice room i love staying at sheraton hotels. this one was no different except for a few things: they do not tell you that you have to pay for parking (an extra$15/day, or valet for, i think $24). the parking lot was in the back of the hotel so it was pretty far. luckily, the weather was nice. the interiors of the hotel were very nice: a little gift shop, a starbucks, nice rooms...bathroom too! staff were nice. like always, my room key didn't work at one point and i had to go all the way downstairs to get it reloaded. the concierge person took the time do it for me instead of having to wait in the line with the people needing to check in. i did not like that sheraton would not let me add points to my rewards card though because i booked through hotwire. the hotel is also very close to the airport (they have a shuttle)...so i could definitely hear airplane noise...not so bad though. location wise, it was a pretty far drive to every where we had to go though. that sucked. l.a. traffic is bad.

good hotel very near the airport for anybody having a very early morning flight out of la this is a very good choice. the (free) shuttle ride to the airport is about 5 minutes and there is shuttle at least every 20 minutes.but coming in at lax i was confused by the way you board hotel shuttles. you have to go designated areas on the sidewalk and flag down the shuttle from your hotel.the hotel itself was clean and so was the room. nothing bad to say.

sheraton lax in june we enjoyed our stay at this hotel. we stayed for two weeks and paid $109/night through hotwire.com. at the time of booking, other comparable hotels were charging closer to $150/night.the amenities provided at the hotel meet the criteria of a 4-star hotel. there is an airport shuttle that runs 24 hours a day (there are multiple shuttles and the wait time is about 5-10 minutes). there are two restaurants in the hotel: the brasserie serves breakfast and lunch (on the expensive side-simple breakfast will run about $12-$14, $16 for the breakfast buffet), and shula's (steaks will run about $40). in addition, there is a starbucks which opens at 5:30am. there is a subway within 1 block which serves from 6:00am to 9pm. if you are renting a car, there are a number of restaurants within 2 miles. for a simple, inexpensive dining place (where the locals go), try dinah's on sepulveda blvd.tips:free coffee is stationed at the bar in the lounge. free tazo tea bags can be taken at the business office center on the 2nd floor. lemonade is served at 3:30pm in the lobby.if you have a car, parking is provided by an independent company towards the back of the hotel. cost is about $13/day. otherwise, the hotel offers valet parking.there is air traffic noise but this can be remedied by purchasing inexpensive ear plugs before you start your trip.the primary clientele of this hotel is conferences and airline pilots/stewardesses, and probably those of us who used hotline.com to book. there are relatively few children in the hotel.we contacted guest services twice during our stay, once for additional towels and once for a/c noise. both issues were handled immediately.all the staff we came in contact with were very courteous, friendly, and efficient. we would definitely stay here again.cons:no free parkingno free continental breakfastno free internetlimited storage space for clothingroom noise was only occassionally a problemair traffic noise can last through the night since this is an international airport.if you are not turned off by any of these issues, then you'll enjoy your stay here, as we did.
nice hotel but extra charges were annoying bedroom

clean and quiet stayed here during a 12-hour layover at lax. worth the cost for solid sleep, use of fitness center and a shower! i slept most of the time so i didn't explore the hotel but i will say my room was huge with a king bed and a queen sleeper sofa in a sitting area around the corner. very masculine decoration. bathroom was kind of small for such a big room, but had great water pressure and towels were thick and soft. fitness center opens to the pool and gets a nice breeze, and the equipment has tvs and fans for comfort. one strange thing is that the fitness center didn't have any dumbbells under 25 lbs. hmm. has a starbucks in the lobby, very convenient. shuttle to airport was very prompt. overall pleasant experience.

nasty extra charges the overall experience was very satisfactory, airport pickup was perfect, room was clean, the concierge was very helpful, but there was a $10.95 surcharge for in room internet and a charge of $ 2.00 per international calling card call. the telephone charge card in the room mentioned a $ 2.00 charge for the first 60 minutes and 10 cents/minute thereafter, but did not mention the $ 2.00 per call charge. i feel that a 4 star hotel should not need to nickel and dime it's guests in this way.

pleasently surprised i was concerned once i found out that i had got this hotel from hotwire. i read reviews on the hotel and i was afraid i had been had by the 4 star rating hotwire had given the sheraton.the checkin went smoothly and i was off to my room. the desk person promised me the room would be quietmy room is large, nicely appointed, and has a wonderful bed. the only downside was the tub, which had a bad refinishing job done to it at some point. there were a few hairs in the tub but more than likely they came from the room attendent. by the way the room was quiet except for a little airplane noise.downsides; to use the phone in the room is very expensive and the $10.95 for the internet is unacceptable in the day of free internet in most hotels.if you are looking for a nice room at a fair price for the location this is not a bad choice.

only stayed a night - very comfy bed! only stayed one night, but it was very nice. large comfortable bed. room was a little dingy, and the view wasn't amazing 0 but then its right next to an airport so what can one expect!?

not a 4-star. a dull 3-star. location was my first instinct, the sheraton was less than 5 miles from work for the week-end of memorial day. this particular need was fulfilled. however a very dull 3- star would be more fitting of a rating.there was never any hot water. granted , i enjoy a hot, hot shower. it was warm, yes but never hot. we showeredearly and late in the evening as well as middle afternoon, hot water temperature availability never changed : warm.the rooms were clean, on the small side for a sheraton.self park, a nice walk, good for the digestion, 10 to 15 mn, depending where you could find parking. there was a shuttle to lot, if you have the luxury of time. i was there on business.the keys had to be changed twice, they simply stopped working, back to the counter to be rekeyed.personnel helpful, friendly and professional. all around from luggage to front desk and all else. no where to eat truly. we had to tackle the long dark walk to the lot for dinner. perhaps for an away flight, this an adequate choice. a 3 -day business trip, no.too many inconveniences.

one night stay myself and a buddy were in palm springs for some golfing and stayed here for one night after dropping off the rental car. arrived and got checked in quickly. as a plat member i was upgraded to the club floor. arrived onto the club floor and floors were dirty and just the overall feel was not very clean. got to our room and found the colors very warm but dull ?? greys. maybe to hide the dirtiness - although the bed sheets seemed very clean the bathroom was in dire need of upgrades and repairs. for a club room this bathroom had mold all over the shower area; shower head coming out of the wall and the shower itself was so low that you had to bend down to have a proper shower ? checked out the club lounge for breaky......pretty lame and ended up going downstairs for breakfast. not a vending machine in the place or anywhere for that matter to get any munchies.......i was told if i was hungry to order room service ? i just wanted a bag of chips or something. had a few drinks in the lounge. no problems. not a bad place but definately not a place that sticks out in my mind. as a starwood member i think the next time i am in the area i will check out the westin down the street and see if it is any better.

wouldn't say it's quite 4 star first of all, i booked this hotel through hotwire and it was given a four star rating for this airport hotel. i had a four day stay in the los angeles area and wanted it close to the airport. once there i was informed of the $24 a day for valet parking or self park in the back of the hotel in an airport parking lot. which cost us roughly $13 a day to park and you had to walk a distance to get back to the hotel. i never saw the shuttle to take us back to the hotel. this was a bit of an inconvenience but nevertheless we had no choice. for the most part i had a decent experience. i was not in the hotel long enough to enjoy any of the amenities. check in went smoothly and the concierge was helpful. as far as the rooms go i was not really impressed (1063). it was a bit small.. outdated televisions, bathroom needs attention. it was small and, they seem to have problems with the tubs not being clean enough and chipping paint. otherwise it was and okay experience and i would visit again, but i wouldn't say it is quite a 4 star hotel, maybe 3.5.

walls very thin! all things started out well here at the sheraton gateway outside of the la airport. check-in was fine and when we requested a discount they provided one. when we got to the room it was nice. relatively clean and bed was comfortable. at this point we were quite pleased with the hotel. the problem began around 2am when the persons in the neighboring room returned. four young men who were obviously wanting to have a fun evening and were under the influence. i don't fault the young men for wanting to have a good time and being loud can be part of that. i do, however, expect the hotel walls to be thick enough to resist some sound. the walls were paper thin and it was as if the young men next door were in bed with us talking and laughing. things went from bad to worse when they started singing badly(at around 4:30am). i am glad they had a good time, but we did not. my wife and i are frequent travelers and are not very finiky, but we have stayed at motel 6's with thicker walls. we will not stay here ever again and will now avoid sheraton hotels in general.

a very nice 4-star airport hotel we found a nice, clean and well-appointed room, with a view on the runway, and excellent soundproofing. staff were pleasant and efficient. one negative: if you plug your computer, the bill goes up $11, and i did not see any warning. wifi is available in the lobby, free of charge.

good for what ii is stayed one night to start our vacation and another on the end of our vacation. rooms are not big but have been updated, althougth they didn't do complete job on the bathrooms.check in was easy.shuttle seemed to take longer to pick up on arrive, but it was at the end of a long day. we left at 5:30 am and shullte was waiting there.pool area looked great for an airport hotel.wouldn't suggest it for an extended stay but was good for an airport hotel.starbucks in the lobby was handy too!
discusting things growing in the tub friendly reception, room luxury, but discusting things growing in the tub. nasty bathroom.

convenient to airport, but inconsiderate we only needed a place to sleep for an overnight layover. the location was very convenient to lax, but finding the shuttle bus was ridiculous. after 20 minutes we hailed a cab only to discover it was just a few blocks away. when we checked in, we reiterated our request for a cot and were told it would be there in 15 minutes. an hour later, my daughter was fast asleep in our bed and we called down to cancel the cot. not a restful sleep at all.no one even bothered to apologize for the inconvenience.one weird thing that happened was the elevators had a mind of their own. there was a guy trapped on there with me who told me he stays in this hotel a few times a year and the elevators have been flakey like that every time he does.

not bad but inconsistent i wanted to update my previous review which was pretty good/neutral about this hotel. i have now stayed here quite a bit on business travel and would now say it's a bit inconsistent. first of all, if you can book with a starwood preferred number, you're going to get a better room. i neglected to do so a few times and ended up getting rooms that smelled like they had *just* been smoked in - floor 4 btw. i went down and asked for a different room and they've always been helpful and switched it immediately, while reminding me that it's a non-smoking hotel. if that's the case, then they have some serious fumigating to do in a couple rooms. i like this hotel - i'm sure most of the rooms are fine, they have good customer service and a great breakfast buffet in the morning - but i'm just saying...
somethings growing in the bathtub spot that was smeared by my toe. the white thing beside it was the towel i put down to take a sh

good for airport hotel on our way to hawaii, leaving nyc at night, we needed a place for a few hours at lax until we could catch the morning flight to honolulu.for $116, this wasn't a bad option and they have a good shuttle to and from the airport being so close.when we checked in, they were friendly and even upgraded us to a small suite. nice big room, but i cannot understand why they still had an old tv instead of a flat panel. the old tv was at an odd angle and distance from the bed and made watching in bed difficult.the only problem is that we got a room that connected next door, and at 1am, we had to call downstairs to have them call the guy to ask him to lower the tv (was watching some church sermon very loudly).otherwise, it was great for what we used it for.

great airport hotel stayed for one night in april 2008. check in was fast and friendly and my room on the 9th floor was great. i was originally in another room which had a noisy aircon and i was moved as soon as i called the front desk. the rooms are tastefully decorated and are very comfortable. the beds are fantastically comfortable. room service was quick. breakfast the nect morning was very good. the hotel deserves it's star rating, and my only complaint is the parking - you can either valet your car at enormous expense or park at a general airport parking lot behind the hotel, which isn't cheap either. people may feel uncomfortable walking around behind the hotel alone at night. would i stay there again? yes. it's a great hotel witn comfortable facilities.

excellent airport hotel we stayed at the sheraton gateway by lax in late march/08. the hotel shuttle is excellent. check-in was wonderful. we stayed on the club floor. the room was large and not to over-crowded with furniture. the lobby is nice and the outdoor pool is very nice. there's a free shuttle bus that takes you from the hotel to manhattan beach area (very nice area)...about a 20 minute ride.

far from a four star experience this hotel looses points for both service and room quality. i would not stay there again and would not recommend it to a friend.my assistant booked my room through hotwire and requested a 4 star hotel in west los angeles. i am familiar with the airport location but was hopeful that the sheraton would infact be a 4 star experience.the lobby is beautiful and the valets very nice. however, it took 20min to check in and there was only 1 person ahead of us. i was told that i couldn't record the stay on my starwood perfered account because it was booked through hotwire. the room was above a very noisy airconditioner unit. i figured that was probably what booking with hotwore is all about. but inspite of location, i would still expect a clean tastefully appointed room. unfortunately i recieved netiher.the bathroom was dirty with a severely chipped and stained bathtub. the room and bedding generally dinghy (579). i attempted to call the front desk after 15min of the phone ringing i was moved to another room (518) the second was dirtier than the first, dirty glasses, severely chipped, mildewed and rusted shower/tub combo, black hairs in the tub and on the toilet.unfortunately, i was late for a dinner reservation and could not wait anouther 40min to change rooms.

above average airport hotel we booked a standard room (room 957) for one night on the return leg of our journey home from new zealand to the uk. the room was spacious and very quiet though the bathroom wasn't that big. our one supper was in the hotels shula's 347 restaurant where the service and steaks were excellent. breakfast the following morning was in the brassiere restaurant which had a good value buffet continental breakfast with lots of choice.the hotel has quite a nice pool and terrace with plenty of sun beds and armchairs. staff throughout were very efficient and there always seemed to be plenty on duty. you could also catch a free bus nearby to take you to a shopping mall and beach at manhattan beach about 30 minutes away. finally, there was a regular (every 20 minutes) shuttle to the airport which was about 10 minutes away.

fabulous hotel this sheraton is right close to the airport - perfect for layovers - which is what it was for us. the beds are incredibly comfortable and the hotel itself is just really great - service, amenities, etc. there is a starbucks downstairs in the lobby, bliss bath products, plush towels and luxury bedding. a perfect spot for an overnight layover. the hotel shuttle was complementary and picked us up at 2am. i highly recommend this spot for layovers - not sure if the location is good for anything else but it was really great for us. i noticed a lot of conferences going on - seems like a good place for that too - esp because its so close to the airport. booked on hotwire and paid $135. well worth it.

service with a smile! what a great experience!the staff in the hotel were courteous, helpful and friendly. our room was very clean and well-appointed and we cannot praise the hotel and its staff enough. a couple of staff are worthy of special mention because their contribution to our stay helped make the difference.albert - the concierge - is worth his weight in gold if you're a tourist and don't know the area. nikki, who works in the bar, is a shining example of what a customer-facing employee should be. choosing the sheraton gateway was a trade-off fo us, as tourists. we needed somewhere close to the airport after an 11-hour flight but wanted to be fairly close to the 'touristy' places. we made the right decision and wouldn't hesitate to say there again.

we would stay again.... the sheraton gateway is a really rare airport hotel. very well maintained as opposed to some of the reviews i've read on trip advisor. our room was pretty clean, the hotel public space was pretty clean as well. one note, it took housekeeping at least two days to notice some nut shells in a public hallway on the 3rd floor. i actually thought that wasn't bad because i notice everything (other guests probably didn't even realize the shells were there) and that was the only housekeeping concern that i had in a public space. as far as the room goes my only issue was the comforter, it had a stain on it but i never use them anyway so i just took it off the bed but wanted to wait and see if housekeeping would notice it and replace it with a clean one. they didn't so on my 2nd night there i asked that it'd be replaced and they responded very quickly to this request and any others that i had. other areas like the hot tub needed to be cleaned as well and the elevators were very slow and probably needed to be serviced; experienced a situation where several guests including myself were stuck on the 1st floor because the doors did not shut properly, a guest had to pull the doors open to reset them. i never reported this incident. though we had some minor issues service was great, the restaurant was great, the room ultimately was very comfortable, beautiful decor and furnishings. i would stay again and more than likely will soon.my biggest problem with the sheraton gateway is parking...yes we've read this before, it is a headache. first off, we did choose to park valet the first day due to schedule constraints...it was just convenient at the time. on the next two days that we had a rental we chose the sheraton/lax lot behind the hotel. it was very inconveniently located. my husband had to shuttle back to the hotel after parking the car!! then, on the day we checked out i noticed we were charged for valet for 5 days instead of 1...we didn't even have a car on the last three days of our stay. i was very disappointed by that...but otherwise this hotel is still one of the best i've experienced at a priceline rate of $90/night for it's star-rating.

80% good, 20% not so good a got a wicked good deal on this hotel through priceline, so i really can't complain about too much.as far as the hotel, it is fairly modern and conveniently located to lax. the shuttle from lax was fast and the driver was very friendly. the room itself was pretty big and had updated decor, but the bathroom was small and in need of renovation. why would you update the room, but not the bathroom? i don't understand it. the enamel on the bathtub was peeling and you could barely close the door while using the toilet. i also expected the bed to be a little more comfortable ... that wasn't the case however.pros: very nice (and free) weight room, free wi-fi in the lobby, starbucks in lobby, shuttle bus to airport, location near lax.cons: elevators were slow and at one point was dropping people off on the wrong floor, $13 for offsite parking, expensive restaurants onsite (i walked to a marriott down the road just to get a cheaper meal at a sports bar), no retail establishments nearby (food or shopping), old 25 inch tvs.overall, i would stay at this property again. if they made some minor improvements it would go from a good place to stay to an excellent place to stay.
pretty decent airport hotel spent 3 nights in march. nice beds, modern decor with lots of black. loved the starbucks in the lobby.the bar - oh well... but staff always very friendly and attentive.

solid business hotel in a good location pros: free shuttle from lax to the hotel, very friendly and helpful staff, very quick room service, comfortable beds, reasonable rates.cons: dated bathroom (the shower head was only at my chin level!), fee for in-room internet.

wonderful night at the sheraton we flew into la late on saturday night, so we decided to spend the night at the sheraton to avoid drivng in the dark. we arrived at the airport, called the sheraton, got our luggage, walked outside and the shuttle pulled up. we got checked in right away and went up to our room. the beds were awesome - we used starpoints to stay here and it was a great night's sleep. there was not a lot of noise - i use ear plugs so you may be able to hear the planes - but i did not. in the morning, we got up and i went downstairs to check email on my laptop (it's free in the lobby) - there was tons of space to sit down and plug in and starbucks is in the hotel so that was an added benefit. we left and shuttled back to airport and picked up the shuttle for thrifty and headed out to pasadena.great hotel near the airport - clean and comfy.

convenient and modern! use the four points hotel phone number in the arrivals area to get put through to this hotel's main desk, so that the 10 minute shuttle can pick you up. the rooms are very modern and trendy, and the view is pretty good (although you're in an industrial airport area, so what can i say).amazingly quiet, considering that planes are flying overhead. breakfast buffet is a bit over priced, and the selection is only ok at best.

very poor for a sheraton service is awful, the elevators werenéˆ¥??› working, we never got attended on the bar. i was very sick and there wasnéˆ¥??› even a doctor available on the hotel. if you need to stay in lax, look somewhere else.
fantastic stay at the sheraton picture from century at night

shame about the parking stayed at this property from jan 26th - jan 29th and again on the night of feb 1st.this hotel is really nice except for a few small details, charging guests to park their cars is a little over the top when the car park (not the valet parking) is a 5 minute walk behind the hotel...not alot you might say, but when i stayed, the car park was almost full and i had to park at the furthest point from the entrance and then had to walk in very heavy rain to get to the hotel...and i got charged about éˆ§?3 per day for this privledge. its a public car park , but sheraton guests get a special rate...big deal!!!my room was excellent but the door lock (electronic) required attention and after i was told it was fixed, it still caused problems...like locking me out of my room each time.the hotels saving grace...the quick shuttle to the airport and the heavenly beds....wow, the best ever

ok stayed here for 2 nights due to location. it was ok, but not great. the room decor was modern, though it did not feel comfortable. there were many conferences going on, so the lobby was busy and noisy. and cold! the food at the bar and in the restaurant was average and a little pricey. front desk staff not knowledgeable about local info. parking fee was a little high, too, as was the internet fee. convenient to lax, but other than that, nothing to write home about.

surprisingly nice airport hotel this is a completely reasonable airport hotel. i was only in la overnight and would have preferred to stay in town, but the rate here was way more affordable. i went expecting the usually below-par airport hotel experience but was very surprised to find a large but fresh hotel. the room was great - very clean with an up to spec. sheraton bed. i had to sleep and was able to make the room 100% dark, but there was some airplane noise audible (granted i did ask for a good view of the southern-most runway).this is still an airport hotel, impersonal and surrounded by parking lots and other airport hotels, but it did provide a good night's sleep. i did have my starwood gold status recognized at check-in and was put in a preferred floor - but had no club access as am not a platinum.

fun memories my husband i stayed here for 1 night before departing via lax for an around-the-world honeymoon trip. we'd actually 1st met at the hotel 10 months earlier during a peace corps orientation before heading overseas for volunteer service. so we stayed more for the memory of it being where we first met, but it would be hard not to really enjoy the nice, clean furnishings and very comfortable accomodations.

it was alright... i had a friend from out of town that stayed at this hotel before flying out of lax. i came down for the night to visit and stayed with her. the room was clean, and that was probably the best part of the stay. the bed was quite hard, and neither of us got much sleep. the sleep we got was also disturbed by planes taking off and landing, which, i admit; is something you have to deal with staying by the airport. we also ate at shula 347, which was the restaurant in the hotel. the prices were reasonable, and the food was quite good. the service could have been a little more attentive; but overall it was a fine experience.overall, it was an okay experience; nothing to rave about, but nothing super exciting either.

enjoyed our stay excellent hotel near lax. got a room for $89 on priceline and it was a steal at that price. we had a late international flight and had to stay overnight in la. couldn't have picked a better hotel. right next to the airport. we were helped with our baggage both ways. the shuttle to the airport is frequent. rooms were nice and clean. room service was good although expensive like most hotels. even though its right next to the runway, there's no airplane sound. nice views of the runway, enjoyed watching the planes land and takeoff.

clean and family friendly we enjoyed our clean room and the wonderful service. we ordered room service and my two young children (4 and 6) had plenty of delicious options on the kid's menu. (for a great price)! also, the breakfast buffet the next morning was wonderful. they didn't even charge for the kids!!

one of the best bargains in la our corporate rate is 90/night for this hotel. given the rate one might think the place is a dump. nothing is further from the truth. the rooms are well furnished, some newer and nicer than others and the staff is excellent.one thing to note though, and this is not unique to just this sheraton, i'd say 80 percent of the time i find urine on the toilet seat upon check in.

boutique-quality hotel right by the airport the sheraton lax felt like a boutique hotel - interesting artwork in the lobby, amazing 1920s-ish furniture all around the public floors, lovely poolside area bar for late-night drinks, and extremely comfortable well-decorated guestrooms; so much nicer than i expected for an airport hotel (and free with starwood points!) transport from the hotel was quick and easy, and we knew we'd made an excellent choice when we saw pilots pouring into the hotel for a good night's sleep...

sheraton lax exceeded expectations we spent 3 nights at this hotel to visit family and friends in the south bay area. the location was very convenient for our purposes. we've stayed at sheraton properties quite often before, and have found them to be generally good, but not usually this good.our room, which i don't think was a special one, was quite spacious with excellent furnishings and a most comfy bed. i wasn't expecting such a large room and first cabin bed, given the price and airport location. all the staff members we encountered were friendly and helpful. there's a starbucks in the lobby, which was an impressively efficient operation in spite of serving a crush of customers every morning. what looked like a twenty minute line for coffee turned out to be a five minute wait at the most. kudos to them!in spite of being an extremely busy airport hotel the elevators were prompt and speedy even early in the morning when they often bog down at most hotels. i had occasion to use the fitness center and found the cardio equipment to be very good, the weight gear is just ok. the only real gripes we could think of was a $6 charge to use the lobby computers, a bit of a silly rip-off of paying guests needing to print a boarding pass. also, a little fridge in the room would be nice.the free shuttle to manhattan beach for shopping and beach stuff is a wonderful service.several times we stopped by the hotel just to freshen up between engagements and i had expected a hassle from the staff about parking in front for a few minutes. they had no problem with it, and i very much appreciated that. for overnight parking we used the self parking lot behind the hotel. that was reasonably priced for the airport and in a handy location, although the attendants (not sheraton people) were invariably rude and functioned at glacier speed, which is why we preferred to park in front for brief stop ins. we didn't eat at the hotel, so i can't comment on that. all in all, a fine choice at lax.one last recommendation: uncle bills in manhattan beach for breakfast. you will wait for a table, but it's a breakfast worth waiting for!

good airport hotel i only stayed here one night, but it was a good experience. i read some of the other reviews about the rooms needing an update, but my room was very modern and new (reminded me more of a w hotel) in the way it was decorated. i am a gold member, so maybe i got a newer, remodeled room? it was on the 12th floor. service was professional -- not overly friendly, but they got the job done. i mostly chose this hotel because of it's location close to the airport, but i would stay here again.

a lovely surprise for an airport hotel! arrived at the sheraton on a late night flight from the east coast and was very surprised because i had expected far less from an airport hotel. the rooms were extremely comfortable, well-decorated, and clean. and the staff was very helpful - when i was in desparate need of a bagel and cream cheese to accompany the starbucks coffee i had purchased in the lobby, the restaurant kindly boxed it up so that i could take it back to my room and get back to some pending work. small details but those are the things that compel an excellent' rating. i would absolutely stay here again - it was fantastic to arrive there in minutes from the hellish experience that is lax. this is the second recent sheraton stay that was a great pleasure - the chain is definitely doing something right!

convenient to lax, average accomodations you probably won't want to stay in this area unless you need easy access to lax, but even amongst the airport hotels this is a subpar choice.- feels more like a 3-star than 4-star property- tub was dirty - and when water was turned on, a gush of dirty brownwater gushed out- felt worn and unkemptpositive points:- bed is standard sheraton, good quality sheets- large number of rooms - decent size roomit's not completely disgusting, but there are other choices in the immediate area and even with the spg group, i prefer to stay at the westin lax which is just down the road

great hotel i stayed at this hotel recently and i had a great experience. i am a starwood gold member so i got the room free through points. at check-in, the employee wasn't too great or nice but did get the job done. i checked in very fast with no problems which i always enjoy. i especially liked the room that they put me in. there are 15 floors and i was on the 14th overlooking lax with a great view of the runways and the airport itself. the room was good size, the sheets, bathroom and everything was clean so i was very satisfied. the only dissatifcation i had was the desk. it was made of wood and there was a lot of chips on the top and the side which were very noticeable. just a little paint would make it look much better but that was just a minute detail. everything else was way above satisfactory. i strongly recommend you stay at the sheraton gateway los angeles. it is very close to lax and everything around and in los angeles.

needed a refurb about 10 years ago!! this was our second visit to the sheraton gateway and it was disappointing to see that it was no closer to feeling like a 21st century hotel, to me it's still stuck in the 80s and needs upgrading soon.check in agent was unhelpful verging on rude but at least this time we didn't get placed next to a family with energetic young children who screamed the place down at 6am!elevators were a lottery, worked okay on arrival, didn't work when going to and from work out room and worked when we checked out.room was a decent size, but no magnifying mirror in the bathroom and few accesible electrical sockets for those all important chargers for phones, ipods, cameras....wait for shuttle was about 15 mins the next morning.for $75 on priceline it's not a bad deal but i wouldn't like to have paid too much more.

decent but dated stopped in for one night with a room booked via my starpoints. nice and close to lax, fast, convenient shuttle, everything you'd really want for an airport hotel.rooms however do feel a bit dated - if you've stayed in various sheratons, you'll know that whilst the services are usually quite similar, the rooms can vary depending on how old the hotel is, and this was on the lower end of the scale. both room and bathroom showing signs of wear+tear, and could use a bit of a makeover. few lights etc not working in room, but no biggie.on a happier note, we did get upgraded to a suite (which wasn't much bigger than a room), and enjoyed a decent meal at the steakhouse on the ground floor which is pretty good.all in all, a decent airport stopover.

good but for the elevators! the sheraton gateway is a consistently good choice for a stay near to lax except for one thing: the elevators. on my most recent stay, none of the guest elevators were working upon check-in. all guests (and housekeepers, room service staff, bellmen, etc.) were being routed to a single service elevator in a utility room. the waits were very long, the elevators very crowded. the elevator problem persisted off and on throughout our stay. i asked a staff member how long this had been going on and he told me there have been elevator problems for several months. i know that any commercial establishment can suffer an elevator outage, but it concerns me that the problem here seems to be both extensive and chronic. in that this is a fifteen floor property, you may wish to call the hotel before booking to determine the current status of their elevator problems.that being said, it is worth checking on this hotel. it is very convenient to lax. the rooms are comfortable, quiet and well appointed. the beds are exceptionally comfortable. the housekeeping is excellent. the staff is hard-working, yet pleasant. this hotel is a good way to begin, end or transit a trip.i have stayed at the sheraton gateway quite a few times so i feel qualified to comment on its consistency. but i am also surprised at this most recent development with its elevators and hope that hotel management will address it more seriously.

any closer to the airport and you'd be under a plane! i arrived at la airport with no accommodation booked for a 20 hour layover and got on the sheraton shuttle bus thinking this was a hotel brand i can usually trust. as usual the sheraton lived up to its expected high standards.my mini suite was perfect. clean, spacious, crisp linen etc. the leather couch was perfect for an afternoon nap in front of the tv. i am actually surprised to read other reviews noting they found this pricey - i found it far cheaper than comparable accommodation and actually asked the receptionist if i had in fact heard the price right it seemed so cheap!the shuttle to the airport was literally minutes and i was assisted on and off both ends by the driver (always a worry getting luggage on and off when you are a female travelling solo).the only minor disappointment i will note is that room service is not 24 hours. being so close to an international airport i was more than a little annoyed i could not get a proper meal because it was 9am la time even though i had just gotten off a 15 hour flight from australia and desperately wanted something more substantial than a bagel!overall though i definitely recommend this place and will definitely stay here again in future.

comfortable beds......ahhhhhhhhhhhh hotel is very clean and neat. the view was fantastic. the price was right for a hotel like this ($110.00) per night. in fact i was surprised at the rate. the company i work for placed the reservation. the valet parking was very expensive $25 or you walk down an alley i did not like to a parking lot behind the hotel. they have air controlled air conditioning in the rooms i was not happy with because it just did not seem to cool off enough and it was very hot humid in la during my stay. breakfest was hot and on time 5:45 am, i couldn't believe that because hardly ever do you get your breakfest delivered by room service like it just came off the stove. the staff was super and the overall experiance other than the air was great!

near airport but pricey we stayed here on our last night as we wanted to be near to the airport. the hotel was pricey and the room were shabby . the only good point was the security to go to the rooms, ie without a room key the lift would not work. there is a shuttle bus to the airport

very nice airport hotel very nice considering it is an airport hotel. it is very clean and comfortable. and i am particular! the staff was very friendly and helpful. the room was large enough for three of us to be comfortable. the beds were comfortable the furnishings were good. the bathroom was a good size and clean. cable internet service in the rooms was $11 per day but wireless was free in the lobby. there is a business center but they charge for internet and printing boarding passes. the hotel was clean and luxurious. the pool was nice with comfortable lounge chairs and good service for food and drink. there was annoying music over the loud speakers though. the shuttle to and from the airport runs about every 10 minutes. the location is fine if you want to walk for exercise, not pleasant in terms of noise and traffic but safe. they offered us a 6 pm checkout for only $50, which was great because we had an 11 pm flight.

declining property first time i reviewed this property it was pretty good. this time, i think there are better options.desk chair does not raise and lower and had a cigarette burn. towles were still damp on the rack. no bath soap, only facial bars. club room had food but not set up on time. club room also over run by kids with no one trying to control them.self-parking has sheraton signage but is not part of the property so you cannot bill it to the room. paying for parking took ten minutes and four different signitures.as a platinum i was offered no upgrade despite a very empty hotel with lots of suites available.better than the westin accross the street, but there are better lax hotels.

parking situation i give this hotel a neutral. i stayed here in my recent trip to la. i find booking through spg.com or starwood phone very conveninent if you are an spg member, so i picked this one up because of location and price.the location is good, i stayed at other hotels at lax, nothing unusual here. rooms are ok sized, nicely furnished, positive sides of my stay.i had 2 issues with the room in my 2 days stay, one with the heater and the other one with the bathtub drainage, but it was taken careof, so it is ok. however, parking drama is another story. hotel only provides valet parking for $24 a day. or you park in the airport parking lots behind the hotel.(for $13). the problem here is, at night, you have to walk back to the front door from parking lot through some dark road, since all the side doors of the hotel are closed.very inconvenient. valet parking is not too good either, because of the crowds picking up their cars. i stayed at the radisson lax and also paid for parking there but at least, parking was closer.

very nice hotel i stayed at the sheraton for one night as i was passing through and found the hotel to be an excellent choice. i've stayed at numerous hotels at lax and found the sheraton be the superior hotel compared to the others next door. the room's were very clean, the staff was very friendly and the beds were very comfortable. i really enjoyed staying at the sheraton and would definitely recommend this hotel for anyone looking for an above average hotel.

pleasantly surprised we spent a night here between international flights.i wasn't expecting a great deal from an airport hotel but was pleasantly surprised. it's literally minutes from lax, probably one of the closest hotels and with acomp shuttle bus that goes very frequently. rooms large, quiet, clean and comfortable. the starbucks in the lobby is a genius idea and much appreciated!only criticism was that there was only one person on reception when we checked in which was somewhat annoying. have more reception staff: travellers relish quick check in and out! otherwise full points!

nice hotel; recently remodeled this hotel currently comes up with some of the best rates for upmarket properties in la -- true it's next to a runway at lax, but it was recently remodeled and the rooms are great -- for the price very very difficult to beat -- we also received complimentary club level (continental breakfast and snacks in p.m. but no complimentary drinks) upgrade for starwood alliance membership which is free. decor is muted grays, browns, and other earthtones -- very modern look in lobby. sweet sleeper beds are pretty nice but only doubles not queens in the rooms with two beds. request an airport view if you like to watch airplanes. other side of the hotel may be a bit quieter but we slept fine with the runway side. lounge off lobby is very nice as is the smallish pool which has free cabanas and teak chairs with cushions and lots of on site towels. not hard to forget you are at airport. we found location convenient for runs up to hollywood/santa monica and to other la sites -- didn't encounter airport traffic congestion as we'd feared. bathroom in hotel was spotless and housekeeping staff very efficient. parking is a bit strange but for a big city relatively cheap (around $10/day but basically a block walk or more to your car which you park in the airport's remote parking entered by a back entrance across street from hotel -- might have misgivings as a single woman needing to access or leave car late at night, but it looked well lit patroled and safe so maybe not a problem -- at least again it was cheap). no attractions or restaurants within walking distance other than inside other hotels. we were very pleased with our 4 night stay and would recommend this sheraton to others without qualification.

ok for sheraton stayed the night of 07/24 in room 1163. this hotel was your typical full service property. standard sheraton hospitality but for all that was touted on its website i felt under served. the rooms are not well insulated so you do here noise throughout the night as guests arrive and depart as is expected of an airport location. but one would think that this would have been better considered for this location.

excellent stay at the gateway usually i'd not stay at an airport hotel unless airport access was key (such as an overnight layover or a quick business trip in and out of town) but some family matters had me traveling to los angeles and having to make last-minute plans not only for a room for myself but also for a couple of relatives for an extended (4+ days) stay. i chose the sheraton gateway because lax would be an easy landmark for my relatives to find and lax is somewhat central to the entire l.a. area (and i'd be driving all over, from orange county to the valley to the high desert, santa monica and everywhere in between during my time in town).check-in was a breeze, and i was upgraded to a suite (thanks to spg status) that was extremely spacious. the entire hotel has received a rather recent upgrade, and the rooms are tastefully and quite well decorated with a modern feel. it had a large desk/workspace, sitting area with couch and two lounge chairs, king bed. only aspect of the new, updated rooms that i found lacking were the bathrooms. they're nice and all, but pretty small. your standard, hotel/motel-sized bathrooms. closet was also small, but there was plenty of dresser space so that wasn't an issue for me.wired and wirless highspeed for about $10/day. 24hr room service and just about everything i ordered while there was really good.the starbucks in the lobby was extremely convenient and great to have handy when heading out for long drives to various relatives' homes every morning. it closes pretty early though so it's no evening hangout place.24hr valet came in handy. the lobby bar was a relaxing place to hangout at night. maid service was attentive (i don't morning maid service and told them my first day there that 3pm was a good time for them to come clean, and they showed up at or shortly after 3pm every day while i was there!) and thorough.i never once heard a plane take off or land while there, though my room faced the airport. so either i got lucky or things were insulated quite well. proximity to the airport actually made for some real convenience, as freeways are very close (405 and 105). all in all, was quite pleased with the stay and the relatives i'd arranged a room for also were very pleased with the hotel.

nice hotel, not the ideal location i stayed at this hotel in march for a couple of days. the hotel is literally steps away from the airport. the hotel does a great job with their shuttle vans...i had no problem getting to/from the airport.the hotel and the room itself are pretty nice. my room was very clean and everything was working fine. the beds were very comfortable! housekeeping staff was friendly. the pool was a little cold (but then again..it was march)...the outdoor jacuzzi was nice, but had an almost unbearable chlorine smell...couldn't stay in there too long.my only real complaint about this hotel is the location! i did not opt to rent a car and was hoping that the bus/subway system would be sufficient to get me around (especially being from ny..i would think la would be just as good with their public transport). i was thoroughly surprised to find this was not true..it's almost impossible to get downtown or to hollywood on the buses/trains! you have to switch 2-3 times (on either bus or subway) and it took me well over an hour and a half one way. this was really disappointing and put a real damper on my trip. additionally..no one knew which buses/trains i should take...in fact everyone gave me a baffled look when i told them i was going to use public transport!also..there isn't that much to do. everyone told me to avoid the downtown/city area..so i did. hollywood can be covered in about an hour or two..and there is nothing else to do! i took the city tour and celebrity homes tour...both of which were good..nothing spectacular. many of the celebrity homes are behind walls..so i couldn't see some of the homes.the best part of my trip was santa monica! the beach/pier are great and shopping area/promenade are really really nice. highly recommend checking it out.

clean comfortable hotel near lax a clean, comfortable, near-luxury hotel with free shuttle service from lax. check in took longer than expected due to small staff and a customer at the front of the line having a complex issue. i was surprised that the front desk staff at such a large hotel was answering the phones as well.the room was nice, especially the beds. the one big disappointment given the overall quality of the hotel: the bathroom was poorly cleaned with gobs of hair leftover from the previous guest.the bar and restaurant were much more expensive than i'd expect for an airport hotel. a simple quesadilla, no drink ended up in a $15 tab. i'd expect this downtown or at a resort, but not out by the airport.

great hotel! stayed for 4 nights, great service, clean room, superior fitness facility, pool and hot tub. found the concierge to be helpful and overall, the hotel's atmosphere is very tastefully done. having a starbucks on the premises adds to it, the rooms are soundproof and it was conveniently located near a major highway. only drawback was getting your car from parking was time consuming.

terrible hotel first for the good: the room and beds were nice. now the rest. parking is far away, valet parking is $22 a day, and allow a half hour to get your car in the morning. breakfast is a ripoff, all a la carte and very expensive. i settled for a roll at the starbucks inside the hotel and even that is very expensive, almost five bucks for a cup of coffee and a roll. no entertainment at night, not even a piano bar, just this awful techno music playing all day and night and the depressing black and white decor. oh, and the high speed interenet. almost $11 a day and i got speeds that reminded me of my old 100 baud modem, when it worked. but it usually didn't, so i called and got connected to some overseas guy who had to tweak it for me. and i had to do this every day, it never worked twice.
above average airport hotel king bed

not bad, not good i have stayed there for about a month. the room is pretty clean. very expensive parking. staff not very nice except for housekeeping. pool only so, so. restaurant - nothing special. overall i am not very happy about my stay. the only positive is that they allow dogs in there. would tell others to look for some other place.

very good airport hotel although i only stayed one night at the sheraton gateway just a few days ago (early july), i was generally pleased with the hotel. it was much quieter than i expected, given its proximity to the airport and some of the reviews on this site. i did ask for a quiet room, but the rooms were well soundproofed anyway (with double pane windows that didn't open). i was also very happy with the air conditioning system--very quiet and adjustable to a specific half a degree. at many hotels, the a/c is too loud to sleep with it on, but not at this sheraton; i didn't even hear it going off and on during the night to keep the temperature at what i'd set it for, and i'm a light sleeper. the bed was quite comfortable with good quality sheets, although i was surprised the blanket didn't get covered with a separate sheet, as at most nicer hotels these days. and--my pet peeve at most hotels--the bottom sheet wasn't fitted so kept moving around during the night. the pillow choice was good, including foam or feather. the staff were friendly and the room was very clean. the room didn't have a refrigerator (or mini-bar), but they sent a small frig. up with no charge. shuttle service from the airport was great; i only had to wait a few minutes for it.the less positive aspects of this hotel: the bathroom was a little small and didn't have a wall mirror or lighted stand mirror as some hotels do, so it was a little hard to see close up in the big mirrors. my primary complaint, though, was that even in a non-smoking room, there was a vague smell of stale cigarette smoke--enough so that i had to buy some air deodorizer and also use a couple of scented candles. of course, i really shouldn't complain about anything, since i stayed for free with points from the starwood preferred guest program. but since one can get a good rate even through the hotel website, and given the airport convenience, quick shuttle, comfy bed, and hotel quietness, i'll definitely stay here again when i'm in la. maybe by then the sheraton chain will do what marriotts have done and go all non-smoking!

comfortable bed! we stayed overnight in june 2007 at this hotel and loved it. the bed is soooo comfortable! great pillows and bedding. the room was clean and comfortable. for being near the airport, i didn't hear much air traffic. i slept quite comfortably and was never disturbed by outside noise. the lobby is beautiful and the starbucks in the lobby was very convenient. we would definitely stay here again and we highly recommend it. you can't beat the price for the quality-it's as close to five star as you can get.

loved it! i could not be more pleased with the sheraton gateway. booked thru expedia, i got a $95/night rate. the bathrooms offered a full complement of lotions/gels/mouthwash as well as a full-length mirror and immaculate robe. a two-phone room, it featured a glass-topped writing desk and computer port, as well as a glass-top side table separating two generously proportioned club chairs. there were four lamps in the bedroom each w/a directional light switch so that one could lower the lights and still sleep. the room was well insulated and i couldn't hear the nearby airport at all. beds had two comforters and a blanket in addition to sheets. colors of room a restful gray complimented with a burnt orange bed backboard with navy pinstripe bed covers and club chairs.staff was exceptional to me and most helpful; oh, and the shuttle runs every 15 minutes -- very convenient for a hotel property 5 minutes from the airport. giftshop also well maintained. will definitely return!!

great airport hotel we booked the sheraton's park and fly package. with sunday arrival it was only $169 plus taxes for a room, and 7 days of valet, covered parking!i wasn't expecting a lot but the hotel was fine. quiet rooms, comfy beds and the starbucks in the lobby was a bonus.the rooms need some updating but are not horrible.the bar downstairs is surprisingly hip with a good vibe, menu and food.there is also a branch of shula's a higher end steakhouse.overall i would say an excellent choice for one night, but no longer. next time we depart early from lax we shall stay here.

poor service rooms ok, but air con not working, some of the staff could not have been more unhelpful if they had tried, especially one of the concierges. looking down his nose at some of the guests is not an appealing trait. hotel ok for an overnight, but not for a stay, which given the fact that it is next door to the airport might seem obvious, but the other hotels seem to have the noise under control.
sharaton a nice experiance w/great room service two chairs

great overnight-not extended this hotel is great for it's main purpose, which is flying into lax and staying one night and leaving. however, do not stay if you intend to stay a few days.1.) no free continental breakfast, you pay for a real breakfast2.) parking is $12 per day one block away! parking at the hotel is $24 per day!3.) no free internet access, that is $10.95however, look of the hotel and comfort is great. hotel food is great but expensive. my recommendation, stay 1 night flying thru la is okay....coming with a car whatsoever, do not stay here.

comfortable airport overnighter we arrived at the gateway rather late after a long and tiring plane journey from england.hotel looks nice from the outside and the check-in was extremely pleasant. we had been upgraded as we are platinum members so our room was better than average.we found the room quite large and pleasant but would not rave about it, however, it is built for people staying overnight and that it accomplished to perfection. the bed was very comfortable. the downside of the room was an extremely tiny bathroom. the room service snack was not very good. we could have had a meal downstairs in their steak house but we arrived when it was closing so cannot review on this restaurant. unfortunately, we had a very early start the following morning (5am) and were not able to have breakfast in their club lounge as it did not open until 6am.would we stay there again, probably as it did have the advantage of only being five minutes from the airport and overall was quite pleasant.

comfort and luxury i really enjoyed the modern lobby and room design. the beds were so comfortable and the business services really fit my needs.if you are staying in the lax area i would suggest you check out this property, especially if you can stay on the club level (great views of lax).

great airport hotel stayed in a junior suite. parking was very expensive and this hotel was right next to the airport. we did not hear any noise from planes and had a very comfortable sleep. not a great choice if you were vacationing and would be coming back/forth ... but perfect for an overnight stay.

disappointed was lured by the marketing. the website described a relaxing atmosphere with sophisticated cabanas and inviting oasis poolside. not the feeling i got. the cocktails were pricey, i was informed that happy hour was 1/2 priced drinks... the waitress/bar charged us full price and only corrected the price after we brought it to their attention. the price of our room included 2 free cocktails, which turned into confusion with the bar. if there was free breakfast/continental breakfast, there was no information of it. the restaurant was very pricey, we left for pizza rather than eat at the hotel. hotel is not kid friendly. not a place for kids. parking and checking in was hectic. checking out not any better-check your bill. small rooms in comparison. next time we'll stay at the embassy-one of our favorites!

very pleased with the sheraton gateway with an early morning flight out of lax, i decided to stay at thesheraton gateway. as soon as i walked in the door, i noticedthat the hotel has an upscale feel to it. check in went flawlessly,and the bellhop ushered us to our room. the beds were verycomfortable and the pillows were the same. we had an upperlevel room, which had a nice view of the airport. the next morning we took the hotel shuttles to the airport. the shuttles were prompt and ontime. i highly recommend this hotelfor any traveler who needs to be near the airport.

surprisingly nice for price and location the past three or four reviews have a theme that i'm going to echo -- i was delightfully surprised by the design of the remodel. i thought i was in a westin, not a sheraton and i certainly didn't expect that. the only reason i was staying there was because there weren't any rooms at the hotels i usually stayed at (westin or sheraton downtown). the service was great. the lobby glam. the only downside (or upside) is that it's right next to the airport. the planes didn't keep me up at night but i could hear them. if there's a reason that you need to be near lax (or on the west side of 405) this hotel is a good choice.

love the gatewat stayer here two different times in a week from april 13th-april 16 and again from april 21st to april 22nd. stayed at this hotel last year and loved it, so we stayed there again. our first stay we had a room on the 15th floor. the view was of the two runways, mainly 24l and r. the room was nice, a little bit of a different set up, the chair was against the inside bathroom wall,instead of against the window. the water pressure in the bathroom was low. we had access to the special room, where they had snacks available, as well as breakfast and dinner. the beds were awesome.our second stay we had a room on the 12th floor. what a difference. my key didn't work, so we had to make a trip back down to the front desk. the view was of the 25l and r runways and of the parking lot. there was somebody else's hair on the toilet,which was kinda weird, and the room didn't have the awesomeness the room on the 15th floor had. the water pressure was much better, still not great, but much better then it was on the 15th floor.the front desk staff the first stay were great, but the girl we had the second time around was pleasant, but not as friendly as the others. she wasn't all that friendly when we asked for a new key, and when we asked if a free breakfast came as part of the reservation, which we had gotten before, and she gave us one, although didn't seem to be very happy doing so. we did use the workout room our first time around and it great.our first stay only 2 of the 5 elevators were working, because a dance competition was using all the ballrooms and overloaded the elevators by a large amount. second time around it appeared that 3 or 4 were working, but were still very shaky and slow.the valet guys were awesome.will absolutely stay there again!

nice, if you can get it cheap enough this is the second time i stayed here. i was pretty happy the first time. like the first time, i booked through priceline (which calls this a 4-star hotel...that's awfully generous) for $80/night. the hotel seemed pretty busy when i checked in, so i guess they figured they could give a cheapskate priceline customer one of the handicapped rooms. i asked for a new room, but they said they had no regular rooms available...right. the quality of their handicapped rooms is just not the same as their regular rooms. in addition to the cheap features in the bathroom (the tile and curtains in the shower reminded me of my days living in the dorms), there was a stain on the curtains, a big chip in the veneer on the furniture (yup...veneer furniture), a huge nasty yellow stain on the desk chair (needless to say i didn't sit on it) and a stain on the carpet. the walls are paper thin -- i could hear phone conversations from the next room at normal volume through the wall.nevertheless, this place is a decent deal at about $75 per night...anything more and you'll probably be severly disappointed. total ripoff at their standard rates. definitely not a 4-star hotel.

great hotel! first of all this sheraton just completed a multi-million dollar renovation and it shows. the lobby and check-in area very open and modern. check-in was a breeze. the guest rooms feature the new sheraton beds, excellent work area and a very nice large chair by the window. i used the fitness center and i must say it is one of the best, each machine has its own flat-screen tv and everyone gets their own pair of headphones. it overlooks the outdoor pool area which has poolside cabanas, palm trees, and in the evening poolside cocktail service. there is a full-service starbucks just off the lobby and its a little oasis from the busy lobby. the airport shuttle is very frequent and depending on which terminal you can even walk. by far the best part of this hotel is the fact that you do not feel like you are right next to lax.

good hotel, but expected more from sheraton. would stay for same price. got a hotel for about $119 through my employer's travel agent. (rooms on web travel sites list $195). picked this hotel because of location (meeting across the street) and the price i paid. room was nice, but i expected more from a sheraton and especially if i would have paid full price. perhaps they give the nicer rooms to those who pay full price. never understand why these hotels nickel and dime you for internet access. it is extra. good choice for a hotel across from lax. free shuttle to the airport and a free shuttle to the $12 night parking (a bit of a walk if you don't want to wait for the shuttle. note: there are spaces reserved on near the entrance for the sheraton, but i did not see them until i had already parked and carried my 2 bags about 100 ft.

perfect for overnight stay before leaving got a great deal via hotwire. very clean and modern hotel and room. unloaded the family and luggage in the loading zone before returning my van to enterprise and getting dropped off back at the hotel. i didn't want the hassle of returning our vehicle or pay for guest parking. we just ate the food we bought from a take-out restaurant in la and slept in our room, then rushed out. i checked out by phone later. the room was quiet and of decent size. i would have liked more than the 10-15 or so tv channels, though. a small refrigerator would have been helpful too. we would have bought coffee at the downstair starbucks if we had time. the close location to the airport and shuttle every 10 minutes was very comforting for a quick departure for a morning flight. my wife was right: if we had stayed where we were previously in orange county, we would've ran into problems getting ready for and catching our flight. i'd definitely stay there again for an overnighter, but that's about it.
good gateway $129/night - nice room and decor. excellent service. had to catch a flight the next day, shuttle came very often. valet is $13. car rental places close by.
