good choice at lax booked this hotel on their website for a business trip. triple aaa rate was $119, which certainly seemed a better deal than something like priceline, given that i was guarenteed a no-smoking room.shuttle from terminal to the hotel came quickly, and got us to the hotel quickly.four of us booked separate rooms for the same meeting and we were all pleased. i asked for a quiet room when i booked, and when i checked in they noted my request and put me in an end room that was indeed very quiet. check in was very pleasant.the room was large (though bathroom was small to average in size), with nice, soothing colors and furnishings. very comfortable king bed with lots of pillows. the room was very clean. one minor rawback: there was high speed internet, but apparently not wireless (at least, i couldn't get my wireless to work but didn't try calling the desk to ask about it, since i was only there one night.)only one of us had a car; she used the valet which she said was only slightly more than the park yourself option.had dinner in shula's, and recommend it, even for those not staying at the hotel.i would definitely stay again at the triple aaa rate. one of the nicer options i've tried near lax.

best hotel by lax when flying out of lax anytime before noon i always try and make it down the night before so i can have a decent night's sleep and avoid having to deal with traffic in addition to getting to the airport on time. i stayed at this hotel about a month prior and they were still doing lots of renovations. this time, all renovations on the floor i was on were finished and very nice. i was given a complimentary upgrade upon check-in because the room type i reserved was full. the service was quick and pleasant and my room was nice. i enjoyed the fact that the air conditioning system actually got down to 65 degrees (most hotels only get down to 70 or 72 no matter what you've set it at). i also enjoyed the steak at their restaurant and drinks at the bar. my one complaint was the lazy service at the bar. they have outdoor tables set up but the cocktail waiters only come out to see if you're doing okay once every 2 hours it seemed. had they bothered to check on us more frequently we'd have spent more money and ordered more drinks. bed was comfortable, slept great - and the hotel shuttle the next morning was nice. the shuttle driver, however,has a chip on his shoulder and i get the feeling he thinks the world owes him something and he hates his job. so he wasn't so happy to assist. but other than that, i'd say this is the only nice place to stay at lax. the only other place i've tried was the raddisson which wasn't half as good as this.

fooled me twice!! the first time i stayed at this hotel, i resolved not to do so again. as luck would have it, we were paired up again on priceline.not much has changed since my last stay. still a very dark, modern-looking hotel with terrible soundproofing. the parking situation seems to have improved, perhaps because the lot was less crowded so i didn't have to walk as far. i knew not to get room service this time.that said, i had a much worse experience than before. why? they had no non-smoking rooms except on the club floor! i tried a smoking room once and the stench was awful. so i paid an extra $30 a night to stay on the top floor. the room was exactly the same. and although the woman at the desk was raving about the free breakfast, it was basically muffins and toast with some weak coffee. next time i will bid an extra $30 in a different area to try to avoid the sheraton, or just forget about priceline altogether. how this place gets four stars is still beyond me!

beware when using valet parking i took advantage of their park fly package and had change stolen from my car. it's not the end of the world and thankfully just change, but it creeps me out that they went thru my car.i've read on other sites that this has happend to others, so i tell fellow ta users to beware. (hotel has not responded to my issue either)the hotel is very nice, and the interior design a welcome change from the corporate look of so many lax hotels. it's almost like a w hotel.rooms have been remodeled too. however, still no safes.the hotel is good a recognizing spg elite members.shuttles to lax seems to run often enough.

buyer beware i was looking for a 4star, 2 rooms overnight, near lax, for my husband i, and my father and his companion, (in their 80's). priceline doesn't guarantee they type of room; i know that. you request the type of room at the time of booking, and i requested non-smoking rooms at the time. a few days before our stay, i followed up with a phone call to the hotel to reconfirm that non-smoking rooms were requested. 'gretchen' in reservations confimed this, and she did ensure our rooms were linked in the system (ie: across the hall)at no time was there any indication that we should be prepared for shoddy, worn out smelly rooms on the smoking floor (4th). . or that renovations were ongoing in the hallway outside our rooms. had i known in advance i could have made the decision to arrange another hotel and forfeited rooms at the sheraton.at check-in, the front desk clerk also failed to mention that were were going to the smoking floor, until she handed me the key cards and i asked her that the rooms would be smoke-free. she appeared not to care less as she condescendingly stated well .. you know you are [just] a priceline customer (interestingly i did pay a little more than the aaa rate customers a couple of postings back).my father's companion wanted to take a bath, but when she looked in the tub, there was hard plaster stuck on the bottom of it.the venting in their room only had cold air, and when the fan came on dust and hairballs blew from the grate like a string of tibetan prayer flags. there were dirty dishes from some previous occupant outside their room for our entire stay. the thin old blue houndstooth check carpet was full of bits of wallpaper and glue that clogged the wheels of my suitcase as i negotiated my way around workmen's pails and equipment on our way to the elevator in the morning.we did have dinner in the restaurant and it was very good. besides, the atmosphere was a welcome relief from our rooms.this stay wasn't just disappointing, it was a horrible experience.

very nice hotel this is a very nice property very close to the airport. we stayed overnight both going to and returning from tahiti. check-in was fast, the rooms are updated and modern in design with an extremely comfortable king bed. it has a good upscale steakhouse (shulass) as well as a general restaurant. it is within walking distance of other hotels that have branded restaurants as well. be careful when booking and don't trust the internet. they quoted $219 a night as the cheapest rate available. when i called, they repeated $219 but when i asked for the aaa rate, it was $119 without batting an eye. for someone looking for a first class hotel right by the ariport, i found it an excellent deal for an excellent hotel.

good airport hotel stayed here for 1 night.hotel: very un-sheraton looking. sleek modern on the inside. doormen did not offer to help with the bags but i guess we looked like we did not need assistance. they were pleasant though. the front desk was very helpful at check in and check out. nice pool area with whirlpool (had leaves in it) as well. there was a bar and 2 restaurants (1 am and 1 pm) and a starbucks. shuttle to the airport very early in the morning was spot on.room: very nice. horrible noise from the air con that the maintenance man fixed straight away. comfy bed. tv had some sound issues. i could not get the broadband to work but that was my computers fault. good size desk. very little outside noise noticed. usa today at the door in the morning. adequate bathroom facilites and good towels. this is a good choice if you need a hotel at lax.
ideal for a layover a very clean comfortable hotel, ideal for an airport layover. no noise from aircraft or roadway. very good value for the money.

a pleasant place to stay i booked the hotel through priceline.com at a resonable rate and i was blown away buy the customer service and pleasant atmosphere. the staff makes you feel welcomed. the rooms are very neat and clean. maid service is very excellent. i would definetly stay again. it's right near the airport. the only downfall is parking... but other than that its very nice to stay close to the airport.

nothing special my husband i spent one night at this hotel and choose it for it's location near lax. we arrived at about 9:30 pm and check-in took forever, even though there were just a few people in line. we had booked a club floor room, knowing that breakfast was offered on the floor beginning at 6am. our flight was due to leave at 8:55 am and we had to return a rental car first.upon taking the elevator up to the club floor, two other guests were complaining that their card to get to that floor hadn't worked the whole time they were there. my card worked on the elevator but not when i tried to get in my room!! i had to find a phone, call the front desk and then wait, and wait, and wait for a security guard to come and unlock the door. i ended up sitting on the floor next to the door for what seemed like forever (especially when you are tired!).the room itself was just okay. the bathroom was small. not what i expected for a club floor room. upon waking and hurrying to get some breakfast before our flight, we found the door locked and no sign of breakfast! (breakfast was listed as being offered from 6am to 9am everyday on the club floor). we called the front desk at 6:10am and were told that it was coming. finally, at about 6:30am, they opened the room and began to serve breakfast. we had to just grab a few things and go! not the relaxing breakfast that we had planned on!also, parking was a pain. the ramp for self-park was several blocks away and almost as expensive as valet.

comfortable accommodations - awkward building as requested, i was given a non-smoking room with a runway view. the room itself seems ideally outfitted for the business traveller - desk, internet, seating area, coffee maker, free shuttle to airport (every 15 minutes). my bed was big and outfitted with high quality linens and lots of pillows but the mattress was in bad condition. i didn't use the robe provided. their business centre closed early on the day i stayed there and since i had no laptop with me was unable to access internet. there was no obvious stairway connecting the lobby level to the business/conference room level on flight above; i felt lazy but took the elevator to go up and down one flight.dinner in the shula steakhouse restaurant was a relaxing but definitely upscale experience. a caesar salad and their award-winning hamburger cost me $22 before tax and tip. it's a good thing the service and food were excellent! at the street corner outside the hotel, visitors can access a free hourly shuttle service to the manhattan beach area and mall - handy for those of us with time to fill and no cars.i do have to agree with other reviewers on the points about hotel staff service. they don't seem to be stressing warmth and welcoming attitudes.

relaxing airport stay my partner and i spent an evening at the sheraton gateway before a next day flight to new zealand. customer service by everyone from the front desk to the hotel restaurant was friendly and efficient. the continuous airport shuttle was frequent and reliable. our room was spacious (though the bathroom was comparatively small) with modern furnishings, very comfortable bed, and an entertaining view of the lax runways.the overall feel of the public areas was like...an airport! the lobby and adjoining lounge were modern in design--clean, cool lines, but had little or no soundproofing. in the evening, the lounge pulsated with techno music and lots of twenty-somethings were drinking the night away. the noise level made it impossible to talk and relax. we arrived at the hotel late in the evening after flying in from portland, or and wanted to have a glass of wine before trying to sleep. we decided to take our wine back up to the room where relaxation was more likely.the fitness center is excellent with up-to-date and well maintained equipment. the room looks out over the pool area, which is nicely landscaped. when sitting by the pool, you can almost forget you're steps away from lax. only the roar of jets taking off and landing keep you in the moment.overall, if staying at lax is appropriate for your travel plans, the sheraton gateway makes a great choice!

very clean this hotel was very nice but very snobby,my grandsons had gone down to the pool,they were 17 and 14 and was told by someone (prob. someones body guard) that they couldn't touch the side of the pool and could not come near these 4 people (the only other ones in the pool) nor talk to them,don't know who they were but no one's that important.my daughter was right behind them and they wern't doing anything but this guy just kept on them.we arrived around 9:00pm and nothing was open,we hadn't had supper yet. i was sure glad we were only going to be there that night and only did so because it was at the airport.as far as looks and cleanness goes,i would give it a 5 star but as far as staff and help goes,it only deserves a 4 or maybe even a 3.the staff was also very snobby and not helpful at all.
room with a runway view! our room

nice, reliable business hotel, close to lax stayed at this hotel for business for 4 nights - sat - wed. room is basic sheraton but comfortable, beds were wonderful. bathroom is ok, not the nicest, but got the jobs done! starwood lounge was nicely appointed, with free internet access, fax, and printer. the breakfast spread looked good, but did not partake. the afternoon snack always had sandwiches, cheese crackers, veggie dip, and a hot pasta dish. also free sodas and bottled water (cash bar for beer liquor) and fresh whole fruit (banana, apple, oranges). perfectly serviceable for a snack before a late dinner. bar in lobby was great, plenty of bartenders so you didn't have to wait too long to be served, also table service if you didn't want to sit at the bar. you can also bring drinks to sit poolside (very lovely).schulers restaurant is a good, basic steakhouse. stick to the steaks, and skip the best burger in la. overall, was a pleasant stay for 4 days of business.

very nice hotel. better than expected we booked on hotwire and gt a good price, but after reading the reviews, i was afraid we had made a mistake.boy, was i wrong. we checked in late (10pm) and the check in was efficient and the room we had asked for was ready. room was much better than expected, modern and very clean. in fact, i stayed at a 5 star resort recently that had more amenities but this room was much nicer. if you are looking for a nice place to stay close to lax, this place would be hard to beat.one tip. if you want to pay for valet parking, its expensive. if you don't mind walking, park in the self parking in back and save $10-15. they offer an in and out rate for hotel guests, but if you just need to park and leave the car there, don't mention you are a hotel guest and pay even less.

fabulous, contemporary hotel this hotel was fantastic! i was bummed we only stayed one night. we booked this hotel because we wanted to make sure to get to the airport early the next day. this hotel is super close to the terminal. the hotel shuttle leaves every 10 minutes and the ride is only about 2 minutes. the staff was very friendly. we drove up in our rental car and the valet let us park the car there temporarily while we checked in to the hotel and took our bags up to our room. the hotel room looked exactly like the photo, same color scheme, mirrors, beds, etc. the room was large for two queen beds. there were down comforters on each bed with four pillows. we had a great view of the pool below so we could see when it was empty. we went down and soaked in the hot tub for about an hour since nobody was around. the pool area is very clean and upscale with double chaise lounges with thick cushions to lay on. the pool was heated but not as much as we would have liked so we stayed in the hot tub. there were lots of lounge chairs and cabana's to enjoy. a few people were dining inside the cabana's enjoying some privacy and the great outdoor setting. we would definitely stay here again since we got a great rate at $89/night (saturday night) through hotwire.

horrible hotel very bad service, forced me to stay in smoking room despite that they had a nonsmoking available and stated that the manager is out on the weekend and can not help me. they stated that my rate of $150 a night gives me only a smoking room and the nonsmoking rooms are reserved for higher rate, despite that they are standard rooms. very nasty hotel with horrible manners. this is the first time i have a had a bad hotel experience. enjoy your trip somewhere else.

better than i expected i booked one night for the end of a california road trip before departing lax, and received a very good rate via my company's travel site. i dropped our rental car off at avis, and walked to the hotel (about 8 blocks). my daughters and i loved our room - simple but luxurious bedding, nice bath, great night view, and quiet. but the best part was the room service meal. the sheraton offers room service for free if it's not delivered within thirty minutes; ours was at our door in 22 minutes. pretty good in such a large hotel! and it was nice and hot, beautifully displayed and delicious!

exactly what you should expect what you would expect from a sheraton. clean rooms, ok check-in, no problem, but nothing memorable. nice if you can get a deal, like on priceline or hotwire, otherwise may be a bit expensive.

good as a priceline option this hotel is worth it for the priceline deal of about $85. i wouldnt be overly impressed if id paid the full rate though. the rooms, like most airport hotels are showing signs of ageing. although the beds are very comfortable. the bathroom is very small. for a layover or just a good nights sleep after a long flight this hotel is fine. although dont consider anything near lax for your vacation.
nice but expensive view from the hotel room (top floor)

a bit less than average! stayed here on a stopover between london and sydney on june 7th 2006. the hotel is close to the airport with a free shuttle every 15 minutes, so i guess you could say that it is convenient. the beds and bedding are nice too - after that i'm struggling to find anything good to say. the check in process was painfully slow - not what you need after a long flight. there was no offer of assistance with baggage or directions given to the room. the bedroom was very disappointing small and dark- but probably not as poor as the club lounge which turned out to be a small sitting room with a coffee machine in it!bathroom amenities were meagre, no separate shower but a half size bath with shower tap over. having paid a reasonable amount for this executive room we were very disappointed and would not trouble this hotel with our custom in the future.

gateway to mediocrity first of all, we booked our room on hotwire, who guaranteed us a 3.5 star hotel. after arriving, i was told i could have a king / smoking or 2 queens / non-smoking, but my preferred king/non-smoking was not available, so 2 qs it was.the bathroom's toilet dispenser was nearly falling off the wall - the tub in the shower looked like someone had spilled acid in the base of it. the coffee pot didn't work and needed to be replaced, as did a light bulb and the tv remote batteries.obviously they reserve this room for their special hotwire customers!now to the service we received here: the breakfast restaurant was fine, very cheerful, prompt, and the food was good. $40 for breakfast was a bit much, but it was our first day, so we weren't quibbling. later that afternoon we tried to get a drink and food at one of the lounge tables, but with only one entirely inadequate cocktail waitress on a saturday afternoon, we finally had to go to the bar to pay $20 for a vodka martini and a virgin bloody mary. yikes! when we finally got our food, it was good, however - one of the best quesadillas i've ever had.the next night we ate at shula's 347, thbe beautiful hotel steakhouse. now, it was a sunday night - not busy at all - and there were diners interspersed throughout the restaurant, but nobody sitting too close to anybody else. we were sat at a table for two in an otherwise deserted part of the restaurant - deserted, that is, until the hostess sat a man with his 5 year old daughter right next to us and then promptly seated a single guy who must have gotten his lobster eating technique from darryl hannah in splash - yes, he crunched his way through the tail, then spit the shell out on the plate. granted, his dining habit wasn't the hostesses fault, nor was the whining 5 year old, but her placement in a sparsely populated restaurant left much to be desired.so while dad and the kid worked thier way through $5 of mac n cheese, our $140 meal was ruined. it doesn't take much brains or training to spread the groupings around. the waitress forgot the wine, the bus person wanted to take our plates every five minutes, even when we weren't done. the food was good - very good, in fact. such a shame their customer service left us with a bad taste in our mouths.oh, and then there was the $50 room service breakfast of lox and english muffins (not a bagel, as the menu said) and a $12 croissant and cup of coffee. one shouldn't expect to get off cheaply on room service, but when you're paying those kind of prices, one should expect the order to be right and adequately substantial.$21 a day for valet parking was a bit much as well. but hey - the maid did a great job cleaning the brokedown palace!we'll never stay here again.

mediocre this is an adequate hotel. its advantages are its friendly, can-do staff and its convenient location. although the building is in good repair for the most part, the public spaces on the main floor are big, empty, and anonymous: all the charm of an empty barn. the rooms are middle-of-the-pack functional. the good news is that mine was comfortable, well-equipped, and recently redecorated. on the other hand, water pressure was a problem, and hot water was in short supply some of the time. along with several other people on my floor, i could never get a swipe card that reliably opened my door. tried several different cards, but ended up unable to enter my own room on more than one occasion.unless you want to use room service, the only on-site restaurant for dinner is a pretentious steak house where the waiters have airs, the food is only middling good, and the prices are steep.do not waste money on the club floor. the amenities in the club lounge are very, very modest -- nothing like the generous food and stylish furniture available in the club lounge at the nearby renaissance.this is on balance an ok hotel. the hot water and room-key problems i encountered were serious, but probably fixable. but nothing about this hotel rises above the ordinary, and to me it has no warmth whatsoever. the nearby renaissance is far better.

got off to a bad start... i was looking last minute for my husband and i to stay prior to an early morning departure out of lax. i decided to give hotwire a try after not finding anything cheaper than $159/night - especially last minute. i found out that we were booked at this hotel and was excited after hearing so many great reviews. it was approximately $125/night (including taxes,etc.). also, my husband is a starwood preferred guest, so i assumed that things would go well. i called the hotel prior after booking to find out what kind of room we had, and that front desk said that we were booked in a non-smoking king room. the night of our arrival, we were exhausted from last minute travel preparations. we got to the front desk and i hate to say it, but felt like we were treated like second class. first of all, the boy at the front desk told us that we could not received spg points because we booked through a third party provider. i was okay with that, knowing that we did get a lower rate. he then questioned us on how much we got the room for and told us that was a really good rate for that hotel. i told him that i called the hotel and we were told we had a non-smoking king room. he then said that we were not down for that type of room and that we were lied to and that they always say that. he said that he didn't know who we talked to, but they just say that. he then acted like he was doing us a huge favor by giving us the non smoking king. we then asked about parking validation or payment and he said that the hotel doesn't have self parking, only valet; but that the hotel just happens to be affliated with the parking lot in back. he said that if we are hotel guests, it would be $13.00/day parking rate. however, if i wasn't staying at the hotel, it is a $10.00/day rate. he then chided us, saying that next time, we should look at sheraton's web site and that we could have gotten a better park and fly rate, and that it really wasn't that expensive. by this point, i was so disappointed that he had decided to make us feel cheap and not worth staying there. i really was scared that our vacation was going to get off to a bad start. the room was great, couldn't hear a thing, but i was glad to get out of there the next morning. we left our car in the parking lot for convenience sake, and after returning from our vacation, didn't mention the sheraton.

disappointing we just returned from a combination business/family trip to california and stayed the last night near lax due to early departure. we booked and paid in advance for a room at the sheraton. our room reservation was downgraded (no of beds). this was not disclosed at check-in. when questioned, the reason given was that room was booked thru expedia. i was offered a rollaway bed - free of charge for my inconvenience. i was required to call the front desk 2 more times to get the bed delivered and twice more with an one hour's wait to get pillows. if that weren't enough there was a dead roach in the shower.i also had a similar experience at a sheraton in boston last fall. i will not be staying in anymore sheraton hotels.

as good as the prior reviews the sheraton gateway has strong review on trip advisor and i found out that it is worthy of the ratings that other travelers have given it.i had a very large room, an awesome corporate rate of $100 a night and it was very quiet, i couldn't hear the planes at all.the bed was comfortable, although i thought the raves on prior postings were a little extreme. it was nice, but certainly not the best ever.the best ever? their workout facility was the best i've seen in a hotel in some time. completely the opposite of the nasty little room at the nashville sheraton. only complaint is the price of room service food, which i suppose is a reflection of la. i got around that by going downstairs to starbuck's and picking up sandwiches down there. lunch sandwiches are $12-14 and when you add in a drink, taxes and tip you're going to be looking at $25 in a heartbeat.all in all, a very solid hotel!

great stay - loved the bed. we just returned for our california trip and spent one night at lax due to our late arrival. we booked the sheraton and were not disappointed. they upgraded us to a suite that could have entertained 50 of your closest friends. someone below mentioned the beds...they were the best...even after 3 nights at the st. regis, this sheraton beat them hands down on bed comfort. very convenient and a great stay.

very nice stayed here for three nights 27th apr - 30th apr 2006 and found this to be a very nice hotel. rooms were large, clean and comfortable. found the staff helpful. used starbucks which was handy to have in the hotel and the staff were always friendly. ate at shulas and the food was good. thought the prices were comparable if not better than a lot of airport hotels i have stayed in around the world. didn't find the noise a problem, we were on 6th floor, not sure if this makes a difference? used the self parking which cost $14 a day and found this acceptable. the area was manned and well lit at night. you can walk back to the hotel, maybe takes 2-3 mins or wait for the courtesy bus back to the hotel.airport bus service is very good and runs every 10-15 mins 24hours a day. the drivers were always pleasant and took our cases on and off the bus. did not have any negative experiences whilst staying here.would definitely stay here again.

omg the bed i only stayed one night but i will remember the bed forever. wow. lax is only a 5-10 minute shuttle ride away but the room was very quiet. another plus, the shuttle is free. and the breakfast buffet was excellent. only one problem, the table in the room was not bolted onto the base. a very wobbly concern. called the front desk to let them know about the problem but nothing happened... again i was only there for one night, slept like a baby.

if this is the best they can do, i'm not impressed i expected better from sheraton but i guess airport hotels care less about regular customers. we were pushed into a smoking room and the reception desk was reluctant to give us a non-smoking room as requested when booking (they did with little grace). while the room was clean enough, the bathroom could do with some attention - the shower handle came off in my hand. service was indifferent - ordered breakfast for two from room service and got only one (the second one came twenty minutes later). the only thing that worked well was the restaurant. there are plenty of hotels to choose from at lax, the sheraton is no longer on my list.

loved this place i stayed here in march of 2006 while returning from my honeymoon if fiji. the hotel staff was wonderful and the hotel upgraded us to a junior suite. the staff was some of the best that i have ever dealt with. the hotel is close to the airport and runs a free shuttle from and to the airport. this was nice especially the day that we were flying out. the junior suite was large and the bed was the most comfortable of all the beds that i slept on during my trip. this is a great hotel with an excellent staff.

if for the bed alone.. my new husband and i stayed here for the last two days of our exotic honeymoon. after traveling in the south pacific, we were just looking for something nice to finish off our trip. i must say that while we truly enjoy luxury hotels, sheraton is quickly becoming a favorite of ours if for it's 'heavenly bed' alone. these beds are amazing!! the hotel is nice, but the rooms are quite comfortable, the beds as i already said are amazing, and the concierge at this hotel in particular is truly par none!! he knew us by name from the first day and always had things 'just so' for us. truly exceptional! not only that, but i must say that the management of this particular hotel is very professional! we selected this hotel on priceline and yet when they knew we were staying there as part of our honeymoon, they quickly upgraded us to a junior suite at no charge. this was a very pleasant surprise and we were quite impressed. overall i would say very nice hotel, very convenient to the airport, and very professional!

i'll go to the crown point plaza down the street next time!!! after staying at the crown point plaza down the street i will not be staying at the sheraton gateway ever again! the used silverware and dirty napkins laying in the hall during the majority of my stay should have been my first clue about the quality and upkeep of this overated hotel. after using the phone to make toll free calls we were informed that toll free is not so toll free at the sheraton gateway. at $2.00 a call (whether you connect or not) it gets expensive to make toll free calls. i can understand charging for long distance...at approx. $10 a minute i will use my cell phone instead...after speaking to management (rude management of course) they informed us that toll free was not complimentary (even though they failed to label it on the phone). the management acted as though $2.00 isn't much but when i asked for $2.00 of his own personal money he acted as though i was asking for his life. i am not worried about the $2.00, but the fact that a supposed reputable hotel did not label items (which at other hotels are complimentary) that cost money is what bothers me. if they would have cleaned the room a little better i probably wouldn't have been in such a mood either. after looking at pictures from other reviews i have concluded that this was not just a hit and miss thing. i can't wait to check into the crown point or any other quality hotel in the vicinity the next time i am in l.a.
a 4* stay at a 2* price. comfy king bed

best hotel in lax area the sheraton lax is my favorite airport area hotel in la. i connect to asia frequently via lax and spend overnights at this hotel. it is recently renovated, spotlessly clean and has excellent room service.the only irritating point is the lack of mini-bars in the room.they treat their starwood preferred guest platinum members very well and i have always been upgraded to a suite upon arrival.the shuttle service from lax to the hotel and back never takes more than 15 minutes. the sheraton lax is very close to the airport. super convenient and a real pleasure. much better than the westin lax airport which i have found to be older, more dated and has smaller suites.highly recommended for those lax overnights!

great location next to lax if you arrive after a long distance flight at lax the sheraton gateway is a wonderful choice. we paid for a room with starwood points and upgraded for $50 to a suite with view on the runway!the hotel pool area is just wonderful for an airport hotel, same is true for the restaurant and bar not to mention the starbucks. parking is easy in case you doné?“t want to pick-up your rental car the next day. very enjoyable place to stay the night before or afterwards! the room was big and very quiet.

nice, clean, friendly hotel stayed here one night with my son on dec 27. we picked this hotel only because of it's proximity to lax because he loves flying and watching aircraft land and take off. in fact, we specifically requested a room with a view of the air traffic. the receptionist was very friendly and put us in room on the 10th floor facing north. the room was decorated in a modern style and very clean. it was not very big, but certainly not small. the beds were soft and the bath room was nice with plenty of towels. the workout area has about 10 cardiovascular machines, each with it's own tv screen. the bar is comfortable. the pool was about 80 degrees and comfortable. we moved to a different room after i walked around and found that the view to the south (which has more traffic noise...but not enough to disturb you) had a better view of the airport. the receptionist was very friendly and helpful in finding a room with a southern view. overall, i'd stay again (especially via the priceline price i got.) parking is a bit steep at $13.50 overnight.

clean, friendly and convenient the sheraton gateway hotel at los angeles airport was not bad. i was traveling with my husband and we checked in, got a smoking room (smoking rooms are available on the 4th floor only) and was fast and friendly. i found the room to be clean and comfortable; however, the window does not open and was dirty. the only real negative issue i found was that telephone access charge. pretty ridiculous. i would not recommend using the telephone in the room unless you want to pay $30.00 for a local telephone call that was under a minute of use. the parking situation could be better, but i felt the walk none the less could not have hurt us any. if you are staying as a guest at the sheraton, parking is $10.00/per day. shula's 347 restaurant in the hotel was just fabulous not to mention very convenient. i would more than likely stay at this hotel again when in los angeles.

good hotel right by the airport stayed at the sheraton for 1 night to split up a akl to lhr plane journey.booked 2 rooms for ?‹¢67 each inc tax. a real bargain!we got the hotel at around 11.30am due to the arrival time of the aircraft from nz. myself and my work colleague decided to try our luck to see if there were any rooms available.we were first told that there were only smoking rooms avaialble. i asked if we could take a look at them to see how bad they smelt. i was informed we couldn't.we were then offered 2 disabled rooms. the only difference being that they didn't have a tub, just a lrge shower.after a 12 hour flight all we needed was a bed! we took these.the rooms were on the 12th floor overlooking lax.rooms were superb.there is some noise from aircraft, but it's an airport hotel!! i'm a light sleeper and it didn't keep me awake.the hotel bar is ok. very dark!checked out at 12pm. by 12.02 we were at the gate at terminal 2!all in all, a superb choice for a lay over.

decent and well decorated hotel, comfortable, new, but a little noisy this hotel has been remodeled and the rooms/lobby look modern and nice. the room was clean and we had a view of the airport, which we liked, but was noisy at night. you can hear the planes even with the ac/fan on. the starbucks to be opened on the lobby floor is a plus. however, the hotel charges $12 for parking i think.

nice remodel, fantastic beds, nicest hotel at lax! the new sheraton gateway, after an extensive lobby overhaul, the addition of the overpriced but above-average shula's, and room renovation (but not the bathrooms) is a pleasant place to stay. like many reviewers state, it's a bit cold - check the pics - greys, blues, and black. while it's a modern feel that looks contemporary, it doesn't feel welcoming, but that will change once you try the new beds, the best part of the renovation. the pool area is fine, small, shaded, andclose to the runways (only the radisson sits closer), but you won't hear much noise from the room. this hotel is a good deal if you're not looking for a warm feel and can spend between $70-100 through hotwire or lastminutetravel. also, be aware - parking is a nightmare, valet is good but expensive, and street spots are non-existent. the sheraton's the newest remodel in the area at the 4 star level, far nicer than the westin, marriot, or crowne plaza.

a great stay we stayed here as part of a conference deal and really enjoyed our visit. the shuttle from the airport was prompt and easy to find. we arrived before midday after a very long and tiring flight from sydney and were afraid we'd have to wait for our room. check in was quick and staff were very couteous. the room was ready straight away. we had a lovely room over looking the pool area and the airport runways. there was very little noise for a hotel so close to such a busy airport. the room was very tastefully furnished and very clean.the concierge(s) was very helpful and would go out of his way to give good advice. he even advised us that we could buy tickets to the dodgers' game on the internet far cheaper than he could get them for us. the hotel shop had a good range of essentials and some of their souveniers were cheaper than in the downtown stores. my son and husband spent a lot of time at the pool area. the pool was clean and the hot tub was also well maintained. there were always staff on hand to replenish towels and generally keep an eye on everything. the towels were large grey and white striped beach towels which was a very nice touch. we did not eat at shulas but did use the bar menu to eat by the pool. the menu was limited but the food was good as was the food ordered from room service. the room service staff were delightful. we did not eat at the sushi bar either as we are not huge fans but it seemed popular. breakfast from the buffet was good and plentiful and we felt it was very reasonably priced.this hotel is located a long way from anywhere except the airport which is a disadvantage for a long stay as cab fares are horrendous - $45 one way to dodgers' stadium. a car would have been helpful and we would rent one if we were staying for the same period of time next time. however, bus fares are cheap and a ride to santa monica or long beach is $1.50 round trip. a trip to downtown la will cost $3.00 for an all day pass. the bus station is 5 minutes walk behind the hotel. make sure you have the exact money.we also found that it was easy to walk up sepulveda ave to the shops - about 20 minutes walk - or the bus will take you there also. there are quite a few cafes, department stores and supermarkets there.we also got wise and checked out the neighbouring hotels for more food choices. if you are desperate, there is a subway outlet next door and other fast food outlets close by.my only gripe with this fine hotel was that when i ordered a cup of tea by the pool, i was charged $4.00 for a very small pot of semi boiling water and a tea bag!we stayed at a neighbouring hotel on our night before returning to australia, and believe me, the sheraton wins hands down. everything at the sheraton is professional and we were always treated with the utmost respect.a tip:if you are clastophobic as i am, elevators are always a bother. the elevator doors at the sheraton gateway are slow at opening, so don't panic!

hotel very nice we stayed here the last night of our california vacation. when we arrived about 9 p.m. the clerk said she had no clean double non-smoking rooms available, so she upgraded us to a suite. the room was spacious and clean and remodeled. asked for more towels, they came right away. breakfast buffet the next day was one of the more reasonably priced hotel buffets ($15 for adults and $6.50 for kids) and very very good, both hot and cold. we were very satisfied with this room

mostly nice surprises booked this through priceline for $55, so my expectations weren't unrealistic. the room was surprisingly nice, in cool grey tones. had the sheraton sweet sleeper bed, and new bedding and carpet. the bathroom was standard, updated decor, but appeared to be original bathtub/shower. did not use the parking, but the airport shuttle was prompt and efficient. had time in the morning to look around a little, and i must say that the pool area is as nice as any i've seen at an airport hotel. the only unpleasant surprise was a problem at shula's with bugs floating in my cocktail. apparently they had gotten into the liquor bottle. the restaurant manager was apologetic, and took appropriate action to remedy the situation.

hardly a 4-star the first rude awakening was that the valet parking was full. i was forced to park in the hotel's off-site parking lot, where they charge more for hotel guests with in and out priveleges ($13/day) than someone not staying at the hotel ($11/day). you'd think they'd give their hotel guests a break. since i am a woman and i was travelling by myself, i didn't relish having to hike back to the hotel late at night from the parking lot. they have a shuttle from the parking lot to the hotel, but you still have to sit at the shuttle stop for quite a while until the shuttle comes. the second night i stayed, the valet parking was also full.the reception check-in was extremely rude. i had purchased the hotel stay on priceline and this proved that internet-paying guests are treated poorly. he said he couldn't guarantee a non-smoking room since i had booked through the internet. i told him that there was no way i could have a smoking room since 1) i'm allergic to smoke and 2) i'm 4 months pregnant. he happened to have two non-smoking rooms left.when i arrived at the room, the carpets were damp as if they had just been cleaned. when i called to complain, they said they'd send someone up to dry them. housekeeping came up with a tiny fan that was meant to somehow dry the entire room of its damp floors. i told them i didn't think that would work and asked if they could just set down towels.i ordered room service and both the woman who took my order and the delivery man were very friendly and professional. after the bad experience i had so far, i really appreciated it.the room was clean, but definitely no-frills. very few amenities -- not even bottled water in the room or a mini bar. the bathroom was looking very worn -- cracks in the tub and the the sink did not drain well.the next morning i had breakfast at the brasserie. the service was very good.besides their food service, this hotel should make a lot of improvements before it can call itself a 4-star hotel.

good stay at the airport! we enjoyed our stay at the sheraton gateway. large, clean rooms and the beds were very comfortable. they were the best beds during our 21-day round trip.the only negative i can say about this hotel is the parking situation. they have no self parking lot, only valet. they have no check in parking available, so you have to carry your luggage from the nearby airport parking lot or discuss with the valet parking personal to get 5 minutes to unload.the whirlpool also wasn't very good. so, choose this hotel as an airport hotel for the night before or after your flight, for that it couldn't be better. but it is not a resort-like hotel to stay more than a few days.all in all, it was a good experience and i recommend it.

great airport hotel booked through priceline for $85/night. rooms are large and very clean. beds are fantastic! free shuttle to and from airport is convenient. this hotel is one of the closest to airport terminals, so not ideal if our planning on staying in la for a while, but for a good nights sleep after a long flight this is a great choice.

exceeded our expectations and would stay there again i booked 3 nights through hotwire for my husband and me and wound up with a non-smoking king room on the top floor directly across from the sheraton club lounge (temporarily located in the presidential suite). our room was $51 per night (plus tax) and allowed us access to the continental breakfast and lunch buffet in the lounge, even though we are not club members. free internet use in the lounge. also free newspaper delivered outside our door. the top floor was accessible on the elevator with a special room key. check-in service and concierge assistance were both top-notch. room was kept clean and bed was comfy. we could see lax runways from our room, but noise (either external or from within the building) was never a problem. we dined at shula's twice. excellent food and service, albeit pricey. hotel shuttle service was prompt and always reliable. our experience exceeded our expectations, especially considering what we paid.

i'll stay here again from the very courteous valet attendants to the complimentary sunday newspaper at my doorstep, my stay was perfect. the room decor was very nice, the beds were extremely comfortable, with minimal noise from airlplanes overhead. the rates were just right. especially for the weekend. i'll definitely make sheraton gateway my first choice when i visit los angeles again.

close to airport positive remarks1 stayed at the sheraton one night in july, great that its only 10 minutes from the airport on the shuttle bus. 2 the rooms were clean and we got a very comfortable super king bed. negative remarks 1 we didn't hear much plane noise, however we could hear the people next door and their tv. we were exhausted after our 10.5 hour flight so would have expected better sound proofing from this highly rated hotel.2 the bathroom's toilet roll holder was coming off the wall.3 shular 357 is over priced - $10 for a bottle of sparkling mineral water! 4 receptionist not very friendly/helpful as she insisted on taking my hotel voucher and only after my insistence would she give me a photo copy.

good, but could be better one walk through the facility and you would say this place gets a 5 star review, but upon further review there were little problems that kept adding up, which ultimately resulted in me giving it 4 stars. the parking here is a nightmare, valet is expensive and although self parking is cheaper (13 dollars per day) it is annoying. many times we grabbed the last or next to the last spot. there were several times when there was a long line waiting to get out and the situation became disorganized. another problem is housekeeping, it took them forever to do our room, it was 1:30 in the afternoon and it still wasn't done. the elevators were broken during our time there, it wasn't that bad of a problem for us because we were on the third floor, but it could become a big problem for someone on a higher floor. another thing i didn't like about this place was that the shower head was too low and i nearly hit my head on it a couple of times and i'm only 5-6. the bed was incredibly comfortable and the pool area was very good as well. what's good is you can order drinks and take them out by the pool. the pool tended to get crowded in the afternoon.the room service food was good and i also liked the bar there too. one thing about room service that i really liked was it is 24 hours, which is great when you are looking for something to eat at midnight. shula's was expensive but the steak was good. i heard the planes a couple of times but it was nothing that was distracting.

we can give you a bed for only $50 more! i booked my reservation on priceline a few hours before arriving at the hotel. when i arrived i was told that the hotel was sold out. i could either have a room with a sofabed or i could pay $50 more for a room with a bed. despite explaining to the front desk clerk that this was totally unaceptable she refused to budge and was less than pleasant. upon return i spoke to priceline and they refunded my money.

wonderful stay we stayed at the gateway for 4 night attending a family reunion. i have nothing but great things to say about this hotel. got a special rate of $99.00 per night, loved the decor, slept like a baby on the sweet sleeper and the staff was really friendly. spent the most relaxing day out by the pool with margarita in hand after most of the guest checked out on sunday. the food at the hotel restaurants was really good but overpriced. my only complaint was the parking fee $20.00 valet but the valet service was excellent. the cheaper lots around the hotel don't have in-and-out access, so you have to pay each time you leave. i would definitely stay at this hotel again.

better than expected first stay since the renovation. has a nice, almost w type vibe to it, and the staff was very nice (sending faxes for me for free after the business center closed). much more than i expected for a sheraton, and for any hotel near lax. if you want a vacation hotel, you probably don't want to lounge at the pool with planes wizzing by all day. but if you want a convenient business hotel with good amenities, great location (minutes to santa monica, lax of course, etc.) you can do much worse.

i don't think so! i'm tired just thinking about our stay at the sheraton this past weekend. slept awful, the bed was on the nicer side, but there was a problem with our room, a high-pitched whine was coming from the temp console that made you feel like you had a really, really bad inner ear problem. the engineers who came were pleasant but couldn't fix the problem. the hotel was booked solid and we couldn't be moved to another room, which is unfortunate, but understandable. the three of us slept, such as we could, with pillows sandwiched between our ears. other complaints: the tub drained super slow, what i would expect from motel 6, not the sheraton. the toilet handle had a tendency to get stuck. and, we could hear every noise from the adjacent rooms, and the sound of running down the hallway the floor above, well past midnight. you can hear everything! thin walls, who are these tripadvisors saying the rooms are soundproof, they are so not!upon checkout the next morning, we told the front desk about our wretched night's sleep and she said sorry and reassured us they would look into it, which you know, that isn't the point, that the next people in the room the following night are going to sleep fine, bewildering response.---we wanted compensation for staying in the night in a room that was not of the same quality as the other rooms, surely you should not have to pay full price! she was not rude, but she wasn't very warm or helpful either. we finally spoke to the manager, who in the end, gave us a free room in the form of equivalent number of starwood points, for the next time we stay at a sheraton, but it will not be the sheraton gateway. one huge benefit was the next morning, when we awoke and were megagroggy, asking my boyfriend for an extra large cup of very strong coffee, and he promptly went down to the starbucks in the lobby and brought it back to the hotel room. so if you have no choice but to stay here and don't sleep well, there's always caffeine to get you through the next day.

very depressing hotel. having read all the reviews before booking i was very disappointed with this hotel.considering the price range i expected more from this very ordinary sheraton.pick up and delivery shuttle was punctual.lobby area is very dark and depressing, as is there choice of furniture.the two dining options run to starbucks at the bottom of the range to shulas at the other end. so you either have a $3 danish or a $40 steak.unfortunately apart from a subways there are no walking options ouside the hotel.rooms were functional but not sheraton standard.no in room safe, mini bar, etc. beds and linens were great. room furniture was minimal and spartan. bathrooms small and dated.pool area that another reviewer called 'resort like', i would hate to see the resorts that he is vacationing at.pool was shaded and dark, on the small side, no atmosphere.overall a 'nothing experience' staying here. functional but not inspiring. similar experience to an interstate motel, you get a bed for the night, but forget the hotel as soon as you leave.

great option near the airport! we spent two nights here in june, on the first and last days of a weeklong trip. we actually booked the room through priceline for $100 a night, which was a great deal! the hotel has been very recently renovated, and as a previous reviewer stated, it is indeed éˆ¥?¸?urprisingly cooléˆ¥? thereéˆ¥??? a starbucks in the lobby, which is very convenient for that early morning caffeine fix. overall, i would definitely recommend this hotel if you need to stay by the airport.rooms a as starwood gold members, we hoped for an upgrade, but there were none available. however, the standard guestrooms were actually quite nice. they are not large, but well decorated and very comfortable. standard starwood heavenly beds, but with a dark blue duvet instead of the usual stark white. the rooms look exactly like the ones shown on the website, which is rare! the windows are triple paned, and we did not hear so much as a whisper of a plane taking off or landing. both rooms we had overlooked the pool, though, so i canéˆ¥??› say how the noise would be on the other side of the building.service athe valets were quick, the bellmen did not complain one bit about the insane amount of luggage we had with us, and the woman who checked us in both nights was very quick and courteous. our wakeup calls came right on time, which is always goodéˆ¥?“¨ am always surprised at how many hotels canéˆ¥??› seem to get this right!bar a we came here for dinner and drinks both nights, and enjoyed it. the mojitos were great, and the food is pretty impressive (taste-wise) for bar fare. the first night we ordered nachos for an appetizer, which were so enormous we didnéˆ¥??› need any dinner! donéˆ¥??› remember what else we ordered, but it was all good. the service is fast and generally friendly, and it is nice to be able to take your drinks and wander out by the pool to relax on a cushy chaise lounge é£¦?business center a the woman working at the desk in here was very helpful and friendly, and they seemed to have anything a business traveler could possibly need. free coffee, too!pool a there are lots of lounge chairs, and well as padded benches and several cabanas. you can get bar service out here as well, which is nice. we saw several planes fly overhead, but somehow could just barely hear them!
excellent hotel this was an excellent hotel. really comfortable beds and classy decor. only one complaint and that was the restaurant was very pricey.

very nice hotel hotel was recently remodeled. have stayed here in the past and the remodel makes it very hip and cool. the decor was modern with an asian flair. the bed is sooooo comfortable. service was nice. it's like they're trying to emulate a w hotel.drawbacks...though newly remodeled, bathroom overall needs work. tub is old, toilet is situated very close to the tub. sink did not have an effective stopper.

we enjoyed our stay! we stayed here on our way to and from australia. we called for shuttle pickup and it arrived within 10 minutes both times. although the hotel was very busy, we were greeted by very pleasant reception staff. we were upgraded to a suite both times. the suite had a very soft and comfortable king bed and a sofa that turned out into a bed. we requested a rollaway and received one very quickly. my family of four was very comfortable in our spacious room. we loved the view of the airport and watching the planes land and take off. i don't remember noise from the airport but i did hear people walking in the hall and heard voices near the connecting doors in our suite. no big deal though! the hotel has a heated outdoor pool, great fitness center, starbucks (that was open on our return) and a restaurant. the convenience of the hotel to the airport is great! if you have time, you can even take the shuttle back to the airport and have lunch or dinner at the encounter restaurant.

wonderful overnight stay we stayed here our honeymoon night before flying out the next day and had a wonderful stay. we never knew the airport was right next door! we did not have to wait more than 5 minutes for the pick up and drop off to and from the airport. the only down fall was that the restaurants were packed and we had to wait 30 mintues for our take out from a restaurant downstairs. however, we would definitely stay here again for a lay over!

dont waste your money on the parknfly package! we stayed at the sheraton gateway for one night at the end of may prior to a very early flight and opted to park our car at the hotel as part of the parknfly package. if you need a good night's sleep, as we did, you wonéˆ¥??› get it here. the windows are extremely thin for a hotel so close to the airport éˆ¥?you will hear the planes taking off and landing at all hours. when we boarded the shuttle in the morning, the driver spoke only limited english and could not understand which airline (united) we were flying on and was therefore very confused about where to drop us off. the worst part however was the pick up. when we arrived at lax from our flight home, we waited for more than 45 minutes for a shuttle to come by éˆ¥?nothing! then when a shuttle did come by it stayed three lanes away from the pickup curb and sped by, not even looking to see if anyone was waving and wanted to be picked up. in the end, we were forced to take a cab to the sheraton to pick up our car. when we arrived at the hotel and explained what happened, the acted as if a 45 minute wait was normal and laughed at us for being upset about it, including the parking manager. only one solitary bellman offered us an apology. in short, youéˆ¥??‡ be better off staying somewhere else, especially if your time is valuable to you.

poolside cabanas and now - shula's steakhouse? i am a starwood frequent guest member and have stayed at the westin lax before. what took me by surprise at the sheraton gateway was the vacation feel of the poolside cabanas - did not expect that from an airport hotel... now, they opened shula's steakhouse and are completing a fully-blown starbucks shop. well, with the brand new rooms, a cool poolside and now - shula's, i really do not feel penalized by my laover stays at the lax anymore. in fact, for the value you get at the sheraton, i would not mind going out of my way to stay there.
what a surprise! this hotel is at the airport?!? this hotel should be in west hollywood it's so cool! i can't tell enough people about it. what a surprise.

surprisingly cool i was in the midst of various business trips in and out of la, so i decided to stay at sheraton gateway because i needed a convenient place to stay. not only was i blown away by the service and people but by the design! i felt like i was on a real vacation at times when i had opportunities to relax on my own by the pool or having dinner inside, etc. i highly recommend this hotel.

great hotel option for lax parking! i stayed at this hotel the night before an early flight to hawaii. i was given a great rate which included valet parking for the week i was in hawaii. it was very convenient to be able to stay in a fabulous room and take the hotel shuttle to the airport the next morning. the bed was the best hotel bed iéˆ¥???e ever slept in and the rooms are very comfortable and furnished quite tastefully. i have no hesitation recommending this hotel!

great hotel, period! stayed here for one night april 15 as i missed my flight to honolulu due to my procrastination and traffic on the freeway. hotel was recommended by the airline. this hotel is one the best hotels i have stayed at. rooms are big, clean and quiet. the staff were very friendly and accomodating. the shuttle to the terminals runs every 15 minutes and the drivers are equally professional and efficient. i definitely would recommend this hotel to anyone.

nice hotel... a bit of confusion upon check-out! i got a good deal for this 4-star hotel on priceline, and was excited to see what a 4-star is all about. (i'm generally a budget traveller.) i checked in and found the room quite nice, the bed comfy. the bathroom was clean but the tub drained very slowly. very good soundproofing: no airplane noise at all!next morning it was almost time for my friend to pick me up, so i packed my things and used the tv check-out system, then sat and waited for her. i sat for an hour and a half, figuring she was stuck in traffic, before i went to the lobby to use the payphone to call her. (using the tv check-out disallows using the room phones, etc.) turns out she had been right on time. she asked for my room in the lobby, but the lobby staff, seeing that i had apparently checked out using the tv screen, told her that there was no way i could possibly be in my room. they didn't try to call up or make an attempt to check if i were there. a bit more creative thinking on their part - the tv check-out system is the hotel's idea, after all - would have saved us both a lot of aggravation. all in all, a good night's sleep at a reasonable price - but i'm not sure i get what all the fuss is about a 4-star hotel.

this place is a winner wow. what a surprise to find such a nice hotel at lax - and a real bargain to boot. i paid $99 for a terrific room (my corporate rate plus starwood preferred guest), which had obviously been renovated recently. what a great job they did! really beautiful, rich colors, even the carpeting was cool. the bathroom was quite clean and simple, nothing fancy. the front desk staff was very friendly and helpful, as were the concierge, the valet parking guys and the waiters at breakfast downstairs. this place is truly a winner - will definitely stay here next time i am in la, as it is very convenient to santa monica and the marina, yet a lot less expensive.it is a nicer hotel than some of the westins i have stayed at.

nice and clean room me and my husband stayed at this hotel for one night in april of 2005 and we loved the decoration of this hotel. lobby was nice and room was clean and neat. had brakfast buffet at the restaurant on the first floor (overlooking the pool area). buffet was about $14.00 per person...it was ok...they let you look around the buffet area before you decide to eat so you can decide for yourself.

great bed i stayed at the sheraton gateway on a one night stopover in march. i checked in at 11.00am and chose to upgrade to a suite for a large discount and was able to go straight to my room, which was great after a flight from new zealand. the staff were all courteous and helpful and the room was great. what made my stay however was the bed. it was the most comfortable bed i have ever slept in and i had the best nights sleep i have ever had in a hotel.

sheraton gateway #1 excellent 1 night stay at this cool hotel. most impressed with restaurants, excited for the new shula's 347 that should be opening in april. i will definately come back and stay here again. awesome beds!!!

great hotel - but parking is a long way off we stayed here for the last day of our vacation - which meant we had to bring everything to the hotel room in order to pack. (including carrying everything backt to the car...) the parking lot is (if you have a lot of stuff and a lot of bags) very far away. you have to cross a street and circle around the hotel (as the postern to the meeting facilies is closed at night). the room is really great - big, nice and very clean with in-room coffeemaker. (just the bed is way too soft. you really sink into it - i had to do some exercise in the morning to uncramp my spine.)hotel staff is very friendly, too. (even if you arrive in dirty hiking clothes.)

great value, excellent service usually, i do not prefer to stay at airport hotels. but the deal i saw on one of these internet sites was one that i could not refuse. hotel lobby is immaculate. the guest services agents were professional, friendly (usually uncommon at airport properties) and exceptional! i had one problem with the key to my room, and when i returned to front desk, the clerk handled it very professionally and apologized. the room was spotless and the bathroom was very clean. the only thing to bring up is the fact that there was only one hangar in the closet. it seemed that when i slept on the bed, that i was on a cloud. wake-up service was very easy. morning paper and express check-out receipts were placed underneath my door by 4:15am. that is very important to business travelers like myself. and there was coffee at the reception area made available to all guests. this hotel underwent a renovation and i must say that it went very well. i did not have the opportunity to try their restaurant and room service, though. i will be returning to this starwood property. this is a jewel close to lax and i will be recommending this hotel to all of my colleagues. great value and, above all, exceptional customer service. well done, sheraton gateway lax!

like a cruise, but on land! stayed here for one night layover on way home from cambodia feb. 5, 2005. made decision based on 1/2 mile proximity to airport, free shuttle and trip advisor reviews. well-appointed clean rooms, with modern style of bedding and furnishings. great service at pool area. attendant rolled chaise into sun for me, gave me table for my drink in a gracious way more typical of a high quality cruise. quite good food in the hotel restaurant. excellent value for money--$89 plus tax per night with aarp card. one thing missing is car rental on site. but can walk down to radisson nearby and rent car there. would stay here again.

a happy accident we were put into this hotel by ba when our aircraft developed a mechanical problem and the return flight to london had to be delayed until the next day. in every way the sheraton gateway was better than the holiday inn at lax where we spent the first night of our recent holiday. the lobby staff were efficient, the food and service in the restaurant were good and our room was great. we will definitely consider returning to this hotel when we stay at lax again.

had an issue - they responded! i stayed at this property quite by accident on the night that the los angeles air traffic center had it's meltdown - back in mid-september. all flights were cancelled, and i found myself stuck in los angeles. i called several hotels and they were either full, or exorbitantly expensive. i booked the sheraton on starwood points, and considered myself lucky. the check-in and check-out were a bit hairy, and crew-oriented (as another poster noted), and the platinum level upgrade had to be drug out of them. however, once inside the room, i could find nothing amiss. the heavenly beds are just that --- the rooms were impeccably clean ... and there was nothing but peace and tranquility around. upon returning home, i voiced my concerns to mr. michael miner, the manager. he was duly concerned, and invited me back the next time i was to be in la. generally, when staying in la, i don't need to be near the airport - but my wife and i took him up on his invitation, and from the reception, it was clear that my comments had been taken to heart, and that mr. miner truly wanted our business back. well done!i highly recommend this property.

i love this hotel spent one night at the sheraton gateway before flying out the next morning. beautiful hotel; great amenities and an amazingly comfortable bed. i felt truly relaxed in my hotel room. morning newspaper and in-room coffee was great. ate at the restaurant in the hotel as there was quite a rainstorm outside and did not want to go out. also, after a long day of travel, just wanted to relax. dinner at restaurant was a wee bit questionable, (service a little shaky). however, breakfast buffet was great. the concierge personnel were also quite nice. overall, i would definitely stay here again whenever i have a layover at lax.
