great service for a moderate sized group this january 2006 my husband and i got married on a cruise and stayed at the holiday inn port of miami with our 50 guests the night before. the hotel staff was efficient with check in and check-out, and went out of their way to help us with special accomodations at the last minute. the hotel even posted our wedding on their bulletin board in the lobby. the rooms were clean and the concierge was helpful. the bayside marketplace offers a variety of shops and restuarants, though the hotel does have its own restaurant. our party did eat breakfast at the hotel. it was just okay and the price was a bit high for the selection offered at the buffet. it was very comfortable and convenient though. overall, our entire group's experience was amazing and we would definitely stay at this hotel again. it is perfect if you are going on a cruise, however be mindful that the hotel does not provide shuttle service to and from the airport or the port for cruises. still it is only a few minutes and dollars away by taxi.

good place! my husband i stayed here for one night before going on a cruise. it is located across from bayside marketplace, which was great in giving us something to do. our room was clean comfortable. we had a nice view too! staff was very friendly. we did have breakfast in the dinning room in the morning, it was only luke warm but ok. i would definately stay here again.

great value, great location my husband and i stayed at this hotel before departing on a cruise. we redeemed a free night from the priorty club which holiday inn participates. this hotel is about 15 miles from the miami airport which is not bad in a taxi. we shared the ride with another couple and it cost about $24 ($12 apiece). we arrived before check in and the hotel was able to stow our bags. they provided luggage tags and gave us tags to match. they placed the luggage in a secured room. we went across the street where there is the bayside mall. we were able to listen to free music at the pier and have our pick of many places to eat like hard rock cafe and bubba gumps. if you go to the hard rock and are a aaa member you can get 10% food and t-shirts. they have boats where you can take a 1.5 hour boat ride to see the sights. i think it was about 15 a person. we got back to the hotel at noon, which was still early for check in and we were able to get a room. we were informed that my husband was chosen for the priorty club member of the day and we were upgraded to a suite. the suite was located on the 5th floor on the corner so we had a great view of the cruise ship pier and the bayside mall. the room was tastefully decorated and it was clean. the king sized bed was comfortable enough. there was a safe in the closet and the ac worked fine. there was a seperate sitting area with an additional tv and telephone. a microwave, fridge and coffee maker. they provided popcorn, bottled water and coffee at no charge. my only complaint about the room was the toilet. it rocked back and forth. this was a livable problem so i didn't care. we were given a voucher for a free buffet breakfast the next morning. the dining room was crowded so i'd suggest that you would go earlier than we did which was around 10am. the food was decent. they had hot food and danish as well. you could order from the menu if you wanted. at this holiday inn as at many kids eat free. we thankfully were able to travel without our kids this time so it didn't apply to us. if you do drive there you will be charged a per night parking fee. the hotel had an outdoor pool which was not very big but fine for a dip. they had a nice exercise room with two treadmills, an elliptical trainer and a bike along with some weights and a scale. the equipment was fine but the readouts on the elliptical were not correct. our cab fare to the cruise ship pier was less than 10 dollars and was a very short ride. all in all our stay at this hotel was very pleasant and comfortable. we would stay there again and would highly recommend it to anyone who was going a night pre-cruise as this hotel is a perfect location and much less expensive than the hotels the cruise line trys to sell you pre-cruise.
nice stay before cruise room again

it's okay... we stayed for 5 nights at the holiday inn port of miami. it is a pretty budget type hotel. it did have this musty smell throughout the room and the hallway. the concierge daniel was very helpful and the bayside marketplace across the road was convenient and it is open till 11pm every night. i prob wouldn't stay here again. i would prob pay a little more and stay somewhere a little nicer. it is a 10 min bus ride away to south beach. it's good if you are staying a few nights - but that is it. we loved miami though!!

average i stayed here with my wife and son for one night post-cruise. the hotel is decent, but the rooms were very cold. normally, the cold might be welcomed in miami, but not when the outside temperature is in the 50's, as it was the night we were there.we got the best 4 breakfast rate, which included a $20 credit for the hotel restaurant's (overpriced) breakfast. it was ok.i would recommend it only if you can get an advance purchase discount rate of $90-100. with parking, i paid a total of $160 for the night, which was too much for this average hotel.additionally, the bayside marketplace across the street is little more than a mall food court with a few souvenir shops. bubba gump shrimp co. does have good food, however.
great location with a brilliant service i went to miami for my 22nd birthday with a friend. had a great time at holiday inn with great customer service. ace service.

fine for one night we stayed at the holiday inn port of miami for one night before our cruise. it was fine - clean, close to the port and across the street from bayside marketplace. if you want to go to south beach, a cab will run about 17 bucks. if we were going out of this port, i would stay again as long as the price was right.

it was ok for one night... the hotel was just ok, not great or nothing to really talk about. but if you are taking a cruise and want to be close to the port of miami this hotel will do. the rates are good, but don't spend or waste your money on getting a suite if your only going to be there for one or two nights it is not worth it. the port of maimi is very very close.

great location my husband and i were going to see a concert at the american airlines arena, and this was the least expensive place within walking distance. perfect location with free parking and in/out priviledges!! you really can't beat that. after the concert, it was nice to just be able to run across the street to the bayside market, which is right across the street from the hotel.i had actually tried to get a room for both sunday and monday night, but sunday was sold out. at 2am monday morning, we were in town and called the hotel just to see if we could park there (and pretty much sleep in our car) because check-in wasn't until 3pm. the woman at the desk said i could check in to our room without paying for an extra night! at 2am!!! that was a godsend. i couldn't believe how accommodating they were to our situation. besides free parking, food right across the street, a business center and workout room, our room had a refridgerator and effeciency kitchen, iron, and everything we needed to have a comfortable stay. the rooms are clean, although the hallway carpeting is worn and the halls can smell a little stuffy. you can't beat the price and location if you're going to the aa arena or on a cruise.
great pre-cruise hotel another room view

close to port my sister and i stayed at this hotel before our cruise. the hotel was clean and the staff very helpful and friendly. this was a great location with the mall across the street.we were two women traveling alone and never felt unsafe.i would definately stay here again.
great pre-cruise stay! across the street- bayside market

going on a cruise? - great place to stay my husband and i stayed here in large part based on the reviews we found here. we stayed for 2 nights before our cruise.check-in was hassle free. the room was smaller, but really - it was nice. granite countertops and nice shower head in the bathrooms. huge closet (all those cruise bags, right?).bayside was right across the street - there were numerous restaurants - including hooters, bubba gump, chilis. there were also traveler shops, food court, standard shopping, etc. near the hotel is also a walgreens for any last minute things you need.taxis are out front waiting to take you to the cruise port. i would definately stay here again.

great hotel in downtown miami we stayed at the holiday inn port miami in the middle of august. this hotel has an excellent location right across the street you have one of the most visited spots bayside. the hotel is nice, not too fancy but has all of the elements to make it a 3 star hotel. the staff is pleasant and hugo the concierge is very helpful... the rooms are big and some are renovated. beware, if you reserve here try to ask for the rooms that face bayside they are more spacious and updated. i've stayed here in june and was given a room facing the port. those rooms were much nicer than the rooms on the back. this time around, they put us towards the back of the hotel and the view was nothing to write home about. also ask for king size beds... the double rooms have full size..who fits on a full size nowadays??? we paid $120.00 for the night, that included breakfast for two.. so in the middle of august thats a great deal. also bare in mind that parking is extra.. i don't understand why, but that is miami for you... the parking is limited on top of that so you may not have a spot secured if you arrive to late.. oh and they also close the gates after midnite, so ask if you will be arriving late. there's much to do at night right across the street so you may just want to park and walk... they have bars/ restaurants/ and live music every night... the hotel's pool is not big, if you want to get some sun you need to wake up early as the sun disappears quickly over the building. some of the rooms need improvement, but overall clean... the hotel has a great location and price which is better than staying at the hotels in sobe.. oh another thing if you are not driving, save your money on cab fare as they will charge you about $25.00 each way to take you there. ask hugo, the concierge, about the bus they only cost $1.50 each way and that is a great savings...

enjoyable pre-cruise stay we stayed at the holiday inn port of miami for two nights prior to a cruise in august, and were satisfied with our stay. we had requested a room with a king size bed on the tenth floor with a view of the port, and all of our requests were met. one bonus about staying on the tenth floor is that the ceilings are extra high, making the room feel more spacious. the room itself was standard, but clean and comfortable and felt relatively new. perhaps they have renovated recently?? the breakfast buffet was i felt a little overpriced but was fine. the pool area was small but was nice with music playing to block out the sound of the surrounding traffic. the location was ideal, with bayside marketplace just across the street. although i would not spend more than a couple of days in downtown miami, the hotel is ideal for a brief pre or post cruise stay.

pretty decent....but...... my friend and i chose this hotel due to its close proximity to the port since we were going on a cruise the next morning and because the bayside marketplace was across the street offering shops to explore and several nice restaurants to eat at. the hotel was nice. we were very pleased with the room itself, especially the bathroom. just off of the lobby is a nice dining area and bar. i had a delicious breakfast the morning we checked out to leave for our cruise. our only complaint was that it was very difficult the sleep because of all the slamming hotel room doors. all of the doors have automatic spring closers, which cause them to slam shut. we stared at the ceiling for hours unable to fall asleep because of all the noise it was making up and down the hall. if it werenéˆ¥??› for this i would give this hotel 10 out of 10 points. being used to super 8 and motel 6, i would say this was a very nice hotel but because of the trouble sleeping i would probably pick another place next time. if noise like this doesnéˆ¥??› bother youéˆ¥î›?hen this is the place to stay!

close to the pier, but that is about it! we stayed at the holiday inn port of miami for 1 night prior to our cruise. the lobby was nice and we checked in early. our room was on the 9th floor and had a great view overlooking bayside marketplace and the pier. it was great to see our ship in the morning. but those are the only positives. the room smelt of mildew and we were awoken several times throughout the night be people getting off the elevators and their doors slamming behind them. we could also hear our neighbors on both sides very clearly. the food was ok, but not spectacular. i would spend the extra money and stay at the marriott or hyatt next time.

i enjoyed staying there i stayed there for three nights this past week. lobby was nice. check-in time is 3pm but i arrived there at 12:30pm and they were able to give me a room right away. i was pleasantly surprised when i saw my room, it was very clean and nicely decorated. i loved the big t.v. the bathroom was small but it was also very clean and had a granite countertop and a shower head that had multiple spray settings. the restaurant was terrible. do not eat dinner there. i ordered the shrimp scampi the first night and i couldn't eat it. the second night i ordered the grilled salmon with rice - the salmon was very dry and the rice was hard. the daiquiri i ordered was not very good. too much ice. their breakfast menu was okay, better than dinner. room service was fast getting the meals to my room.i also loved the fact that they had a laundry facility and a business center that had free internet access. made my stay a lot better.bayside was just across the street. i had lunch at bubba gumps - the fried calmari was very good.i would definately stay there again. it is in a great location and the room was very clean. the only thing they need to do is change all of the chefs in the restaurant. lol.
location, location, location holiday inn/bayside at night

not what i expected! we stayed here for one night prior to a cruise. this place isn't what i expected. the rooms were smelly and the faucets in the bathroom were loose. there was only 2 windows in the room which over looked the air conditioners on the roof. we requested a port view, but i really don't think you could see the port from any room. we had to pay $10 a day to park, which i think is crazy since we are paying to stay there anyway. we had a room for 5 people and only had enough towels and wash cloths for 4. when we called to get additional towels and wash cloths they brought us 2 of each. so we had to re-use towels the next morning for our shower. the front desk staff wasn't friendly at all. we stood there forever before they finally looked up at us to check us in. the continental breakfast was a joke. we had to pay $9.99 for each person to eat and what tipped it off they added a 15% gratuity and they never touched anything. we got our on food and drinks we never were approached by anyone except to give us the bill. i wouldn't suggest this hotel for a long stay.

it's nice until you get to your room... if your main priority is being close to bayfront park, this is your hotel. but that's about it. room was moldy. we had a smoking room but the windows were bolted shut. housekeeping service was horrible. they would sort of clean your room and not restock all of your towels, shampoo etc. front desk was slow and unresponsive. i would've been better off at the courtyard downtown.
great location! nice hotel more photos

location is it's best asset! i stayed at the hi on a saturday night prior to boarding a ship sailing out of the port of miami, along with 22 other people. although there were mixed reviews from my group on quality of accommodations, we all pretty much agreed that you couldn't beat the location for the purpose of our trip.we were all able to check into our rooms fairly quickly, there were 8 rooms in all. the rooms were adequate; our bathroom seemed to be recently retiled and was clean. we were on the bayside, so it was a pretty sight at 4:30am when we were able to see our ship positioning itself in port.getting breakfast in the hotel on sunday morning was a bit difficult. they had quite a line waiting to be seated. also, kids eat free didn't apply to the breakfast buffet (fyi). the service in the restaurant was definitely not efficient and quick, and the food quality was mediocre. there really wasn't any place else to have breakfast either.check-out time was the biggest headache. mostly everyone in the hotel seemed to be staying there for the same reason....leaving for a cruise. at about 10:00am the lobby was jam-packed, the elevators were full, and would go up and down without getting down to the first floor to let people off. my husband and my son finally took most of the bags down by the stairs, but they could only get down to the 2nd floor through the staircase, so they had to wait until they could get on an empty elevator for the last floor. it was crazy!! the bell captain was busy taking people's suitcases after they'd checked out so he couldn't help that much with questions for transportation. we were supposed to have vans take us to the pier, but we ended up just walking out and taking cabs because we got tired of waiting for him. the cab fare was $10, and it took just about 5 minutes. if you choose to take van shuttles, it's $5 per person. would i stay here again? absolutely, but i would make sure that i'd beat the rush in the morning, or i'd wait it out until 1 or 2p.m. and have my bags held after check-out at 11:00am.bayside is a great place to visit for the evening. we ate at bubba gump's, which was a great experience. you can't make reservations, but when our group arrived they were able to seat us in about 15-20 minutes. the service was quick, prices were reasonable, and the waitors were lively. we were out of there in about 1 1/2 hours. there was a band playing near the water, and various other entertainers around. it was a pretty festive atmosphere.feel free to email me with any questions.

great pre-cruise hotel we just returned from a one night pre-cruise stay at the holiday inn - port of miami. i found the hotel to be clean and accomodating of my requests. after reading several reviews, i requested a room facing the bay on the 6th floor or higher...i got it. the view was wonderful and made us all the more excited about our cruise. the convenience of being able to walk to the bayside marketplace across the street was absolutely wonderfull. we were not interested in going to south beach because we were only going to be staying in miami one night, but having shopping and entertainment so close gave us something to do that evening. i have nothing negative to say about this hotel and would recommend it to anyone. i will be staying here again for my next pre-cruise stay.

good room with reasonable rates my family and i spent a night at this holiday inn and had a very good experience. we booked the room through travelocity and got, what i thought was a very reasonable rate ($87). we were cruising out the next morning on the explorer of the seas, so when i arrived, i asked for a room with a view of the ships. they granted my request without hesitation. i was also pleased to find out the bayside was right across the street. this is an area right on the water of shops, restaurants, bands that play outside! restaurants included hard rock cafe', hooters, chile's, bubba gump's. we spent the whole day there with a group of friends who were cruising with us. we even spent another day there when we returned from the cruise while waiting for our flight out! also the miami heat's arena is right in that area also.considering all of the above, i'd recommend this hotel highly.

room with a view! we stayed at this hotel beginning of march 2005. taking the advise of previous reviews we asked for a view of the port. we were lucky enough to have our request granted and the view was worth the accomodation price alone. the hotel staff were very friendly, efficient and helped with any questions asked.the location was also ideal, close to bayside market and only a short taxi ride to south beach.when we return to miami we will definitely stay here again.

clean and calm in a bustling metropolis my 9 year old daughter and i stayed here for one night after a cruise. i rated this hotel above average because it was nicer than i expected for a typical holiday inn or comparable hotel. it was very clean and comfortable. they let us check in early--about 10:00 because we arrived immediately after disembarking from the cruise ship.my package included a $20 breakfast allowance which we used on the breakfast buffet because the cinnamon roll french toast they advertised was not available during the two mornings we were there. however, it is my understanding that the hotel was booked up solid until the day we checked in (spring break and easter weekend) so it's possible they ran out of the cinnamon roll french toast. it really looked good on the menu though.the room was very clean and cool. (our previous hotel, the fairfield inn airport south was quite the opposite. it was dark and dingy.) we had views of the bayside mall across the street and the cruise ships in the background until they departed. (we sadly looked upon the majesty of the seas which we had spent our weekend on.)cabs were pretty abundant until we were rushing to catch our flight the next day. however, we took a cab the first day to south beach and back--cost was roughly $15 each way). the following morning we caught the bus to the aventura mall which was typical of a large mall. the bus ride was approxiamtely 1.5 hours. on the way back, we learned how to catch the express bus , but we were still rushing to get to the airport.my only problem is that the hotel would not honor a late check-out of 2:00 p.m. i felt it was the attitude the desk clerk i asked because the hotel clearly was not half full so i felt they could have accommodate us. but i could not complain because they clearly gave us an early check-in. i just felt so misplaced without having a room to go back to. we locked our luggage up with the bell station and proceeded to the mall to hang out for the entire day. keep in mind the clerk was not rude, just not accomodating!oh, one other thing, i was unable to print my boarding pass because there was a problem with the internet service the hotel offered. but had it been working, it was a great free service that they offer--to use the internet for free. so don't forget to print your boarding passes and seat assignments.other than not receiving the late check-out, our stay was good and i would not hesitate to stay there again when i take another cruise out of miami--which i am sure i will.

nice hotel for the price, clean and quiet this was a nice hotel for the price. this hotel is an older hotel but the rooms have been recently updated and are clean and modern. the room was small but sufficient with nice appointments. the bathroom was clean and even had a granite sink. the location of the hotel is good, it is right across the street from the basketball stadium and a nice shopping area. would stay here again.

doing it all over again we(group of 10) stayed here october 2, 2004 before we boarded the explorer of the sea's the next day. most of us arrived at the hotel before 2:00pm and rooms were ready for some of us, and maria was really generous to the one's who's rooms were not ready. she ended up giving all of us rooms that faced the port, so we could see our ship pull in that morning. we paid $83.99+tax for our rooms and it was wonderful. they offer a nice breakfast in the morning for additional cost.this year we are doing a cruise in august and we are already booked at the hi once again, i guess it is the second time around

great place to stay before cruise with some trepidation about the area in downtown miami we decided to reserve a room at this refurbished holiday inn. comments on this forum encouraged us. we got there two days before our cruise and had a really good time exploring the bay market place and park across the street. around the corner from the hotel is a free metro mover monorail which we rode in both north and south directions for a view of downtown miami. we did not get to south beach but it was quite accessible by taxi or bus from our location. holiday inn was clean and friendly. we had a great view from our ninth floor room and can recommend it as a nice place to stay if you wish to arrive early for a cruise. price was great as we reserved many months ahead. room was $101.00 plus tax. the area was fine to walk around. it is near little havana which is all spanish speaking. we enjoyed breakfast at a little street cafe there. the bay market place is safe at night but you wouldn't want to walk anywhere else in the area after dark. not enough people around. all in all we had a great stay. nothing negative.

great pre-cruise hotel!!! we paid $105 plus tax so $115 for one night pre-cruise at this hotel on jan 13, 2005. we booked it 8 or so months in advance and asked for a room high up overlooking the pier. we were supposed to be in miami around 12:30 pm. unfortunately, we had weather problems that caused flight delays and missed connections. i called the hotel to advise that we would be arriving late. we didn't end up getting there until almost midnight, and figured we'd get the worst room in the hotel since we were probably the last to arrive. the hotel was fully booked that night. however, upon arrival, we were pleasantly surprised. we were given a room on the 10th floor overlooking the pier. it was a gorgeous view at night and in the morning. also, although we had not tied our reservations together, we were only a couple of doors down from family who traveled with us, which worked out nicely. the hotel itself was clean and nicely decorated. the staff was very friendly and accommodating. this hotel is just across the street from bayside marketplace which is a great place to shop, eat, and walk around near the pier. unfortunately, we didn't get to do that on our first day, but did a little bit before going on our cruise the next morning. this hotel is also only 3 blocks from a walgreens to pick up any soda/water or other necessities prior to the cruise. beware there were a lot of homeless people around when we got there at midnight, but otherwise it was a great location and i would definitely stay there again!

great place we arrived the day before our cruise was to depart and met another couple that was going to sail with us. we were allowed to check in early. the other couple had already checked in so when we arrived we asked the front desk if they could move them to adjoining rooms with us, which they did. shopping across the street at bayside was a good experience, lots to see, large variety at the food court other restaurants (hard rock. chiliéˆ¥??? ect.) with in walking distance. checked out at 11:00 was effortless and taxis were plentiful. we boarded the ship after we checked out. we plan on staying there again next year when we go on next years cruise.

great for pre/post cruise we just stayed here jan. 13, 2005 and the 17th, for pre and post cruise nights. the hotel itself was fine, typical holiday inn with a restaurant, a small pool and the rooms were clean. the best part of it was the location to the cruise port and mainly the bayside marketplace across the street. lots of great shops and booths set up, good restaurants (chili's and hard rock- and hooters if you're into that). it's about a $25 taxi ride to the airport, and about $10 to the port. we hopped on a bus that took us to south beach which is where the nice beaches to swim and lay out are. there's no water access from this hotel, since it's more of a marina/port type waterfront area. i'd probably stay there again, just for price and convenience, even though south beach looks like a better place to stay for beaches and amenities (it's just a lot farther from airport and cruise port, which means more taxi $ and higher priced hotels).

wonderful place to stay we arrived early and had to wait 2 hours before getting into our room, the bellman stored our luggage and we took off to the bayside marketplace directly across the street with plenty of shops and places to eat. our room was wonderful with the refridgerator, microwave, sofabed and, chairs overlooking the marketplace. we were very thankful for the self service laundry. staff was courteous and i don't know what the bellman makes but he deserves a raise!

a good precruise stay we stayed here january 2004 before leaving on a cruise. we arrived early and did have to wait two hours before we could check in, however we were able to leave out luggage with a bellhop and walked across the street to bayside shopping and entertainment center. it was lovely. we had left minnesota with below zero temperatures so sitting on the deck at hardrock cafe and having a drink while watching the boats come and go from the harbor was just divine. we ate some lunch, listened to some salsa bands that were playing and then headed back to the hotel. it did take some time to actually get into our room as the line was very long at the check-in desk and service was slow, but we weren't going anywhere and we were on vacation...that evening we walked back over to bayside and ate at bubba gumps. very nice experience. it was a nice evening before our cruise. the next morning we did have quite a wait at breakfast and there were several families waiting to go to the port to board their ships, but it all happened in due time and i would stay here again. there was a walgreen's within walking distance and we found we needed a few things for our cruise that we had forgotten to pack. it was convenient and non'threatening to walk the three blocks. we liked this pre-cruise stay.

nice hotel, but wouldn't do it again we stayed one night after a cruise, nov 2004.when we arrived at the hi the lobby was packed with people waiting to check in or out for the cruises. we were happy that our room was ready. we were staying 1 night after the cruise. the room was very nice and the view of the bay and the cruise ships was beautiful. i could have sat looking out the window all day but i couldn't wait to get down to the pool. the pool is very small and the water was freezing. there is construction going on right in the back of the hotel. the seating area is also very small and most of the loungers were taken by people who have all their luggage. i guess they were either waiting to leave for their cruise, an air flight or a room. because of all the high buildings there really was not much sun.we stayed at this hotel because the last time we were in miami we went to the bayfront shopping area and had a good time. the second visit was disappointing. the area seemed different.i also want to let you know that if you are returning from a cruise the taxi drivers do not want to take you from the port to the hotel because it is such a small fare. there was a moan when we told them where we wanted to go and the taxi driver seemed mad that he got such a small fare and the only thing he said was i want 1 dollar for the bridge toll. it's a 6 dollar fare. at least the 4 dollar tip made him smile.since our cruise came in early in the morning, the next time i would book a 2o'clock flight and take the tour offered by the cruiseline to the everglades or go all the way to the airport and stay at one of those hotels if i needed to. there is nothing wrong with the hotel. i just would do things differently next time because i felt bored and thought that it was a waste of time sitting at the hotel all day when i could have gone home.

disappointed again we've stayed here before, but not when it was a holiday inn. despite lots of fanfare, not much seems to have changed above the lobby floor. the location is still the best thing this hotel has going for it. registration was okay (at 8:30 am) once they found our paperwork, which took ten minutes. i returned at 3 pm to check in, and all was well. sixth or seventh floor, as requested, bayside, near the elevators. things went well till i got up at 7 am, used the bathroom, turned to flush, and found myself staring at a 2-long palmetto bug (florida cockroach, to you non-floridians) on the floor next to the commode! a ten-minute battle with the in-wall hair blower and a bottle of hair lacquer ensued, but in the end, we were victorious. a talk with the rooms manager got us half off the bill (originally $89 + 13% tax). check out went smoothly, we stored our bags, and went out. when we retrieved them, the strap on one inexpensive vinyl rolling bag snapped, but i was in a hurry to drive home before dark, so we left. at home, we discovered that someone on the hotel staff had put three staples into the strap, in an attempt to cover up the damage they'd done! i'm debating what further action to take, up to and including disputing the rest of the bill. unfortunately, there's no real alternative to this location, until the everglades-on-the-bay reopens, one block away. we can't wait!!!!!

night before our cruise nov 6 2004 a great location. right across the street was bayside with the mall and several restaurants. beds were very comfortable and the breakfast was delicous. we stayed overnight before our cruise. taxi from the hotel to the port was less than $10. staff was very friendly and helpfullmy only complaint was at checkout, dozens of other guests were leaving for cruises too and the elevators were terrribly slow. we tried the stairs, but none of them led to the lobby! you had to wait for an elevator.if you are taking a cruise out of miami, this is the hotel to stay in before or after.

nice hotel for the price! this is a nice hotel for the price. we booked this hotel for a one day stay on 10/24/2004. the lobby was very nice. the check-in process was easy and quick. the front desk person was very helpful. the room was small but that was ok because it was just a one day stay before going out on our cruise. the bath room was newly remodeled. the bed was pretty comfortable. the room was clean. nice size tv. the very best thing about the hotel was the location. the bayside market place is right across the street. many shops and a great food court. water is everywhere with great views of the city and miami port. great music and dancing. the miami port is a 5 minute cab ride for about $7.00 i would stay at this hotel again. we paid $69.00 + tax.

nice rooms, good price stayed at the holiday inn marina park on september 24th, 2004 for one night prior to driving to kissimmee.very nice hotel. the rooms are a bit small, so i would not recommed it for long stays. everything in the room (and all of the hotel) seems like it's pretty new. my guess is that it must have undergone a renovation recently. the private parking in the back of the hotel is a plus. the location is also great, since it's right across the road to bayside marketplace, which is a shoping mall right on biscayne bay offering quite some stores and restaurants.the price of the room (we got it at us$ 89.00 the night) was very good, considering the location and the competition (other hotels in that area were eighter cheap but bad or nice but outrageosly expensive). i would surely recommend this hotel!

much better than expected! 9/11-9/13, 2004. we booked a cruise from the port of miami and wanted to stay somewhere close as we arrived 2 days early. i read reviews of the holiday inn - port of miami and they were mostly poor to fair.expecting the worst, all four of us were pleasantly surprised. the rooms were big and clean, the staff was very friendly, and the location (right across the street from bayside marketplace) was fantastic! yes the pool was small, but i came here for a cruise, not to swim laps. we paid $85.00 per night (booked throught holiday inn website), and it was money well spent.i will definitely stay here again the next time i cruise out of miami.

pre cruise favorite we chose port of miami holiday inn to be close to pier for a cruise. taxi fare to hotel was $24.00 from the airport and $10.00 to pier the next morning. we decided to go this route instead of the airport hotels with shuttles so we could be close to bayside to have something to do. the hotel was spotless and the staff very friendly. our room was more spacious than other holiday inns we've been in, and we had the great view of three cruise ships coming in to port. we ate meals at bayside, many restaurants to choose from. breakfast much more interesting there than at the hotel too. we plan to come again on our next miami based cruise

nothing special, and overpriced we go to miami once a year to stay overnight, for the fabulous miami book fair. we've stayed here six times over the past 10 years, both as a holiday inn and as a best western (till 2003). the location cannot be beat for the heart of downtown miami, with access to bayside across the street, and the port, american airlines arena, and shopping nearby. but when the owner switched affiliation to holiday inn, the prices skyrocketed and the policies changed to require multi-night stays, cancellation fees, etc., so we went elsewhere in 2003. the hotel is said to have received a complete makeover in 2003; if so, it was badly in need of one. on our last stay, the toilet ran all night, despite repeated calls for maintenance (no one on duty at night, we were finally told); we shut the bathroom door rather than shut off the valve. we shall see, now that prices have come down a fair bit, whether things have improved, when we stay there later this year.one bit of advice: if you're too near the top floors, you hear the frequent airplanes overhead, all night long; if you're too close to the ground, the noise from open-air concerts at bayside can be deafening. best bet, stay on the 6th or 7th floor. also keep in mind that not all floors have ice machines, if that's important to you. also handy to know: there's a second, unisex public bathroom on the second floor, right next to the elevators (where the marketing office used to be).now, if the renovation has changed any of this, i'll be sure to let you know.

beautiful renovated hotel this is a favorite long time hotel of my family. we just stayed again for christmas eve and loved the new renovations. staff was excellent as usual. this in my opinion is the best hotel on nob hill. beautiful and elegant, but not over crowded with tourists the way the fairmont and mark hopkins are.now my critic; they moved the restaurant from the far corner of the hotel into the lobby area to be more centeralized and accessible to the guests. the result is a beautiful restaurant, but left us all wondering where is the lobby. there is no lobby sitting area, unless you go into the restaurant. this felt very weird. come on put a couple of couches out near the front desk.second the old restaurant space is now empty. it had overlooked the cable car intersection. this would make an excellent and very interesting bar area. i suspect they will just use it as meeting/function space. too bad.overall a great hotel and will stay again in the future.

five stars my husband and i stayed at the stanford court for one nite as we were in the city to go to the ballet. we were pleasantly surprised that it had been renovated and is so beautiful,modern, fresh and clean. our room had amazing views of the bay and the city and was very modern. the lobby looks great and we enjoyed some appetizers and drinks at the bar. all the staff were friendly and accommodating. i highly recommend this hotel and we will be back!!

stunning hotel i booked this hotel for work since i mostly stay at marriott properties when traveling. marriott's are usually consistent and nice business hotels. i stayed for thanksgiving weekend before work at the hilton on 333 ofarrell street. it was a little outdated and there were a lot of panhandlers outside the hotel even though it was right near market street with the flagship bloomingdale's and barney's. i was disappointed in my selection.for all that was at fault with the hilton, just a short distance away was paradise. this hotel was at the top of nob hill. it was devoid of the problems i previously experienced. i stayed on the 5th floor which could have had street level noise but it was no problem. it was classic san francisco with incredible views of the bay.the $32 million renovation was just completed. it is magnificent and a wonderful combination of vintage charm with modern comfort. the only negative is the pricing on parking. $45/night is steep but it is san fran. i have a feeling this hotel will raise its room rates soon once the word is out. i highly recommend staying here.

awesome! stayed here on dec 4. i did not stay here before the renovation. the money was well invested. the staff is 5 star. not one complaint. excellent service from the valet to the check-in to housekeeping. the hotel feels like a ritz. everything is nice. i had a corner room on the 7th floor with a bay view. unbelieveable. awesome views of the city and the bay. the room was huge! the tv was great, too. the fitness center is top notch! location can not be beat in nob hill. cable cars are right out the door. i booked on the marriott site and got a mid-week rate for $159. it included to cabel car passes and a free breakfast. you can't beat this deal in downtown san fran! it is unheard of! i'm sure i won't get this deal next time i book, but it was a great deal on this last trip.i usually stay at the hilton downtown or the courtyard at oyster point. the stanford court is my new #1 hotel in san fran!!

would not return again my wife and i recently stayed overnight for a conference. had dinner, breakfast and stayed one night in what i presume is a typical single queen bed room. on the upside the service (especially at dinner) is very attentive. the food was above average - nothing to come back for though. the place has been recently remodeled and very clean overall. on the downside, the rooms don't offer much sound insulation - you can hear a lot from neighbors running water and flushing to people talking in the hallway just outside the room. the rooms are relatively small given this place is older so the beds are close to the doors. we had a room that faced the interior (and ugly) courtyard which is supposedly quieter but not by much. keep in mind the outer facing rooms can be noisy with clanging cable cars til 1am. what made it worse is that a bunch of drunk women were rudely talking loudly in the hallway and next door at 2am waking both of us and making us lose about 1.5-2 hours of sleep that night. we called security which arrived in about 5-10 minutes to shut them up. however, the night front desk man called me 1/2 hour after the security arrived just to see if these drunkards shut up just when i was trying to fall back asleep. i mean, why call me, man? if there is a problem i will call back. how stupid! he must have been a rookie. lastly, the wait to get my car back from valet parking was longer than reasonable - not enough personnel. i would definitely shop around for a better place since there are many fine hotels to choose from in sf.

renovation produces a gem stayed a delightful weekend in mid november. the ambiance is as if you had just arrived at a friend's house. easy arrival and check-in. concierge was well informed.located at the corner where all the cable cars pass thus union square, market powell and fisherman's wharf are all accessible without effort.top of the mark is just up the street.newly decorated rooms and public spaces are scrumptious to the eye.as the renovations are still underway (rooms 90 percent converted), there are still some startup glitches. my room did not have the promised safe and mini bar, which was brought promptly when i asked. the tv remote did not work and was replaced promptly. the new tv channel lineups were not yet published to the in-room directory.

loved stanford court my husband and i stayed in this hotel for 3 nights while we were visiting san francisco. we had a great stay in this hotel. only complains are the water pressure was slow from the sink faucet and the valet fees are a little high. our room was on the 5th floor facing to powell and we saw the cable car . it also has a nice view. we heard some street noise on the first night since it was sat. sun was a little quiet or may be we got used to the noise, it did not bother us much. starbucks coffee is a nice touch in the morning especially my husband is a coffee person. we missed the champagne since we were always out during that time. the hotel room had no fridge. but we requested one. the front desk staff was very nice and also greeted us. we borrowed an umbrella from the concierge since it was raining on one of the nights. the valet parking service was very good and staff was very friendly as well. the court yard of the hotel is big (not on the street) so we did not feel rush when we dropped off the car for valet service. we walked to union square. going there was easy. coming back was hard since we had to walk up to the hill. but we enjoyed the walk. we also walked to chinatown and tadich grill for dinner. be prepared to involve a lot of climbings if you are not using car/cable car.

nice place! this is a very nice refurbished hotel. i had a request for a king, they were out when we checked in, so they gave us a queen with a great view of the bay. it was very nice and clean. i thought the size of the room was fine. something i noticed is that the front desk area always smelled good, kind of like a spa. i thought that was a nice touch. they have free starbucks coffee in the morning and champagne at about 5 by the front desk. the ice machines are not in yet so just call and they will deliver it, and anything else you need right away. it is at the top of a very steep hill so just be sure to get a cable car pass so you can jump on if you are not always up for the walk. the staff was very nice and always greeted us weather we were leaving or returning. concierge was very informative and helpful.

first class i got an excellent rate via expedia. never heard of this hotel before. i was satisfied alone with the price... but when i arrived at the hotel, i was immediately impressed with every aspect that this establishment had to offer. we arrived at 11 am and check-in is 3 pm. however, the front desk advised me that they had a room available and at no extra charge i was in my room at 11 am. they serve complimentary starbucks coffee and morning champaigne in the lobby. the ammenities are remarkable and so many details that i can not explain here. i forgot my shaving cream and razor; the front desk had them delivered to me within 5 minutes. the staff is absolutely friendly and the whole place had a friendly and welcoming!the location is right off powell street so the trolley is literally right outside the hotel. very convenient to fishermans wharf, snobb hill, and the mall. i highly recommend this hotel to everyone!!! mu
couldn't find a single fault.. the stained glass atrium over the courtyard

come here and enjoy- the renovations are over! i used priceline and paid $115- so inexpensive. the check in rep. offered me a view on the 3rd floor (highest priceline option) which may have cable car noise, or an interior room. i chose the view and the windows were so well insulated that the noise was no problem (and i am a very light sleeper). the view was great because the hotel is on top of a hill.the room was huge and gorgeous. the staff was professional and friendly. the location was excellent and all the public areas were we appointed. they had evening free champaign (unlimited). the parking was an insult (over $50 w/tax), but the masonic events center two short blocks away had it for $30 (a fair price in this city).i would definately recommend this hotel.
seemed to work hard to make up happy and they did! view from room

wonderful customer service and location i must admit i had no baseline of this hotel before the rennovation so i arrived with an open mind. often one can tell by employee interaction if the property is synrchronized, and as evidenced by the smiles, the tenue of employees, and the care and feeding the employees give to this grand old property, it's not just another prefabricated downtown highrise.the color scheme throughout the hotel is bright and cheery and much time was spent reusing some of the stately elements rarely found in a business hotel. from the beautiful stained glass to the marble in my bathroom, it was nice to see how much time was spent preserving the past.since older hotels tend to have smaller rooms, i was surprised at how someone had taken the time to plan out a space to provide today's basics, large flat screen television, comfortable computer desk, and lots of electrical outlets for phone chargers, computers, and all the other gadgets we carry. the restaurant i understand was previously located downstairs and was more in keeping with the older, darker established restaurant theme. the restaurant has been moved to the main level, where the marble floor shines and the little plate menu is perfect for those of us who do not want a large slab of steak before we retire to bed. i understand in the near future their bar will offer an extensive collection of top end wines by the glass, and the executive chef personally stopped by to inquire about my dinner - you can tell he is a stickler for details and customer experience.i opt to take a taxi to my downtown hotel and then take taxis to my meetings, as parking on the hills is not one of my favorite things. as a bonus, this hotel offers is the availability of two car services during the day that will take you for what you would pay for a taxi to most destinations within the city. i used the service and was very impressed with the cleanliness of the cars and courtesy of the drivers.overall, i would recommend staying at this hotel; it's a treat for us business travelers that are used to the cookie-cutter chain hotel accomodations, and i would also stay at this hotel while on holiday. the stanford court is a grand hotel, with boutique charm, and wonderful service.

i really felt like home !!! me and my wife stayed in the stanford court 4 days, then i went to wine country and carmel and returned for more 3 days. and both of my stays were very pleasant.the renovation was almost done, and did not bothered we at all.....and in the end of our stay we could see part of the new lobby already.the rooms were fully renovated very good with all the ammenities you'll find in a 4 star hotel.if you want a silent room ask for a courtyard view room. you will lost the partial bay area view, but won't get annoyed by the cable cars bell (they run until 12 pm)the staff is absolutely friendly from the front desk to the house keeping staff, everybody was naturally warm.other special point was the attention we had from the master concierge, mr. ric lee, who help us with the reservations in some of the best restaurants, and they also helped me with flowers for my wife's birthday.the only con i can say was the us$45/day parking, except for that everything else was great.

overrated stanford court we recently stayed at the stanford court on nob hill in san francisco. it has just undergone a major renovation. unfortunately the rooms are extremely small and the closet is in the bathroom. we were unable to get breakfast at the hotel and our tv didn't work most of one day -all we got was excuses. this hotel does not now live up to its old reputation for excellence. there are many good hotels in san francisco and this is not one of them. the stanford court has 4 star prices and 2 star service.

great location - great rooms we stayed for 2 nights here at the end of a west coast road trip. the hotel is undergoing some renovations to its lobby area, i would have like to see it in its 'full glory' once complete, but didn't bother us really - we were out most of the day. the room we had must have been one that had been updated recently. it was lovely... the best of our 2 week trip. we cant believe what good value we go it for (booked before we went through tour operator). it had a lovely big bathroom, and the bed was big and comfy. we asked to be on the road side overlooking the street. you can hear the trams going past but this didn't bother us.we didn't use any of the other services at the hotel, apart from the concierge (helpful), so cant comment on these.location wise it was great - right at the stop for the trams. before we got the hang of them though we did do a couple of trips up and down the hill which was not a good idea!!!! my calf muscles didnt recover for a few days!!all in all i really like this hotel.... and would definitely recommend it.

stay somewhere else- i called this hotel 6 months in advance to book 2 connecting rooms. my kids are 9, 10 and 13. i was able to use my marriot rewards to pay for the 2 rooms for 2 nights. the hotel looked beautiful on the web site and had decent reviews. prior to our trip, i called the front desk to confirm our reservations and the connecting rooms. the front desk was not friendly and quite annoyed that i called . marriot has a horrble policy of not guaranteeing connecting rooms, even when booking so far in advance. i was told to call back a few days before we arrived. we did call the day before check in and was told we didn't have connecting rooms and they would see what they could do. they did accomodate us. upon arrival, the place is under construction and there is no lobby to speak of . the man at the front desk had an attitude and when i gave him our name, he said, i worked really hard to get you those rooms. i informed him that i made the reservation 6 months ago ! isn't that their job ???the rooms are nice, a bit on the small side. we were on the top floor in an already renovated area. the bedroom was area was fine, but the bathroom was disgusting. i found a housekeeping cart and took the disinfectant to clean the two bathrooms. the tubs were stained, grout was black in spots, mold on the shower curtains and our tiolet leaked black oily stuff from the handle. i know we were in the heart of the city, but they have done nothing to sound proof their windows or walls. it was very noisy ! i heard this complaint from other guests , as well as, how horribel the lobby area is with the construction.we would not stay here again . i'd rather pay for another hotel and use my points elsewhere.

under construction... i booked this through my company's travel agency because i have stayed here before and also because of the price ($209). i stayed for 3 nights. the hotel is under construction, so if the renovation has been completed, this review will be less valuable. however, i was put in a room that had been updated. it had two double beds and was decent sized. it sat above california street, and the cable cars can be heard along with some traffic sounds. while somewhat noticeable, not a show stopper. the room had a large flat screen tv that had a lot of channels. internet (both wired and wireless) was available for $10 per day from noon to noon. a coffee pot in the room and starbucks located in the lobby were free. the room was clean but the bathtub hadn't been given much of a makeover. they mostly updated other parts of the room. i was satisfied but the room wasn't anything special. also, the elevators were slow and i was only on the 6th floor. the construction was a bit obtrusive in the lobby and they had makeshift check-in, lobby and other areas. really not very appealing as long as it's under construction. breakfast in forneau's oven was nice, although not much of a view. food was ala carte only, no buffet. i only had oatmeal so i can't comment too much on the quality. parking was $45 per day which is par for the course in sf. service for the car was fast. the location is atop of nob hill near the fairmont, mark hopkins and the ritz. you can walk down the hill easily, but those with physical limitations may want to consider a cab back up the hill. overall a decent place, but hard to rate that high with the construction going on. be sure to ask before you book a room.
