a great place to stay in san francisco! my husband and i chose this hotel for out new year's eve gettaway based on the great reviews from trip advisor and we were not dissapointed! i booked a standard king room and was up graded to a premier king free of charge upon our arrival. the staff were very nice. the wine hour in the cozy lobby was great. enjoyed talking with fellow travelers by the warm and inviting fireplace. our room was very nice. we expected the room to be small based on all the reviews but it was very nicely decorated and super clean. the bed was very comfortable and the room itself was very quiet. the hotel is walking distance to many attractions. we ate at the italian restaraunt located in the hotel and the food and service was outstanding. check out the following morning was fast and flawless as we enjoyed fresh coffee and biscotti served complimentary in the lobby. i will go back to this hotel again!

again, a nice quaint hotel, perfect location having stayed at this hotel awhile back, i sort of knew what to expect. check in was flawless, and we were even early arrivals at approx 12 noon. room was on 4th floor overlooking the interior garden area. seems the hotel has been completely renovated since our last stay. our room had a nice clean bath/shower, all tile, and sink that was marble. plenty of toiletries. the bed was very plush, and king size that was very comfortable. there were 2 alarm clocks on either side of the bed. nice mini bar, and plenty of tv stations to watch before going to bed. the rooms are done in an italian hue, and recently new carpet through out the entire hotel and our floor. the refridge was a bit noisy, and the air conditioner seemed a bit loud and woke me several times during the night, but really was not bad at all. never experienced the room service. never did partake in the 5 pm wine tasting as we were usually out at the buena vista chugging down irish coffee until the late night. the hotel is very well located as previously mentioned in other reviews. we ate dinner at the attached restaurant the night prior to our departure for convenience, and was pleasantly surprised at the quality of the food. well done. all in all, would and have stayed here again. paid around 205 a night booked through a hotel vendor website. it is very touristy by the wharf. as other times we have stayed more in the financial district, and probably would the next time for a different feel again.

room 200 is noisy... we stayed in room 200 which is on the corner of hyde and north point. this is directly above the cable car stop. we heard cable cars and traffic going back and forth until 0100 and starting again at 0500. apparently, cable cars are taken to the barn most all night for maintainence. the windows are single payne and provide no sound proofing. others in our group stayed in the middle of the hotel and had no problem with traffic noise. the rooms were large and comfortable and the location was fine if you don't mind a little walking to the wharf and other attractions. at least the cable car is close...maybe a little too close.

great time in san francisco we have just returned from a 3 week vacation incorporating 6 days in california followed by a cruise.we chose the best western tuscan inn as our base whilst in san francisco on the first three nights of our tour.we arrived at sfr approximately 1 hour late due to flight delays at london heathrow and in the pouring rain and, of course, suffering from jet lag. despite all this, we found the tuscan inn easily in a city strange to us.after reading other reviews on trip advisor we made sure that we had a garden view room as we knew that the jet lag would see us awake at about 2:00am!i don't know about the street view rooms but we had no problems with noise whatsoever.the rooms were pleasant, clean and did not disappoint.the hotel is certainly well placed for access to fisherman's wharf, pier 39 etc. my wife suffers from arthritis and cannot walk far but we had no problems in walking to the departure point for alcatraz tours, mr. toad's city tour, cable cars, etc.staff were helpful and generally friendly.the daily wine reception was a great idea as it got guests together and talking about their experiences of the day.was a little upset by waiter serving wine at the second of these we went to. on arriving we initially spoke to some other guests and i then went to request two glasses of wine on behalf of myself and my wife - reaction was, in broken english, - only two glasses each!i explained we had just arrived and this was our first drink.no, only two glasses we haven't had one yet!i must see your room keywith annoyance i retrieved and displayed the key and finally got a glass of wine.i know they don't want clients getting drunk at their expense but at the end of the day it wasn't even quality wine just a very cheap plonk.only other downer was $38 per night for valet parking. being from uk this kind of thing is alien to me but i did know in advance and chose to accept it - apparently other guests with larger cars were paying over $50 !apart from the one incident above i would have no reservations about recommending this hotel

a great stay we had a comfortable and enjoyable stay. the hotel was clean and convenient. the staff was helpful and friendly. we never went to the evening wine party but it looked very popular. we were street side which was a bit noisy some mornings with truck deliveries.

very dog-friendly this is a hassle-free place to stay with a dog. i travel with my small poodle and usually, even though hotels will say that they welcome pets, the front desk people give you a certain look when you walk in and out of the lobby with your dog.......not here!!! i've never stayed at a more dog-friendly place. i saw a couple checking in with 3 large dogs (retrievers) so apparently there isn't a weight limit, maybe a limit of 3 dogs??? i stayed in a suite.......a note to those considering staying in a suite....i thought that mine was rather small so i asked if the suites were the same size and was told, they're about the same. ended up staying in my suite as it was a busy weekend but i did get to view the suite directly across from mine and there was a huge difference ( i would guess about an extra 100 sf). so, make sure that you request one of the larger suites, they are all priced the same. if your dog tends to be a little disruptive or on the noisy side, there is a bathroom fan that you can keep on to make noise. also, the room air conditioners/heaters make some sound which can also help to mask noise. my dog is very well-behaved so i'm lucky but i never once heard any other dog noise while i was there. stay here, your dog (and you) will love it.
liked it room was quiet, clean with good beds but very very smallnot a cheap hotelvalit parking was to much expencive but oke its the location

awesome hotel!! i stayed at this tuscan inn in the fisherman's wharf in san francisco recently. what a lovely place in the midst of a fast-paced environment! the thought that it was a best western made me think ahead of my stay that this is an okay place to rest a night but what a surprise when i found the cutest place in the city of san francisco. the room was adorable and had everything i needed. the concierge, hugo vides, is the absolute best. the welcoming wine event between 5 and 6 p.m. was a nice twist to get to know others who were staying there. i only wish i would have had more time there and hope to someday return. i am so glad my travel agent at liberty travel suggested this.

liked staying at tuscon inn i booked this hotel via booking.com at klm website. i went through a lot of reviews and the one from frommers guide was most helpful. i got a good rate and no prepayment from the klm website( linked to booking.com). tuscon inn was near the pier 39, which is a great location, checking in and out was easy. the staff were very helpful. the room was nice, good size and quite clean. the bathroom was big and clean as well. although i was alone, room was good enough for a couple. the hotel had free coffee and drinks everyday and free access to wireless internet. the adjacent served nice breakfast. great location and hotel. try and not book anything from the hotel though, just walk up pier 39 and you will have more choice. the hotel does arrange a shuttle to the airport without any extra charge.

cozy, friendly place to stay on the wharf we had a quick trip to sf and decided to stay here so we could easily walk to the wharf, pier 39 and ghirardeli chocolate square. we choose this place primarily based on other user reviews on tripadvisor. the room is nice, very cozy (i.e. fairly small) but well put together and comfortable. we took everyone's advice and requested an interior courtyard view (basically looking at the opposing wall of the hotel) and so we didn't hear any noise.we were incredibly lucky and came here when the weather was very good. free coffee and biscotti in the morning helped get the gf out of bed. it was funny to run into a fellow husband in the elevator bringing back coffee for this wife as well. parking is crazy expensive, we drove up from la so we had a car - but otherwise, you really don't need it. staff was friendly and helpful - we had no issues. most of the other guests are foreigners.

nice, convenient hotel we stayed for 4 nights mid october, in a suite to cater for 2 couples. the first room we had was kinda worn, no view, and you could hear noisy a/c units, and the beds felt worn, as you could feel the springs if you pressed firmly!! not good! unfortunately, i had come down with a rather nasty throat infection on this, the 2nd leg of our extensive trip, coming from 5 nights in santa monica, la. anyway, the next morning i requested another room with either a street or garden courtyard view.big difference! the room we got was bigger, toward the rear of the building, so a long walk from lift, but well worth it. it also had a pleasant courtyard view. this room also felt as if it had been used maybe a third as much as the other one!! perhaps they like to let out all the 'close to lift ' rooms to be kind to housekeeping?!? biggest difference though - the beds - no uncomfortable springs!! also, the bathrooms were quite well set up, with a seperate toilet/shower to basin, so whilst one guest is showering another can use the basin.decor etc. was quite nice and fresh looking, and it is because of this that i would not hesitate to come back - provided i got a similar room! internet provided via a pc in foyer was very handy!!only thing i missed was a gym, for some reason i had an inclination to use the gyms while we were o/s!? service was all good, albeit a bit stoic. i was dutifully helped at 130am when i wanted a hospital to nip my sickness in the bud, which was much appreciated. however, i felt a little weird, almost uncomfortable when on a couple of nights, whilst suffering coughing fits, i decided to go downstairs and use the internet, so as to not keep my fellow guests awake. upon arriving downstairs, i found the duty manager/staff napping on the (guest?) lounges !!. it didn't bother me, but felt a little weird, like i was interrupting them!! anyways, one night we came back just after they had turned off the coffee machine in the restaurant, but the wonderful waiter/maitre'd organised some hot drinks for us in the biggest mugs i've ever seen - legend!!! we all loved san fran - fantastic city with great selection of restaurants etc, fishermans wharf was great also - ate at wipeout, where the waiters were very honest with what to order!! ate at caesars old style italian - fantastic for price, and also mona lisa on columbus in awesome little italy. unfortunately we didn't get to dine in the hotel restaurant, but i'd say it would be good, if the after hours service is anything to go by! can't wait to go back to sf and explore some more, i.e.berkely sausalito etc. if you like architectural history do the 'ghost tour' from queen anne hotel...fantastic, intriguing history in most exclusive area of city.the hotel is nice and close to fishermans wharf and other attractions, which was really handy.

ok for the price... booked two rooms on priceline for $139 each, just an overnight stay while flying home the next morning. check in was good, rooms both ready, and we upgraded with no problems. room was very small for 4, we apparently had an outside room, because trucks crashed around all night loading and unloading. tried to tip the maids for 2 extra towels as there were 4 of us and it was a huge problem, apparently no more than 4 towels per room? didn't want to pay for the mini-bar, but frig leaked all over floor. when maintenance guy came in, he blamed us for turning it down, it was in a locked cabinet! asked for a wake up call and did not get it. one male working the desk the morning of 10/20 was rushed, rude, so checked out without talking to them. hotel is clean, very convenient to the wharf and shopping. would not stay here again, due to noise and staff, but ok for the price, if i would have paid rack rate, i would have been more upset.

our comfy room at the tuscan inn we stayed at this lovely, incredibly well located hotel for 6 nights as we explored the hills of san francisco. the staff was wonderful, our room was very pretty with a view of the fisherman's wharf area. the bathroom was marble and we had luxurious bathrobes and really, every detail attended to. when we first arrived at 2am, there had been a mixup with the room reservation and the man at the desk was so competent and accomodating - while the hotel was full, he found a room for us, for which we were eternally grateful. we met the manager, who was incredibly helpful about restaurants in the area, and also a lovely person to talk to. the breakfast at the neighboring restaurant (attached to the hotel) was delicious and the evening wine hour was the perfect thing after a day on one's feet. i'd highly recommend the tuscan inn based on location, cheerfulness of staff, aesthetics in the room and general overall service.

great stay at the tuscan inn stayed for three nights at the tuscan inn. easy walking distance to fishermans wharf , cable cars, and streetcar stop to ferry building. older hotel with smaller rooms but updated nicely. thin walled rooms. only coffee and bisquits for breakfast. overall a pleasant stay.

loved the wine at 5pm we stayed two nights in august following a flight from uk. we had a room on the ground floor that was very well decorated but a bit gloomy. as we had come to sleep that actually helped. it was large with enough space for our cases. disappointed with coffee making faclities.breakfast at the hotel was fine, and we had lunch and dinner there as well. lunch time staff were miserable and in the evening we did not book so had ages to wait for a table, crowded and noisy.we would have gone elsewhere but around 21:00 found most other places closing so it was hobsons choicethe best part of the stay were the free wine and eats in the lounge arond 17:00, absolutely great and a warm fire as well! very cosy and friendly. staff were always helpful. even when we were charged in error on our credit card after our return to uk it was sorted out with grace and effortlessly.we were only using it as a stopover and it met the bill on that front.

perfect location this was our first visit to san francisco and we were unsure which area to stay in. fishermans wharf was just perfect. the best western was excellently located, about 3 blocks from the sea front and within 5 minutes walk to pier 39.the room was abit on the small side, but ok for a 3 night stay. the front desk staff were very friendly with a dedicated concierge desk where guests could book excursions or just get information.the free wine and nibbles served between 5pm and 6pm were a lovely touch. at first we thought there must be a catch, but the reception area was packed every evening and it was a great place to talk to fellow travellers.the area felt safe to walk around at night as there were lots of people about with plenty of restaurants and bars to frequent.i would stay at this hotel again without question.
great hotel great location bed at tuscan

just the job my wife and i stayed for 3 nights in august and couldn't fault it for what we wanted.great location, the concierge guy was fantastic and there is a lovely restaurant attached to the hotel that does a great breakfast!no bar as such in the hotel but they have free wine tasting every day at 5p.m.!
great time in san fran down the powell-hyde line

excellent service, great location, good value we spent 2 nights and found the staff to be very friendly. the location is great, only 2 blocks from fisherman's wharf. the room was nice given this is not a 5 star property so our expectations were exceeded. overall, it was a great value and we would stay again.

lovely hotel my boyfriend and i stayed at this hotel on the 23rd august for 3 nights and had an enjoyable stay. it is in a great location, 5 minute walk to fisherman 's wharf promenade and 5 minute walk to a tram stop.we were given a room over looking the street which proved to be noisey. the reception staff were very accommodating and said the hotel was fully booked but first thing in the morning they would move our luggage to a room over looking the courtyard. this room was alot quiter and you could also open the windows as apposed to the room on street level.the complimentry tea and biscuits in the morning were very good and the restaurant ajoined to the hotel was very pleasant.the hotel was clean, in a good location and we would reccommend it to other travelors.

great stay completed a 3 night stay at the end of september, at the tuscan inn - which was excellent! great location. room was great - this was an outside room - so a bit of expected street noise - but not obtrusive. staff were knowledgeable and friendly. the concierge staff - exceptional and extremely helpful - right from suggestions on transportation/excursion options to recommending an amazing restaurant.

lovely stay at the tuscan inn this hotel seems to get very mixed reviews, particularly about the reception desk staff. i can only think that some of the staff are very good and some equally bad, since our experience was a very positive one. we were greeted warmly and asked how we had enjoyed our stay on leaving. both check in (when we were able to check in very early) and check out were fine and friendly. we have stayed at this hotel once before, a few years ago, so knew that the rooms were not particularly large. on this occasion our room was quite small, but extremely nice, although it did contain the smallest wardrobe i had ever seen! the hotel is very well situated, 5 minutes walk from fishermans wharf, shops, restaurants and cable cars etc. we were fortunate to get an inside (or courtyard) room, so were not disturbed by noise at all (except for 1 night when the fridge went mad!) we had a problem with the ac whilst we were there, but a very friendly and helpful maintenance man came within minutes of reporting it, and had it fixed at the touch of a button. valet parking is, in my view, unreasonably high at $38 per night, but again we knew this before we arrived so can't really complain. the best point about this hotel is the wonderful restaurant attached to it - cafe pescatore. both breakfast and evening meal were excellent - it is very well used, so bookings are advised for the evening. the late afternoon free wine reception was a really nice touch and we enjoyed this very much. so once again, we enjoyed a lovely stay at this hotel and will almost certainly go back when we next visit sf.

disappointed in front desk staff and room size we were anticipating a special stay for our anniversary trip.the front desk staff couldnéˆ¥??› even be bothered to greet us hello. she took our confirmation information and was annoyed that we didn't have an additional copy to give her. the room was clean and nicely decorated but very small. the view from our 4th floor window was of two outside building walls, but it was very quiet. my husband talked with the concierge, who he found very helpful. the daily coffee and newspaper in the lobby were nice to have in the early morning. the location is great, only a few blocks from the wharf. when we checked-out, the front desk clerk didnéˆ¥??› even bother to ask about our stay, which is very unusual. fortunately, the hotel we stayed at in monteray more than made up for our disappointing experience at this hotel.

lovely boutique hotel in convenient location having stayed at the argonaut on a previous trip, we were interested to see how the tuscan would compare. it did not disappoint and cost less for our 4 day stay. the location is fantastic - a 5 minute walk to the wharf and close to bus and trolley stops.having read previous reviews, we requested a courtyard room. we were given a room on the 4th floor with a view of a partially constructed building. we were not not concerned about the lack of view as we did not intend spending much time in our room but we did wonder whether there would be any early morning noise. our concerns were unfounded as we did not hear a sound.the room was a nice size and beautifully furnished. the bed was comfortable and the bathroom was clean with a nice selection of toiletries. there was a fully-stocked fridge with snacks and drinks. although we didn't use it, there was free internet access in the room. we did however make use of the pc/internet access available in the lobby without cost.the staff at the front desk could not have been more helpful and whilst we did not avail his services, the concierge always seemed to be busy with guests giving info and advice.the wine reception is a good way to wind down at the end of a busy day sightseeing and also to meet and share experiences with other guests. there was also a gentleman offering massage at this time and we met a few people who had enjoyed his services.upon checking-in, we were told that we would receive complementary continental breakfast for each morning of our stay. we do not usually rate these well but this was really nice - a large dish of fresh fruit, croissant or a muffin, juice and coffee. we also ate dinner at the hotel restaurant (cafe pescatore) one night. the food and service were both excellent.the only negative point was that when we booked our airport transfer through the hotel, we were charged $10 more than the going rate.all in all, we would recommend a stay at the tuscan and would definitely stay there again.

good value in heart of fishermans wharf the hotel was nice. the rooms were nice. no complaints. close to public transport and walking distance to restaraunt. this was probably not the best pick for us as we don't like tourist areas and fishermans wharf if one big tourist service. the food and drink prices in the area were outrageous.summary: best place to stay in a tourist trap. especially if you don't have a car.

charming and comfortable! i originally requested a courtyard room but since we checked in around 11 a.m. the front desk person said one would be available around 3 p.m. but they had a 4th floor room facing the street available immediately. i am a very light sleeper so iéˆ¥??’l admit i was apprehensive about having a room facing the street. we were pleased that the room was very nice and a decent size for the three of us plus it had a great view of coit tower, the transamerica building and a partial view of alcatraz through the bay window. the street noise can get loud but we already knew it would be since it is a street-side window in a busy tourist area. i also brought a sound machine which pretty much drowns out most of the annoying noises so i did manage to sleep very well. the mini fridge was filled with the snacks drinks but we rearranged things so we could put our own bottles in there. the fridge made no noise at all, the a/c worked fine although we only used it once because it was cool enough for us. our 11 year old son said that the sofa bed was not comfortable but that is normal for most sofa beds and he slept soundly every night anyway. our king size bed was comfy, but i thought it should have had king sized pillows as well instead of three standard size ones. the lighting was good which my husband really appreciated because he did a lot of reading during our down time. the bathroom was an adequate size. the sink area is a bit small but there is a small glass shelf above the toilet and one shelf under the sink where hotel towels and a blow dryer are stored but there is enough room for a couple of toiletry bags. the bath has one of those large rain shower heads which we loved and it was so quiet too! the shower curtain rod curves outward to allow more éˆ¥?¸†lbowéˆ¥?room which we really liked. as most hotels in the city, parking is expensive so unless you really need a vehicle itéˆ¥??? cheaper to just buy a muni passport during your stay. there is a nice clock/radio which also has a cd player. we couldnéˆ¥??› figure out how to change the time on it so we just called front desk to request a wake up call each morning. the hotel is charming and comfortable, and the staff is great. the location is hard to beat with a safeway, trader joeéˆ¥???, borders, world market and the cable car all within a block of this hotel. pier 39 is just a short 5-10 minutes away. we were sort of sad to leave as we transferred to another hotel at union square for the second part of our stay. if we were to stay in the fishermanéˆ¥??? wharf area, i would absolutely stay at the tuscan inn again!

great hotel this was a wonderful hotel. after reading some of the bad reviews, we started to worry about staying here. our worries washed away the moment we reached the hotel. the staff was amazing, and went out of their way to help us. the coffee and treats in the moring was amazing. the wine and treats at night were great also, nice touch. we took the advice from other reviewers and requested a court-yard side room. glad we did, it was very quite. some say the rooms are small, but ours wasn't that tiny. a normal size hotel room compared to other hotel rooms we have stayed in, besides we didn't spend much time in the room when there is so much to do around san francisco.i will stay here again if i ever get the chance to go back to san francisco.

helpful staff and great location this hotel is in a convenient location. it is within walking distance to the wharf, as well as the pier that sails boats to alcatraz. there are many public transportation options including the cable cars, the trolley line and bus service. it is within easy walking distance to china town and sits within the city's italian neighborhood. the hotel is across the street from a dollar rental car drop off, so you can rent a car at the airport, tour the area and then drop the car off when you get into the city. the hotel does have parking, but it is expensive and hard to get around the city while driving. the hotel itself had attractive common areas. the rooms were small, very small. they were, however clean and well equipped. the staff at the hotel more than made up for the tiny rooms. they were extremely helpful and would go out of their way to meet your every demand. the consigliore was extremely knowledgeable and very helpful. if you are looking for an inexpensive hotel to stay at where the staff will make your tour of their city a good experience, this is it.

great location! my wife and i stayed two nights to kick off our honeymoon. the staff was very friendly and we really enjoyed their dinner recommendations. the hotel was clean, and the evening wine hour was a nice touch. the parking was steep (over $40/day after taxes), so if i had to do it again i would have parked 1/2 block north for about half of that. overall, we would highly recommend this hotel as it is two block from the warf, dining, etc. mm

would not recommend it i am not a hotel snob - i don't mind a little noise, a little bit of dirt, etc. , but given the fairly strong review for this place, i was very disappointed.first, from day one our bathroom had a urine smell that never went away. otherwise the bathroom was decent enough - decent temperature and decent water pressure.the room was loud loud loud. we were on the fourth floor and could literally hear conversations on the street, with our windows shut. the ac did not seem very accurate or effective and do not book a room with a sleeper sofa. don't get me going on the noise the fridge made - it sounded like a jet plane every time the motor shifted. i finally had to buy sleeping pill across the street to try to sleep through all of this.then my last morning, i got to hear a heated argument between the reception desk and the police. the police were investigating something that had happened and staff would not cooperate so the police got very annoyed...all this in front of guest.on a positive note, we did like having a trader joe's right behind the hotel and used the mini bar to store our goods.l also enjoyed the morning coffee in the lobby and the free wine. but not enough to every bring me back here.

good hotel stayed at this hotel for three days and then moved down the street to the hyatt(also reviewed the hyatt) for three days on our trip.this hotel was clean and in a excellent location to everything.the cable cars were one block behind the hotel,waterfront was two blocks in front of the hotel and the #10 bus to att ballpark was right across the street from the main entrance.we arrived early in the morning and tried to check in and the front desk staff said they would have a room cleaned asap for us.we left and came back two hours later and room was still not ready.we had tickets to a 12:45pm giants game and were hoping to get our room before going to the game.we were having a casual conversation with the concierge and mentioned this fact to him,he then said he'd see what he could do and had us checked into our room in minutes.the front desk staff didn't seem to care but the concierge who took care of us was great(there were two of them working different days)he also had many suggestions and tips for us about the bay area.the only other negative and its a small one, was the size of the rooms,they are tiny but were cleaned well and were ready when we returned every day.

good location, great value a good location if you want to be walking distance to sights and transportation. the rooms were very nice, clean and comfortable. the 2-room suite was a little crowded, too much furniture, nicely done otherwise. it's walking distance to many sights,, as well as the cable car line,and the trolleys. very convenient. every day in the lobby: a very nice complimentary coffee and biscotti in the morning, and a wine tasting in the evening. wifi was included if you have your own laptop, otherwise internet available in the lobby. the highlight of this hotel for us was the service offered by the staff, particularly the two concierges on duty while we were there. their service was of the level and knowledge i would expect at at 5-star hotel. i had also called ahead for some information regarding bilingual tours (information i had a very hard time finding on the internet) , and everything was taken care of for us before we arrived.

nice, but has it's drawbacks the best thing about this hotel is the close proximity to fisherman's wharf. the lobby is nice, and the staff was very friendly. the cons about this place is the $38(plus $5.32 tax) a night parking fee. the room was nice (king bed) although smaller than most, and the sink area was poorly designed (functionality) and small. i don't think i would stay here again.

experienced the good and the bad similar to some other disgruntled reviewers here i was assigned a different room than i had booked. there were three of us and i had booked a two double bed room and had a confirmation to prove it. i had chosen this hotel for that particular reason as i was having difficulty getting a two bed room at nearby wharf hotels. i was given a king room with a cot on check-in. after a few trips by the clerk back to the manager who remained out of site i was told i had not booked a double bed room but a double occupancy room which wasn't true. they said they noticed we had three people so had automatically provided a cot to our room, i was told they were full and there were no other rooms available. when we got to our room the cot was already there but due to the small room i had to re-arrange furniture to get it to fit, in doing so having to re-assemble their cheap particle board table. the room faced a side street, the street directly below became very active at 5 am with motorcycles in particular in addition to trucks noisily heading up the street. i'm a sound sleeper normally and nothing wakes me so this was just a sign of how noisy it was. i managed to get switched to a two double bed room for our next couple of nights and experienced what all the good reviewers must have. the room was significantly larger, still small but liveable, and although still on the 3rd floor it faced the wharf and what i would have thought was the busier street but the traffic was much quieter and i didn't hear much at all the next two mornings. the valet's were a little slow and i hated the vulture baggage guy. i don't have a problem being helped up to the room although i;m fine doing it myself. this guy immediately put all my bags on the cart while i was pre-occupied with the valet but then while i was trying to correct the problems with the room at check-in he was impatiently trying to get us to hurry up in spite of me telling him just to leave the bags. the location is great, i opted for a fisherman's wharf stay for vacation having stayed near union square on business in the past and i'm glad i did as it was easy walking distance to chinatown and the touristy area of the wharf. i'd be leaving a better rating if i were given the 2nd room on arrival but due to the mix-up and the fact others have experienced the same i'd avoid this hotel in the future opting not to take the chance of another mix-up.

a brilliant start to our vacation myself and my wife stayed at the tuscan for 3 nights last month, this was our first stop off to a 3 week vacation in the usa and what great a start,....... a superb hotel with staff so helpful/efficient, the food at the pescadora restaurant is a must, and to be quite honest better than most of the other places we ate at on the wharf whilst there, one of which being quoted to being the best ,......... but to us a tourist trap and a big rip off. name given on request.location of the hotel was ideal to explore the know attractions, with just a 2 min walk to the wharf / ferries and the famous cable cars, which transported you to union square /lombard st etc..afternoon wine tasting was a cool touch by the hotel staff, and proved very popular with most of the guest including us.had a problem with air-con in the room but within minutes of reporting it to front desk plans were in place to sort, we returned later ot find the room chilled to satisfaction and even a personal note left by the engineer.would stay here everytime sf

check out the free wine our room was small by american standards but really comfortable, well appointed, and quiet. the location is ideal but the car park is really expensive, so if you are ending a trip here, take your hire car back after you have unloaded your luggage and get a taxi to the airport. you can walk or ride the buses in sf, its fun. the lobby area was really pleasant and the free wine (or coffee) gets you talking to other guests. staff were pleasant and helpful. don't pay full price there are lots of cheap deals.

absolutely loved it this hotel is awesome..we stayed here for our honeymoon and they had a bottle of bubbly on ice waiting for us in our room..nice touch.the staff were very helpful with suggesting places to eat and with directions of how to get to places eg.baseball.the room was nice. the house keeping ladies were pleasant and always greeted us when we walked past.this hotel is in a perfect location. it is only several blocks from fishermans wharf, not far from the cable cars to union square.the free morning hot cocoa and coffee was nice before our daily excursions.

enjoyed the tuscan inn the tuscan inn was in a great location a few minutes from fisherman's wharf. it was easy to walk to north beach as well. we didnt' have a car, so we liked the fact it was a short walk to the cable car stop. the room was small, but clean, quiet, and suited our needs. the afternoon wine and cheese was a nice bonus as was the free internet. the concierge at the hotel was extremely helpful and nice. he checked into baseball tickets, offered dinner reccomendations, and answered all of our san francisco questions. i would definitely stay at this hotel again in the future. it was a great base to explore san francisco.

a nice surprise..... what can you say about a place that does not dazzle but delivers solid consistent performance.. the price was reasonable based on others in the vicinity and it does a good job. the room was clean, the staff was great and it was close to pier 39 and fisherman's wharf (easy walk). i'd stay there again. the restaurant looks nice but i'm not a big italian food fan so i bypassed the place. i went with average expectations and came away pleasantly surprised.

fisherman's wharf overrated although we enjoyed our stay at the tuscan inn it wasn't all i'd hoped it would be. probably because i was so disappointed in the fisherman's wharf area itself. it was really dirty, crowded, crime-ridden and touristy. the food was bad and overpriced in general. the only place i really liked were some of the places on pier 39, but i wouldn't eat at a sit-down restaurant here. i would stay in north beach or sausalito next trip. food in north beach was fabulous!.as far as the hotel, the room was clean but small. beds very comfortable - we had a king with pull-out sofa for our 12-yr-old son. nice big flat screen tv. they comped us an in-room movie when i reported that it was jerky. bathroom shower curtain reeked of mildew enough to smell up the room. i should have had them take it down and wash it, but probably got used to it. staff was great. concierge very helpful. location was convenient. grocery store and trader joe's just down the block. pretty close to north beach and cable car stops. one afternoon, a car window was broken right outside the hotel so they could steal the contents of the car. lots of panhandlers. one lady reported cash was stolen out of her car by the valet parkers, but that was too stupid of her to leave it in the car. parking at $45 a night was outrageous, but probably worth it to keep your car safe.

a good hotel san francisco was our final stop on a drive up highway 1. my wife and two friends stayed here for four nights in july 08. this was our third visit to the city but the first stay at the tuscan inn and we would strongly recommend it. we were surprised and delighted when, on arrival, we were given tokens for free continental breakasts. this was unexpected as we hadn't been informed about this by our travel agent. the hotel has a certain individual style that distinguishes it from the sheratons, holiday inns, etc. the reception area is compact and during the free evening wine sampling gets quite busy. the free morning coffee is also well appreciated and attended. we had a rear room which at first disappointed me but the air-con was much quieter than that of our friends who also had a bit of bother with noise from the street. the rooms were a little bit tired and with the simple expedient of renewing the wallcovering would show a great improvement. the bed was comfortable and the rooms and bathrooms were kept clean and although the refrigerators are honour bars the hotel is happy for you to chill your own drinks in them. we found the reception staff, maids and porters friendly and helpful. we have now stayed in three hotels in fisherman's wharf but the tuscan inn represents a good comprise of location, cost and facilities. oh and before i forget, the hotel restaurant el pescatore serves excellent food at reasonable prices. i would recommend a stay at the tuscan inn when visiting san francisco.

right position to visit sfo the hotel is in the right position to visit the city. the price is really convenient. remember to ask for having a courtyard room ... the risk is to have a room in the street.

tuscan is great location three friends and i just returned from tuscan inn, fisherman'swharf, in san francisco. we booked our reservation with southwest vacations. we had a great time and could havestayed longer. the room was very nice, and had a nice bathroom. we did have a wall view from the window, but since i was not in the room except to sleep i did not make a big fuss. it was nice having the safeway store across the street to get snacks. i enjoyed the hot chocolate every morning in the lobby. the fireplace in the lobby was very pretty, and the courtyard flowers were beautiful. the location was perfect. alot of other hotels were more expensive but we were very happy at the tuscan. the desk clerks were nice and helpful. my friend celebrated his birthday there!we walked to a lot of places. it was very convenient. we did not have a car, hotel parking is expensive. we had a tower tourbus pick us up every morning at the hotel and they did anexcellent job. also plenty of busses and taxis. everyone there was friendly to us. we had a great and exciting trip.

loved it! i spent two nights at this hotel back in august of 2007 at the beginning and end a trip from san francisco to monterey. we booked the standard two queen room and were very happy with our stay. the room was wonderful with great beds, a nice bathroom and we also had an excellent view of coit tower as well. the location only 2 blocks from fisherman's wharf made it a perfect base for exploring the area, we were able to walk or take public transportation everywhere we went. if we hadn't been driving to monterey the next day i wouldn't have rented a car. there's no need when staying in this hotel. the valet parking was very convenient and seemed secure as it is attached to the hotel. a lot of hotel parking garages/lots are not on the same premises as the hotel in the area. the restaurant located in the hotel was excellent and the morning coffee/biscotti was really nice as well. would love to stay there again if we're in the area.
no problems great location to fishermans wharf. hotel was excellent. staff great and helpful. fishermans wharf tacky.

ok but not as good as our last stay i have stayed at this hotel in the past and liked it very much. this time, i was not very impressed. the room was small, with a king bed, and a truly claustrophobic bathroom. two bath towels for two adults is just skimpy, and when you close the door to the tub/toilet combination, there is no room to breathe. the bed was comfortable. we were awakened by a loud racket at 0730 - construction nearby. there is no place to conveniently charge phone/blackberry/laptop without crawling around on the floor. why do hotels not install convenient plugs for guests to recharge the devices with which we are all travelling? morning coffee quite delicious, but when we checked out at 0545, we were never offered any to drink. would it have been so difficult to offer us a little coffee, as it was probably ready by then? location is good.

perfect locatin for exploring the city stayed at the tuscan inn over the fourth of july weekend after using priceline before christmas to book a room (although i didn't actually think i would get one for only $75/nt over a holiday weekend!).check in was quick and my boyfriend and i were given a queen room on the fourth floor facing the street. my boyfriend's first response was wow, this is a tiny room, but it was what i was expecting considering the location and that this is only a 3-star property. it was in fact a small room (a king size bed would not have fit) with a tiny closet and 2 drawers for storing clothes. good thing we only packed carry on luggage and didn't have much to put away!the room was always clean and the maid staff was friendly, saying hello and have a nice day as you passed. we were frequently in and out of the room to change clothes or take a nap and never walked in on a maid (or were walked in on ourselves). one day we had the do not disturb sign on the door before the maid had come so we could rest, and when we finally stepped out for about an hour, we changed the sign for maid service and everything was perfect when we returned!one bad part about the room was that some street noise traveled up, although we were only really disturbed one night when there was a car parked on the street playing loud music with people around it laughing and talking loudly.pros at the hotel:staff - very friendly and helpful. we had to send and receive several faxes during our stay and they were always happy to help. we used the concierge to book theater tickets, which worked flawlessly, and we also called the front desk around midnight our last evening and asked them to arrange an airport shuttle the next day, which they did the following morning when the shuttle company opened.amenities - while this hotel isn't a luxury property, they have some nice touches like marble bathrooms, mini bar, room service and an evening wine reception every day (which many people attended). the restaurant attached to the hotel is nice, with a great little bar area and friendly bartenders. the restaurant breakfast menu is pretty minimal, but it does the trick.location - this is the best part of the hotel. two blocks from pier 41, one block to the f line street car two blocks to the cable car. this was an awesome area to gain access to many different parts of the city without trying too hard.overall, i would say this room was not worth the rack rate of $250+ per night, but it was far beyond my expectations at the priceline bargain rate!

that one suite was ready and the other would be an hour or so. when we got to the suite that was ready we found that it was not a one king bed suite but a two bed suite.i rang reception and spoke to a great experience we stayed here for 4 nights for $125 from hotwire. the first night we were on the street, and could here motorcycles racing all night. we complained, and were moved to a quiet room for the duration of our stay. on the morning of the second day my daughter had stomach cramps and we had to go to the emergency room. we left at 6:30 am, and the front desk and valet had a cab ready with instructions on where to go by the time we came down the elevator. we were very impressed with the service we received. the location for tourists can not be beat. you are 2 blocks from the wharf, the mason line cable car is right behind the hotel, the f line street car is a block away, and pier 39 and the alcatraz tour is with in walking distance. there is a trader joes, safeway, and walgreens close by too.the rooms were nice, comfortable, and clean. the shower was great. i am still missing the strong coffee and biscotti we had for breakfast every morning. the next time we are in sf, we will be staying at the tuscan inn again.

bunch of criminals, be warned be aware - they do not honor their reservation guarantees.booked a most expensive room there a suite - more then $350 per night. they have charged a credit card, send an email - reservation guaranteed. upon arrival, we've been told that they have no room for us. and a manager on duty - gregory abdon has started lying to us. his first sentence was - the room is under maintenance. asked to show the room, which is under maintenance - refused. asked to speak to his supervisor - refused.his next version was - we do not guarantee the reservations - first come- first served. but what about the 'reservation guarantee' letter, i've got from them? next version was - well it is not the suite, which is under maintenance, but another room, but refused to show that room as well. next, we been told, that they have a replacement suite for us in a different hotel, in the different part of city, having no other choice, went there just to find out that was not a suite, but a regular room.bunch of liars the most funny part is they have placed us in $125 room (have a print out of it), still trying to charge $350 as for initial charge. had forced them to get all the charges reversed.by my opinion, that hotel is a bunch of criminals, trying to implement the following criminal scheme.1. overbook the most desirable hotel in the kimpton chain.2. move overbooked people to a different hotel in a different part of the city, within the chain, which is virtually empty.3. collect the same rate as for fisherman's wharf location.4. the child hotel in the different part of city returns fisherman's wharf's hotel part of the initial fee, and they simply collect a difference from the air.anyone with the same experience - i'll be glad to file a law suite against them.our well planned vacation has been ruined.be warned.

amazing find! i stayed at this hotel because of a booking on priceline. i got a great price on the hotel and was extremely happy with the hotel. first, it is in a fantastic location - blocks from fisherman's wharf and within walking distance to so many things! right from checking in, the staff was unbelievable! every single staff member we came into contact with was extremely helpful and very nice! the room was on the smaller side but there was definitely enough room for two of us. the coffee, tea and biscotti in the morning is very nice. i would highly recommend this hotel!!

loved it, but noisy! this hotel was wonderful in every way except it was noisy at night. our rooms faced the street rather than the courtyard and the traffic - especially the motorcycles - were loud all night long. you can drown out the noise with the fan, except if the fan is on then the air conditioner will cause it to go on an off, so you have the fan on and are too hot or the air on and intermittent noise. i suggest you request a room facing the courtyard (even numbered rooms, i think?) or pack a fan!very comfortable beds and rooms - nice decor!don't miss the 5 o'clock wine hour. this is a great italian tradition that matches the theme of the hotel.

great experience we have been planning this trip for a year. we used priceline to try to find us a 4 star hotel near the wharf. well we got a hotel . we arrived wondering what to expect and as soon as we arrived the staff made us feel welcomed .the 5 o'clock wine gathering in the lobby is terrific. rooms are clean,new, quiet, and relaxing.the concierge service is second to none. i highly recommend this hotel and even my call it a 5 star...

don't stay here- they charge $75 if you depart a day early on mult- night stay i was told that they required 24 hours to change dates of stay or cancel. i checked in and had planned on staying three nights. after the first night, i found out that i would be leaving one day early and told them -- more than 24 hours in advance -- that i would be leaving one day early. i was charged a $75 early departure fee. i will never stay here again and recommend you do not either.

great find in the city charming hotel, reasonably priced right at fisherman's wharf.in the same area as the radisson and the sheraton. when i walked in i immediately thought boutique hotel not best western. it reminded me of the napa river inn in napa, ca.they take the tuscan theme all the way. when you call the hotel they say buon giorno and play italian music while you are on hold. the valets are dressed like venetian gondoliers. the lobby is reminiscent of italy. lovely potted flowering plants and trees fill the view from the picture window in the lobby, while a welcoming fire is lit in the lobby fireplace.... even though the day we were there, it was sunny and a pleasant 78. the next day was windy and the fog was blowing in, so the fire was quite apropos. we arrived early - noonish, and check-in is not til 3 p.m. they were very accomodating and allowed us to park the car in their garage (added charge at all hotels in sfo) and leave our bags in a secure room until check-in, so we could go out and start our day in sfo. they upgraded us to a suite and told us they would call on our cell phone when the room was ready. they called within an hour! the room was spacious, very clean and tastefully decorated. they could have made the lr area smaller to accomodate the king size bed in the br better - not much room between the bed and the tv stand to squeeze by. be sure to ask not to be put in the rooms right above the driveway/entry. at 6 a.m. they roll out the dumpster and the garbage truck comes roaring up to empty it (clang, bang) and then backs up to leave (beep, beep, beep). a half hour later the neighboring business hauls their dumpster out for pick-up and another garbage truck comes along.... a minor disturbance in an otherwise great hotel.overall i would rate this hotel as excellent.

ok, but....... i'm not quite as impressed with the place as most seem to be. to begin, i'm more of what you'd call a budget traveler, and although i got this place at a good price via priceline, there are some things to consider. first, the biggest gotcha is the mandatory valet parking. with taxes, it set me back over $43; and for me, that's rather stiff. the room was clean, but on the small side, especially in width. if someone was sitting at the desk (located at the center of the room in front of the bed), there is no room for another person to get by.comfortable bed, but nothing special. no pool, spa or workout room that i could find. it is centrally located to the wharf, within reasonable walking distance of pier 39, etc. not trying to bad mouth the tuscan, it is a nice place to stay, and if you're not put off by the valet parking, you shouldn't be too disappointed.

great hotel my son, his girlfriend, and i stayed four nights recently at tuscan inn. the location is great, the hotel is very clean and nicely decorated. rooms are small, but they have everything you need. coffee in the mornings in the lobby, and wine in the afternoons are a nice touch. adjoining restaurant was really good. tourists from all over the usa and world were there. concierge desk stayed very busy. i enjoyed my four nights there and i will definitely stay there again.

pleasantly surprised my wife and i took a weekend trip up to san francisco and wanted to stay at a place that was cheap and close to fisherman's wharf. this place did not disappoint.our room was only $99 per night through some promotion found on travelzoo. i figure you get what you pay for... but the room was actually pretty nice. there wasn't much of a view (i think the window faced the adjacent building) but the room was fairly large, clean, and the room (as well as the whole floor) was nice and quiet. there was a very private feel to the hotel. they also had a staffmember serve soda and wine in the loungy lobby area in the early evening, which was a nice bonus. the surrounding area of the hotel, to our surprise, seemed safe and relatively clean. but the location was great... just a few blocks from the touristy parts of the wharf. would definitely recommend this hotel for your next brief stay in the bay.

great hotel we just stayed at the tuscan inn for about 5 nights. it was definetely worth it. we had a great room, clean and spacious enough for 2 adults and 2 small kids. and the price was fantastic. we first booked thru hotels.com and thought we got a great deal..our sf itinerary changed a bit, and we needed another 2 nights at the tuscan inn, and the hotel said they would match our hotels.com price, they actually gave us a lower price than that! wow! all the staff we encountered were super friendly and the hotel location is great..enjoy your stay there, i'm sure you'll love it.

really enjoyed this hotel i really enjoyed the atmosphere of the hotel. it was reasonable and close to fisherman's wharf. the hotel offered coffee, tea, and biscotti in the morning and wine and an appetizer in the late afternoon. the staff were helpful and efficient. i had not stayed in a best western in a while, and i was very pleased.
fantastic stay the delicious clam chowder

overall excellence! arriving mid-afternoon, after a rather fast shuttle ride from the airport to fishermans wharf, we entered the hotel lobby, and was quite surprised. from outside, the building didn't really shout out to us. checking in was easy, with very friendly, helpful front desk staff. our room was upgraded complimentary. the room was clean, quite large with a very large bed, plus room for a sofa, table, large tv and extra chair. the bathroom was clean, well lit, and always well stocked with shampoo etc and towels. the bed was really comfortable, and we had a good nights sleep every night. the only odd thing was the bathroom door and room door opened outwards into the room and hallway respectively. our room faced the small courtyard in the centre of the hotel, not the street, so noise was kept to a minimum.the complimentary wine in the evening was a great bonus as was the tea, coffee and hot chocolate in the morning. not very far at all to the seafront. only 2 blocks!!safeway and walgreens across the road for those little snacks,drinks and souveneirs. denny's about 3 blocks away! great!! there is plenty to do here in fishermans wharf. would recommend to anyone to stay here, and we would stay here again.

fantastic hotel fantastic choice, 10 days at the tuscan, location is wonderful only a couple of blocks from pier 39. the coffee and biscotti in the morning were a nice touch, and the wine tasting every evening became a must get back to the hotel for. room spacious 2 double beds gave us plenty of room, the beds were comfortable and the bathroom was a good size. there is a bar up the road if you are a sports fan at the grand hyatt which is worth a visit. overall a fantastic time was had there and i look forward to returning a+++++++++++++

perfect location and lovely inn our room was absolutely lovely, although dresser drawers and closet were small. the bed was very comfortable. windows don't open - so no fresh air. internet is free. i needed something printed two different times, and after following their directions i went to the front desk and was able to get it right away. there is a small refrigerator, but it was stocked so very little space for our own goodies. the location is perfect - two blocks from fisherman's wharf and only a block to the street car and trolley. the bathroom was large and included a mounted makeup mirror. towels were large and soft. the shampoo, conditioner, soap and lotion they provide is heavenly! coffeemaker in the room and when regular coffee wasn't left one day, it was delivered immediately when i requested it. lots and lots of restaurants nearby. we had a wonderful time and would definitely stay here again.

tuscan inn was incredible i cannot say enough good things about this hotel. i was on a strict budget for my trip to sf and was thrilled to get this hotel for $59 on priceline (off season, and between conventions, i did my homework). the hotel is perfectly located in my opinion: close to fisherman's wharf, but away from the crowds; within a very short walk to north beach (an absolute must see); literally around the corner from the cable cars (buy a multi day pass-much cheaper); stores and restaurants closeby; excellent transportation connections besides the cable car. the hotel itself is elegant, but not stuffy. one of the friendliest desk/concierge staffs i've encountered (they made a luggage tag, mapped out driving directions, gave bus/trolley directions, gracious with special requests, wine cheese hour etc). the rooms are abit smallish (absolutely typical of sf), but immaculately maintained, and tastefully decorated, with excellent bathroom facilities. one stand out example: the painter who was touching up nicks on the hall mouldings, cheerfully greeted me in the morning on my way out. i am a budget traveller who has travelled all over the world, and this hotel is one of my top five picks for best value (just don't pay rack rate). this hotel is managed by the kimpton folks and they do a great job for the price.

terrific stay at the tuscan inn tuscan inn has it all, exellant location,very close to public transport, very clean, impeccable, friendly service and a supermarket opposite. our king bed room was quite overlooking the courtyard and the decor lovely. the complimentary toiletries, coffee and biscotti and the happy hour drinks each eveing just go to prove they go the extra mile.we found a great breakfast place just around the corner in taylor st, called darren's cafe, good prices with excellant food and service. i would not hesitate to stay here again and highly recommend it.shona of sydney/london
would stay here again, eventhough we had an issue our cute, small room

reasonable value for money hotels in sf are not cheap,and room sizes are not overly big,so a pretty tiny room for $180 was no big surprise. valet parking for $40 per night seems a bit steep,but at least the service was efficient and quick.overall the tuscan inn is a nice hotel. very clean,well maintained,with efficient,if not overly friendly service. the couple of faults with room features were fixed very quickly,which was a nice change from the interminable wait often suffered in european properties.the hotel makes a big thing of the coffee/bisc service in the morning,and this is quite nice. i'd say that,as far as the evening (5 to 6 ) wine service is concerned,if you happen to be in the hotel,it's fine. but not worth rushing back from a day out for.breakfast was ok,but expensive. much better option is pats cafe,just round the corner nr the cable car terminus.

nice hotel! this hotel is close to where you want to be. great room! everything was clean, good staff...the hotel is in very good condition. the prize for vallet parking is steep but i think you can expect that anywhere you go in san francisco. would stay here again!

beautiful hotel wow it was absolutely beautiful. easy walking distance to all the attractions at fishermans wharf.really enjoyed the friendliness of the staff and the big rooms.very clean and a wonderful atmosphere.complimentary drinks are provided each evening for an hour.trolley car was just down the street and plenty of supermarkets in the area to pick up supplies.we had the most wonderful time and as arnie says........i will be back !

great stay have just returned from a 5 day stay -we are a family of 4 with 2 daughters aged 15 and 20. we stayed in a family room which was not enormous but plenty big enough for us all. shower/bathroom was good with good shower and plenty of space.we had a fridge and television and coffee making facilities. beds were very comfortable and although we were at street level it was not noisy at all.the free coffee and biscotti in the morning kept us going until breakfast. we used the hollywood cafe-turn left out of hotel and it is a short distance up on the other side of the road opposite the hilton. the breakfasts are brilliant and cheap.evening wine hour from 5-6 was also good -free wine and nibbles and a chance to talk to other guests about places to visit , eat etc.rooms were well cleaned and reception staff helpful.take a jacket -it was sunny but windy on the wharf-we were also glad of a scarf.it meant we did not have to buy a sf fleece like a lot of other people!our best bits were a visit to the coit tower, lunch at the cheesecake factory at the top of macey's, riding the cable cars, the bus tour and exploring the wharf area as well as the shops downtown. we walked a lot which meant we could eat the fantastic pancakes every day and plenty of cheesecake.we felt totally safe wherever we went.we all found plenty to do and had a great time -we flew to las vegas after that!

very nice --would recommend to my friends we read reviews on many hotels looking for above average accomodations in a convenient location. the tuscan inn fit that well. very comfortable stay and got a good deal on orbitz to boot. only drawback is room size. we started w/ a king w/ sofa bed for my son but we were tripping on each other so we upgraded to a suite. we also moved from a street view room to a courtyard as the street noise was extremely loud. staff was some of the nicest i have encountered in a long time. the concierge here was 1st class. would highly remonmmend this hotel.

great hotel great hotel, nice location for everything! very clean, get a glass of wine free between 56pm in the lobby. get an internal top floor room if you can, no noise from traffic or people upstairs. there's no view anyway so best to get some peace and quiet (no that it a noisy hotel anyway). also book alcatraze trip as soon as you get there (from pier 31 i think it was) as it gets busy days in advance.

great rooms; great staff; great hotel just got back from a recent trip to san francisco. stayed at the tuscan inn near fisherman's wharf and it was excellent. tuscan inn has exceptionally helpful and friendly staff. there was never a time where i saw the concierge desk unstaffed. in fact, the concierges seemed to be the busiest people in the hotel; always assisting someone with a reservation, recommendation, a jogging route, etc. the hotel had nice, well-decorated, fairly-modern rooms. some of the common spaces are a little worn but our king guest room was very comfortable. ok... this is fisherman's wharf so there are some obnoxious, tourist-trap activities around. but.. the hotel is also only a few blocks from north beach where we found some great little restaurants and cafes. would definitely return to sfo and to the tuscan inn!

excellent location, friendly staff, clean and pleasant rooms i was forwarned to expect small rooms, but i thought the tuscan inn had rooms typical or even generous for an urban hotel -exceeded my expectations. our family of 2 adults and one teen was comfortable with two double beds. the hotel has recently been refurbished, and was very clean and comfortable. our 4th floor room was street side so there was some traffic noise at night, but not so much that it bothered any of us. all the staff was excellent, but the concereige, clay, really went above and beyond to help us find our way around san fransisco. i was very delighted with the pleasant and professional hotel staff all the way from the doormen to the desk clerks. the hotel has a wine reception from 5-6pm every evening which is a nice touch. the location was excellent - near the waterfront, the aquarium, pier 39, giradelli square etc and very easy walk to cable cars, trolleys and bus routes. we didn't rent a car and instead bought a 3 day transit pass for 18pp which saved alot of money considering our frequent use of the cable cars especially. it was very easy to get around using the transit system. we had a wonderful time in sf and the tuscan inn was a part of it.

location, location, location stayed march 14 - 17, 2008. the tuscin inn is a great hotel depending your room location. location is the best. everything is in walking distance, shopping, etc. the weather is great, just a little cold and windy but no rain; there were sunny days on our trip. walgreens was a great store and purchase clothing less than the vendor on the street were offering. i had a government rate which was very good for the room selection. we had a double beds for the first 2 nights and a suite for the next two nights. the room are exact has they appear on the wedsite. made our reservations on best western.com. the room 454 had double beds and no view. the closet are very small but the room was comfortable. when checking in remember to asked for the bar key so you can store beverages in the refrigerator. room 402, was the suite, large bathrooom, no closet space, nice room, fireplace, but the sofa bed was terrible. in addition, the heater did not work, so i had to order additional blankets to get warm...even received a slight cold upon return. room 402 did have a view, they were willing to change room but we had already uppacked and did not realize the heater was not working until our 2nd night. did not asked for a discount; they told me to contact manager who was unable at the time each time i inquired. the corceige was excellent and some of the hotel staff did care and others did not (may be the government rate). the coffee in the morning was great; did not attend the wine party. did not eat at the restaurant, but room service was great. if you book a room, asked for the courtyard view if possibe. location is everything at this site; everything you need is right in the area. pier 39 and other activities are in walking distance. do you go the aquarium; not worth the price.grayline tours were great. took the $10 per person on the ride around the bay (best price). the battleship was a great tour also. did not do alcaraz tour due to the kids. overall, the stay at the tuscan inn was great and would highly recommend due to the room service. there are other hotels in the area who do not offer room service. we traveled with 2 adults and 2 children.

loved the tuscan inn san francisco i am always concerned when i book a hotel on fishermans wharf in san francisco, as many are very run down. when i drove up to this hotel it was excellent. there were 2 doormen just waiting to help you. the hotel has been renovated in the past 2 years and it was great. the staff very polite smiling and helpful.the lobby was comfortable every evening, guests are welcome to the hosted evening wine and italian beer reception from 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m and always have italian roast coffee, tea and biscotti in the lobby. free high speed wireless internet access, which in san francisco most always has a charge. i will always come back to this hotel for business travel or for pleasure.i travel quite often and have stayed in many different hotels. right now this hotel is at the top of my list. i will always tell everyone to try it.

loved this hotel and location! great city for couples loved the location of this hotel! it was near the ocean- about 2 blocks away. location was also near pier 39 (shopping, sea lions, and marina), ghiradelli's chocolate factory, and alcatraz. lots of little shops nearby- very touristy. at pier 39 the shops were nicer with a great outdoor atmosphere. loved eating at bubba gump shrimp co.- as in forest gump. great shrimp, fish, chicken fingers, hushpuppies, etc with lots of windows to enjoy the ocean and marina. the gift shop is great, too, if forest gump is one of your favorite movies like mine. my husband and i went for our anniversary and it was perfect. the golden gate bridge is unbelievable! it just makes you happy inside seeing it. we walked across and back which was so nice to enjoy each other's company without toddlers wrapped around our legs. with this hotel we received a free 1 hour tour/cruise around alcatraz and down to the golden gate bridge. you also get 2 free transportation passes each day of your stay that we used for the trolley systems. their travel system is called the muni and includes the trolleys or the city buses. the drivers are a great help for any questions you have. we used the trolley and buses for the golden gate bridge. we loved the trolleys! you can just ride with no particular destination in mind to get a feel for the city. also great for going to the section of the city for the major shopping area (i can't remember what it's called but the area feels like new york city- very busy, hustle and bustle.) and remember the muni passes were free! we rented a car to go to napa valley to see the vineyards and muir woods to see the giant redwood trees. this was a nice little morning hike that my husband really enjoyed. whatever the weather says for your trip to san fran, take a heavy jacket/ coat. everybody that doesn't do this buys one at the little tourist shops. (smile) hotel was clean and a great price. however, don't count on the concierge for help. he was always covered up when we went by. this city is a must for any couple!

great stay!! great location, near lots of stuff to walk too. concierge was excellent!!! his name was clay, very helpful and spent lots of time with you. has a restraunt/bar in hotel, limited italian food, but nice to sit and have a few drinks. rooms nice, beds very comfortable!. would stay again.

a great hotel in a great location we stayed here for 3 nights on our way to new zealand.the reception staff were very welcoming and the room was large and well appointed.we were worried about walking around the area at night but there is no problem. it is 2 blocks from the wharf and the roads are wide and well lit. we walked all over the area in the evenings and didn't encounter any problems. the cable car is a couple of blocks away so from the hotel you can get around most of the tourist sights easily.breakfast is taken in their italian restaurant and it was very good. we also ate one evening meal here and again the food was good. we would definitely stay here again

couldn't have been better booked this on expedia on one of their 24 hour half-price specials. for $99, we had a room on the fourth floor with courtyard view. it was quiet and comfortable. both the bedroom and bathroom had plenty of room. tuscan inn is within walking distance of fisherman's wharf, ghiradelli square, lombard street, cable cars. the front desk was helpful in providing the $11 all-day cable car/f-line pass (otherwise it's $5 per one-way ride). the concierge was knowledgeable not only about where to eat but where to find the cheapest gas on the way to the airport. valet parking was $45 per night with tax, but that includes in and out privileges and my car was there whenever i needed it. next time we have a layover in san francisco, tuscan inn will be our first choice.

warm and comfortable stayed three nights and wish we could stay longer. the staff members were extra helpful, the room well decorated, detailed, clean, and bright. liked the wine, beer, and soft drinks happy hour, the proximity to all points of interest in fisherman's wharf, the cable cars, grocery stores, gym, etc. this is a real find. nice italian restaurant in hotel, too. watch out for steep parking rates of about $45 per night. this total includes the taxes and tips for mandatory valet parking.aside from the parking rate, you won't be disappointed.

loved the tuscan inn beautifully furnished rooms. was disappointed not to have a small refrigerator or a clock radio.maid service was excellent ! front desk and bell men were all very friendly and efficient. they gave out maps to help us find chinatown, union square, fisherman's wharf, pier 39, as well as point out bus routes.the flower boxes around the hotel and in the court yard were beautiful as well. we would stay here again.

will stay again we found a friendly staff through out the hotel great location,rooms were small but as pointed out to me all land is prime in the area and all places have small rooms. we had 4 adults and 2 double beds but so much to do in the area only used our room to sleep anyway. large clean bathrooms fully stocked with everything needed. all 4 of us said we would go back there again. what a nice clean friendly place to stay,

good experience we stayed for two nights (sat/sun) in mid-february. didn't notice any renovation noise, as noted by a few other reviewers. however, when we arrived at our room there was a maintenance worker there measuring the bathroom counter, so maybe they're doing work in some units.the tuscan theme, although not entirely successful in making you forget what continent you're on, made for a very pleasant and comfortable decor nonetheless. we had a standard king room (ask for courtyard view to avoid street noise) -- the room was small but it worked fine for a short stay. the room has a mini-fridge/bar. no breakfast provided other than coffee/tea and small biscotti pieces. they do host a wine/beer reception from 5-6pm every evening.the location is fabulous. walk in one direction, and you're at the bay looking for the golden gate bridge through the fog. walk in another direction, and you're soon on columbus avenue heading toward the italian neighborhood of north beach. walk in a third direction, and you'll be sipping ghiradelli hot chocolate very soon.for entertainment, i highly recommend the musical comedy currently at the pier 39 theatre: insignificant others. it's about 5 friends from ohio (3 straight women, 2 gay men) who all move to san francisco and help each other navigate through their new lives (and loves) in the city by the bay.

stay away during renos we stayed here for 4 nights in early/mid february, after much research online and in travel books. i thought that i had found accommodation that was both within our budget and of high quality. yes, there is construction going on, and it started every morning at 9:00am for us; if you will be gone by this time, and away until after supper, then there shouldn't be a problem, provided you have a room facing the courtyard (away from the busy street in front). issues we ran into:-didn't have the room as requested in my reservation, so they had to put me in a queen bed on day 1, then move to a king days 2-4.-the first night, we also had to be moved at 2:00am because our ventilation started clicking non-stop--repair person came, suggested we just move rooms. would have been ok, if not for:-construction at 9:00am each morning. heard it loud and clear on floors 2 and 4.-also, placed us in a king suite that was joined with another room via a private doorway; the noise from the other family with kids was evident as of 7am as well. but, we couldn't move again because there were no other rooms available with king.-showed up for breakfast in their restaurant at 10:31am--i'm not exaggerating--would not serve us, since they said they stop taking orders at 10:30am--the place had one other couple in it--could they afford to lose business over one minute? i guess so.perhaps i had higher expectations, or perhaps not...staff at front desk was fine, obviously the restaurant could use some work...rooms were clean, always done promptly. location was nice for getting all around the city; we mostly walked from place to place, even to and from downtown along the embarcadero.the reno's look to be in full swing; i would doubt anything will be winding down in the near future; i'd certainly call their front desk and make sure that there are no renovations being done prior to coming. happy travelling!

good location but teeny rooms we stayed at the best western tuscan inn for 2 nights in january. staff was pleasant, bellhops were more than happy to get us a cab. good location a few blocks from fisherman's wharf, if that's where you want to be. after strolling around the city, i thought a more fun neighborhood to stay in would have been italy. also, our room was so teeny tiny, we had to let each other pass by between the end of the bed and the desk, because there wasn't enough room for two people. i guess the price was good for the city, but the room was just too small.
