beware of jack-hammering renovations we booked our stay at the best western tuscan inn fisherman's wharf in san francisco based on it's #1 status on trip advisor and great review in frommer's san francisco 2007 travel guide. we booked directly with the hotel and called to confirm our reservation the night before. we were very pleased with the hotel's location right in the heart of fisherman's wharf/north beach...close to great restaurants (pat's cafe the buena vista), transportation (buses, trolleys, ferries), and the waterfront but what we weren't informed of was the on-going, messy noisy renovations (frommer's listed the property as having completed room renovations in 2005). there was no mention from hotel staff...all that was present was a dumpster out front and a small sign on our floor (2nd) saying sorry for any inconvenience. thankfully we took off early every morning so we really didn't hear the workers until our last day. the jack-hammering in the room next to us started at 8:30am and was still in full swing at noon when we checked out. my husband mentioned to the front desk staff that it would have been appreciated if someone had told us about the renovations when we made our reservation or at check in and was told that the hotel manager set the policy that the staff was to not tell guests. we would recommend this hotel but not until the renovations are fully complete.

great hotel the service in the hotel was really good. the room was large and very comfortable with a nice large bathroom. the location was also right next to fisherman's wharf and a 3 minute walk to the cable car. would definitely stay here again.

the perfect san francisco treat..... i stayed at the best western tuscan inn at fishermans wharf last year, and when i booked the room i was just glad that i got a room at a good location in s.f. but when i got there ...i was truly impressed. you immediately get the feel of tuscan inn as soon as you walk in. the hotel has the perfect location for a s.f. weekend....you can walk to a lot of the city and there is a trolly car ride not too far. the hotel is clean and very nicely decorated. they even have a nice evening cocktail hour. the rooms were nice but not spectaular...as they were a little small. but stil thats being picky. in the morning the conceirge , told us about a little breakfast place in the morning only a 5 minute walk from the hotel that was out of this world. sometimes , you get such a perfect vacation that you feel like you have to take a new trip more often , this hotel definetly made me feel that way. highly recommended , for a great weekend getaway to the bay area.

10 gold stars the tuscan hotel in fishermans wharf is outstanding.the location; the rooms; the staff; the concierge; the managers nightly wine reception (nice touch); everything about this hotel made our holiday magic.thanks to all.

highly recommend highly recommend, great location, clean, quiet, friendly, nicely decorated, happy hour 5p-6p, just tea/coffee avail in am.less expensive than originally booked b/c special winter rate.

a little gem in a sea of tourist schlock the tuscan inn at fisherman's wharf in san francisco is in such a great location for tourism, i'm surprised there isn't a much larger hotel here. after reading countless reviews of this property, i was confident we could have an enjoyable stay here and avoid any potential pitfalls - and we were not disappointed. i discovered a special rate at travelzoo, which probably swayed me to try this hotel, and made my own reservation with best western. there was no problem in them honoring the special rate. if you are bothered by street noise then be sure to ask for a room with a courtyard view. the courtyard is tiny - but we could not detect any street noise in our room on the second floor looking over the courtyard. currently (january 2008) they are remodeling some rooms on the upper floors, and there is considerable construction noise in some areas that started after 9:30 am and stopped by 5:00 pm. it would be a good idea to ask for a room away from the construction for the least noise, if you are going to be in your room during the day or sleeping in late. gregory, at check in, was quick and polite and helpful with our request for a courtyard room. the room is a bit on the small-side, but i think that is the standard in san francisco with only a few exceptions. our room was very clean and fresh-smelling. one window did open, which kept the room from getting stale. drawer space was minimal, with only two small but deep drawers, and the closet was a little small. clothes for two people for five days maxed out the tiny closet. there is a refrigerator in the room with is also the mini-bar, so there isn't a lot of room in there for take-out food, but is ample for medications, etc. if you plan to use the refrigerator, make sure to take a key to the mini bar, or it will be able to get into it. the room includes a ironing board and iron, although using it would make the room a bit cramped. there is a wall-mounted hair dryer in the bathroom. the restaurant in the hotel - cafe pescatore - does the breakfast run for room service, it was adequate but a little overpriced. lunch and dinner room service is provided by north beach pizza, which deliveries many italian specialties including pasta, entrees, salads, sandwiches and of course - pizza. however, there are countless restaurants of all sorts and price ranges within a 1-4 block walk of this hotel, there is little reason to order room service. we were very happy with the location of this hotel. within two blocks (and not even uphill!) you could catch the mason-powell cable car, also many of the muni buses go by the hotel and the f line historic streetcar is only one block away. just a 3 block walk north and you are on the waterfront of fisherman's wharf. there are two grocery stores (safeway and trader joe's) within 2 blocks of the hotel. one of the things we enjoyed most, was walking away from the touristy area of fisherman's wharf and onto the side streets to look for restaurants. there are many smaller places with very good food at very reasonable prices, all within walking distance. each night when we returned to our room, it had been cleaned up very nicely and restocked. we made sure to tip the housekeeping staff each morning, perhaps that insured that they did an outstanding job every day. we felt we got a reasonable value for the $99 rate we received and assuming we could get a similar or better rate, we would stay here again.

nice hotel, close to many attractions i spent three nights here while attending a conference. i had a room on the fourth (top) floor, overlooking north point street. no problem with traffic noise.room was very nice, staff was very helpful, location was within walking distance of many attractions. lots of restaurants and shopping nearby. excellent public transportation via bus, streetcars, and cable cars.my favorite feature: the clock radio was also a cd player, so i could listen to new discs i purchased while in town.the only disappointment was no public access internet computer for guests.this hotel was more expensive than places i usually stay, but conference sponsors selected it and paid for it. if you can afford it, it's a great place to stay while in san francisco.

warm cozy inn :) the chinese lady manager who checked us in was a little on the snobbish side. the room is a little small, not much space for walkin after putting 2 open luggages. overall it was cozy, love the folded little wooden planks window. our windows faced the interior part of the hotel, no noise disturbance at all. the free drinks held every evening are welcoming after a long day out.location wise, it is very centralized, walkable distance to the fisherman's wharf as well as the cable cars at both hyde and powell streets (that is if you were to visit chinatown, unionsquare, etc). there is a bus going to japantown just right opposite of the inn.

great stay, but room 127 noisy we stayed at the best western tuscan inn between chirstmas and new years. we too had a bad experience with street noise in room 127. it seemed as if the windows were open as it was that loud. we requested a change to another room for the remainder of our stay and they were very helpful and immediately moved us to room 361 which was quiet and peaceful. i would definately stay there again and recommend it to others, but only if you reserve an off-street or courtyard room.we were able to get a great $99.00 per night rate through travelzoo.com and i did not felt we received a great value.
great location! famous cable cars. big lineups get there early!

the good hubby i stayed here for a few days in november 2007. my biggest problem was our room. we were on the 2nd leg of our journey but if i had the energy i would have asked to be moved. our room looked most like the photo of the room done in red,black and white without the red velvet couch in our room. it was very very small. we were facing the street and it was a bit noisey at times.the thing that bothered me the most was the bathroom was very dated. on top of that the wall paper was actually peeling. i am so dispapointed that i can't remember what room # it was becasue apparantly after reading other reviews, there are some newer and nicer rooms.i felt we paid too much for the particaulr room we got. now on to the good: location location location! also, the wine hour is very nice and i don't even drink wine. a hot tip from the bell boy: arrive in the lobby about 10 minutes before wine hour begins. they usually bring in a deep dish pizza from the restaurant which is gone in a flash. we did and enjoyed it very much. in the morning a nice touch along with coffee and hot tea was hot chocoalte. now would i stay here again? well...maybe. if i got a really nice room like some of the other writers describe with a fridge too...perhaps...i still wonder if another hotel in the same area would have been a better deal. the other thing that i found disappointing was i can't remember the exact details but something like the charge they quote for parking (very pricey) was even more than that because there was some sort of a tax...

great hotel had a wonderful 5 nights staying at the tuscan inn at fisherman's wharf. the front desk staff were very helpful. the hotel itself was one of the best we have stayed in. it had such a warm and friendly atmosphere. the wine tasting in the afternoon made available from the manager was a really nice touch as was the free tea and coffee in the lobby in the morning which got you off to a great start for the day. the hotel was very central to everything. we walked to fisherman's wharf, union square, starbuck's, laundromat (1/2mile from hotel). italian restaurant next door to hotel had fantastic food. as for the room we could only find one complaint which was the shower head. apart from this the room itself was perfect, very clean and fresh clean amenities every day. attractions that we feel are a must are:- segway tour, cable car and ghiradelli ice cream is a must!! these attractions are in very close proximity to each other. jacob on the segway tour was very patient and lots of fun. also make sure you visit alcatraz.

great location for tourists location was great. hotel was pretty good too.don't miss the complimentary wine tasting at 5pm every day - great way to meet other travellers and enjoy a glass or two.rooms have a fridge which is handy and there are safety deposit boxes available (not in room which is a little bit of a pain).within walking distance to everything at fisherman's wharf which is the tourist hub. there's a supermarket (safeway i think) next door which is very handy!rooms were pretty standard (we had a 2 x double one which was big enough for 2 adults and 2 kids) - but it's the location which sells this place.

a nice comfortable hotel in a good location. the tuscan inn is a moderately priced hotel located near fisherman's wharf, dozens of good restaurants and ten minutes to downtown by cab. the cable car is only a few blocks away. the rooms are large comfortable and well furnished, suitable for business travelers or tourists. onsite parking is available. the hotel has free wireless. the restaurant attached to the hotel is good and well priced. you'll need a reservation for dinner. each evening the hotel hosts a wine and cheese bar between 5 and 6pm. it is well attended and provides an opportunity to hear other tourists tales of the city. we stay here every time we come to san francisco.

good location!! this place is just as the way it has been described.the pics of the rooms are the same as they present them online.nice location.easy walkable accessibility to pier 39 and the tram ride.

staying here next time we're in san francisco this hotel is in the perfect location whether you are focusing your sightseeing at the wharf or all over town. bus lines run out front and the wharf is a couple short blocks away. the staff was great, all the way around, helpful and polite. the room was clean, well decorated and had all you could ask for. one of the cable car lines in a block or two away along with a pharmacy, starbucks and barnes and noble right around the corner. convenient if nothing else. we stayed in a room overlooking mason (which actually overlooks a small parking stack) but i thought it was great one morning to wake up to the sound of sea lions barking, where else but san francisco! when standing in the window we could see coit tower with the moon rising in the background...not too bad for 125 a night on thanksgiving weekend!i will return and recommend this hotel!

loved teh best western we stayed at the best western for four nights commencing oct 30th for the start of our honeymoon. we had spent all day travelling (flying from ireland) and when we arrived to check in the hotel had upgraded us and there was a bottle of champagne in the room for us. this was a lovely surprise and was much appreciated. the room itself was lovely and spotlessly clean.the hotel itself is in a perfect location for all the attractions. its about a five minute walk to the end of the road and you are at pier 39 where you can book your trips to the various attractions. there are also plenty of restaurants, bars and shops.at 5 o'clock every evening in the hotel lobby there is a free wine reception for an hour. this is a great idea as everyone sits around and chills out for an hour. there is also a lovely italian restaurant attached to the hotel and the food in there is lovely.the staff were very friendly and you could book any trips you wanted with them. i could not fault this hotel at all and thank them for a wonderful four days.

will definitely return for our next vacation! excellent location, very close to the fisherman's wharf (walking distance) that made it very convenient to do the tourist things. a car was not needed as we caught a shuttle to the hotel. i highly recommend going to the cable car turn around at powell/hyde which is used less. the staff were very friendly and helpful during our stay. the restaurant pescatore was excellent, friendly staff, and enjoyable food. we will definitely return to this hotel on our return visit to san francisco!

best stay in sf by far!!!!! my husband and i take annual trips to san francisco and have stayed at many different hotels. this trip and hotel stay was by far the best ever!!!! from the time we walked into the lobby until the time we checked out the stafff was always very hellpful and the room was very nice, clean, and quiet. this time we brought our one year old son and the fact that there was a grocery store (safeway) next door to the hotel made it very convenient for us. he had an amazing time as well. i definitely recommend the tuscan inn @ fisherman's wharf.

great hotel this was my 9th trip to san francisco but unlike prior trips i was with my in-laws and had different criteria for the trip, they wanted to be close to all the fishermanéˆ¥??? wharf action and walking distance to the main tourist attractions, this hotel was ideal and the best value we could find in the location. the hotel was clean, quiet, large rooms and very close to the wharf and local restaurants. nothing disappointed us about our stay and we didnéˆ¥??› even take advantage of the free wine tasting between 5-6pm. we did however make use of the free tea and coffee when we had an early start. the hotel gives a feeling of a small family run business whilst being under the umbrella of a brand you know. if you want to know what youéˆ¥??™e getting, stay in a larger than average sf hotel room and be walking distance to the bay area then i donéˆ¥??› believe you can do better.

nice hotel my family and i stayed at the tuscan inn for three nights. the hotel was a wonderful place to stay and we were very comforatble. the lobby was welcoming, the staff was friendly and we felt good about being there. i would say, though, that the price was just a bit too high for what we got. $175 per night (after the discount for firefighters, mind you). there is virtually no counterspace in the bathroom at all. upon our arrival, there was a slight odor in bathroom but nothing worth complaining about. maid service was prompt and outstanding. but, it was close to the wharf and soooo convenient. so, maybe the price was warranted. beware though....parking is $45 + tax. i called before we ever arrived to inquire about it and was told that parking was no problem at all. then the clerk told me the price. woah!!! when we arrive at the valet stop, the valet told me that if we have aaa, the price would be $25. cool. when we went to check out, the front desk clerk said that we could not have the discount because we did not make a reservation to park. what??? i guess calling to inquire about parking while giving them our name and reservation dates didn't warrant the clerk to inform us that we should make a reservation for our car also. trader joe's is right around the corner and so is a safeway. made it nice for a morning breakfast with the kids. i would definately stay there again. but, next time, i will leave my car at home!

great location with nice rooms stayed here for our honeymoon. overall we were very happy and comfortable here. rooms were a bit small and appear to be older construction, rooms facing the road are a bit noisey at am rush hour so we requested to be moved to the courtyard side which was a good move. these were the only negatives that i can think of with this hotel. room was very clean and that to me is the most important. hotel staff was polite and helpful. they have a nice lobby area where a wine hour (free) is hosted every evening between 5 and 6:00 which gives you the opportunity to mingle with the other guests and get to know people from the world over. if you're looking for the ultimate luxury in a hotel you may want to look elsewhere but if you want a nice clean comfortable room that is close to everything with a friendly atmosphere, i would highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting san francisco.

great stay! our first impression of the best westen tuscan inn was nice, it was clean and nicely decorated. the staff helped make our stay a great experience. our request were promptly met, they made last minute reservations for us at a very popular restaurant on the wharf and had a cab waiting when we needed it. the rooms were decent size, clean and had all of the basic amenities. the wine hour was nice was a little crowded but it was pleasant to sit in front of the fireplace and visit with others with a complimentary glass of wine. for the cost of our stay i was a little dissapointed with the coffee and biscotti in the am but it was better than nothing. access to the wharf was a very easy walk from our hotel. we would definately stay again.

very good hotel, great location very good hotel - great location, concierge extremely helpful, decor is nice and the maid service was excellent (room was cleaned by the time we got back from breakfast each morning). they have coffee in the morning and wine hour each evening in the lobby. the location is great, 2 blocks from fw and 5-6 blocks from really good italian food in north beach and chinatown is in that area as well. the only problem we had was on our last day; we were awoken at 6am by the banging on the roof (they were trying to fix the boiler or something) when i called the front desk all they could say was, sorry (we had stayed on the top floor). also, if you have a rental car, do not park there, it's upwards of $40 per day (with taxes) - park around the block at a pay garage which i think the sign said was $14 max per day. i had asked for late check out of 130pm and that was not a problem. also, take the shuttle to the airport which is only $15 per person as opposed to taxi which is $40 each way.

fantastic!! we stayed at the best western tuscan inn for a 4 night getaway for our anniversary. we loved the location as it was convenient to everything and a short walk to many attractions. the king room we had was lovely...and large. i was surprised by the size of it, because we've stayed in other hotel rooms in large cities and the rooms were always tiny. the bed was very comfy and the room itself was very clean. we were pleasantly surprised to find a complimentary bottle of champagne on ice when we arrived on our first night (our actual anniversary day). the only problem we had with the room was the noise level coming from the street. we were on the 2nd floor and facing the street and the noise was awful. we were woken up once or twice by really rowdy passersby. the hotel can't control this, but there should be better windows or something to insulate the sound. we've stayed in large cities before and have never had this kind of problem. i'd stay at the tuscan inn again, but i'd request a room facing the courtyard. we missed the wine reception every evening we were there, but we did get coffee and biscotti every morning, which was nice. we had dinner in the restaurant once and it was very good. it got quite crowded as the evening progressed. hotel staff was friendly and helpful...especially concierge. he was one of the better concierge staff i've encountered at a hotel. all in all, a great stay and i'd stay there again in a heartbeat!

4 nights no sleep we stayed in this hotel from 10-14 october 07 and did not get a full nightéˆ¥??? sleep in that time. the weekend nights were horrendous, we were kept awake for nearly 2 hours each night with the noise of what we assume were people leaving local clubs. as a result we were too tired to enjoy our visit to san francisco and have decided never to go there again. i also found the room was much too small with a tiny closet and nowhere to store luggage, and the restaurant to be expensive, particularly when you share the very limited space with the bar and cannot enjoy your meal without noise. the only good thing about our stay in this hotel was the nightly wine reception but that certainly was not enough to make up for the down sides. my advice is if you like your sleep do not stay at this hotel.

great hotel we travel to san francisco once a year have stayed at many hotels. the tuscan rates as one of the best. although small (no counter space at all in the bathroom) the room was very clean with modern decor. the customer service was wonderful. the entire staff was helpful. this was the first hotel to offer complimentary wine tasting coffee. we hope to stay there again next year. we have stayed acrossed the street at the sheraton found that our stay at the tuscan inn was much better.

good location ; avoid restaurant would not recommend the travel agent booked this hotel and this was the only hotel out of 10 that i did not book myself although hotel sounded ok this was part of the deal for the airfares location is excellent , rooms ok staff variable some very helpful others not so . we stayed here for 5 nights and then 1 night later in our trip problems (a) given a smoking room when a non smoking room was asked were re allocated but it was a hassle (b) came back one afternoon not only had the room be tidied but things had been put away which immediately led to the thoughts that stuff had been stolen but nothing was missing complained and assistant manager very undestanding and gave us a voucher for a meal in their restaurant . (c) restaurant very expensive and only ate there because of the voucher for 1 night staff arrogant also charged us for items we did not have felt very uncomfortable (d) on second stay room only had 1 shutter complained and comment was the problem had not been reported did get another room but it was more hassle especially as it did not get to hotel till 1 in the morning as there were delays on the train

great! quiet room #s provided here previously we stayed at the sheraton across the street. the tuscan inn is markedly less expensive, and the location is identical. the room was clean and well decorated. no room darkening curtains (as others mentioned in their reviews) but the shutters do a good job for light and privacy. to get a quiet room, you need to ask for a courtyard room that doesn't face a brick wall. there are actually room (as others have mentioned) that literally face a brick wall. otherwise, ask for the 4th floor. 439, 441, 443, 444, 045 face a good direction to the outside of the hotel. the rooms (on floors 2 3 also) that number 401, 402, 403, 405, 406, 408, 409, 412, 414, and 415 face out to the main street. you will hear street noise, garbage trucks, buses, etc.it's a best western - so it's not luxery, but it's a nice hotel in a great location at a great price.

great hotel in a great location for fisherman's wharf this is a very stylish hotel, a couple of hundred yards from the wharf. we stayed for two nights and had requested a high floor on the front, which is exactly what we got - not that the view was very good but we did have a view of the water (but only just!).the room was well presented with modern fixtures and fittings in good working order. staff were friendly and helpful and we enjoyed the complimentary wine tasting (1 hour) each evening. coffee and biscuits were also priovided for 3 hours each morning.only two negatives worth mentioning:-1. the shower pressure was so low that it was a challenge to get wet all over!!2. valet parking is provided at $36/day which was, i thought, excessive. you could, for example, park across the street for only $10/day nb but this was only open until early evening, after which you would need to park on the street (which is free overnight).we ate both nights at fisherman's wharf - the first night at alioti's and then at nick's lighthouse. both were really good - alioti's was more grand than nick's with a view and prices to match but we thought we got value-for-money at each.i thought that, all in all, the tuscan was an excellent hotel and i would happily recommend it to anyone visiting the area.

don't leave anything important in your room the stay was great until the last day. we checked out. i forgot and expensive item. we went back to our room and it was gone. the room was not even changed over. a staff member must have gone in right after we checked out. the staff gave the typical run around. no help. it was terrible. we are still waiting for an answer.we recommend don't stay and if you do...don't leave or forget anything in your room that is important.

excellent location the hotel is in an excellent position, close to pier 39 and restaurants. the room we stayed in was a little old and could have done with an update to the dèœ…cor (especially the bathroom) with no outlook whatsoever. one big down side for us was the lack of a safety deposit box in the room, there are boxes available at reception but most of them are quite small in size so if you have camera equipment you may need to lock it in your suitcase!we had a king size standard room and found the bed quite uncomfortable; the sheets didnéˆ¥??› fit the bed which meant you woke up in the middle of the night fighting with the covers. the air conditioning was extremely noisy and i found it quite alarming that the windows didnéˆ¥??› open!the reception staff were extremely helpful and polite and couldnéˆ¥??› do enough for you; all in all a good stay for a couple of nights.

very enjoyable i stayed in the tuscan inn in san francisco in february of 2007 and loved every minute of it. the check in was quick and fast and the staff and nice concierge was very pleasurable. i couldn't have asked for anything better. our room was quite small but for a family of four it was perfect. at night we had wonderful channel on our television and would not be bored after a late night out on town. also every night at 5:00 they would have wine in the lobby which was very enjoyable. the tuscan inn is in the center of everything. its just a quick walk to fisherman's wharf, pier 39, little italy, china town and everything else that san francisco has to offer. it was perfect and i will definitly be going back. even if you do not stay at this hotel there are many other delightful hotels nearby. san francisco is a beauty of its own and you would not be spending a lot of time in the hotel anyway but if you want a good night sleep have it at the tuscan inn.

great location - hotel room good also this hotel is very centrally located near the wharf and that is probably it's best selling point. the hotel itself is what you would expect from a best western - clean, comfortable with all the amenities. the room size was okay - we got 2 double bed, however, would have preferred a room with one king bed but they had none available. the restaurant next door was fine also - however, on the 2nd morning we went down for breakfast at 10.30 and they had stopped serving which i thought was a little early. overall an average hotel in a great location

great hotel stayed for two nights, there were six of us in three rooms. we all had the same great opinion of this property. very clean and well maintained through-out. it was an easy walk to the bus stops and fisherman's wharf areas. there was a trader joes and safeway within a block of the hotel to buy snacks and such. the adjacent cafe pescatero was handy for breakfast but had some hiccups in service, but it was okay overall. we would highly recommend this hotel to others.

great hotel!!! my sister and i stayed at the tuscan inn over the weekend. it is a great hotel - clean and comfortable. we had a courtyard view, and there was no noise at night. a lot of the people staying there were older and very quiet. i would definitely stay there again. it was a couple of blocks from the warf. the streets in san fran were filthy and the homeless people were scary, but the hotel was wonderful!!!

great place to lay your head and tour from this was our second stay at the tuscan (the first was 10 years ago). it is a wonderful clean place to stay and but two short blocks to fisherman's wharf. earily evening free wine tasting (or wine drinking- they give you a full glass af several wines). in the morning free great coffee and biscotti in the lobby- with carry-out cups.our room was always cleaned but they only give out 2 towels? i guess you only get one towel per day.it was interesting that we received a better room price by going thru travelocity then by calling the hotel direct???if we ever return we would try to stay here for the third time..

loved the tuscan inn my husband and i stayed at the tuscan inn for our honeymoon and we can't say enough about how wonderful our stay was. we were complimentarily upgraded to the king premier since we were on our honeymoon. the room was beautiful; the view wasn't the greatest, but we didn't care. i loved the view in the lobby as there was a lush garden in the window. the hotel offered complimentary wine tasting each evening which we enjoyed. the location was great as we were within walking distance to just about everything. the transportation systems were great and easy to use. the concierge's were extremely helpful and were very eager to assist us in anything we needed. i would definitely stay at this hotel again.

tuscan inn 2 blocks from the piers small enough, very personable.very cleansmall rooms, but have a couch, chair, desk, etc., w king bed, which was very comfortable w pillow top pillowsvery small 1 person closet, do not bring many clothes! shutters nice.lobby, downstairs restrooms decor beautiful, flower courtyard nice.restaurant/patio excellent food, high breakfast $, greast coffee.all the porters, etc., provide service like high end hotels.walking distance, 2 blocks to the piers.tuscan/botique theme nice.housekeeping is quiet in the ams, not vacuming @ 0700, etc., get in inside room facing courtyard if you are light sleeper as outside rooms face the streets.will store your luggage in separate room on your check out day if you have late flight, want to spend more time,oldest italian restaurant in the country w/in walking distance, back east service, integrity, etc., fiore d'italiawait until monday to take the bay cruises if a holiday weekenddantes best view for seafood lunch of the bay bridge/baywalgreens trader joes w/in walking distance for we forgot...walgreens has same souvenirs the airport shops do for 1/2 $do not rent a car, waste of time, money, no parking! split a fare w a private service i.e., escalade etc., for return to airportyou can walk, take a cab, trolley, etc., we walked everywhere including up the hill to coit tower then walked down just in time to attend 1300 service @ st. peters cathedral, beautiful!my first time to spend time in san francisco, my husband's 3rd.he wants to re-locate there, desppite the real estate $$, taxes, etc., that is how nice it is...

great place to stay we checked into this hotel after a long flight from florida. they were very efficient at the reservation desk and surprised us with an upgrade to a suite. the rooms seemed to have been recently renovated with updated decor. they were very comfortable and quite attractive. the bed was perfect as were the pillows. (i always carry travel down pillows, but didn't even unpack them.) the wine reception in the late afternoon is a nice extra. the bathroom was adequate with thick, fluffy towels. if i had any complaints, it would be that there could be a larger sink area to hold cosmetics.i would highly recommend this hotel. it is a great value.

great stay we stayed for three nights,our room was on the fourth floor and adequately big enough for the three of us, my husband and adult daughter.the staff were friendly and helpful,it was a good base from which to explore san francisco.we took an evening alcatraz tour and a city tour with shuttle tours which i would recommend if you have limited time in town.

excellent hotel the best western in fishermans wharf is a fabulous hotel and an ideal base to enjoy your trip to san francisco.the hotel is newly decorated and rooms are a nice size, extremely new and clean. staff are very helpful. the hotel is ideally lcoated 2 minutes walk from pier 39 on fishermans wharf.there is loads to do in this area and hotel is perfect base to see san fran, its 2 minutes walk to the nearest cable car stop and about 10 minutes drive to union sqaure or marina district.

loved it!! my friends and i stayed at the bw tuscan inn last week and i am so excited to write this review. from beginning to end it was a perfect experience. the staff was so friendly and helpful and the concierge service was very knowledgeable. the hotel itself was so beautiful and very boutique-like (don't let the best western in the name fool you). my room was clean and nicely decorated - the bed was extremely comfortable and also had a nice down comforter and comfy pillows. the bathroom was large and private. the room has an honor bar, which i didn't use, but did use the refrigerator to store some of my own snacks and wine. another great thing about the hotel is that every day, they offer wine and beer from 5-6pm for free for all hotel guests. we took advantage of the offer and many other guests did too. it is very nice. all in all, highly recommended!

great location and staff ! excellent location 2 blocks from fishermans wharf and 1 block from cable car. room on 4 th floor on roadside and heard no noise from anywhere. room was nice , looked quite new and very clean and big enough for the 4 of us and our cases ! all staff very friendly and could not have been more helpful. complimentary morning hot drinks were lovely and comlimentary wine around a log fire even better !! make sure you bring warm clothes as it is chilly. although there are plenty of cheap fleeces for sale.

a nice hotel for a short getaway we stayed here for the first 3 days of our honeymoon beofre getting some sun in palm springs. the room was lovely and clean with everything you need wether on business or pleasure.all the staff were extremely helpful and polite and always saying hi when eye contact was made.a good hotel in a good location for all the tourist attractions if you're walking, taxi or by bus.we ate at the hotel restaurant on our first night which was value for money.we would definately stay in this hotel again if we're ever in san fran again.

great location we booked on the recomendation of a friend who is particular with her accomodation, and the tuscan inn checked all the boxes for her, and so we decided to book directly with the property. we received a pleasant email from the booking manager, but never got to meet her to say thatnks for her prompt attention.checkin was a no stress affair, and we were directed to our room with luggage arriving promptly. the room was not large, but then this was just a base for exploring all that san francisco has to offer, and we did not need heaps of room to spead out in, just enough room to lay out our cases (4) and sit somewhere other than on the bed. the bathroom was very clean and well appointed with nice towels and toiletries, it was not big, but room enough to do what one needs to. the evening wine tasting was well patronized, and although we arrived just after the starting time, all the savouries were gone. a masseur was giving guests a massage at the same location, not sure if there was a charge involved for that service, as there was no information about that anywhere.the foyer was very cozy with the inviting fireplace and had large sofas and arm chairs and a bookcase full of interesting books, overlooking a courtyard garden filled with attractive landscaping.a consierge desk was also located in this area, and he was rather busy on the occasions he was there. we found the tourist advice to be slightly biased towards a particular company, and knew little about the sevices of other tour companies, even though one is very well know and patronized. there is a large tourist information stand near the lifts so you can peruse any of the brochures and make your own choice if he is not there or too busy.the hotel is conveniently located to the shopping centre across the road, and we made use of this to purchase our breakfast requirements, as we had not had great service from the adjoining cafe pescatore for our evening meal and thought we would do our own thing each morning. the room has a coffee perculator and a supply of reasonable coffee was repenished daily.it is in an ideal situation to acess public transport, a short walk to the end of the street near the cruise pier is the trolley car, and another short walk the other way takes you to the cable cars. pier 39 is close by and so are many other attractions such as the maratime museum, ghiradelli square, fishermans wharf, and many great vistas can be seen walking along the promenade down along the embarcadero. i would have no hesitiation in recomending this establisment to my friends, and we would return here on any future visits to san francisco, esp if we were cruising out of this port as it is very close to the cruise terminal.

great hotel good location positivesthe staff were friendly and helpful.the room was clean, nicely decorated and quiet. the location is within walking distance of fishermanéˆ¥??? wharf. there is a supermarket located within 1 block.negativesthe room was a bit on the small side.overall a very positive experience.ps san francisco is a fantastic city i would encourage anyone to visit.

great hotel, great experience!! stayed here for our first visit to san fran and the us.we'd read some ok reviews, bad reviews and great reviews so were a bit nervous but thought - what the hell, we won't be in it much anyway!!.we were very suprised when we got there - the location was great, just set back enough to miss the noise of the warf but within a stones throw of all the action. the food stores were near by too which was great for getting those much needed essentials. (twinkies!!)we were there for 10 nights, the staff were very friendly and pleased to help. we were always greated with a smile by the valet guys too.the only bad thing is that they didn't reply to my girlfriend regarding a suprise birthday cake for me until we were at the checkout desk...together!!! oh well it's the thought that countswe did have a snoop around some of the other hotels and went to a few for breakfast, some were grander but by no means over shadowing the tuscan inn. our room was both spacious, airy and light whilst being quiet at night. the room was always perfectly cleaned each day.the italian restaurant linked to the hotel was great, both for food and just popping in for a quick beer by the bar, very friendly!!!the only dissapointing thing is that we were so busy we missed the wine tasting - from the looks of the people who took part though, it's designed for the older generation!!!all in all a great place to stay, very comfortable and would definitely go back there and would recommend it to anyone.

some disappointments we'd heard a lot of good things about the tuscan inn from people who'd stayed there for a night or two before cruising out of the port of san francisco. normally we'd stay at the sf hilton, or one of the marriott properties, but we decided this time to try something else.the tuscan inn room was quite nicely appointed, the bed was comfortable the chairs tv adequate, the bathroom reasonably good. street noise can be a problem in an outside room, though, and the window coverings (sliding roman blinds that don't quite meet) left a lot to be desired if you don't want to get up with the sun.housekeeping service was very inadequate, though. we left the room at 10:30 am, placing the please make up room tag in the key slot. there were at least 4, and maybe 6, housekeeping carts between our room the elevator. yet when we returned at 3:30 the room hadn't been touched! the attached restaurant (cafe pescadore) is open for breakfast with a fairly skimpy menu - but quite good coffee.on balance, it was an ok place to stay but, perhaps, not to return to. it's fine if it's convenient to what you're doing in the city.

hotel ok, good location. we stayed here for three nights in early august before heading to the tenaya lodge in yosemite. the hotel was clean and decorated nicely, and biscotti and coffee in the morning was nice. staff was friendly. the rooms and the double beds were very small, both quite a bit smaller than the tenaya.we had booked two connecting rooms since we were travelling with our boys, ages 11 15, and i called several days prior to arriving to remind them of our request. at check-in, they had our kids in a room at the end of the hallway, which we were not comfortable with. we took just one room for that night and they moved us to adjacent, though not connecting, rooms the next two nights. this was much better and gave us a lot more space. beware, if you request adjoining rooms, they are not guaranteed and really not even planned. they told me they don't assign rooms until the day of check-in, and they were also overbooked. the tuscan inn is in a great location in fishermen's wharf and our boys really enjoyed pier 39. i'm glad we stayed in fw instead of downtown - much more for kids to do there.
nearby the wharf and charming lobby view

great location, clean rooms, we enjoyed our visit.... we stayed at this hotel the first week of august. we really enjoyed our stay here. the location is great. it is a short walk to fisherman's wharf, the f line, pier 39 etc but is far enough away away from the ticky tacky areas. the hotel was clean and decorated nicely. the rooms are a bit small, but not uncomfortably so. the linens and bed were comfortable. the shower head was stong and the water was nice and warm.on the first part of our stay, we were in a courtyard room. this made the room seem a bit larger by the way that it was set up. when we returned later in the week we were put in an outside room. it was noisier and even with the shutters closed the light from the safeway sign kept the room pretty bright. i work night shift and am used to sleeping during the daylight, but for people who like it dark, that might be more difficult. the second room also smelled a bit musty (think mothballs) and we could never get it aired out. only a mild inconvenience though.the am coffee/tea/biscotti is nice. it was a nice stop before heading out for a bigger breakfast. only participated in the evening reception once. the wine was good, but the appetizers were gone. lots of people take advantage of this time, it was always busy.we did eat at the hotel restaurant for one breakfast. the food was ok...and the service was just ok too. nothing to write home about for the price. next time i would probably go somewhere else.the front desk staff recommended fior d'italia for a dinner reservation. it was a 2 block walk and so great!! it was a wonderful suggestion. we also enjoyed the stinking rose on another afternoon.the tuscan inn is a great hotel and we would return again.

enjoyed the wine in the afternoon this hotel offers clean, well-kept rooms which are good value for money. although breakfast isn't really included in the room rates, you can get tea / coffee / hot chocolate biscotti in the reception / lounge area every morning. we particularly enjoyed the nightly 'manager's reception' when wine and nibbles are freely available! we were a little disappointed with the location of this hotel as although it is close to fisherman's wharf / pier 39, it wasn't very busy in the nearby streets so we didn't feel like lingering in the restaurants before returning at night. the local restaurants are a bit cheap and cheerful, but if you are travelling as a family or are on a tight budget, there is sufficient choice. you have to brave the f-market streetcar (which was often jam-packed) to get to downtown san francisco for more 'up-market' dining. however, it was very convenient for the ferry to alcatraz (which you must book in advance of your visit) and for hiring bikes to go over the golden gate bridge into marin county.overall, this hotel provides a good base, particularly if you are willing to get acquainted with san francisco's extensive and varied public transport network.

pa traveler great hotel! the staff was very helpful and the rooms were well apportioned. the rooms are a bit small for more than three adults. but, they were very clean and up to date. the location is excellent for access to the cable cars and the wharf. we enjoyed the morning coffee and evening wine in the lobby.

central and clean very central for wharf and walked to north beach area in about 10/15 mins. had an outside room which was nice, request high floor room for less noise. the room was fairly quiet and adequate. wharf is tacky, pier 39 smarter. went to north beach at night for italian restaurants. if you like garlic, the stinking rose is for you! open top bus to golden gate bridge was great and book alcatraz before you come on the official site or you may not get to it and may have to pay a lot more. hotel restaurant is good and worth going to. enjoy.

laura meith i was visiting from a three day layover flight from boston, and i wanted to visit the wharf. i was recommended to the hotel from a dear friend of mine. the whole trip was ruined by the guest service of the hotel. they say they pride themselves on being the best in guest service but i was not impressed at all. during my stay i complained about a dent that was put in my rental car by a valet, and i was directed to speak with the assistant general manager laura meith. she was rude and insincere about repairing the damage done to my vehicle. i will never stay there again because of this incident.the valet parking was overpriced, the service was terrible, and the coffe was cold. take my word for it, stay at the hilton or the marriot.

great, cozy hotel!! we stayed at the tuscan inn in san francisco at the end of july----it was a very, beautiful, cozy hotel---all the customer pictures captured it exactly----the room was beautiful, tho kind of small we didn't get the 2 double beds, but that was my mistake for booking through orbitz------the coffee in the room was nice, and the cozy fireplace in the lobby was wonderful, altho we didn't partake of the wine cheese reception----my only real complaint would be that the bathroom does not have a separate vanity area, so 2 people getting dressed had to improvise, which was kind of surprising since the bathrooms were all redone on 2005--------service was extra good, very friendly---and there is a great cafe across the street (hollywood cafe) which has the best breakfast in the world

great location for san francisco sightseeing we stayed at tuscan inn for four nights at the end of july and found it a very enjoyable stay. to be honest, the hotel was just a base for exploring and we didn't spend a lot of time in the room however, the room was lovely. the staff were friendly and helpful. the morning tea/coffee/biscotti and afternoon wine reception was an added bonus. the hotel is central to transportation and a number of tourist areas particularly alcatraz ferry and the fisherman's wharf. it was great having so many fantastic restaurants close by - it made is difficult to choose. overall, i was very happy with this hotel and would recommend it especially since it was reasonable priced.

very comfortable. i stayed here based on the reviews i read on this site. i was not disappointed. we had a small suite. the linens and decor were lovely. our room did overlook the street, so we did hear the street sounds. i've been to sf many times, and have just accepted when you stay down at the wharf, you are going to hear street noises. we did take one person's recommendations to park in the lot just across the street. this saved us some money and we had access to our vehicle whenever we wanted it. at the hotel, it is valet only parking. we tried to have the wine/appetizers at night, but all nights we were there, it was always crowded. what we did sample was good, but it wasn't worth standing in line. the hotel is within short walking distance of a grocery store and trader joe's, so we picked up our own snacks. the rooms had dvd players. when we asked if they had dvd's to watch, they told me their one and only copy of the tuscan sun had been stolen, and they did not replace it. the location of this hotel is great if you are there to enjoy the tourist stuff of sf. the hotel staff was a hit and miss situation. mostly, they were very nice, but occasionally we'd get a stressed out person. i would stay here again. check for internet deals and don't pay for their parking.

tuscan inn a great location very pleased with our recent stay. very close to all the public transportation to get to all the sites in the city. reasonable price for the area. staff was courteous and the wine hour each evening gave us a chance to meet many people from all over the world. wish the morning coffee time would be extended for those of us who like to sleep in.

great location for exploring san francisco we arrived at the tuscan inn at 1:00 am and quickly checked in. we were exhausted from traveling from boston. the room, (an inner courtyard room) while adequate, had a wall air condtioner which was very noisy. the next morning the hotel staff were very accomodating in changing our room and moving our belongings to an outside room which was not only larger, but had central air. apparently the inner rooms have the wall units. the hotel staff was consistently friendly and helpful throughout our stay, especially cliff, the consierge, providing directions, maps, dinner recommendations and reservations, and suggestions for sightseeing.the location is perfect to explore the city. fisherman's wharf (pier 39) is a very short walk, the embarcadero, ferry to alcatraz, cable cars, and giardelli square are all within walking distance. bart is also convenient to the hotel.the complementary wine hour offers the opportunity to relax and meet other guests before heading out to evening activities.we recommend this hotel without hesitation, and will definatly stay there again on return the san francisco.

an excellent choice! my wife and i stayed at the tuscan inn at fisherman's wharf four nights during our recent vacation in san francisco. we were very satisfied with our entire experience. the location is great, the staff very friendly and helpful, and the room was neat and clean though a bit small. the morning coffee and biscotti and the evening wine reception were both nice touches and well attended. but the thing that impressed us the most was the overall friendliness and helpfulness of the entire staff. this was our first visit to san francisco so we had many questions especially about how to get around--and everyone we talked to was always willing to provide us with the info we needed. they certainly helped to make our vacation a wonderful experience and one we will remember for a long time to come.

great base to discover san francisco this hotel is a great place to use as a base to discover the joys of san francisco. we booked this by checking other travellers comments on trip advisor and were pleased with the helpfulness of the staff, the location and overall cleanliness and comfort of our room. we would certainly recommend this hotel.

enjoyable stay at the tuscan inn my family and i stayed at the best western tuscan inn for three nights this past june. this hotel is above average for a best western. the rooms were clean, nicely decorated, and comfortable. i did not have any issue with noise; the air conditioning units were not quiet but i didn't find them bothersome. we had no noise from the street. i don't remember our view- we were basically just in the room to rest up for the next activity. the location of the hotel was within easy walking distance of fisherman's wharf and ghiardelli square. cable cars, trams, and muni buses to various parts of the city were within 1 to 2 blocks of the hotel as well. the service was fine with the exception of check-in. we made our reservations several months ahead of time and requested two adjacent double rooms as my husband and i were travelling with our two teenage daughters. they gave us two rooms on the same floor but on opposite sides of the hotel. since our daughters are older teenagers, we accepted this arrangement. a couple of years ago it would have been a deal breaker. we've gone many places and made this request and this hotel is the first one that did not put us within a couple rooms of each other. from reading other reviews, it seems as though this hotel has significant lapses in service from time to time. nevertheless, i did like this hotel- the rooms, location, and most of the service and i would stay here again.

wonderful stay my sister and i stayed at this hotel and just returned. absolutely loved everything about this hotel. the location is fabulous for getting around the fisherman's wharf and the concierge-hugo and cliff-are fantastic and full of wonderful ideas. the nightly free wine reception is a great way to meet people and find out what is worth seeing and what is not. this is how we found out not to pay for the more expensive napa valley wine train, but to stick with the sonoma tour. i do think that if you are staying at a hotel you should not have to pay for parking. san francisco is such a great city with so much to do, and the public transportation is the best.i would highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the city.

great stay in san fran great place to stay - very clean and confortable rooms and helpful staff. added touches like the evening wine reception and morning coffee in the lobby add to the experience. some people have said it is a long walk to some places such as the ferry and bridge but it is a large city and you can't be close to everywhere! the walk to the city centre shops was about 20 mins but there were different ways to go to see different places along the way such as china town and the italia areas. close to the wharf which is a great place to visit in the evening and seemed to be a safer area than a lot in the city. we stayed over new year and it was close to good viewing spot for the fireworks. i would recommend this hotel as a good base for a short break to san fran - the hotel rooms weren't the biggest so a longer stay might not be as enjoyable

nice place but service could be better we just returned from a stay at the tuscan inn. easy walking distance to fisherman's wharf, but a pretty good walk to alcatraz ferry. the room was small, but nice. beds were very comfortable. overall we had a nice stay but just had some minor service issues. we had some problems with the lack of concierge when needed. no concierge there at 6:30pm when we needed dinner advice. we were looking for a church on sunday morning and no concierge was on duty. the girl at the front desk gave us the name of a church with mass times and showed us on a map where it was. she sent us in the completely opposite direction of where we should have gone. when we finally found the church later, the service times she had given us were wrong, too. i have been to many hotels and asked for local churches and it is usually on a pre-printed form listing churches for each denomination. i was surprised this seemed so difficult. the morning biscotti was empty every time we tried to get some and the afternoon wine and cheese was wine only. we also had to ask for more towels each night as they consistently only gave us 3 towels although 4 of us were registered. no big deal, just felt for over $200/night we'd get a better experience. probably wouldn't stay there again.

great hotel we stayed at the tuscan inn for four nights last week. i was traveling with my 83 year old mother who has a hard time walking long distances and my 79 year old aunt. the hotel was great because it was so close to the cable cars, the wharf and had a grocery store and drug store across the street. the staff was terrific. we called for an extra luggage rack and not only was it there when we got back from dinner -- the luggage was on it. our room was bigger than i was led to believe through the other reviews. i asked the desk clerk when we checked in if the rooms were as small as they said they were in the reviews. she gave us a courtyard room -- she said they were larger! we turned in our rental car before we went into san francisco and didn't miss it. we used super sightseeing to go to alcatraz and the city tour. and, used the grey line tours for yosemite and the muir woods/sausolito tours. both companies picked you up and dropped you off at your hotel. although, super sightseeing is only a block from the hotel and grey line is about 2 1/2 blocks from the hotel. we used the cable cars to get to china town and union square.i would definitely use this hotel again.

great staff we stayed here for two nights in early june. i was very pleased with the hotel. the room was small, i guess because we had booked under a government rate, so they probably gave us the smallest they had. it was on the top (the 4th) floor, though. a view of the courtyard, which seems to be an inaccessible small yard with some trees planted and a net on top, so no birds to watch. the bed was very comfy, the minibar well stocked and the tv worked. the room was very clean and the shower had one of the curved curtain rods, so plenty of room.the front desk staff was great, helpful on check-in, had supply of extra coffee supplies for the room and stamps for purchase, offered to mail our postcards, and the concierge desk seemed very busy. we didn't use them, but people over there looked happy and satisfied. the wine in the evening was nice (go early or you will miss appetizers), as was the coffee and (very small) biscottis in the morning. my husband wanted a more substantial breakfast. great location, if you are doing north and east san francisco stuff. walking distance to the wharf, the north beach area (great food!!!) and the alcatraz ferry dock.
thoroughly enjoyed our stay bw tuscan inn sf - king room

just ok we stayed here for 4 nights may 24-27we booked on the basis of the reviews here and were a little disappointed.positives.it's in a good location by fisherman's wharf/pier 39.it's a good base for exploring and near the cable car stops.complimentatry coffee/tea in the morning and wine/beer in the evening.free wireless internet access.staff courteous and helpful.price.negativessmall room - not enough storage room if you had suitcases.noisy a/c - i mentioned this and it was made quieter but still unusable for more than a few minutes at a time because of the noise.housekeeping - we returned one evening and the bed appeared to have been made but when the sheets were pulled back the mattress was exposed. also the sheets had holes.room generally had a 'tired' feel.this is a good base if that's all you are using it for but don't expect too much.ps we did the segway tour and it was excellent - highly recommended!

a decent place to stay while in san fran the tuscan inn is typical of the city hotels we've stayed at in the past. that basically means it costs a lot more than a roadside/highway exit hotel but isn't quite as nice.we heard numerous things about the fisherman's wharf area, and many of them were true. there is plenty to do during the day because of the endless shops and restaurants, and transportation is available to take you to all places in the city as well as other destinations like alcatraz. at night the area takes on a different persona with homeless people hanging around the darkness, but at no point did we ever feel unsafe walking the streets. the weirdest thing was how everything seemed to close between 9 and 10 at night when there seemed to be so many tourists lurking about.the hotel, located a few blocks from fisherman's wharf as well as ghiardelli square, has a nice italian theme that carries into the lobby as well as the uniforms for the parking valets. speaking of parking, you're going to have to pay and it's going to have to be valet service, as there are no free/self park lots that are part of the hotel. not only is it pricey at $36/day, but having nothing but valet parking means you have no access to your car unless you have one of the valets fetch it from the lot for you.our hotel room was very small and felt absolutely cramped when we had our two suitcases opened on the floor. the bathroom containing the toilet and the shower was also very small, not to mention the sink and counter directly outside of it. the overall look was fairly bland and a bit dated, but all of the furniture was in excellent shape and nothing appeared worn, dirty or neglected. two negatives: turning the bathroom light on also turns the counter light on, meaning a middle-of-the-night trip to the bathroom means the whole side of the room gets illuminated; and the wooden shutters that were installed in place of traditional curtains to add to the hotel's theme do absolutely nothing to keep the room dark once the sun comes up.i'm sure there are better hotels in the area but considering how expensive most are, the tuscan inn ends up being a relative bargain. if you're willing to accept a hotel that can best be described as clean and comfortable, this one will do you just fine.

tuscan inn diane from edmonton, alberta, canadawe stayed at the hotel may 22 to may 25, 2007 and found the staff and particularly the concierge very helpful. the location is great and accessible to all parts of the city by bus, cable car or the f train. room was clean and had everything we needed. the whole staff at the tuscan inn was very hospitable and i highly recommend this hotel.

san frantastic! we have just returned from a week long holiday in san francisco. i just wanted to convey what a great destination it is. we stayed in the best western, tuscan inn on fishermans wharf. the hotel is pretty much as you'd expect from the chain , nice clean rooms well serviced, and the staff were extremely helpful- very pleasant to deal with. the decor is nice and the evening wine reception is pretty entertaining! however the hotel internet at 6usd for 15 mins is a bit pricey.we felt the fisherman's wharf area while touristy is not without some charm. check out the old arcade games in the musee mechanique if the weather's not great.!!

perfect wow!! this hotel is a gem. great location in fishermans wharf.the hotel gave us a bottle of sparkling wine and cookies on arrival, as it was my boyfriends birthday which i thought was a lovely gesture. the room was a good size but the bathroomm was very small. not good if you have children with you i guess. the bonus in the room was a coffee maker which is a rare find in the usa. will be going back there for sure!

adequate but overrated we stayed here for 4 nights. the hotel was extremely busy (apparently fully booked) during our stay although once out of the lobby area we did not see or hear many other guests. we did not avail ourselves of the morning coffee (tried it on day one and it wasnéˆ¥??› particularly nice coffee) or the éˆ¥?¦¤anagers evening wine receptionéˆ¥? in our opinion, a bit of faux italian dèœ…cor, some nice throw pillows on the bed and smaller than average rooms doesnéˆ¥??› really stretch to éˆ¥?·“uropean-style boutique hoteléˆ¥? this hotel can trade on its location which, although a rather ugly and unappealing area full of tacky tourist shops, predictable chain restaurants and large number of tour groups, is an excellent base to explore the city. we booked a non-smoking room with for much better italian food head up to north beach éˆ¥?5 to 10 minute walk éˆ¥?where you will find a good choice of independent restaurants and cafes around the colombus ave/washington square area. you will be surrounded by locals (rather than tour groups) and will have a more realistic italian experience. and if you really canéˆ¥??› live without burgers, donéˆ¥??› go to the usual chains, make the 5 minute walk to burgermeister at 759 columbus.

location, location, location the best western tuscan inn is at the perfect location in san francisco. it is two blocks from fisherman's wharf, and in walking distance to pier 39, ghirardelli square and many other tourist spots. the rooms were cozy, very tastefully done and included a fantastic bed. the convenience of a very good restaurant on site added to its value. i would not consider staying anywhere else for future visits to san francisco. i highly recommend this property. the only minor complaint was the a/c unit which was a bit noisy. we experienced an unusal heat wave while we were there so normally, you would not even turn on the a/c unit and would enjoy a perfectly, quiet sleep.

good value we stayed for 3 nights as a stopover before spending a month in australia. we found the hotel and room clean and perfectly adequate. the staff were friendly and the free coffee and biscoti each morning and wine at 6pm each evening were occassions when one could meet other guests. the location was excellent for the whalf attractions including cruises and tram/bus tours and for the cable car into union square. the restaurant attached to the hotel was very good and there were many others within walking distance with fresh fish being the speciality.all in all we found the hotel to be good value and ideal for a leisure visit to san francisco.

nice hotel - won't be going again though the hotel was nicely decorated and so too were the rooms. initially, a new receptionist mistakenly gave us a smoking room but the very capable and pleasant assistant general manager laura rectified this problem the next day.the second room we had was really noisy because the inconsiderate people in the next room continually had their loud air-conditioning units on all day and all night.someone attempted to get into our room at 4:20am on night and fortunately we had our deadbolt and chain on the door. this kind of security issue must be a regular problem because there is a rather large section on safety security in the room directory and warnings on the card that they give you with your key cards in. following the hotels guidance about dealing with a security issue, we reported the incident immediately with the front desk. the gentleman who answered spoke little english and clearly didnéˆ¥??› really understand what we were trying to say. my husband gave up and wedged two suitcases and a chair in front of the door too.the area (fishermanéˆ¥??? wharf) can be unsafe at times. we spotted the usual pick-pocketers/bag snatchers hanging around the crossings in the area early evening time. they work in teams waiting for you to be distracted waiting for the walking man signal. if go to this area always be extra vigilant, also with street performers, again they are a distraction to you.we used to love san francisco but weéˆ¥???e decided we wonéˆ¥??› be going again. we were there for four nights/three full days and beggars must have asked us for money at least 100 times (iéˆ¥??“ not exaggerating), itéˆ¥??? bad.

great location really good location for fisherman's wharf. however i was a little disappointed with tuscan inn. i'd read good reviews on here so maybe my expectations were high, but this was the first hotel i stayed in during my tour of n america out of a total of 10 hotels of similar standard. i'd say it came about 7th in preference. the main fault was that the room was small and cramped. however it was clean and the bed was comfortable and it had a good shower and plenty of hot water. the staff were very pleasant but i don't think i'd stay there again.

great location but not great experiance the tuscan inn is in a great location if you want to do the touristy things around fisherman's wharf but don't expect anything grand. the hotel is quite small and isn't in a very smart area, it's surrounded by car parks and some shops, but on the plus side it is very close to the cable car terminal and the boudin bread bakery. so it's good for pier 39, the bay trips, ghirardelli centre and the cannery, but that is really all it has going for it.the room was small but it did have a desk, table chairs and unit for fridge/tv stand. this meant it was all a little cramped. there was no wardrobe , just a curtained off rail. the wash basin was in the room without any privacy and there was a small bathroom for the toilet and bath/shower. there was an individual air-con unit in the window which was very noisy and didnéˆ¥??› generate much cold air. we found it much better to just open the window which obviously wouldnéˆ¥??› work on hot days. we overlooked a small courtyard but the other windows were very close so privacy was an issue.the maids woke us the first day by shouting to each other outside the room at 8am but it didnéˆ¥??› happen after that. the room was cleaned, but not spotless, and the bed was made badly. this sloppy attitude was much the same at the front desk where they didnéˆ¥??› really seem to know what was going on and there were usually queues as they were slow to deal with people. they were polite and did help eventually, but it was hard work.the hotel provides free hot drinks and biscotti in the mornings, which was good quality but why? itéˆ¥??? not a great breakfast is it? and there is a coffee machine in the room. i would rather save the money.it has an adjoining restaurant which we used for lunch one day. service was poor and they got our order wrong, but they did correct it at no extra cost and the food was good. i personally would look around for a better hotel a little way out , maybe further over towards the ghirardelli centre and the other cable car stop, if i was to stay on the bay front.

great location.. my only regret is that we could only stay one night because of work obligations. the hotel is in a great location, close to fishermans wharf, cable cars, ect. when we arrived we were pleasantly suprised . this place looks nothing like your typical best western. very nice warm, welcoming lobby. the room was decent. a little on the small side. but very nicely furnished. the mini bar was a nice touch, but very $$$. there is a safeway trader joes within walking distance , my advice , better to purchase your own snacks drinks. (we did indulge in the oj vodka and 1 beer . the cost was almost 16 $. !!!!) as far as the parking ...it's san francisco .it's going to cost you no matter what. plan on spending 36 to 40 $. all in all it was nice overnight getaway .i would stay again.
location,location,location clean,friendly,and the location was perfect. transportation is close by. i highly recommend this hotel..i can promise you will not be dissappointed.

fantastic in every way this is a gem of a hotel. we just returned from a one week stay. perfect location on the edge of fisherman's wharf. mason cable car line around the corner. bus route across the street. within close walking distance to everything - fisherman's wharf, safeway (for groceries), barnes noble, etc. safe neighbourhood. hotel restaurant was superb.great service and friendly front desk. the concierge service is excellent. made arrangements for car rental and recommended several great restaurants. free wine and mingle from 5 to 6pm. each night. what a treat. plus the price was way cheaper than other hotels nearby. rooms are small but very quaint. choose a courtyard view room (ours was rm. 255 - away from elevators). very clean. we would return in an instant!staying at the tuscan inn really topped off a perfect stay in san francisco.
best ever stay at sf wharf tuscan inn entry

great location for alcatraz this is a great hotel amongst the many that are close to fisherman's wharf. i had a room at the back that was quiet and very nicely furnished. my friends had an identical room at the front of the hotel that was, however, quite noisy at night. there was a free wine tasting that the hotel put on that we were, unfortunately, too jet-lagged to participate in.

great find upon arriving late through no fault of our own and finding our room double booked we were put up in a nearby sister hotel (anchorage) until our room was ready the next day and they give us a complimentary bottle of champagne - after this though there were no more snags and everything went great - hotel staff friendly and helpful - rooms were quiet, clean and comfortable - food in the restaurant fabulous - the situation of the hotel was very convenient - just a few mins walk from fishermans wharf with a public transport stop, supermarket, small shops, bars and cafes also really close at hand - approx 10 mins walking distance for ferries to alcatraz and bay cruise, etc - would definitely stop here again

good hotel,great location had a great 2 night stay,returning from nz.on 15th march 2007. rooms good, decor very well done in italian style (tuscan!) exellent location for pier39, fishermans wharf and trams etc, with a large safeway a block away. all within easy walking distance.
convenient to fishermans wharf excellent location near fishermans wharf. rooms very impressively decorated and clean.

wonderful --- not! we're sitting in our hotel room, waiting for another set of towels (there are three of us and we were given towels for two). the ice machine is empty. the vending machine doesn't work. the concierge does not answer the phone. exactly who runs this place!?!?!?!?!

fabulous hotel from checkin to checkout, our stay was fabulous. the staff's professional, spirited attitude--be they reservationist, valet, front desk, or housekeeper--deserves 5 stars. for instance, mention in passing by one of us about an allergy to down brought an instant change of linens. the hotel's evening wine hour and morning's biscotti hour also distinguish the property as a cut above, and our group, which has stayed at many a biz hotel, had no problem whatsoever; in fact, a courtesy upgrade got us a fine meeting space with free internet, which even impressed our boss. and while we weren't expecting to dine at their restaurant, given how many fine ones there are to choose from in this neighborhood, as it turns out we relished the food, both dinner and breakfast. we're already planning our next stay.

great find in touristy fishermans wharf just came back from a one night stay at the tuscan inn. although we are locals having lived in sf bay area for the last 16 years, we were attending a wine event at fort mason and didn't want to have to drive home. when i got a great deal ($99 including parking!!!!) i jumped at it. but being the wharf had no great expectations, and didn't really need much more than a bed for the night.this hotel is a weird hybrid.. calling itself best western, but being in partnership with kimpton hotels (which for those that don't know is a chain of more upscale boutique hotels). i have to think this is why the hotel looks and feels a lot better than other wharf hotels i've stayed at previously. and frankly more upscale than other best westerns too.staff were very pleasant, always asking if we needed directions or anything (we didn't, but it's nice to be asked) and smiling and opening doors etc. (including all the maids and bell boys we encountered) small touches, but very pleasant. we didn't make it to the wine hour (having been drinking wine all day, it was not high on our agenda!) but have done that at other kimpton hotels and it's a nice extra.our room looked like a room in a kimpton hotel, nice bed with decent white linens with burgundy and black throw pillows and accents. the bathroom had not been remodeled in alignment, but it was all very clean and perfectly acceptable.the great thing for us was the free parking. normally parking is $36 a night so getting that thrown in was a fantastic steal. what i didn't realize at the time is that the park the car across the street in a public lot (i assumed it would be in covered hotel parking). agree with other comments that breakfast at cafe pescatore is nothing to write home about, but again, my expectations were low, as it is just that kind of area.but if i could get a deal like this on the same hotel, i'd go back every year as we attend the same event every year, and the location and facilities were exactly what we needed.

good place, if you can get a discount we stayed at the bw tuscan inn only because they were offering a great winter deal -$99 for a room with king-size bed and free parking (which usually goes for at least $30 in this part of town). the room was nicely decorated - nothing too fancy. staff were very friendly and courteous. and, we appreciated the complementary touches - wine/cheese in the evening and coffee/tea and biscotti in the morning. location is very convenient to fisherman's wharf, north beach, russian hill, and the embarcadero. overall, we would recommend this place to friends, especially if they are able to get a good discount and free parking.
