wonderful stay at hyatt just stayed at this great property. the hotel has gone through a $30 million renovation looks updated, modern, fresh. beautiful public spaces to enjoy as well. pool area was lovely, spacious. get a room facing the ocean pool...lovely to see west hollywood the santa monica mountains as well. the rooms are large for a city hotel with the terrace it feels even larger. the rooms are clean and very well decorated. the staff was incredibly nice. very prompt service, and personalized as well. they always try to use your name, which makes this large chain hotel a little more personal. the concierge arranged our tours restaurant reservations with a keen idea of our needs.......a family la experience made excellent recommendations for us. especially enjoyed the tour they recommended from the hotel. nice not to have to drive into hollywood to get it it's a small co. that offers a very knowledgable tour. originally had hoped to stay in santa monica, but after this experience would definately return here again. the location was superb-centrally located to everything. less driving as a result. also nice outdoor mall across the street which had a nice food court. a great option when you just don't want to get in the car or eat at the hotel, although we did enjoy the restaurant here too. going to la with children, i would highly recommend this location the hotel. it was fantastic!

older, but still a winner. this hotel is an older property. i last stayed here about ten years ago or more. it has a good feel to it. service is pretty good. the bed was comfortable. the large flat screen tv in the room was a plus.parking is expensive -- $31 a day valet, the pay lot was $20 a day.there was no coffee in the room. i could not get the golf channel which was a disappointment.the banquet facilities and meeting facilities were excellent. of course, century city is a great area in la.

one of the best hotels in the us stayed there for a conference. newly renovated, beautiful property. i stayed in a classic room and it even had a flat screen tv, a beautiful bathroom, and a balcony. the staff at the hotel is also amazing and willing to help. the conceirge was even able to get me tickets to see jay leno.

good quality 4* hotel the plaza is as you would expect a 4* us hotel. the bedrooms are large, with balconies and the beds incredibly comfortable. the hotel has a nice bustling lobby area. the pool area is nice although the gym is currently in a temporary marquee as the new gym is being finished (it looks like it will be a high quality gym) just across the road is an excellent shopping mall with a really good food court.the one thing i would say this hotel lacks is any evidence of its history, it is just like any other 4* hotel.

very kind restaurant manager in breeze from ireland or scotland we had an excellent time here at the new century plaza hotel, which is now run by the hyatt company - what a change in service, as we have come here every december from france for a week to do shopping for christmas in this area.we ate at breeze each morning and got to know all the staff in breeze, after a few days the managers got to know us -+i forget hi name + from ireland, he had a lot of laughs each morning and it was a great highlight to our day.what a wonderful hotel and staffjean blanc
nicely renovated hyatt near century city/beverly hills view from entrance
a pleasant la hyatt experience more photos

good location, rooms as new stayed at this hotel for 1 night back on october 2 2006, at the end of our 3 month around the world trip.the hotel is going through a major renovation, and check in upgraded us to a newly renovated floor (12th) which was a nice gesture.rooms were very nice, with lcd tv and lovely king size beds.didnt eat at hotel, because generally find them all too pricey but there is a westfield accross the road with some nice restaraunts open at night.hotel has a hertz agency located in it, which was handy because we hired a car and drove around mailub, santa monica and beverley hills. the hotel is centrally located which is a major plus.also not too far to lax either.hope this helps

nice introduction to la but no pool i was staying here because of a conference. i was looking forward to this conference for quite some time and kept checking the hotel's website for more information. no where on the website was i told that the pool was going to be closed due to construction, or that the hotel would be renovating. the lobby construction wasn't that bad, but when it sounds like people are bowling on the floor above, that's when you begin to expect some type of forewarning. i'm used to staying in best western's and quality inn's, so i was really looking forward to staying in a nice hotel. the room was nice, but some basic ammenities found in lower class hotels were missing. for instance, no refrigerator or coffee maker and no hand soap in the bathroom. but, most importantly, when one is traveling to la from seattle in october, one expects a pool at the hotel. the closed pool was probably the biggest disappointment. the bowling alley sounds above were another strike against this hotel. you'd think if construction was happening they wouldn't put people on the same floor or directly underneath the construction, but they did. this hotel was definitely lacking in basic communication and customer service skills. the valets were nice and the conference facilities were good, too. the location is right next to an outdoor mall, which is nice, too.

cursed behemoth i first stayed at the century plaza back in the late 1980's, when it was at its peak, and played host to luminaries like ronald reagan and others....in the early 90s, it started to slide. it was bought by the westin chain, abandoned by them, and most recently appropriated by hyatt. for the last fifteen years or so, it's been somewhat cursed; business has fallen, and the hotel has lost the glossy, sprawling sheen that it used to have...and now feels like a great, barren architectural husk, left by the side of the highway. admittedly, it is--once again--in transition. signboards in the lobby tout the glories to come in 2007--redesigned rooms, a new spa, sumptuous new restaurants! right now, however, it's a disaster...the gift shop is having a fire-sale; cleaning carts stand idle and abandoned in the lobby; room service trays with congealed food line the hall. the staff is doing its utmost to look positive and offer brisk service in the midst of the gloomy malestrom around them, but they're fighting a losing battle. to make matters worse, all of century city is under construction these days, not just the hotel...a mammoth business complex--future home to talent agency caa---is being erected right across the street; i awakened every morning to the sound of ear-splitting jackhammers. i was forced to stay at this hotel on business, but spent the whole time wishing i could slip next door, to the far grander park hyatt, or--even better--the four seasons on doheny. give the century plaza a second chance in the new year....it would be rude and pre-emptive not to, i suppose...but right now? avoid at all costs!
star treatment! front view of hotel

exceptional hotel located just a 10 minute drive from the sunset strip, this is an exceptional hotel as regards both the amenities and the staff. the hotel is undergoing a $20 million dollar renovation. i stayed in a renovated section of the hotel. the rooms were large, extremely clean and newly furnished with an exceptionally modern bathroom. the fitness centre rivals a professional gym with both its size and the quality and quantity of equipment and the pool and hot tub (outdoors) area provide a great place to relax. the staff was very curteous and helpful, always offering a friendly hello, good afternoon or good evening.the only drawback is the price of parking: $29 valet with the only other option being a public lot which charges $20 everytime you enter the lot. however, the valet service, while expensive, is quite convenient as a quick call will guaranty that your car is waiting for you once you exit and you can exit and re-enter as many times a you like.

love this hotel just returned from staying at the hyatt regency century plaza for a convention july 26-30th. pricey even at the convention rate but well worth the money. from the time i pulled into the valet parking area until i checked-out the hotel treated us as if we were the most important guests in the hotel. the hotel check-in was great our room wasn't ready but the lady at the desk put a hold on a room with 2 double beds and we were able to check in within the next hour. our bags were promptly brought to our room by a bell man. the room was wonderful with down duvet covers a table and two chairs (workstation), bedside chair and stand, mini-bar (which they emptied for a small fee so we could use the refrig.for our picnic supplies), closet with ironing board, safe, bathroom wonderful, and a coffee maker. we also had a nice view of the pool and mall next door. all rooms have sliding patio doors and a balcony. we felt like we were getting the star treatment. the hotel was able to handle a convention of over 1000 people and then turn around the day after and handle a high profile political person staying with them without compromising the convention activities. the hotel was located in a wonderful area 30 minutes from hollywood, 20-30 minutes from the grove, 10-15 minutes from beverly center, 30 minutes from lax. i would definately stay here again and recommend it to others.

not impressed with the century plaza i stayed here for 4 nights, before moving to the world class beverly hills hotel. this hotel is very bland, the lobby does not have much character and kind of reminded me of walking into a large office building, just very plain and lackluster, not at all like it was years ago. i stayed in room #631, which had some issues. two of the three telephones in the room did not work, one of the lamps in back of the chair was missing a light bulb, the balcony was filthy, stains on the balcony carpet, cigarette butts left in the corner from the previous guests. the entire 6th floor had a musty smell to it as well, they should invest in some air freshener. as far as the staff, the most outstanding was the valet, he was very friendly and kind, went out of his way for the guests. housekeeping was bad, they left trash in the room, knocked on the door at 7:45am even with my do not disturb sign out. i got a decent internet rate of $209 per night, plus tax, which was not great but not bad considering this hotel is close to beverly hills. also, the pool can have potential if the poolside attendents actually do their job and bring guests drinks, all they were doing was standing around talking, not waiting on the guests....i think this hotel ran better under westin management.

loved it!! we stayed at the century plaza for a week for our 5th wedding anniversary trip. it was worth every penny! we got a double bed suite that had breath taking views of the city. the linens were the most comfortable we have ever slept on! the pool area is beautiful and very peaceful. the rooms are cozy and spotless. the parking is pricey-$29.00 a day but the valets treat you like gold and we never waited long for our car. they have a public parking lot behind the hotel that you can choose to use that has no affliation with the hotel. however, it is $20.00 in and $20.00 out so its much better just to use the hotels valet service. i would highly recommend this hotel for romantics or just a quick getaway weekend. we plan on staying there again.

pricey, but worth it some friends and i traveled to la for a conference at the hyatt. there is some construction on little santa monica blvd (after exitng the freeway) and several lanes were closed during our time there. upon arrival at the hyatt, we were able to check-in very quickly and the front desk staff were friendly and accomodating. there was some congestion at the front of the hotel (like most others) with guests loading, unloading, valet parking, etc. parking at the hotel was an issue for us because the hotel is only 'responsible' for their valet parking area ($20/day). self-parking can be found at a garage behind the hotel spa that is owned by a third party, but used by hotel guests and shoppers at the century plaza mall. the guest rooms were farily large with double closets and an in-room safe (extremely small, only good for jewelry). our room faced the construction site across the street (yuck!), but had a cute balcony with chairs that let you get some beverly hills sunshine during the day. the bed and bathroom was clean and well-maintained. the bed pillows were very comfortable, plentiful, and fluffy (not like most hotels). the meeting facilities had great acoustics (always a plus) and were mostly accesible by the main bank of elevators. there is a mezzanine level that is only accesible by staircase from the lobby and a second bank of elevators. if you're a shopper, you'll love the close proximity to everything. century plaza (macy's, louis v., ann taylor, etc.) is directly across the street from the rear door of the hyatt. rodeo drive and the beverly center are only about a 15 mintue drive away. the nightly rate at the hyatt will run you upwards of $200 (in most cases), but it was worth it for us.

not the best hyatt...but not bad we got a decent price from priceline. the location was great, easy to get to beverly hills/the strip, and also to santa monica. the concierge service was fantastic--not only called multiple restaurants to get a us a table for a saturday night, but also made good suggestions and followed up with calls to my cell phone to confirm our plans. excellent service. the valet price is over the top, but you do have no choice, so just consider it part of the cost. sign up for the hyatt gold passport (free to do at their website) so you can use the gym for free, otherwise you have to pay some exorbinate fee (again, nickel and dimed). the bed is comfortable and the rooms are a good size. we didn't hear any real hallway noise, though the street noise was present, even on the 12th floor. they obviously put a lot of money into updating what would otherwise be a very dated hotel. we did not eat/drink there, but the lobby had a great vibe and lots of business travelers were having drinks and a good time.

nice experience tarnished by all the gothchas check in was fast after our car was surrounded by valet parking guys who aggresively hyped valet by saying it would save me money over self-park. when i got the bill i was shocked, as they added $29 for half day of parking. add tips, and it came to nearly $35. the first room offered smelled strongly like smokers, but they moved us quickly down the hall to a similar otherwise ample room. the rollaway was delivered quickly, and the only other unpleasant surprise was $13 for a supposed tv movie we did not order. my daughter simply turned on the tv and watched a 1 hr. disney sit-com. if that costs $13 (!), they should be very obvious in disclosing that to guests. they did remove the charge when i politely protested it. the hotel is in the heart of century city's business district, so no street parking whatsoever -- they kind of have you where they want you and in my opinion exploit that. otherwise a decent stay accross from major high-rise construction. not quite worth the $130 (incl. taxes, etc.) we paid, but we were down to the wire.... i have gotten much better values from priceline at half or one-third the cost, as nearby as anaheim doubletree suites. reading other reviews of this hyatt, a common theme emerges of aggressive charging of extras, which clouds your view of an otherwise nice roomstay in a comfortable bed and bath, etc.

great hotel we stayed here for 3 days while visiting la. the valets were terrific, although the daily price of $29 was a little high. lounge area was very nice to have a drink and appetizers. the wait staff in the restaurant were superb and had us taste testing different smoothies. the hotel is walking distance to a great mall and movie theater. we ate at a fabulous italian restaurant called carmine's on santa monica blvd, a short drive or a long walk from the hyatt. the beds, pillows and the rollaway bed were first class.

great location, nice pool, ok food .... i stayed at the hyatt century city for 4 days for a business conference. the hotel rooms are spacious as are the bathrooms. my only negative comment about the hotel rooms would be the housekeeping, it took over 45 minutes to get fresh towels one evening and 2 days in a row the bathroom area was not swept or mopped, as there was still plenty of hair on the bathroom floor. when you are paying over $250/night and in la you expect housekeeping services to be a bit better.the hotel catering is not good at all, they served the same bellpepper goulash on 3 different occasions and it gets old fast. if you are going to use the hotel's catering department please taste the food before hand.i would stay here again, the location is suberb and the staff very friendly.

nice stay! after reading some of the reviews on this hotel, i was a bit skeptical upon our arrival. i was pleasantly surprised to find out that we had none of the problems that others had experienced on this board. the hotel is very nice and clean with very comfy beds! nice, spacious baths as well. our car was parked in valet with in/out priveledges and within 10 minutes of calling our car was waiting out front.there is a mini bar/snacks in the room that are quite expensive. when we noticed on our sheet that some of the products were checked off as used, we contacted the front desk and they told us that we would not be charged for them. we also had some incorrect room charges upon check out but they were taken care of as well. the front desk staff was very polite, friendly, and helpful (they printed out our boarding passes for us).i would definitely recommend this hotel for your la stay. be aware that there is not much in the way of entertainment, restaurants, etc. surrounding the hotel so you will need to have a car available to you.

can i live there? beautiful place! the room was very clean and nicely decorated with the kind of beds, pillows and comforters that you never want to get out of. for just an extra $12 per day, there is a lovely spa (steam room, sauna, fabulous showers) and excellent work-out facility. the front desk and room service staff were great . . . although the spa staff weren't especially adept at helping acquaint this first time user to their facilities. i hope to stay there as much as possible!!!

wonderful stay! we got to the hotel late, because of a delayed flight. when we arrived we were told that they had given away the last room with 2 beds.( i had requested ahead of time) i was upset because there was 3 of us and i did not want to have to share a full size bed. before i said anything the woman checking us in said we are going to give you a suite. the suite was huge, two bathrooms, two large rooms, a dining area that seated 6. we had two large balconies with nice view of the pool.the room was spotless, and comfortable. the valet staff was very nice, the restaurant staff at breeze was extra nice and the food was great. the room service was quick and the food was very good. we loved the lobby with the piano playing, and light food and cocktails available. we had a wonderful time in beverly hills and the hotel stay made it even better!!

very comfortable hotel spent one night here in decmeber at a great rate on priceline. very well furnished room, comfortable bed and very welcoming staff. was treated as if i were paying full price too! very clean room with all the ameneties one would expect from a hotel of this class. lovely balcony with a good view. it is now operating under the hyatt umbrella and is no longer a westin.
wonderful experience!! beautiful suite on 18th floor - view 2

good value stayed at the hotel (now carrying the hyatt, not the westin name) for four nights. my room, on one of the top floors, was very well furnished, with a beautiful modern bathroom. the bed was extremely comfortable and the room had free etherent internet access. upon arrival, in the early hours of the morning, i noticed the tv wasn't working. the quick arrival of the maintenance technician soon solved the problem, in spite of the very late hour. i was initially concerned to see a major construction site across the road from the hotel. i nevertheless never heard anything, and forgot all about it during my stay. first class (expensive)spa in the hotel. nice mall (currently under refurbishment) 2 minutes away. all in all - a good experience.
it was a great hotel this hotel was a nice one i stayed here in the middle of july and it was a bit chilly but we loved it the pool could have been a bit cleaner but overall i liked it a lot

very disappointed i recently stayed at the century plaza hotel in los angeles and was quite disappointed. stained carpets, mildew in bath along with missing grout. floor was actually slanted at walls to the point that the tv armoire was acutally secured to the wall with a heavy chain. i spent over $250 per night for this.....only positive was that the bed was very comfortable. i was charged for use of the courtesy bar...when i never opened it...although they took the charge off when i complained, when i went down to the front desk to get a new invoice, i noted the clerk on the phone with another guest who was apparently charged for the bar too and calling to complain about the erroneous charge...almost felt like this was some kind of scam. valet parking (with in and out privileges) was a pricey $27 per day. i would not recommend this hotel given the poor condition of the rooms.

pleasant rooms but terrible customer service i stayed at this hotel for 4 days in may. i was somewhat apprehensive due to the prior reviews i had read regarding indifferent and rude staff. unfortunately, i found this to be true. the valet staff was wonderful but the front desk staff (every single person i dealt with) was boderline sullen. i happen to meet a very nice starwood employee staying at the hotel for a training class and she had the same experience. she also encourgaged us to voice our complaints in writing to the corporate office. the concierge was even worse. everytime we approached the concierge he was either on a personal call or chatitng with a hotel employee. he acted annoyed that we would interrupt his personal conversations. the spa staff and the gift shop employee were very pleasant and helpful.our room was clean, spacious and in fairly good condition. we had a great view overlooking portions of the city and beyond to the ocean. i liked the location because it was in a quiet location near two malls, several studios, good eateries, the expressway and rodeo drive. we also made it to santa monica with no traffic in a little under 30 minutes.if the staff's customer service skills were improved (or the lot of them fired and people who actually wanted the jobs hired), it would be a totally pleasant experience. i would only return if i could not find a comparable hotel which was not that much more expensive.

nice hotel stayed there for 5 nights in september 2005. had a nice room overlooking the pool. i thought the decor in the room was nice and the bathroom decor was very hip. room and bathroom were clean and the room was a good size too. the bed was super comfortable. i normally don't like hotel beds but this one was great! the ammenities in the room were good too. the only down side is the price. i was fortunate that i got a special rate as i was there on business, however, i just think the price overall is too high and you don't even get breakfast nor is the gym free to use! that's ridiculous! also for the price, i'd expect the common corridors to be a lot cleaner. i thought the carpet area looked a bit dingy, personally, and when someone left their room service dishes in the hall or dropped something it was there forever. i just think that for a hotel of this star rating and the price that should be cleaned. i've stayed at other hotels at the same price and star rating that would never leave dirty room service dishes in the hall way. they send someone to collect the dishes.anyway if you're going anytime soon, get a room facing the pool as there is some construction across the street so it's not a nice view. the valet parking is pricey at $23 but you have all day in and out privilges (i believe there is a cheaper self park). i wasn't floored with the service of the staff, though the cleaning staff were exceptional. also, on thursdays in the patio area they give complementary manicures for a tip, and their is entertainment, etc. very nice!

dump! this place is pathetic! the rooms are so musty that i was sure to see mold growing on the walls. the furniture is 70s, the carpet is worn-out, and the down comforters are never clean - i stay here every week for work unfortunately. was staying at the park hyatt down the street (which is awesome) but had to switch because this place is $15 cheaper - company policy.i received 10,000 starwood points the first week i stayed because of the filthy room. the breeze restaurant is really bad - they charged my room for somebody elses meal and the front desk would not take it off even though they had a copy of the bill with somebody else's name clearly printed on it. the service ----! they always have 1 or 2 people checking in 30 guests on monday nights.the gym charges $12 (free if your platinum or $6 if you are gold). starwood preferred guests gets no preferential treatment. the valet parking is a ripoff (again it is cheaper at the hyatt down the road).really bad hotel!

okay room, awful staff this hotel is convenient to the century city mall, which if you don't have a car, are on a budget and staying there for 5 days quickly become boring.the hall and lobby are luxurious (gotta keep the appearences up). the room we were in was always clean. but that's all for the good points.we spent 5 days there in the beggining of august, and here's what happened,we arrived at the hotel after midnight, arms full of bagages, but none of the staff helped us, two women.we made it to the lobby by ourselves but could not understand a word the lady who checked us in was saying.we went up to the room on the 14th floor, following the staff orders, to take the elevators on the opposite side from the check in desk, still no one to help us with our baggages.we entered the room, the smell was musty and old, we dropped on the bed and slept instantly, but we were awoken by construction at 6 a.m!!!the cold came into the room from the balcony made our room icy cold at about 3 a.m, even with the drapes closed (not so useful when they don't touch the floor) then, on the 3rd day, a employee knocked and told us that we were due to leave earlier in the morning, then we told her it was not 3 days but 5 days and she excused herself saying it must have been an computer error.we ran down at the cheking desk, scared that they would charge us 2 imaginary days on our credit card, there they confirmed that their computer said we were supposed to have a 3 days stay, we told them the voucher we gave when we checked in said 5 days, of course they said they had lost the voucher, and that they would make their researches, and that everything would be settled on our departure date, with a tone that clearly said they would leave it on the side until we check out and just take the 2 days stay on our credit card, then pay back we were not lying.i had to call our travel agency and have them call the hotel so they could confirm it was a 5 days stay all paid.then we went back to the desk asking for a paper saying they wouldn't take any money for the stay from the credit card. they told me i would have it at the end of the day, but nothing, they said the manager wanted them to wait 24 hours to make the papers, could not understand why but said ok, again nothing when we asked the paper the next day.i had to yell at them for a young guy to nicely print the front page of our file on their computer, eventually. i don't know what irritated me more, the women who told me to come back again and again and again for nothing, or the women who pretended to help us, but looked at us like we were dirt on her shoes after our travel agency called them.even the concierge wasn't very helpful, but i think it was more because of a limited knowledge about their job.

better options in la but better then the bonaventure just ok. rooms are a good size and have been redone to catch up to the 90's but none of the cool new features like flat panels.very limited benefits for platinum members. no club or concierge level. no free breakfast. no welcome gift. no bonus points to exchange for lack of welcome gift. even though they have tons of suites, no upgrade was offered upon check in. valet is 27 bucks and self par does not include in and out priviledges.staff is just ok. pool is ok. location is so so due to massive construction accross the street on the fron side and noise from the hvac system at the mall on the back side.spa and fitness center look nice but are beverly hills prices.in room internet worked fine.tv has around 30 channels, ten of which are espn and sports networks.

classic la hotel stayed here recently on a business trip. the hotel is quintessential l.a.; even if i had been plopped into this hotel blindfolded, i would've known i was in la--it's just got that feel. rooms were large and clean and the heavenly bed did not dissapoint. the room service food was exceptional (steak sandwich was best i'd ever had) and delivered quickly. the pool and bar areas also looked very enticing, very hollywood, although i never used them. two very minor complaints: 1) service was average, but you pretty much expect that in an impersonal chain hotel, 2) while the hotel is very, very centrally located, the actual location of the building is kind of desolate, as it's surrounded by office buildings and a mall. then again, who walks in la? i would stay at the westin with no hesitation and recommend the hotel to anyone in la on business or pleasure.

overpriced and short on service i was excited to stay at this hotel because i love westin hotels and this was supposed to be a nice place. you can imagine my disappointment when my stay at the westin century plaza hotel spa was nowhere near satisfactory!in fact, my experience with this hotel was so miserable that i could not wait to check out and go home!!here is a list of just some of the things that went wrong:-in-room internet connection did not work-in-room tv internet did not work-a stranger's bag was left on my bed by a bell hop the first night of my stay-spa overcharged me for one service and refuses to refund me for a service i did not receivethis does not include all of the things that went wrong . . . i will save you from the misery of reading every single detail of my awful experience at the westin.i am a platinum starwood member and i will never ever stay at a westin hotel after my experience at the westin century plaza hotel spa in la.

great, clean, well located hotel this hotel was great!the furniture in all of the rooms is updated, with very modern bathrooms. i'm really picky and the only thing i noticed was that the carpet was a little worn, but nothing to complain about! the beds and the bathroom were great! every room has a balcony, ours had a great view of downtown la.the pool and patio area seemed great, we didn't get to spend enough time there though!our only complaints, the valet and parking is kind of a mess and it took a little while to get a cab.keep in mind that la is not really a walk around city, so you have to drive or take a cab pretty much everywhere. the hotel is located right by a huge shopping area and a short cab from the rodeo drive area and sunset strip. all in all this is a great hotel and we would go back in a heartbeat! fyi, we got a great deal on this hotel through priceline which made it even better!

rude staff the physical plant is very lovely - public areas, pool, etc. - but:- i stay in westins several times a month and usually the service is very good. for a luxe hotel and for a westin, the staff at this property was very rude and unhelpful. examples: - someone calling herself a sales manager was incredibly snobby and snippy with me when i asked her a very simple question. she had chin length straight blondish hair. look out for her. - i went to the pool towel stand, which was empty of towels. two people were standing behind the counter, a woman in uniform and a man in a suit. i asked them both where i could find towels. they both just stared coldly at me and didn't respond. i guess it was beneath them to answer a very standard and justifiable question. - some of the valets were incredibly cold and snobby, as if they were movie stars and i had dared to approach and ask for an autograph. i was driving a very expensive car, and i tip extravagantly, so it wasn't on that basis. i have no idea what their problem was. the only exception that i recall was a very sweet, older asian gentleman, who was very polite and helpful. the worst was one of the valets in tails and top hat, an older man who bore a slight resemblance to victor garber. he treated us as if we were filthy street urchins who had stuck our fingers in his food. also, the heavenly bed here was the least heavenly of all the westins i've stayed in. the mattress was not especially comfortable at all.

fine hotel (beware of construction) we spent three nights at this lovely hotel, and had a great stay. however, there is significant construction happening across the street, so if you do not get a room facing the ocean, your view and quiet will be destroyed. we had booked two king beds rooms, but, when i said we did not want construction views, we had to get two rooms with two double beds. supposedly, the king rooms all face the construction--and when i did see into one, it looked nightmarish. romantic stays beware if a large bed is crucial to your enjoyment.however, our spacious balconies had an excellent view of the hills, west la, santa monica, and off to the pacific horizon. fantastic for ocean breezes!the check-in process was smooth and friendly, and the valet service is excellent---efficient and fast. the rooms were clean, with comfy beds and nice bathrooms (including double-headed showers and decent (but not super-spacious) bathtubs.) the internet service in-room is very fast, and gives you a genuine 24 hours for 10 dollars. there is wireless in the lobby as well.room service was fast and efficient, and breeze, the on-site restaurant, is delicious. many of the items are organic, with free-range and hormone-free meat and veggies grown in their dedicated garden, cooked fresh. it's very pleasant to dine outside on the patio, too. all and all, i would definitely come back, but only if i was assured i would not face the construction--not until it's done.

disasterous stay i was expecting this hotel to be very classy given most of the write-up's i read and what with the price they charge here. i stayed here for 5 nights and by the 2nd night i could not wait to get out of there. it was a string of disasters basically. i am not usually one to complain, but i ended up being a regular at the concierge desk several times a day. i had to move rooms the first night due to construction across the road. i was placed in a room on the other side of the hotel which was not much better. the key i was given for the fridge did not fit and it took 3 attempts and visits to the concierge to get this sorted out. i had a telephone line in my room which was not working for the first 3 days and no-one could figure out why. it turned out the previous occupant had a bar placed on the phone line which was not taken off after their stay. the 3rd evening i had a couple walk in on me whilst i was dining. the hotel had double booked my room and reception made several phone calls to my room asking what i was doing in there. on my last evening i had no less than 6 or 7 phone calls and 2 knocks at my door asking what time i would be checking out the next morning as well as housekeeping under the impression i was checking out that evening for some reason and wanting to service my room. this hotel is definitely 'never again' and considering it is westin it was a very disorganised and unprofessional to say the least - especially for a business based guest. the hotel also needs a refurbisment, though they claim it had one recently. it was very outdated and rooms had a musty smell.

a great location and a fine stay i enjoyed a lovely weekend at the westin century plaza when i came to la to see the king tut exhibit. with my spg gold membership, i was upgraded to a lovely suite with a view of the pool and a hint of the pacific ocean. all rooms however enjoy the comforatable beds and contemporary bathrooms. i would have liked turn-down service or twice daily housekeeping, but the staff was happy to supply extra towel and a robe on request. the location of the hotel is superb--close to beverly hills and shopping. the pool is nice in the morning--but the afternoon sun is blocked by the neighboring mgm building. the spa looked nice--but they were booked up for treatments--my fault for not planning ahead. i had lunch and dinner at breeze-- both very pleasant-- and room service was prompt and acurate. i had no problems with the valet parking--as i would call ahead for my car from the room. overall-- a nice stay and i would return.

good hotel $25 valet parking seemed a little steep. you don't get in/out privileges with self parking. quick service but $25? whoa. even by la standards was pretty high.rooms are hugh with high ceilings. i think all or at least most of the rooms have a balcony. there's actually construction on both sides of the building so you're not going to escape noise. the side facing the swimming pool appears to get less construction noise. some signs of aging. the carpet seemed worn. bathtub wasn't shiny white marble. beds were nice but wasn't 100% heavenly bed quality -- a little softer than expected.good location -- only minutes to rodeo drive / bev hills. a 10 minute ride to west hollywood and santa monica.agree with other reviews that breakfast at breezes is pretty good. overall a nice hotel.

very good hotel stayed here for 2 nights in may 2005 while on a shopping vacation. the hotel is in a great location, convenient to both beverly hills and santa monica (it is right off of santa monica blvd in century city). obviously, if you are visiting la you need a car and this location is no exception. but it is a short drive from almost any attraction. the rooms are very comfortable, with good bedding. the bathrooms have excellent counter space, enough for three women to get ready at once! good closet space as well, and each room has a balcony. the pool area appeared to be very nice, however, it was too cold to explore fully. do not attempt to self-park! the self-parking signs take you to a garage that is not affiliated with the hotel and has no in and out privileges. service was good. we asked for the air conditioning to be turned on and for extra towels and received both requests immediately. also, they allowed us to check out at 4:00 pm on the day we were leaving, rather than 12:00, with no problem. i would definitely stay here again on my next la trip.

couldn't wait to get out i cancelled a best western to stay at this hotel and wish now i'd saved my money. i thought i'd treat myself but this hotel is a soulless place and does not match up to other westin hotels i've stayed in. i had avidly read other reviews on this site and had high expectations that this would be a good place to spend my first night in la in. big disappointment. the staff are very workmanlike but you don't feel they are really welcoming you as an individual. i don't expect to pay $25 for car valet parking and have them suggest i take my own bags up to my room. once there, i was deeply disappointed not to have a bath tub. as it was only a one night stay i couldn't be bothered to complain (as a starwood preferred customer) but i was also annoyed not to get a bath robe. it is very convenient for the century city mall but that's about it. staff in the breeze restaurant were great (never easy for a woman on her own to eat somewhere) but i was relieved to check out at 7am.

great urban style celebrity hotle stayed at the westin century plaza in la 2x in april for various business meetings in la. loved it two times. i can't help but fall in love with the heavenly bed. recovered from back surgery about a month ago and was concerned about sleeping in hotel beds, (my bed is custom) and it was a great feel and so comfortable. slept like a baby.staff was terriffic, valets bell hops were very nice and helpful. liked the free evian from the valet. washed my windows too...unexpected...and appreciated.checked in , had to wait a little while but got a nice upgrade and comp breakfast. front desk people were exceptionally pleasant, especially the tall brunnett (couldn't remember name) . food at breeze was pleasantly surprising. big treat was the celebrity event i happened to watch from the lobby one evening on my way back. never saw so many stars in one place. that was really cool. this hotel has a great hollywood history, as i've learned. looking forward to bringing the family for summer weekend jaunts. great location too. central to just about everything in la. room were also pleasant and clean, although i was out a lot and didn't get to enjoy the room...except the heavenly bed.exactly what i would expect from a westin.

everything wonderful! we stayed at the century plaza in april for 3 nights. everything was wonderful! we arrived at the hotel at about 1:00 or 1:30. we were able to check in right away. we enjoyed all of their restaurants like breeze and their cafe overlooking the pool. we also used their business center. every staff member we encountered at the hotel was more than happy to help us with every question we had. the hotel was conveniently located and service was incredible. we will be back again. highly recommended hotel!

nice for a weekend the family went down for a mother's day getaway. nice property. the pools were nice for our son, 4 wading pools of various sizes, the hot tub and the full sized pool w/ steps going from end to end.my wife did a treatment in the spa next door, she said it was busy, but nice inside.the room was smallish, but the beds were nice, some of the wood on the closets looked worn, bathroom was nice and modern, but again small.only stayed one night, but saw there was a problem w/ the tv, called down to the front desk and it was promptly replaced, so we could watch the corny national treasure without 1/4 of the screen having a green cast to it.we took a room on the 18th on the backside, which seems to have better views of the city/sprawl and some of the mountains, but it will not get you away from construction which is happening both directly in front of the hotel and in the westfield mall in the back of the hotel.definetly go for the starwood preferred membership (and if you are aaa or aarp, go for starwood preferred plus). apply online, it's free (as noted in an earlier review - thanks!) with spg+ were able to do a 4pm checkout, got bumped to the 18th floor (preferred floor) and got 1/2 price on general spa access $6 instead of $12 (but no discount on the treatments :) we also did pirceline - $136 dd the trick, $126 failed. valet is $25, which seemed on the steep side, considering most people had to wait a little longer then what i consider normal for their cars.internet is $10 / day. however i got wireless reception from the westfield mall in our room on the backside / 18th floor facing the mall. they charge $3 / day, but i'm not sure what the b/w will be like, i'll leave that for a future reviewer to try out.easy walk to the mall (which is undergoing redevelopment, but still has many stores and the movie theater open).we had mother's day brunch at the breeze, $58. nice outdoor table and they let us really take our time. good service, good food.at night, i smoked my andrew estates wimpy kahlua cigar and watched the city lights from our 18th floor balcony, good times, good times.

bad news... i booked the westin century city for a birthday getaway, but i spent most of my time arguing with the front desk, valet, and room service. i waited over 20 minutes at the front desk to check in, and then i was not even given the accomodations i had reserved. the elevators were broken, none of the ammenties for preffered guests were in the room (robe, coffee, etc) and the operator was impossible to reach on the phone. i travel over 18 days a month, mostly staying at high end properties. i have never had so many things be wrong in one stay, compounded with the most disinterested personnel i have ever encountered. i realize now that many of the deficiencies are due to a long running union strike. this would explain why at around midnight every night, horns and megaphones are engaged outside in the street to draw attention to the strike. i'd say that is not necessary, it is very evident. to add insult, when i received my ax bill i was charged incorrectly and had to spend further time arguing with them. i'd make a wide detour around this disaster.

no complaints i worked in the twin towers across the street from the hotel for years. i've eaten there, had meetings there and had company parties there. recently, i had my first opportunity to stay there (3/4-5) when attending some back to back ucla events. the building of the hotel itself is not the newest. the curve of the building is a bit of a throw back to a different era, but only adds to the charm. ample upgrades have been made. westin beds are always comfortable and the bathrooms are far from lacking. the rooms are a bit cozy and i wouldn't recommend more than 2 people staying in one room. there is only one sink in the bathroom (big whoop). there is quite a bit of construction going on with the abc entertainment center across the street being transformed. it wasn't enough to wake me up, but it wasn't silent either. valet wasn't impressively prompt, but not obnoxiously long a wait, either. room service was decent - nothing spectacular. breakfast at breezes was a bit overpriced, but typical of hotel dining. for more variety and affordability, walk across the street to the century city plaza. food court is on the other side of the mall, but you will enjoy the walk through (my favorite mall). best of all, as a starwood preferred guest (sign up online with no charge) you can request a late check out at 4pm! relax, lay in bed and watch a movie!

very comfy! we stayed here for one night at the end of a disneyland trip to be closer to lax. the hotel is very attractive and the beds were super. our only problem was that the first room we were given had a barking dog in the next room.we were quickly switched to another room which was quiet, but not as large and nice as the first room. since it was only for one night, i did not complain. we had breakfast the next morning in the breeze dining room. the food and service were very good, but a bit pricey at $75 for 2 adults and 2 children. the location of the hotel is very nice for visiting the getty center and hollywood.

4 star amenities/ 3 star service my wife and i stayed at the westin century plaza from march 1-3. i actually used my starwood points for this trip, and got a nice room overlooking 2 giant office buildings that were under construction. to comment on the parking situation based on previous reviews, i had no problems with the self-parking lot. you do have to go right past the hotel and make a right onto st. regis ave to get to the garage, and walk across a pedestrian bridge from the garage back to the hotel. but i'd rather pay $20/day, than $25/day + tip for valet and be able to get my car whenever i want.we checked in and were given a room on the 17th floor right next to the elevators. the room was very clean and updated and was truly a 4-star quality room. the beds were very comfy and the shower is highly enjoyable.we arrived late in the evening and had already eaten dinner, but my wife wanted desert so we ordered room service. i was put on hold and had to wait for the next available room service agent which actually took close to 10 minutes, something i've never experienced before. i ordered a bowl of berries normally on the breakfast menu. 2 minutes later, my wife wanted me to add a glass of milk to the order. i called back and they told me that would be fine. however, when the order arrived, there was no milk. my wife decided to forget about it.we chose the hotel #1 because i could get it free with my starwood points and #2 because we were going to a taping of the price is right and also wanted to tour hollywood. the hotel is a is in a good location to all of these things as we got lost trying to find cbs television city at 5:30 am, but still managed to get there in time. the restaurant, breeze, is excellent. they are supposedly known for their sushi, which i had. it was very good, but i've had better. i live in san diego where i have my pick of about 50 sushi restaurants within a 10 mile radius, so i know sushi. the prices are typical la prices if not a little on the cheaper side if possible. my wife ordered filet mignon which came with a nice portion of mashed potatoes and spinach which cost $32.all in all, i found the hotel to be enjoyable and in a decent location if you are planning on visiting hollywood and/or beverly hills.

great place great hotel. i booked it having never seen it. was given a great room looking east toward the city and mountains. large, clean rooms that are well equipped. great, updated bathrooms. pool is connected to the separate spa and very cool. great service except the valet parkers take a little time to get your car. pretty conveniently located for west l.a. and highways. right next to fox studios and century mall. if you get the same rate i did, $169, you can't go wrong.

would stay again! stayed at this hotel on 1/14-1/16/05. definitely worth the price that we paid thru priceline ($125/nt). the hotel's lobby was beautiful and elegant. check in was quick and efficient. our room was spacious and very clean with a nice patio with a view of the pool. the heavenly bed was extremely comfortable. parking was a little high ($25 valet with no restrictions) but that's to be expected. no doubt that i will stay again on my next visit.

no internet access, something like a business centre?!!?? good hotel. breakfast restaurant???? only in-room dining every day??no computers anywhere for internet access !!!! you are lost without your own laptop.very clean hotel, nice bed. friendly staff at the reception...maria was wonderful.couldn`t try the pool due to the bad weather (storm). location good.price ok for the value.

take the good with the bad my wife and i stayed at the century city plaza and spa for a long weekend this past summer. having not read the warnings on this website about the parking situation, my initial experience with the hotel was poor (i followed the self-park signs, was charged $20, only to be then told about the only hotel-affilitiated parking option - valet, which was also a frustrating $25 per day, no refund for the self-park, so started off down $50 for the first day of just parking). be prepared for this to avoid the initial damper on your stay.the hotel lobby and meeting area was nicely appointed with a plush seating area, full-bar, and big screen televisions. the backdrop for the lobby was the pool area, which can be seen through a wall of windows opposite the entrance. (however, i would guess the self-conscious would not find the concept of sunbathing in front of a bar audience to be a positive characterisitic). the pools themselves were not impressive, but i did enjoy boucing between the pool cool water and the nearby sauanas.our standard room was just that - standard. nothing special but nothing as dirty as some other folks apparently experienced. the bed was the highlight of the room. the highly hyped heavenly bed was quite heavenly. my wife and i slept like babies from the very first night and that is an accomplishment in itself. we have never before been able to get comfortable in a hotel bed on the very first night. the balacony was nice touch, albeit barely large enough for accommodate 3 people.the hotel staff was not memorable as being overly friendly nor exceptionally indifferent. we did have a problem with the safe in the room as it was locked and there was no key. when we called to the report the problem, we were treated as if we were just too stupid to find the key. they sent someone to the room to find the key and when they did not find it themselves, they offered to give us a safe deposit box. no big deal.the immediate area is not so great, but bev hills is not far. it didn't take much to get to the major highways either.overall i would say that the hotel was fair to above average.

very nice hotel (beware of ongoing construction) i got my reservation through priceline and was very pleased with this hotel, especially for at $136 a night. at check-in, i casually mentioned that i was a starwood preferred guest member (which i am) and was promptly upgraded from the 11th floor to the 18th floor and received free use of the health club/spa facilities. although the construction did not wake me the first day i was there, it was still loud if i sat on the balcony or even opened the sliding glass door. i asked to be moved and the staff was very accomodating. the room was large and nicely furnished. the bathroom was also very nicely equiped. this is definitely a four-star hotel and worth the price (whether priceline or expedia). just ask for the western (back) side of the hotel and enjoy peaceful mornings and beautiful sunsets.

enjoyed the stay we stayed from nov. 12-18. rooms were small, but large enough for a rollaway (at no charge). the construction across the street started around 7:15am and ended promptly at 5pm, so it did not bother us. i had my wife and two children (ages 12 and 10), so we ate most meals across the street in the open-air mall. there are plenty of places to eat, and a well hidden grocery store. i never saw any signs or advertisements, but found an average grocery store located under the mall in the parking garage. the hotel was convenient to the blue bus stop (santa monica bus), and the metro buses (both within a block of the hotel). there is also a hertz rental car agency in the lobby. we rented a car and were pleased to find that it could be dropped with the parking attendant even after the agency was closed. we did notice that food trays and used linens often stayed in the hall all day, but everything else was clean. the pools are heated and plenty of towels were provided so swimming was good. we also called the desk twice (once for a toothbrush, and once for pillows), and found that we were served very fast. there was an $8 bar charge on our bill when we left, but the desk clerk removed it promptly when i explained we did not use the bar.i would stay here again.

a dull place for snobs this hotel is located in a dull enclave of buildings in century city, with nothing of interest in the vicinity. upon entering, i was startled at how many rich, arrogant snobs there were here and i knew that i would be disappointed. the hotel charges for everything, including the use of the gym ($14) and parking ($27 valet) and other services, where they rip you off. the food is expensive, the employees (except for the maids) are really stuck up. security has an attitude problem, as they harassed me for being in the hotel (i was wearing jeans!). the hotel itself is hideous, it looks like a thing from the bad 1970's and the rooms aren't very roomy. i found small problems that for an upscale hotel shouldn't have been evident, incl mold on the curtain/tiles, no ice bags/tonsils, bad tv remote, stains on the pillows and sheets. i won't be staying here again because i felt uncomfortable and the snobish attitude is a big factor, if you dress casual, you'll stand out and have the security think that you just walked in from the street. boring place, avoid at all costs.
great stay great room and the bed was amazing. room service really fast. i found staff friendly. also had a massage at the spa and it was amazing (80 min was $165).

westin pleases westin never lets me down. i am a travel professional and am very particular. this hotel is very nice and the location is fantastic for a los angeles visit. the room was smaller than other westin properties, but the balcony was nice. (construction across the street was noisy, but that is something they cannot control) service was a bit off, as our coffee/tea supplies were not replenished and when i called for tea bags and creamer, they brought coffee. the bathroom was nice, and i love the mirrors and tile. however, i was disappointed to find that the second showerhead was not working on the heavenly shower. of course the heavenly bed is just that - starwood has a lock on the beds - with westin and sheraton.overall, this is a very good hotel to choose for the area, but it is not my favorite westin - so far that distinction goes to the one in atlanta - peachtree.

nice deal we booked via price line and got a rate of 115 per night and it was well worth it. the rooms are not as large as some business hotels, but they make up for it with the balcony, excellent patented bed and great shower. they are clean, modern and upscale.the work out facilities are part of the spa ($12 per day) and are more than above average for a hotel. you also get access to the locker room with sauna, steam room, whirlpool, and rainfall showers. the location is good, a five minute drive to rodeo and 10 min at most to west hollywood.

only adequate i have stayed at the century plaza hotel twice recently, and my last stay was marginal. first, the good things. the hotel is pretty centrally located, so you can get downtown, to the west side, to the valley or the canyon communities easily. the staff is courteous and helpful. on the other hand, my standard room was only adequate for a short stay; the room was quite small by business or spa facilities standards. the most glaring problem for me was room service. the bill was highly padded with fees, delivery, and services charges and the food was inedible. i ordered calamari, ceasar salad, and apple pie. the calamari was just balls of batter, the dipping sauce was rancid, the salad dressing was an oily mess that was not even ceasar, and the apple pie was bitter. fortunately, after a discussion upon checkout the meal was removed from my bill. i won't be staying at the century plaza hotel again.

good hotel with some drawbacks stayed there for a week in august 2004. nicely decorated rooms, with ample space. the service in general (front desk, bell hop, valet parking) was very good and professional. the beds, linens and bath towels were very comfortable. had breakfast at the breeze (hotel restaurant) one morning. our experience was very good - both with the service and the quality of food. the hotel restaurant is expensive (no surprise). however, there is a starbucks across the street in the aig sun life building that is open on weekdays for a good and cheap breakfast that you can carry back to your hotel room. there is also a large shopping center right next door to starbucks where you can get a variety of meals 7 days per week. both starbucks and the shopping center are a short and pleasant walk. every room has a terrace which provides a wonderful night time view of the surrounding area (from a high floor especially). we liked the location because it was quiter than other hotel locations in la, and found it central for our travels and activities - universal studios, hollywood, sony studios, pasedena and very near to beverly hills. but, remember, you're in la and that means driving everywhere, no matter where you stay for a family vacation. parking in all la is at a cost - so don't expect to get it for free (except at the sunset plaza strip shopping center, near mel's diner). the hotel valet parking is $25 per night, with unlimited in/out. we found it very convenient. the hotel has a charge for everything - including a $1 fee for making toll free phone calls and use of the internet at the business center (many smaller chains do not charge for local/toll free calls and often provide free high speed internet access from pc's in their business center). we did not have any billing errors. the drawback was that we thought the hotel could do a better job of cleaning; we never heard a vacuum during our entire stay, and felt the bathrooms simply recieved a wipe-down instead of a disinfectant cleaning, which is why we didn't give it a 5 star rating. an expensive place to stay, but we felt we received our money's worth (used the starwood best rate internet price guarantee to match a lower price we found on the web for this hotel).

loved it! wow! we were upgraded to a suite complete with a living room, dining table, large bedroom and 2 bathrooms. the furniture and decorations are dated but elegant. the grounds and pool are fabulous. westin hotels are awesome to kids. they deliver the high chair, crib and anything else you need at no cost. my toddler received complimentary cookies and milk before bed time, and they have a kid's menu for room service. we could not have asked for a better stay. the staff is very helpful and friendly.

good hotel, poor location stayed here as part of a honeymoon package in august 2004,hotel was very pleasant, nicely appointed and the heavenly beds were indeed heavenly.they were filming in the swimming pool area on our first day at the hotel, which mean't that we were restricted on our movements outside in the hotel grounds - disappointing.there is a shopping complex nearby (about 2/3 minutes walk) and we ate at a restaurant there which was good value and good food.did a city tour and found la lacks the charm and character of san diego and san francisco. this said, we did enjoy hollywood, beverly hills and bel-air, amazing houses and very detached from the rest of la.if you are stopping at this hotel, you need a car to get round and see the sites. we managed to walk to rodeo drive and saw the outskirts of beverly hills on foot, but the nearest metro station from this hotel is 30 minutes walk!still an enjoyable place and would stop here again.

perfect location my family consistently visits la each summer and has stayed at many 4+ star hotels in the la and santa monica area. the century plaza hotel was a pleasant surprise for our family, not éˆ¥?¸“uxuriouséˆ¥? but nicely decorated and maintained. the valet service was more than helpful and assisted us with directions around town. the room was spacious and nicely decorated with a great balcony overlooking the pool and garden. the landscaping and pool area is fabulous with great pool side menu! the hotel is located directly across from a westfield mall, grocery store and movie theater. the spa is top notch with a great array of services to pamper you. my only two complaints are that our heavenly bed with all white bedding was consistently stained. even when we asked for a bedding change, the éˆ¥?¸?ewéˆ¥?bedding was stained as well. yuck. my other complaint is that we had to pay $12 each time we used the fitness facility. when paying for such a grand hotel, the fitness should be included, not a surcharge. regardless of the bedding and fitness, i would absolutely stay at the century plaza again. we canéˆ¥??› wait for our next la visit to book the century plaza!

a nice time!! we stayed at the century plaza from jul23-jul28 and thought that it was a great hotel. we made the same mistake as everyone else and parked our car in self park - came back one hour and 10 minutes later to a 15.00 bill. when we got back to our hotel we valeted the car for the rest of our trip and the hotel re-imbersed our 15.00 from self park. when we needed the car they brought it up right away and we thought that their service was wonderful. our maid however was a different story. she never refilled our sugars and creams in the room so around day number 3 my husband ran our of both for his morning coffee. (not pleased) we also came back to the hotel one day at 2:00 and our room was still not made up. the concierge was very helpful and the front desk was very polite to us throughout our whole stay. overall a great stay we would go back.

great location, awful food the food at this hotel was expensive and bad...breakfast for three people was $60, not including the tip. i was attending a convention and the meals at the luncheons and dinners were awful. this was a great location though...it was near beverly hills and a mall across the street had an extensive food court and nice restaurants. heavenly bed and shower are wonderful. watch out for the in room, daily starbucks coffee though...the first item is free and the hotel charges you if you make the second packet.

thanks for the wonderful stay i stayed at the westin century plaza from the 28th june 04 till the 2nd july 04 to celebrate part of my honeymoon. i did not advise them but as soon as they got to know via the concierge they send me a champagne bottle up to the room for free. the concierge were really helpful and very kind whenever we needed directions or places to visit.the room was done up really nicely and room service was up at the room within 15mins of calling. keep up the good work. i will surely return.

disgusted i have never been more disapponted in a hotel than i am of the century plaza westin in los angeles. this is truly one of the worst hotels that i have ever stayed at in my life. upon checking in, the first room we were given had a huge bug squashed on the wall urine in the toilet. when we called down to the front desk to get a different room, we were treated very rudely, as if we were bothering them (including being put on hold 10 minutes). there was no sign of chagrin or even an apology at the unclean state of our room. furthermore, despite signs pointing to 'century plaza self parking' we were told there was only valet parking at the hotel, which upon returning home reviewing my credit card charges, they charged me $50 for (the correct charge for valet was $25). despite calling the hotel to discuss the invalid charge, i have yet to receive a call back. i will never stay at this hotel again it undermines my confidence in the westin chain, which was previously one of my favorite hotel chains.

worse than terrible i am disbelief at the lack of class this hotel had. here is a summary of my experience:followed self parking for the century plaza hotel signs and parked in the garage. when i checked in i was told that the hotel was not affiliated with the garage and i could only valet. when i went to move my car, the garage charged me $18 plus i had to pay $28 for valet - to top it off, my credit card is showing a $50 valet charge. total crooks and use every trick in the book to get more money out of you.dirty room - pee and feces in the toilet of the room i checked into. dirt everywhere, dead bugs smashed on the walls. not apologetic at all and put me on hold for 20 minutes when i called down to get a new room - acted like i was the inconvenience. do not believe the hype - this hotel is skanky and overpriced. i have never been so disappointed in a westin property.

terrific mid-century hotel with good spa my wife and i stayed here with a great rate we got on hotwire. when i paid with a starwood american express, we were upgraded to a beautiful room on the concierge level -- we even received starwood points for our stay, although stays booked through hotwire are not supposed to be eligible.the property is a classic mid-century cosmopolitan hotel. though it has been remodeled, it retains all of the distinctive 1960s design elements and charm of the original hotel. our room was on the small side, but well-appointed with nice furniture, a balcony with a great view, and the westin heavenly bed. the bathroom was the best remodel i've ever seen in a hotel of this age, with custom fixtures and great lighting.attached to the hotel is a complete spa, added fairly recently. my wife and i got a couples massage and used all the spa facilities -- on par with some of the beautiful resort spas in our home town of phoenix.the location is great, and the staff is friendly and helpful. be sure to use the valet to park your car, as it's actually less expensive than the self-park garage -- and the self-park garage is a good ten-minute walk and several sets of stairs away from the front desk and guest elevators.very nice hotel oozing with 1960s charm; good location, nice staff, comfortable rooms. i would definitely stay here again.

great hotel, wish i'd spend more time! after checking in i went down to the spa mystique for a couples massage with my spouse, and it was quite an experience. even though we got there late, and didn't have much time, the massage was really nice as was the relaxation area before and after the massage. i was sore the day after because i got the sleeping tiger deep tissue massage, and boy did it loosen my muscles. each room has a balcony which was really nice from the 11th floor, and the view was very nice as well. the bathroom was pretty large and very stylish. all in all, i loved this hotel, and would definately stay there again.

it was nice :) i stayed overnight at this hotel with a few of my cousins and friends. just a girls night out. the reason i chose this hotel is because i got a good deal on hotwire for it ($115). i think it was worth the price, but i wouldn't pay any more than that. i haven't been to too many 4 star hotels, but i thought it was kind of ridiculous to have to pay $18 for self parking. i mean, i didn't have any other option since there was no street parking. the pool area was very nice and quiet, although it did seem a bit different on the website. the room was also very clean and elegant. i probably wouldn't stay here again, though, just because there isn't too much to do within walking distance other than the shopping center across the street. there is also a lot of traffic around the area, which can be heard from the pool area. other than that, it was a nice stay.

very comfortable stayed at the century plaza for a quick overnight trip. nice, good sized room and bathroom, very quiet. the best part was the heavenly bed - which is what makes the room worth it. in at a close second was the best showerhead i have had at a hotel. everything was very well accommodated. parking was expensive - $18 for self park or $25 for valet - but expected. did not have time to try the restaurant, bar, or pool. would definitely stay there again, and at any westin hotel, just for that dreamy heavenly bed. hotel is in a good location and very close to ucla/westwood.

very nice we had a very nice time here. the lobby, pool, and room were all great. one negative: fitness center (which is really nice) costs $12/day, though they do waive that if you buy spa treatments that day.the only other negative is the location: there's a nice outdoor mall next door, but not much else within walking distance, as far as we could tell. but if you have a car then you're fine: it's a short drive to santa monica, rodeo drive, etc. try eating outside at mccormick schmick's at rodeo and wilshire!

a lovely place to stay the lobby is very nice and spacious. the pool is very nice and spacious. there are extensive spa facilities onsite, but the cost is extra. the restaurant food was good, but uninteresting. for the price, the menu could have been more extensive and creative. for an outstanding breakfast buffet, take a walk next door to the park hyatt. the century plazaéˆ¥??? rooms are comfortable and spacious. the concierge staff is prompt and friendly. the property as a whole is beautiful, and with the minor exception of the restaurant, the hotel really is great. itéˆ¥??? a solid choice for business travelers as well as for couples.
