15minutes everthing was quiet.we could not speak to anybody first thing the next day due to us leaving for a trip early and nobody available.to cut a long story short it took 2 hours of chasing when we returned to get an solution from the management about the next night because our child was to scared to stay in the room.we were told to our amazement that it was not the hotel's policy to throw these type of noisy people out or move them and it would have to be us that moved room's.the only positive thing about this incident is they put us in a suite but the only thing we wanted was common sense as we were not after a freebie.pleased be warned of our experience if you are due to take family's their and require a good nights sleep! this hotel is set up to be a adult playground which is a pity because as a hotel it is quite unique and different than more modern hotels.

lovely hotel stayed at hollywood roosevelt for 8 days lovley hotel great american service great views to manns chinese theatre, loads to do during the day but night time beware hookers, beggars about. had tours from here to santa monica ,venice beach, easy access to hollywood bowl hollywood sign disney land universal studios. hotel has spa in march we had the spa to ourselfs. didnt eat in hotel local cafes 2 mins from hotel cheap buffet breakfast. only downfall was when movie stars use part of hotel we were aksed nicely to use back entrance only once

great vacation!! i had read some sketchy reviews about the roosevelt but decided to check it out anyway. the location of the hotel is awesome and is very close to everything. we arrived at the hotel around 2pm and our room was ready for check in. the room was nicely renovated with 2 queen beds and 2 bathrooms. it was pretty big and very clean.the cleaning staff was amazing. everytime i returned to the room it was clean and the beds were made up. the pool area was beautiful and the bar had a large selection of mojitos and other drinks and snacks. the food was ok and a liitle pricey but hey, you're at a pool so what do you expect. the hotel had a few restaurants, the tropicana (pool) bar and teddys, which is independently owned. we had no problem getting in to teddys and also had a great time.the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. the concierge people, lauren and adam, def made our trip great. they got us dinner reservations to koi and boa, both great, and also got us into goa and villa lounge. granted, we spent over $3000 at villa, but it's still the toughest club to get into in la at this time. sunday and monday there were pool parties at the hotel which featured different dj's and a ton of hot people.loved the roosevelt, can't wait to go back.constantine, ny,ny
the place in l.a. to "see and be seen"... balcony/pool view from our 2nd room (#223)

worst hotel experience ever i was very optimistic to experience the roosevelt during a busy summer weekend. however, my experience was awful. the hotel's elevators were broken the entire weekend which resulted in a 20 minute waiting period to take my bags up to the room and several trip up and down the stairs to the 8th floor. the staff was also very unaccommodating. i got the feeling that they didn't care if we enjoyed our stay or were satisfied because they would have guests no matter what because of their name and didn't care if we ever returned, which we wouldn't anyways. they also would not allow more than 2 guests per a room at the pool, which only has 90 chairs for the 700 guests to boot. if you wanted a chair you had to get up a dawn and sit in your chair for the entire day or else you would lose it. if you expect to lay out or party at the pool, it is very difficult to do. the hotel also allows their guests aka, people who greased the pool bouncers and front desk people, to be at the pool making it even more crowded and much harder to get a $15 drink. don't stay here, you will be disappointed. this is not only my opinion, but many other people who were staying there at the same time also spoke this way and said they would never stay there again. being a guest also does not give you any priority at the door for teddy's or the tropicana bar. use your money elsewhere.

not worth the money the hotel is nice. rooms are small. my ac was not blowing air my first night. this was probably due do a dirty filter. the smoke alarm in front of the vent was covered in dirt.the shower pressure was so high i couldn't put my face under it-and i'm not exaggerating. it was the worst shower ever and that is not good early in the am. the stall was 1/2 door style so the water soaked the floor unavoidably. i had to shower with my side pressed against the shower wall. the sink was leaking water from the pipes. the bottom of the porcelain was mildewy because of this. the staff corrected the ac problem when advised but not the shower issue. the pool is beautiful but the servers are want to be actresses who are lazy, slow and less than friendly. they are not much to look at either. this hotel is way overpriced. i don't mind paying for a nice stay-i expense it anyway-this was just not worth it.

nice stay at the roosevelt after a terrible experience at the standard i was very pleased with my stay at the roosevelt. first of, i just want to say that the staff (especially after staying at the standard) is extremely nice and helpful. they really do go out of their way to make you stay pleasant.we got a garden view cabana room....and...were frightened when we walked in...to put in nicely, you want to commit suicide if you stay there too long...dont know who's brilliant idea was to paint a room black (!!!) but it doesnt add cheerfulness to say the least. after staying there for a few hours we headed to the front desk at around 2am and after speaking the with concierge (who smiled upon hearing the suicidal remark) were offered a second floor pool view cabana room for no extra charge. normally these rooms go for about $400 (we originally paid $240 on expedia)the beds are super-comfortable and the mini bar is great....i think a bottle of patron really changes ones mood...pool area is very nice and big....its really busy on the weekends and there are quite a few good looking la folks hanging aroundoverall, i would recommend this hotel...just stay away from the black room :)))

probably a good hotel for europeans who want the surreal hollywood experience first i will say that this hotel tries so hard to be cool and the 'it' place to stay but would be better suited to invest that money on a new elevator and carpeting. recently stayed here to find the elevator broken, the gym and fitness center shut down. so i thought, hey i'll go for a swim in the famed hockney pool. well that pool is only for supermodel wannabe types and there's a major scene there--so if that's the kind of hollywod experience you want then the hotel pool is for you. the rooms are small, and while there have been some nice touches like quality bedding, nice vibe, it just doesn't mask that this is essentially an ancient hotel.last, my pre-ordered room service didn't arrive and that really cheesed me off .....and i don't like having to pay for coffee when they provide a coffee maker...so, that's the negative, there are many positives to this place although i'm not sure if they'd be enough for me to stay again. the location is great, right across from mann's chinese theatre and on the walk of fame. the fresh toiletries are a really nice touch, the rooms are immaculate and the linens are good quality. free internet access in lobby is nice and the hamburger restaurant attached to the hotel is excellent.

do not charge room service!!!!! i stayed for two nights in october 2007 with a friend. i had stayed in la before and had drinks in the roosevelt and promised myself if i ever returned i would stay there really because of its location. hotel didnt fail to impress, rooms were spacious, well stocked mini bar( which caused me to cry upon checking out) and lovely bathroom products. back to the mini bar...... my friend and i emptied the mini bar on our first night, we knew we were paying a premium but what the heck we were on our holidays. the second night we noticed that the minibar hadn't been restocked during the day so i rang house keeping and asked them to refill it. housekeeping asked if there was anything in particular i required. i said vodka! certainly madam, would you prefer a large bottle yes please. checking out the next day noticed bill was twice what i was expecting. i queried it with reception and they explained there was a 515 dollar charge to the room. the litre of voda cost 400 dollars, 6 cans of coke and state tax bought the total to 515 dollars. if we had bought the equivalent in minatures from the mini bar the cost would have only been 170 dollars. i have never felt so done in my entire life. please dont let my tale of woe put you off staying at this hotel, but beware mini bars are the work of the devil!!!

loved the ambience we wanted to stay in a hotel that had some character this hotel oozes glamour and is very elegant. we were not disappointed with our choice. we did book a supieror room and on checking in found the reception and bell staff very friendly and helpful. we were upgraded to a poolside cabana room and we accepted even though we were fully aware of the reviews mentioning the noise problem from tropicana bar. we found the music was louder during the day then late at night, however we were at the tropicana bar until 12.30am anyway. i have read alot of the comments that the hotel is dark this is true however i found it to be in keeping with the hotels atmosphere and creates the elegant ambience expecially in the main lobby and bar areas. we had pre dinner drinks in teddys/library bar great atmosphere and dined in dakota for dinner the service and food was great. the hotel is very central to everything in hollywood and there was even a movie premier across the road. you will also find that most of the tour groups leave from the kodak theatre across the road. the only down side was that the concierge didn't book our airport shuttle after she said she would and we were lucky enough to get one at the last minute (1 hour before we had be picked up).

great hotel - not for families my brother and i stayed at the roosevelt from april 9 to 13, 2008. front desk staff was extremely helpful and polite, as was the concierge, both giving us great dining and partying suggestions, and helping get us in to the hottest places in hollywood.the room was average, nothing to brag about. we had room 510 (2 double beds). it is true that the bathrooms are a bit tight, and the furniture, although it looks modern (due to dark colors) is a bit old and chipped here and there, but i really can't complain that much. if you're staying at the roosevelt, it's not cause you're going to be in the room much!!!25 degrees and dakota are both excellent restaurants. i had one of the best steaks of my life at dakota (and i've eaten alot of steak all over the us and canada!!!). tropicana bar is the place to be in hollywood after dark, as well as happy hour! (don't even bother going to clubs, tropicana and the lobby bar is where the action is at!!)the hotel is great for the 21-35 crowd, but i don't see it being that great for families (it's kind of dark, literally not much lighting, everywhere) and lots socializing... overall, great place to stay, would stay again, but hollywood and l.a. in general is not what we expected. if you go to california, go to san diego, santa monica, pasadena, venice beach and disney land (all beautiful), and try to spend as little time in hollywood or l.a. as possible (beverly hills is the only thing to see there, and that's a half day situation, extensive shopping included!)

unique experience if you want a brand new hotel with all the amenities and clean lines of a new hotel, this place is not for you. however, if you want a unique experience at an old hollywood hotel, then book it. while some of the rooms are very small, and they don't come cheaply, the service that we received from the concierges (lauren and adam), bellhops, and parking attendants was outstanding. they exerted a fair amount of effort to ensure that our trip was pleasant and our needs were taken care of. the lobby of the roosevelt is one of the prettiest lobbies (again old) of any hotel i have stayed. i found the 25 degrees restaurant (open 24 hours) to be above average - although their menu was a little oddly set up. the room was not spectacular, but i believe that is what you get with an older hotel. the bed was relatively comfortable and bathroom was small (hard for the fatter than average american) and had a shower drain that drained very slowly. however, the location was amazing, convenient to many things (we drove to beverly hills in 15 minutes, west hollywood in 10, hollywood sign in 5, warner studios in 15-20, and out to santa monica in 30-35 - all in la traffic). i would recommend as long as you are okay with older hotels.

very very disappointing. besides the great location, there is nothing else going for the roosevelt hotel. we arrived in the morning to find very rude and unfriendly front desk staff. when i got to my room 503, it was small, smelly, and dark. i had nowhere to put my clothes, so kept them in my suitcase in the cupboard. the cupboard was so dark; i had to take the suitcase out every time to see what i was doing. the tv was on top of the fridge. the furniture was old and chipped.my son had room 502. it was much bigger, had a chest of drawers for clothes plus the fridge. it had a big flat screen tv and it did not smell. i rang the front desk to ask why both rooms are the same rate, yet one is far inferior to the other? i was told, the cost of a queen bed is the same no matter the surroundings.the bathroom s are extremely inconvenient. the tiny scratched shelf above the toilet, and the vertical storage that looks like an old cd unit, were not adequate at all. i had no where to put my toiletries, as that unit isnéˆ¥??› big enough to hold bottles upright. i had to close the toilet and use the lid when i wanted to apply my make up or dry my hair. i had to bend down under the basin to find the hair dryer.i was waiting for an envelope to be left for me at the hotel in the afternoon. i asked the desk many times from about 6pm to 9pm, if the envelope had arrived. i was told no. at about 10.30pm i found it underneath my door. please be advised that on enquiry the envelope had been delivered to the roosevelt at 5.30pm!!! it took 5 hours to go up 5 floors. at 1am on the same night, i was woken by room service who asked me what i wanted to order.i had not put in a call or an order to room service.lauren the concerge is very nice, and the food at 25deg. other than that, i will not ever give the roosevelt even a second thought.

not at all what i was expecting we were told that the roosevelt was the place to stay in hollywood. our check in time was 3p.m. and we arrived at 8p.m. we were told our room was not ready and could be put into a different room. the hotel is very dark, and the room was not as clean as we would have expected it to be. the airconditioning stayed on all night and would not turn off. the carpet was old and very stained. the following night we left our room and returned in the evening around 8p.m to find a do not disturb sign on our door. we entered to find housekeeping changing the beds kind of late i would have thought they did this in the morning. they had no cleaning supplies and a small black tote bag in which she emptied the garbage cans. the whole thing was unsettling. next we decided to unwind at the pool, we read the clearly visible sign that said the pool was open until 10p.m. this was 8:30 we were asked to leave by a large very unfriendly thugish looking man in a trench coat. he said there was no swimming after 8 and that the sign was a techinicality. the whole experience was bad, i wish we had stayed at the renassaince infact the days inn would have been better. upon check out we were asked how are stay was, we said horrible and they said oh. do yourself a favor and dont ruin your trip here

bring your own beer? not here!!!!!! overpriced, overrated rooms that resemble more of a glorified best western than a historical top-rated hotel. worst of all, security confiscated our 12-pack of beer in elevator, citing hotel policy that prohibits guests from taking alcohol to their rooms!!! this after paying $300/night. although the front desk returned our beer in the morning and promised to refund our mini-bar charges, we had to call the hotel several times to actually get the credit posted. in addition, the credit manager promised to refund our $30 parking charge but later reneged on this and offered no other remuneration.

great location stayed for 6 nights in two different rooms . great location across the road from the kodak theatre. unique hotel with a very dark atmosphere, rooms were very modern recently remodelled. negatives were the parking is very expensive, $28 per night valet. after the first night i hunted around for cheaper parking in the area and found great overnight parking next to the renaissance hotel for only $10 per night in a very safe,huge parking garage,only a short walk up the road. i had similar problems as previous reviewers firstly the fan for the aircon wouldn't turn off , it was very noisy and i wouldn't have been able to sleep, had to call maintence to turn off via a circuit breaker.when checking into hotel please check room first as they vary, we had a room across the hall from the x35 room previously mentioned by a reviewer and i agree the elevator is very noisy it sounded like thunder every time it went up and down. we also had the problem of the front and side entrance being locked because of a function , which meant we had to walk around the back in the cold wind, they should have a security entrance that uses the room key. in my opinion i would have rather stayed at the renaissance hotel it still has the same great location .

outstanding experience at hollywood roosevelt hotel we stayed at the hotel for our anniversay on march 24, 2008.the front desk staff was extremely accomodating very pleasant.our room was beautiful, large and more than we expected.the view from our windows overlooked hollywood blvd and we didn't hear any noises from below. we chose to stay at the hotel so we could walk to other restaurants, the kodak theater ,mann's chinese theater and other attractions. we enjoyed the look and feel of a older, historic hotel, but with the amenities of a newer facility.it was a perfect evening and will return again soon. from huntington beach, ca

no more history at the roosevelt the new hollywood roosevelt now hides its historical legacy. this is a very different hotel than it was 5-10 years ago. its' location along hollywood boulevard is still unbeatable, but the hotel's atmosphere does not welcome tourists and history buffs anymore...

great location expensive but great location, nice swimmingpool, altough too bad they took the jaccuzi out. nice poolbar and lobby. very historial building. everything is pretty much remodeled a few years ago, now it's one of the hippest places too hang out.parking very expensive: 25 usd a day.

all gloss- less substance... we had travelled the length of california and were winding our trip in hotel roosevelt. based on all the hype we were probably more excited about tis place than anywhere else we had stayed. however, on arrival we were told the pool was closed (there was a film premiere party there that night) and we would have to use a nearby hotel (across the road) if we wanted a swim. call me old fashioned but at the rates we were paying i didn't fancy flip flopping my way across hollywood boulevard to get to someone else's pool!the room was small with an atrocious view of the roof where maintainance men had decided to crack open a crate of beers and have a bit of a chin wag. a loud chin wag that went on for a few hours...there's no denying that the lobby of the hotel is beautiful, the location excellent and that the staff were helpful (apart from the bouncer who tried to throw us out of the hotel when he thought we were trying to gatecrash the aforementioned premiere- despite our displaying a room key and obviously walking towards our room!). ultimately i think that this is one hotel that needs to offer a consistent service to live up to its own hype.

great location!!! we arrived in hollywood and were quite overwelmed by the fast pace of the place and were even more shocked by the valet parking at the roosevelt hotel - it was very expensive. we were a bit early for check in but there were no problems. the room itself was a bit small but had everything in it.the decor of the hotel was lovely and the lobby was out of this world. there were quite a few weddings taking place in it while we were there.the pool was a different story!! impossible to get a bed and at times was closed without any notice!! the one time that we did actually get to the pool (a sunday) it was terrible!! there seemed to be an influx of young, hip, toned and very loud people who had stayed in the hotel for the weekend. we felt totally out of place with our books while quietly sunbathing!! the norm appeared to be very much loudness, drinking and dancing by the pool!! one of these sunbathers was one of the contestants from americas next top model - not our cup of tea i'm afraid.overall the location is excellent. mann's chinese theatre and the kodak theatre are across the road and all the other main attractions such as universal studios and venice beach are all very close by. great hotel for celeb spotting - rushour 3 premiered across the road!the staff were also very friendly and it was nice to say we stayed in the roosevelt hotel but i don't think we would stay in it again.

closed pool at no notice. dodgy local cabs nice rooms, if a bit small and only showers we have cabanna pool rooms, but on second day at no notice (we negotiated the pool rooms on arrival) they simply closed the pool for renovation for a week. so in instead of pool rooms, we had building site rooms! compliants lead to an upgrade, but would i have booked an la hotel with no pool in first place? no. it was an expensive con.watch out for local taxi rank - utter rip off as they take the long route, and room service ridiculously expensive. gym nice, but no sauna or steam room. dont book cabanna rooms if you like an early night. stupid loud music played into the night some nights.le montrose better.

could use some sprucing up! the roosevelt hotel is a totally fine experience for someone who wants to be out and about and enjoy la. the price was reasonable enough, the rooms were fine, and there is a fun scene at the pool bar. as per other reviewers, the parking is expensive-- it is actually $28/day and we imagined we would just use public parking but all the parking nearby is closed overnight, so this is impossible. we looked at 5 rooms before we found one that was a reasonable size (and we were not in the cheapest room category) and then, picked one that smelled of smoke, because at least we could walk around it. the rooms were all quite worn-- chipped furniture, chipped bathtubs, but it did seem clean enough. all in all, i don't feel the need to complain about the hotel, but i wouldn't give it a rave either. it is a good place to stay if you are in la to have fun-- out and about during the day and on the town at night...

very good, couple of reservations this is a very good historic hotel that has been extremely well restored (check out the lobby). excellent location virtually opposite grauman's theatre. the room was an ok size, sufficient for the 4 nights i stayed there. staff very helpful and friendly - excellent concierge. nice pool and bar. main gripe was that you can hear every word of your neighbours next door. no soundproofing in evidence -- i am encountering this problem regularly when i stay in hotels worldwide these days.other than that treat yourself to a nice merger of old and new hollywood (also recommended an excellent steak at the hotels dakota restaurant and propably the best burger i've ever had at 25 degrees also on site).

romantic honeymoon after getting married in las vegas we stayed for seven nights in the roosevelt hotel we had a wonderful stay this is a fab hotel we would highly recomment it our only regret is we didnt bring a sauvonior from the mini bar home to the uk with us

great hotel! i stayed at this hotel for two nights while on business in hollywood, ca and i really enjoyed my stay. this is a great hotel (high 4 stars) and it is very different from most luxury hotels i've stayed at. the design is modern and chique and this fits in well with hollywood blvd. overall, i enjoyed the atmosphere, the cleanliness of the hotel, the quality of the accommodations, and the convenience to where i needed to be. also, it was nice meeting celebrities by the pool at night!here are some things i did not like:1. no heat. there was ac only. at night, temperatures in la dropped to 30 degrees and heat was needed.2. there is only a fitted sheet and a comforter on the bed. there is no sheets between the fitted sheet and the comforter. you use the comforter as your only blanket. while the front desk assured me they clean each comforter every night, i like a sheet and i found this unusual.3. the bathroom was dimly lit.4. the lobby is a historic and well decorated lobby. yet, it has the atmosphere of a night club. there is virtually no light except for candles and i thought this was a shame. it's an impressive lobby and i would have liked to enjoy this room.

interesting i'd booked a deluxe room as i was hoping this would be away from the noise. i was offered an upgrade to a suite for $50. great i thought until he told me it was $50 a night. i was there for 3 and we took the upgrade as we'd just stayed at the best hotel ever in vegas (thanks tripadvisor!). this is an old hotel that has had a facelift (or two, this being la and all!!) . the room was probably two rooms in a past life, but it was worth the extra money to have all that space. half of it may have been too small. we had a great view of the chinese theatre and hollywood sign. we were on the 9th floor.it was too cold and grey to use the pool, and we only saw it on our last day anyway. looks like a great place to spend time. the lobby bar is pricey, but it is classy and funky. we could hear it from our room at night, the bass throbbing through the building. thankfully earplugs and sleeping tablets helped hide that! as a first time tourist to la its hard to find somewhere central to stay in a town that has no heart. for a location though this wasn't bad as the boulovard wasn't too unsafe at night, given the crowds outside. loads of safe places in the hollywood and highlands complex next to the kodak theatre as well as the ones in the hotel - note 21 degrees burgers - order one mixed portion of onion rings and fries for two as it's plenty! this isn't a cookie cutter hotel, so expect it to have a bit of charm and character for it's age. it's a funky place to stay and if you are looking for the different, then come here. if you want a standard type of hotel, then go to a hitlon or marriot etc.

over-rated closet location, location, location!!those would be the only 3 reasons why you should consider the roosevelt. can't complain about the rate cos they tell you that before you hand over your credit card. however, they really should be more realistic in their room descriptions!i stayed in a traditional guest room for $299/night (and this was discounted). the room turned out to be dark, musty, and tiny with barely any artwork or furniture. just a lumpy, platform bed with old sheets, a desk with office chair, an older model tv, a mini fridge and a wall mirror. i've stayed at the sheraton for $199 with more luxurious amenities! my view?? i had a spectacular view of the roosevelt's rooftop and air conditioning units! lovely.i would love to go on about the bathroom but that would bring on a claustrophobic attack.

great hollywood location stayed here early november 07 and had a great time. would recommend to someone who hasn't been to la and wants to be close to the sites like hollywood blvd walk of fame, hollywood highland shopping mall (at your doorsteps) and universal studios hollywood bowl (15mins drive away). the good - great location - beautiful historic hotel - rooms overlooking the pool / tropicana bar are new and modern, comfy bed, adequate size bathroom shower. - great hotel dining options: dakota is worth the splurge and they serve great burgers at the 25 degrees diner. - free internet service in lobby - celebrities do frequent the hotel, we saw colin farrel having a few drinks at the tropicana bar one afternoon while we were there - tropicana does a great cheese platethe bad - rooms overlooking the pool are noisy - the tropicana bar is open till 2am - its a shame they didn't double glaze the windowsdining tipswe ate at some great places, and would recommend them: - dakota - the hotel restaurant and a famous steakhouse. very nice and good if you don't like steak also. - the bowery, on w sunst blvd (about 15 mins walk) - nice burgers - franko and musso's grill: this place has a lot of history and it was cool to visit

ok experience the hotel is located in a great area within driving and walking to distances to just about anything. just be warned...if you have a car you have to pay to park the car overnight for 23 bucks. the pool parties there are fun but hotel not very kid friendly. i would stay there again only not with my kid.

pretty cool place my friends and i came to stay at the roosevelt for halloween weekend. we had a blast at the party, the rooms are pretty big, my only complaint is how small the bathrooms are. everyone at the hotel is really nice, check in was a breeze, make sure you ask for ingrid . the y have an aewsome gift store thats kinda hard to find but it has great stuff, ask for tayler. overall, its a cool place to party with your friends, but the halls are really poorly lit and its really dark, so its not for older people.

cool, cool, cool - a great place to stay. as a traveling musician, i stayed at the roosevelt while playing a show in hollywood. my wife and i were issued a beautiful corner room overlooking the famed hollywood sign and the chinese theater out one window, and and the walk of fame, a great view of the city and other landmarks out the other window. the room was very modern, but homey, with a flat screen television, high speed internet, a very comfortable bed, and a great bathroom. lots of storage space was nice as well.as great as the accomodations were, the service is what really knocked me off my feet. everyone on staff, from the waiters and waitresses, the front desk personel, the cleaning staff, and even the valet staff were very courteous, friendly and - gasp - helpful! much different from what i expected in los angeles of all places.(if you're into it, we also saw a number of celebrities while staying at the roosevelt. not necessarily my thing, but still kinda cool.....) the restaurants in the hotel were top notch as well, especially 25 degrees, where i had one of the best gourment hamburgers i've ever tasted (at 4am in the morning, nonetheless). if you're in town to see the sights of hollywood, there's probably no better place to stay. the price might be a deterrent to some, but if you want to truly experience the area, this is worth every penny.

feel like a movie star this is a great place for someone who wants to relax during the day, be close to tons of tourist attractions, and party at night. i stayed here on a business trip and was so sad when business got in the way. great location, close to shopping, the chinese theatre, in and out burger, and everything la. the pool is defintely amazing! the waitress service is a little slow but just relaxing in the sun on the comfy lounge chairs makes up for it. great bar at the pool as well. the rooms were huge with tons of space. the bathrooms were a bit small but everything was extremely clean. the only issue we had with the hotel was that they lost our boxes for 12 hours. the staff decided to take a break and go watch the prince concert in the hotel and we were put behind our deadline by 12 hours. make sure if you are shipping they check everywhere! overall amazing experience and will defintely go back. something is always happening at night and you are mixed in with the hollywood a listers.

the place to be i have read many mixed reviews so i was a bit skeptical on staying here but i'm glad i did! the hotel is in great shape and i love the minimalistic approach on design! if you are looking for an american chain type hotel this is not it! also if you are on a budget this is not the place to stay. it is minimally lit but it adds to the ambience and feel. the staff was awesome, there were several celebs there at the time i was and i can honestly say i was treated with the same respect as they were. this demonstrated a truly proffesional staff to me! gm/cadillac had a vip comp ride promo going and the staff who ran that were awesome too (thanks guys!) it's a hip, happening place, the poolside bar was fun (except is closes too early!) it's like an oasis from the street scene. food was good and not any higher priced than what i am use to paying at home (bay area). you are close to theaters and the very touristy hollywood blvd. i would reccommend this hotel to my friends and look forward to staying there again! the rooms were very clean and i don't know what the people were saying when they stated the beds were aweful, mine was so comfy i got the best sleep i've had in a long time! i didn't have a camera so no pictures, but the website gives a very good depiction of what you will see when you get there.
loved the roosevelt! i highly reccomend this hotel. from the friendly staff to the comfortable beds- its a great hotel. everyone is very nice, not stuffy at all!!! stay here!

there's better in la the roosevelt is a good quality hotel with a lot of history. the location isn't the best with many homeless people lurching around outside. handy for the kodak theatre i guess though.the pool is lovely and the rooms are of a good size and are well equipped. the bar and retaurant are also very good, even if the lobby is extremly dark.it's not cheap though and for the money there are better located hotels of a smilar standard in la.

loved the roosevelt we recently stayed at the hollywood roosevelt hotel for a short girls weekend to l.a (my friends and i are 30). the hotel is in a perfect location to many great restaurants and night clubs. the entire hotel staff were very friendly and accomodating, particularly the bellmen and concierge service. the hotel itself is very nice including the pool area, the weather was a little cool for us so we did not spend much time by the pool, if it had been warmer i think the pool area would have been great. the only time we actually ate at one of the hotel restaurants was for lunch by the pool, the food was excellent. the hotel rooms were very spacious, we had 4 girls in one room and did not have any issues with it feeling too crowded compared to other places we have stayed.we also were a little concerned with some of the reviews we had read but had no issues getting whatever we needed as far as room service/housekeeping and overall just very friendly service. i would definately reccommend this hotel to anyone. i would also strongly recommend that guests use the concierge service. they are absolutely wonderful here (andrea and ben) and were very helpful to us with getting reservations, recommendations on where to go, answering our questions, etc. we had a great time at the roosevelt and will definately stay here again the next time we come to l.a.!

scarey neighborhood roosevelt hotel is nice with nice pool. very dark interior. on a scarey street with many homeless. many young people staying there. i'm only 43!?! not for kids. the pool and bar turns into a really cool atmosophere at night with fireplaces, etc. perfect to see jimmy kimmel show though.

not a 4 star this hotel is not a 4 star in my book. it may have been so when roosevelt was president, but not any longer. the service was good, but the room was a bit of a beater. for example, the paint/varnish on the wood trim was considerably chipped and worn. the rooms could use remodeling. the room was very small for american standards. there was little room to walk around or place luggage. the bath was quite small as well.

an 'ok' hotel i don't really have much good or bad to say about this hotel. the staff were friendly, the pool has nice. didn't really like the location but that depends on what your looking for !! the room was small but thats what you expect in a city hotel. i did like the old hollywood feel to the hotel.

week in california we spent 3 nights at the roosevelt and enjoyed our time overall. the check in process was very smooth and the staff treated us very well and made us feel very welcome. when we arrived to our room it was very warm. told the bell boy about it when he brought our luggage and house keeping was notified right away. seems all you need to fix anything at the roosevelt is a pair of pliers! maintance opened up several boxes in the room and hit the air conditioner several times with the pliers and we had a comfortable room! made us laugh very hard when they left. on our second day at the roosevelt they had some sort of function going on in the lobby so it was closed to guest. the lobby elevator button was even disconnected so you could not get to that floor at all. the only way into the hotel was in the back where the valet was, i think the hotel staff should have told guests that the main entrances would be locked all day. we would stay at the roosevelt again if we were ever in the area. bed was very comfortable.

loved the roosevelt what a great hotel.after reading some of the reviews on here i was a bit worried about going but as soon as we arrived we were treated really well.the valet guys were really friendlly and the front desk girls were like supermodels (the 3 we saw anyway).the rooms are a bit dark and small but as we didn`t spend much time in them it was not a problem.the pool area is lovelly with a very big pool and plenty of sunbeds if you get down before noon.the food they serve at the pool is fantastic especially the salads and burgers.there are lots of gorgeous people parading around especially at weekends.the service we received and saw other people receive was fantastic so cant understand the people who compalin.the pool turns into a club at night and as long as you get your hand stamped by reception before 9 then all hotel guests are allowed access.we saw mike tyson the night we went there and the atmosphere was great with many people stripping off into their swimwear and swimming in the pool.overall the hotel is great and would recommend but dont think it will be suitable for businessmen who want to get a good nights sleep or older couples as the hotel is a bit noisy and catered for people in their twenties.

birthday weekend i recently stayed at the hotel for my birthday weekend. i live in los angeles, but thought it would be nice to lay by the pool by day with friends and party by the pool by night. we had a great time. every one at the front desk was very nice. the concierge was helpful in booking us a last minute dinner reservation. and the pool staff did their job in taking care of us with drinks all day long. in fact a few of my friends came late to join and they found a place for everyone to sit together. looks like the staff really has a good time, which makes the guests want to have a good time. my only recommendation is try to book a room in the tower since there are very dark hallways and no ice machines on the cabana floors.

first class service at this beautiful hotel absolutely magnificent! there is no other way to describe my weekend stay at this glorious property. check out was such a sad occasion, as we did not want to leave.this property is beautiful. it is old hollywood glamor at its best. you half expect to see marilyn monroe walking past you in the halls. old world style and grace is also reflected in the service; as everyone from the bellman, the valets, the front desk and poolside bartenders treated us like royalty.the concierge was amazing, and arranged a fabulous dinner and night club experience for my friend and i in 1 phone call. this was not simply a hotel. the roosevelt is an experience. the only place to stay if you want to enjoy the best that la has to offer.

pleasant surprise my daughter and i took a quick one-night trip to la to see wicked. since we were only staying for one night, i used priceline which came up with the roosevelt hotel. after reading many reviews of this hotel, i must admit that i had low expectations. the review comments that most stood out were small dark rooms and rude staff. i must say that my experience was very different. we arrived at noon, before check-in, but were treated very politely at the front desk. they advised that only one room with two beds was available, it was 'nice' and on the 8th floor, but was handicapped accessible. we decided to take the room and it was lovely. it had views of the hollywood sign, the chinese theater and the magic castle. it was also quite large and bright. when we got to the room, we noticed that the shower had been used, a bathmat was on the floor and a towel was in the sink. i called housekeeping, they were very apologetic, and said it would be taken care of. we were not really bothered by this, and assume the room was cleaned while the previous guest was at the pool. (this happened to us once when we were at the pool and our room was cleaned early - we did tell the front desk upon checkout, but have no idea if they relayed the message to the housekeeping staff.) we left to do some shopping and have lunch, when we returned the room had been re-cleaned. the poolside bar/restaurant was really nice and since it was extremely hot, the staff was very obliging and moved an umbrella over to our table to provide shade. about the only negative comment is that there are no ice machines, and ice must be ordered from room service. after returning from the theater we really wanted ice water, so i called room service to ask how long it would take. i was assured that it would only be about 10 minutes, but after 45 minutes, we gave up and went to sleep. next time, i would just go to the 24 hr. restaurant and ask for a glass of ice. breakfast in the restaurant was also very good. other comments on this site have mentioned that the pool area and bar are sometimes closed for private parties, but since we had no intention of using the pool at night, or going to the bar (since my daughter is too young) it was not an issue. all in all, it was a very wonderful experience and i would recommend this hotel.

great hotel great hotel, incredible location, rooms and housekeeping service is excellent. but make sure you get to the pool early in the morning if you want a lounger, there seems to be some kind of hierarchy as most are reserved for somebody other than the normal hotel guest. also food and drinks are good once you can flag down the many servers that are about.

chic but really loud at night this is a very chic hotel (consistent with the thompson hotel properties in nyc). the rooms are elegantly understated with hardwood floors, platform bed, and miminalist design. i had a cabana room that overlooked the pool. during the day you will see many locals hanging around the pool or a production company shooting a commercial. celebrity sightings are common here.at night, this pool area is quite the party scene. if you have any plans to sleep at night, don't stay at this hotel. seriously. i am a heavy sleeper, but the noise was so loud, and it went on until at least 1 am, and this was on a wednesday night!! so, if you are here on a business trip and need to be awake for an early morning meeting or to get to the airport, stay somewhere else.

yes - the best - do you have star quality ? yes - hollywood roosevelt hotel.ambiance of the hotel makes the guest feel like star, if you have passion to spend to enjoy the star status, appreciate luxury, comfort ...this is the best hotel with excellent service in the area, country.valet service and staff is excellent with a beautiful lobby. staff, management, ownership appears to be caring for all conveniences of the guest, thank you everyone for the efforts.excellent high speed internet both wired and wireless all over the hotel. guest services, front desk staff is excellent to help with any needs. every staff member is well informed, just need to get in touch with someone, call the front desk or security to get connected to have the best experience and the stay to come back.convenience and all the services are highly appreciable.whenever in the area i stay here and is always better experience than the previous. i recommend highly to all my friends, associates and others who read here. i don't want to keep writing too much good as i'm not part of management or ownership but wanted to share positive about this heritage, we are proud of.color black, furniture, paintings, design, layout is the great symbol of great heritage. yes some people have negative but did they try to think, why ? and did they even try to contact someone from the hotel staff.you got to try it, give someone chance to help you and will know yes its the best. sure if you want to complain without talking to anyone what to say... post a bad review, does it matter for anyone who reads that...it all makes a difference, how to enjoy star status, luxury, comfort, beauty, elegance ...

great time in hollywood hotel: very nice. room was great. shower was huge! stayed in room 821 i want to say and would go back in a heartbeat. pool: place to be. very nice. spent all day here.shopping: walked over to melrose and found great shops. shopping off hollywood blvd too.nightlife: les deux right off las palmas, area in west hollywood. tons of other places too.dining: ate at blowfish (great food) and dolce (good as well) did room service in the hotel one night too.car: i wasn't traveling all through l.a. no car was needed. i wouldn't recommend it. plenty to do within the area.

good for the experience i was a bit nervous about staying here after reading some of the reviews on here, however our stay was great. i guess those with the loudest voices are complainers. the staff was very friendly and accommodating. free coffee was available by the pool from 8am - 10am, and it was wonderful sitting by the pool in the sun. the hotel is not outdated, it's a beautiful historic buidling...if you want a white box with windows, go stay at a chain hotel. it was a great hollywood experience and i would stay again.

a great one night stay. i was very concerned after booking this hotel through priceline that i had made a big mistake! small rooms, poor service and noise seemed to be the general feeling coming from many reviewers. i was considering walking away from the reservation but in the end decided to 'chance' it.i was so glad i did, check in staff where friendly and efficient and after discovering it was our first time staying at the roosevelt spent a good few minutes going through all the facilities that were on offer.after expecting a tiny room i was delighted with the corner room i was given on the 7th floor. it had two twin beds with very comfortable linens, very effective air conditioning and a great view towards downtown la. the bathroom was not huge, however, it was fine for 1 night, there was also plenty of storage space in the closets in the small corridor as you entered the room. the mini-bar was well stocked however, the prices were extremely expensive. it was good to see that it wasn't one of those mini-bars were the slightest movement of an item causes a charge to be made. this meant it was possible to store a few beers and other items in there with no problem. the historic lobby is dark as had been stated previously however, it was like a calm oasis after battling through the heat and crowds on hollywood boulevard. it was also a great place to enjoy a few drinks before retiring as the pool bar is closed on sunday evenings.i only had a brief opportunity to see the pool area on the sunday afternoon of my stay, however it definitely had a 'vibe' about the place and was certainly full of 'beautiful' people. all in all it was a great 'hollywood' experience for the end of my vacation and if people get the same treatment as i and my partner did i can whole-heartedly recommend this hotel.

people watching at its best fabulous location. if you arrive via union station the red line subway (yes subway in la) takes you to the intersection of highland hollywood for $1.25. this beats the $28 parking fee.rooms are remodeled include coffee pot, hair dryer and irons. beds showers are good. my pet peeve is the $3.50 the hotel charges you for coffee packets (to make coffee in the room). but, there is free coffee poolside from 8-10 a.m.. the pool is heated. when we were there all of the unoccupied lounges were reserved and the pool guy told us we needed to make pool reservations like you do dinner reservations at a restaurant. management de bunked this myth stating the lounges were available to guests on a first come first serve basis. the antic's of the pool crowd (average age is about 24) is well worth the effort of getting a seat. we set by valet from 11:30 - mid-night watching people come and go from the pool bar on a saturday night. this was highly a entertaining activity. i will stay here again. i don't know where you get a bigger entertainment bang for your buck.

historic hollywood meets luxurious fun even if you live in southern california, you shouldn't miss a chance to stay at the hollywood roosevelt hotel. the ambiance of the hotel makes the guest feel like a star - if only for the night. every detail in our renovated room was perfect - the modern but comfortable furniture, the marble-clad bath, the view of grauman's chinese theatre across the street. the room included great (and stylish) lighting for working at the desk or reading in bed. i loved the photos of movie stars lining the hallways and the sense of historic hollywood. if only the walls could talk! the interiors of the hotel public rooms are amazing. you can sit in the library bar and marvel at all the intricate details in the woodwork, textiles and tile. it's a marvelous mix of different styles that echo the historic past and current scene that is the hollywood. best of all, and in spite of it's celebrity power, it isn't fussy. check-in was professional yet friendly. you'll wait for your car at valet parking just like any popular spot but this doesn't diminish the fun of staying here. you are so distracted by the lux autos and the people driving them that it doesn't matter. highly recommended for a true taste of hollywood glamour!

good location for me my son lives in the hollywood hills so my choice in staying at this hotel was based on proximity to his home. the hotel lobby is beautfiul. valet service is excellent. there are two restaurants on site, one very casual and one upscale steak house. i did not use them. the library bar is nice for a nightcap. friendly, timely service. the poolside bar has limited offerings and was not adequately staffed on our evening visit resulting in delays in service. the rooms are well priced for la but compact. noise was not an issue. room service for coffee in the am was prompt.there is some kind of very hip club on the premises that many try to get into in order to see a celebrity. since i was visiting the biggest celebrity in my life, my son - i skipped that part.

good hotel for the most part we stayed at the hotel mostly because of the buzz and the history of the place and found it to be nice, friendly if not occasionaly loud and busy. the dark of the lobby that others mention we didn't mind because of the hustle bustle of hollywood blvd and the l.a. heat...it was actually calming. staff and front desk were attentive and friendly. room was fine but certainly not historical. pool area is beautiful but noisy and crazy on weekends...go mid week if you want to properly enjoy it. the location is the best so outside of a little noise and wait for your car, it is a good hotel for what it does. we would go back.

great hotel and great experience this is the place to stay in hollywood. i read some scathing reviews and was prepared to walk if all was not in order (actually had a back up reservation across the street). we booked a pool view cabana room. we got a very nice sized room with an awesome king bed with great sheets. the room was dark but not uncomfortably so. the view of the pool and immediate access to the pool was nice. i can't imagine being in the tower rooms since so much of this hotel revolves around the pool and the tropicana. when we arrived the valet was courteous, check in efficient and the bellman superb giving us some hints. this was my girlfriend's birthday and all was in order. oh yeah, we are not in our 20's, but late 40's, and we did not feel out of place at the pool. we made contact with a pool attendant greg immediately, and made arrangements for specific lounge chairs by hollywood's most popular pool. it helps if you are wiling to tip to get prime real estate by the pool, and want to sleep in. while the drinks and pool snacks are a little pricey hey it's a vacation relax and go with it. the pool becomes a nightclub at night with a line, but as a cabana guest you have access with no questions. it can be loud until about 1:20am, so be warned. well worth stopping here for a drink on the way to your room the library lobby bar is beautiful and serves up drinks in a more sedate atmosphere. while there you really should try dakota for a high end steak dining experience. excellent service and corkage for $20.00. also try the killer hamburger and breakfast bar open 24 hours it is called 25 degrees. the hotel walking distance to all the great places in hollywood. we did the magic castle and pantages (wicked). the only bummer is we did not have time for musso and frank grill. i am already thinking about booking another weekend here.

worst hotel experience i have ever had my friend and i decided to go down to la for a girls long weekend getaway. i had heard that the roosevelt was a fun hotel providing a true la experience, so we booked it. worst hotel choice i have ever made. the nicest people at the hotel are those who don't actually work for the hotel -- i.e., the security and valet parking staff who are contracted out. we had booked our room through a very reputable travel website. after schlepping my suitcase down the stairs to the reception area with travel confirmation in hand, the front desk staff told us that the travel website had sent them different room preferences (we wanted 2 double beds, they had 1 king own for us) than those printed on my confirmation directly from the travel website. they told us it was not their fault and that they may change rooms for us as a favor. the room itself was decent except, for a very poorly designed half glass door fo the shower (saturating the bathroom floor) and the very very bright light outside the building that shined right into our room all night. this light was intended to light up the hotel, i guess. very poor design and poor consideration for guests trying to sleep in those rooms. we didn't actually get moved until our last night. we also never received a bottle of wine or a call from the manager, as promised. the hotel staff and the concierge made us feel like we were lucky to even be allowed to stay at the hotel and that we were very low on the totum pole. i have never been so disrespected as hotel guest in my life. don't waste your money... you'll probably get better treatment at a 2-star hotel.

don't make the same mistake we did... where shall i begin... this hotel has the darkest, gloomiest hallways i've ever come across. we had to navigate our way through the maze of hallways to reach our sorry excuse of a room. upon opening the door, we could barely fit our suitcases and when we looked up we were disturbed to find what seemed to be a painting of two serial killer women on acid. we immediately had to use our limited towel supply to cover up this monstrosity. from there, my girlfriend decided to take a shower and was pleased to find half of a glass shower door that left our floor sopping wet. other than that, the bathroom resembled any typical shanty motel bathroom. back to the room itself, it was as small as a closet and this was a deluxe size room. the pool area itself was very nice and the highlight of the hotel. had we only spent $100 a nite, we wouldn't have been as upset as we were. however, if you think you're going to get value for your dollar, think again. please don't be fooled by the pictures because you'll be in for a rude awakening.

full service hotel or private club? i've given an above average rating despite a mixed experience. the hotel and pool area are beautiful however the hotel needs to decide who it is serving. on check in we were advised that the pool was unavailable to guests as a commercial was being filmed! the room itself was much larger than expected and we had a nice view of hollywood boulevard. free internet access was welcome. on day 2 we visited the pool about 4pm after a day out and were asked to move at around 5pm because a vip private party was taking place beside the pool. we expressed concern but did go inside as the sun was going down. that evening we took the elevator to the ground floor to go out for dinner only to be prevented from walking through the main lobby because of another private event (this time a prince concert).we complained to the duty manager about the way paying guests were being treated and she apologised and offered a complementary cocktailat the poolside bar. this meant we were escorted past the velvet ropeand for a short while joined the beautiful party people - sorry folksbut we sold out! seriously the hotel can't keep both guests and visiting vips happy and needs to decide who it is serving.

find somewhere else to stay i stayed at the roosevelt in january for business, because i wanted something historic. this was honestly the worst hotel experience i have ever had.once i actually got to the hotel (which is no small feat with all the traffic from the kodak), i realized that i had to go downstairs (dragging suitcase) into a dark reception area. they told me to come back in about a half an hour to check in because they had no clean rooms (at their normal check in time).i eventually checked in and found the room to be small and the entire hotel to be dark and unwelcoming. my shower also leaked all over the floor, due to poor design, as opposed to a need for maintenance.on the second night i was there (a tuesday, mind you), there was some sort of event going on. parking was a major issue. once i returned to the hotel, i realized the bass from whatever music was playing was so loud i could barely talk to the other people i was traveling with. my room was on the 4th floor and things in the room literally shook from the vibrations from the music. i think i finally fell asleep out of sheer exhaustion at around 2 am.i tried changing hotels for the final 2 nights of my stay, but couldn't find anything....

hip trendy hotel suprisingly child friendly we arrived at this hotel with our 8 year old late at night just as a party for richard branson was finishing and immediatly thought our 8 year old would not be welcome at a such a trendy hotel,we were so wrong. upon check in we were given an upgrade as the reception thought we would need a bigger room as we were traveling with a child.this hotel is fab great looking and trendy and the staff are so friendly and welcoming .the location is fantastic located on the walk of fame ( two stars down from samuel l jackson) and opposite the chinese theatre. it has a great pool with a david hockney painting at the bottom and the food and restaurants are very good and well priced just like the hotel. the rooms are big have cd players and flat screen tv and plenty of famouse people lounging by the pool. i cannot recomend this hotel enough to everyone families teenagers older couples and honeymooners a fantastic great priced trendy child friendly hotel deffinatly deserves 5 stars and will make your trip to la the formal restaurant is fab and they did there best to accomadate are child.
disappointing tiny room, only about a foot of space around the bed

good location, good hotel this was our first stop before our honeymoon in hawaii started. we stayed there three nights, just enough time to get used to west coast/us time. the hotel was great, the staff very helpful, the food and drinks delicious. but, it was very, very noisy. you could hear everything in the rooms around you and we had the feeling a jazz band was playing in our room on our last night. other than that, very entertaining stay.

in 2 nights i saw jermaine dupri, jewel and richard branson i stayed at the hotel for two nights on july 1st and 2nd after staying at the mondrian for one night. i got a great deal for the hotel and i was happy with the overall service i received. the bellman, and the front desk girls were very helpful and nice. they actually made a mistake on my bill but cleared it up right away and they apologized for their mistake. warning about the pool scene. every one is young, pretty and in shape, not really a family venue, as it can be intimidating. i myself am in good shape but was surprised at how everyone looked poolside. i had a blast and met some great people while hanging out with my fiance. the party on sunday at the pool during the day is very popular so get there by 10am or earlier otherwise you won't find a spot by the pool. they check to make sure you are a guest of the pool before you enter as well. the rooms are average size and a little on the dark side, but this is the ambience of the overall hotel. it is rumored to be haunted and i don't doubt that for a minute, its got that old hollywood feel to it. while there we saw producer jd at the sunday pool party and the following night richard branson threw a fundraiser we saw him and jewel at the hotel. over all a pretty good experience but as a young couple we enjoyed the mondrian a little more.

ikea knockoff heaven i was so excited to take my husband to this hotel selected by bid on priceline for father's day. i read the negative reviews , but kept hope that a four star hotel would be great , especially for one night.the room is sparcely decorated with ikea look low flat peeling painted dark mahogany (mostly just brown) furniture (including the king bed). the rooms are quite dreary the hallways very dark. the small tv is located on a small painted stand too far away from the bed for the size of the screen. the concrete bathroom floor is in need of much repair black stain removal. the shower door covers only half of the tub, making for a very wet floor when you get out of the shower. i wondered why such an old ( supposedly historic) hotel would remodel the rooms and hallways as it did. modern day bad ikea. the main lobby check in floor (they are seperate) give the impression of great elegant things to come. the main lobby is extremely dark. the 24 hour eatery , too, is dark. you are greeted by a glued on menu on a table that indicates that this is just a burger joint with no prices listed except for $1.50 for extra cheese.there is no self parking, so don't forget anything have to run back to your room. you will have to turn your keys over to the valet wait for your car to be returned after the few minutes it took for you to get what you wanted. you must pay for overnight parking too @$28.00. i apologized to my husband.

awful, awful, awful!! stayed for 3 nights - final stop on a great honeymoon, on the way back to the uk from fiji. chose the hotel because we were expecting a little bit of old-hollywood chic, and because of it's central location.room was tiny by american standards. particularly the bathroom which more closely resembled one from a japanese capsule hotel. room was decorated with a frankly disgusting large canvas photograph. walls were paper-thin (we could hear conversations in the room next door), bed and pillows weren't particularly comfortable (and my partner swears there was bed bugs due to the mysterious bites she kept waking up with), though the tv had a good selection of channels.the hotel istself is so dark and dingy. even with blazing sunshine outside, it's very gloomy in the lobby. it's also very noisy and busy; there always seemed to be something happening. the doors are also patrolled by angry doorman, who on more than one occasion prevented me entrance into my own hotel! it felt like tryng to get into a trendy nightclub at times.worst experience by far was on our last night (hoping to get a good night's sleep in preperation for an 11 hour flight!). having played host to a high-school prom, the hotel obviously allowed a load of the recent graduates to rent rooms. cue a night of screaming, banging, singing, running around corridors, etc. i've stayed in numerous hotels around the world, and never experienced noise like it. even my university halls were quieter. at 3am, i finally caved and rang the front-desk. the phone rang for 5 minutes before finally being picked up - we'll send someone right up sir - which of course they didn't. it got to 4am when i eventually went out into the corridor myself to try and reason with them. in fairness, they did start to quiten down, but it was a draining and restless night to say the least.ironically, despite the dark gloom of the main hotel, the rooms are suprisingly and dissapointingly bright at night. a combination of the cheap curtains, and the fact a spotlight shines directly at the windows... used to highlight a 50-foot high fashion advetrtisment emblazoned on the side of the building. that, in itself sums up the general cheap and tacky feel of this hotel.a hotel with a great legacy destroyed by pretentious owners. avoid like the plague.

do not stay here!!!!!! you can't even go to the hotel pool bar if you are guest. they kick you out of the swimming pool for private parties. they tell you all the bars are not associated with the hotel although they are listed as amenities on their website. the make reservations and don't hold them. terrible service!!!!!!! terrible door men!!!!!!! terrible excuses and absolutely no customer service!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

multiple personality disorder service we booked a room at the roosevelt for a girl's night out in hollywood. i have to say that the service resembled a person with multiple personality disorder. the valet check in were more than polite, they were both extremely nice. our towel boy and server during the day at the pool were outstanding. however! at 11 am there were no chairs available around the pool (the hotel allows locals to come use the pool without checking keys, i know because i am local and i have friends who do this). so we were relgated to a sectional couch at the back, a nice spot but unfortunately shady. at 4 pm we were informed our section was going to be cordoned off for vip and that we would have to move. this was after spending the afternoon and $300+ from the bar/restaurant. the staff was informed if they could find us seats around the pool sitting together we would move, but that aside we weren't leaving until 5. they left us alone for the most part after that.going back up to our hotel room to ready ourselves for dinner, one of my friends brought a beautiful bottle of champagne for us to drink while doing so. calling room service i was told they would not send us up flutes or even wine glasses, but we could call the pool and they might send us up some plastic flutes. (whatever). the pool sent up plastic beer cups. um, no! i sent the poor man back downstairs for either plastic flutes or glass glasses. the thoughts of my friend in terms of service versus labor cost, they had to endure 3 phone calls and 2 trips on the part of the server to finally send us up glass wine glasses. if they had done it the first time, it would have been far less hassle in terms of time and money. either way you slice it, it's ridiculous.i do have to say that the room and our view was gorgeous, they supplied is with fresh brand amenities (my personal favorite), the sheets and towels were all top quality (even though some of the towels had a ritz-calrton label) and we had a wonderful time. this hotel needs to offer in the way of service what it can offer in the way of fun. and it would be nothing more simple than common consideration and even just attending to the most simplistic of requests.

beware! aren't hotels supposed to make you feel welcomed? the reader's digest version: bad service, dark, obnoxious, pretentious. just head to the viceroy santa monica for a better take on hip luxury.the long, whiny version: i live in laurel canyon and booked the roosevelt for a girl's night out at teddy's and a hotel stay while my friend was visiting from seattle. i even called to make sure that teddy's would be open and that we, as hotel guests, would be able to get in to the famously hard-to-get-into club. after being downgraded to a dumpy dark room with a view of the airconditioners upon check-in (the $350 room we booked a month prior was no longer available because we were trying to check in after 3:00 pm -- it was 3:30), we found out teddy's wasn't even open that night, there was a really obnoxious, frat-style 20-something party going on at the pool (which required a neon green wristband) we could attend up until 6:00, but then even the front desk people could not tell us if we'd be able to get into our own hotel pool after 6:00 pm that night. none of this was ever communicated when i booked it. let's just say the roosevelt is all about making you feel excluded. we were there one hour and checked out and headed to the viceroy in santa monica. so happy we did. the viceroy was perfect! hip for people over 25. gorgeous, fresh, bright, fun decor and great service! great margies, too.
young and trendy vibe combined with historic ambience corridor outside 4th floor rooms

pretty much evrything that you read about this place is true i booked this place through quikbook and got a great deal. we arrivedat around 10 pm on a saturday night! i too was going to cancel my reservations after reading some of the negative comments. here are the facts; if you are a guest, you will always be able to have your car parked here whether or not the lot is closed for non-guests. the staff here is very friendly and accomodating, (with no attitude).since it was a warm satuturday evening, the pool party was in full swing. the pool area was busy but not rowdy. we had a cabana room with a king sized bed that was facing the street so it was quiet. youneed a key card to access the hallways of the hotel, so the room areas were very quiet, (even near the cabana). the rooms of the hotel are very dark. i needed a flashlight to see the thermostat! my room was decent sized but only had one small bench to sit on. i also did not like the fact that i needed to call room service if i wanted some ice because there are no ice machines for guests of this hotel.to be honest, this is not my kind of hotel, (i later stayed at the century city intercontinental) but i have no major complaints.if i got a good deal, i would stay here again.

hurry up and wait at the roosevelt the roosevelt is known for being a bit of a hollywood scene (or at least it was a year ago) which does not interest me, so i wouldn't have stayed there had it not been for a good deal through a business associate. but i was intrigued to see the property.first of all, arrival is a nightmare. the valets were so behind on a saturday afternoon that traffic was backed up all the way down the side street next to the hotel. after waiting for a minute i swung around and parked on hollywood boulevard. the line at reception was 20 people long, and took forever -- one gets the feeling the young women working the desk were not hired for their brilliant interpersonal skills.over to the elevator, and there's a crowd there as well. one of the two elevators is broken, and people are waiting up to a half hour for a lift. finally making it to the room, and yes, it's nice -- due to a problem with the reservation i've had to get a nicer room (long storyand not the hotel's fault), and it's quite the space -- two bathrooms, a sitting area, all very well designed, a step up from thecheese-modern standard. but then i open up the laptop to get some work done and the complimentary wifi is barely functional -- a website takes 5 or 10 minutes to load, if it loads at all. it was like that all weekend.i went to check out the fitness center, but even though it was mid-afternoon, it seemed closed, and very small. the party scene around the pool was amusing (if a little crowded for someone just interestedin a swim). every girl was a hollywood proto-starlet, every guy was a steroid-enhanced dude in a baseball cap. getting my car back, even though it was parked right there in the parking lot, was a nightmare -- a line for the valet window, then a giant crowd of angry people outside, and it took about 45 minutes. i learned quickly to avoid hollywood boulevard which was always snarled with traffic, and just walking to the hollywood and highland mall to buy a swimsuit was a challenge. again, the room itself was lovely, with a large bed and a great shower with nice soaps and stuff. rowdiness on lower floors (and especially around the pool) seemed like it would have been a nightmare for anyone wanting to sleep, but i didn't have a noise problem, other than the deafeningly loud fan that i couldn't figure out how to shut off until i called the front desk the next day (hint: it was the giant switch in the circuit breaker). so, if i was paying full price, i'd never, ever stay here again. while the infrastructure and design is nice, the service level is nonexistent, and every aspect of the hotel is geared towards a scene not a happy traveler.

big room, nice stop over have just stayed in this hotel on a stop over back from new zealand, we had interconnecting rooms which was important as we were travelling with our 3 children. our room was large with 2 double bedsand a unusually big bathroom, however my childrens bedroom was smaller with the same beds in it including an extra single bed and the bathroom was tiny? nice view of lower roof and air con units!the restaurant was very expensive but there are plenty of diners on sunset but the hotels diner was a little more reasonable and we ate breakfast there on one of our mornings. (bottomless coffee!)the staff were friendly but on a couple of calls from our room to the front desk they were unhelpful and put us through to other deptments?the pool was lovely and warm (outside) and pool bar service was good, very busy and hard to get a bed in the sun but my kids spent all the time in the water so not too much of a prob! (in the eves the pool has a more adult scene! (say no more)this hotel was very exclusive, probally a little too posh for me and my family as we felt a little out of place at times. (no fault of thehotel)good location as you only have to step out of door to sunset strip beware of characters outside cinema, they are good fun but want a tip if you photograph them!would stay again but only for stopover!

a great unique place my wife and stayed here may 14th-18, and loved just about everything about it. we pulled up in our rental car and saw there was a ferrari and a bently in front of us at the valet. ($28 a day though) we tried to checkin at 3 which is their checkin time, but they werent ready. they offerred us a smaller room, but we waited till 4:30 by the pool for our room. (i usually would have asked to see the manager for an upgrade, but i argue for a living, and didnt feel like getting started on my vacation). the front desk was nice, but maybe a lil snobbish, but that could just be hollywood. the valet, doormen, maids, and bellboys always said hello and had a smile on their face. we stayed on the 10th floor and had a pretty nice room. the bed was very comfortable, but the tv was about 10 years old, but we werent there to watch tv. i think on alot of the rooms, they converted 2 rooms into one large one because it was a somewhat strange layout, but it was a large room. the location is absolutely perfect for everythig in hollywood, restaurants, shops, tours, bars. its all right outside the frontdoor, or even inside the hotel. the pool was gorgeous. never had a problem getting a lounge. drinks were very expsnsive there, so we went to the store down the street and bought a 12 pack and brought that but we didnt see anyone else doing that because everyone else there seemed to have no budget. the dakota restaurant inside was very good, a lil pricey but we enjoyed the experience. the burger place was also a lil pricey, but it was the best darn burger i have had at a restaurant. teh hotel is a lil bit older, so we did hear quite of bit of hall noice in our room.

hotel staffs are bunch of posers it was the worst hotel experience we had. we traveled a lot and only stayed at great hotels. i thought for the amount of money they charged and the location, it can't go bad. so wrong! hotel staffs were rude, unhelpful, had no idea of what they were doing. concierge was too busy booking her own gigs and told us that she had no time to help us. front desk missed our wake up calls and could not find a package that was sent to us. cracks at the bathroom wall. loud noises from the hallway at 3 am in the morning. should i go on? pelnty of nice hotels in the area, never stay here!!

great hotel, but sleazy billing department... check your bill!! we loved the hotel and took full advantage of the wonderful ambiance- lunches for four and numerous rounds of drinks by the fab pool, room service, etc.... so we were expecting quite a large bill. we didn't expect being double billed for the lovely room and while rushing to the airport, we hadn't noticed until reviewing the bill in the car.numerous calls to the hotel to address the situation have resulted in no return phone calls.great hotel, but not at twice the room rate that we were expecting and quite horrible customer service in our attempts to rectify it. it put a huge damper on an otherwise wonderful stay- and we were planning to return often, as our son has moved to la. there are other hotels...we'll be finding them.
