fab hotel my husband and i stayed at the roosevelt in december 2005 for the first 3 days of our honeymoon. i can honestly say that i am quite shocked at some of the negative comments written about this hotel. we could not fault it in any way. we had a fab room which we were upgraded to, the reception staff were great, really friendly - once they knew we had just got married in las vegas they insisted on upgrading us! they were really friendly and helpful.the hotel itself was lovely, very trendy, and we really got the feeling that we chose the best hotel to stay in hollywood. there was a real buzz about the place.the only thing that was a little dissapointing was the fact that for two days of our stay the pool area was closed off, because there was some celebrity resident - but hey we were in la baby!!! it all added to the atmosphere of this wonderful hotel, right in the heart of hollywood! please stay here... fab!

great girls getaway i almost switched hotels after reading some of the reviews. i really wanted to stay somewhere that was part of the scene for a girls' weekend in l.a., but got nervous after reading the negative comments. once we got there, however, i was glad i stuck with my original choice. the hotel had great ambiance. i loved the cavernous effect with the dark hallways and low lighting. it made it feel like old hollywood, but with a modern twist. the crowd was a good mix of young privileged partyers and wealthy grown-ups and there were a few events going on that made us feel as though we were at the place to be. the staff was excellent; very friendly and accommodating. our room was quirky with the bathroom through the closet, but the beds were cozy and it was plenty of room for three of us. the rooms didn't have the level of luxury that you might find at hotels going for this rate in other cities like the omni in san diego, but in l.a., this is what you get for the money; clean, comfortable, hip and right smack in the middle of everything. i can't wait to go back and spend some time by the pool, which was great for people watching, (and for good food and drinks).

overall good hotel! we were scared when we read all the reviews of the roosevelt - this hotel is defintely a party hotel - but we liked it overall -we stayed in 2 cabana rooms - one facing the tropicana bar and the other facing the street - the tropicana bar is open daily until 2am and so if you do not like noise, do not stay in one of these! the cabana room facing the street was fine in terms of noise..staff was really friendly and helpful. the concierge booked us a great tour of the hollywood homes and also got us into spago's- which was amazing -overall - the hotel has a really nice atmosphere- very dark - but the lobby is all lit up with candles - its very nice - the cabana rooms were nice and the toiletries were amazing. the 25 degrees restaurant was actually very good - we didn't eat burgers but we had grilled cheese and other things and it was good.overall we were very hapy with the hotel - it was clean, people were friendly and we had a good time.

loved this place my wife and i spent 5 nights at the roosevelt in match 2007.we were worried because we had read some negative comments, but wondered what the hell the people were on about when we got there.check in went smoothly and the staff were very friendly and helpfull, from check in, to the concierge, to getting an iron delivered to our room.room was on 13th floor, was agreat size with a great bathroom and the most comfy bed we have ever slept in.had great view from our room looking over chinese theatre and the hollywood sign.everything is on your doorstep, from in and out burgers, yum, to a myriad great restaurants, and the best discount shoe shop in la just one block behind the hotel.would recommend staying here to anyone.

very good, but not a world beater i just spent five nights in a studio suite on the tenth floor of the roosevelt. it cost around $370 per night. i was there on business, so the first thing i wanted to do was go online, but the wi-fi in the room wasn't particularly dependable.so i settled into what was a fairly well-appointed room. two bathrooms, a very comfartable bed, lounge space with a sofa separated from the bed by a wooden screen.the room was quiet, but luckily the poolside bar was buzzy, if pricey. i've partied at the standard on the sunset strip before, but the roosevelt apparently now rivals it as one of the spots to head for in hollywood. paris and lindsay weren't about, but there was a decent atmosphere and a smattering of poseurs. because of that, don't stay in one of the surrounding cabana rooms if you want to get any sleep.room service was prompt, friendly and efficient, as were the front desk staff. taxis wait on the street so you don't have to and i can't comment on the restaurants as i didn't use them.

stayed here a while ago... was a little bit disapointed i haven't stayed here in a while, but i did a couple years ago and was sort of disappointed. the hotel itself has an incredible history (with the academy awards having been here for many years) and its fun to just drop by the hotel lobby and walk around or get a cocktail at the lobby bar and soak up the atmosphere. but when i stayed here one night, i was given a room out by the pool. the room was not very clean and the pool area was noisy (partiers walking out there late into the night). it is a beautiful hotel on the exterior, but i was underwhelmed by this bare bones hotel room. the sheets were itchy. don't know why. didn't sleep well. i expected a romantic, old fashioned hollywood inn that had that 30s-40s retro feel with very clean rooms. instead it was more of the kind of party room you would get in palm springs near the pool area of a small to midsize hotel during spring break. i'm sure the hotel probably has other rooms that are more what i was thinking of. but i was slightly disappointed anyway. the hotel restaurant has ugly decor that looks like something someone's grandmother picked out. not retro and not period style, like it should have. food was over-priced and mediocre. they need to develop the lobby bar area into a more user-friendly part of the hotel. it's too small. they should spritz up the outside of the hotel with fresh paint and some cool old-style awnings. class it up a bit. and retro-fy the rooms back to the old style.

love the roosevelt my mother and i stayed at the roosevelt march 3-6. we absolutely loved it! check-in went smoothly and we had no problem with the girls at check-in. they were helpful and friendly. we were suppossed to have a cabana room but there was some confusion with our reservation and our room was given away. we were accomodated with a room on the 12th floor overlooking graumans chinese theater with the hollywood sign in the background. i definately recommend it. we couldn't have asked for better. the room we had was big and we loved the decor. the old lobby is dark but i agree that it adds to the mystique and style of the hotel. we ate at 25 degrees a couple times and loved it. make sure to eat there. it is a bit pricey but worth the money for the best burger i have ever had. we were staying in the hotel during the premier for the movie 300, which was at graumans. it was exciting to watch the red carpet from our room. the post-premier party was at our hotel on the old lobby floor. they were setting up for most of the day and shut off access from the elevators to this floor. that was a bit of a pain but that's the roosevelt. staying at the roosevelt you just have to understand that a lot of events are held there.the pool area and tropicana bar are beautiful. i am sure the cabana rooms and great to stay in too.

loved it! will stay again! my husband and i stayed for nights and loved it. we got the cabana room balcony which overlooked the pool and tropicana bar. we booked directly and paid $259 + valet. unsure if it is a good deal but after staying in new york hotels, we were happy with the price. we found the room modern and tastefully decorated. it was large too. plasma tv was small but suffice. toiletries from fresh (paris) and cookies on the turndown service was a nice touch. the hotel lounge and lobby dark but adds to the seductive and sophisticted atmosphere. beautiful chesterfield chairs and lounges, and leather papasan chairs! we loved the decor even though other reviewers have found it depressing. the staff were really friendly and helpful in a waiter in the dining rooms in particular, was charming! we had a wonderful breakfast one morning. a bit pricey but you have to treat yourself sometimes! the servings are generous anyway. i recommend the pineapple roasted french toast!tropicana bar was dead and perhaps is so on weekdays. too bad the weather was not warm enough to have a swim as they have a fantastic pool. while we were there, csi miami was being filmed in the pool area. we snuck a peek and was tempted to run down and ask for autographs!could not ask for a better location! the chinese mann's theater is right accross the street and there is a shopping mall with several restaurants. the pharmacy around the corner (to the left and across the street) has some groceries. if you want a cheap meal, we went to across the street one morning to shelly's diner for breakfast, where they shot million dollar baby.

party here, but don't stay here! just got back from an overnight trip to la to see wicked at the pantages. luckily the play and theater were great, because the hotel was not.to sum it up --- the hollywood roosevelt is a 4 star location to hang out, drink at the bars, eat at the restaurants, and do some celebrity sighting, but it is a 2 star hotel when it comes to room quality.our room was tiny! the rooms i stayed at in hotels in europe were much larger.they need to bite the bullet, and half the number of rooms at the hotel, but knocking down walls and combining two rooms into one.they had to shave the bathroom door down to get it to swing past the toilet. there were no sheets on the bed. the carpet in the hallways was musty and wet. the decor in the room was depressing and strange. i don't really enjoy looking at a huge fisheye view of an androgenous 70's glam rocker staring at me when i'm supposed to be on a romantic night out.the dark look in the lobby, restaurant, etc.. works. it doesn't work in the room. this place needs a serious makeover.i got my room on priceline, but i still think i overpaid. i would not pay over $100 a night for this place.it is in a great location though. across the street from mann's chinese theater and the kodak theater and shopping centers. you can walk out the front door onto the hollywood walk of fame and other hollywood tourist attractions.

nice hotel! we stayed 2 nights feb 20-22. price awesome on priceline!the hotel staff were all very nice and soooo helpful. the girls at the front desk were very pleasant which was a nice change from other hotels. andrea, the concierge, was also great and she actually seemed to want to help and was always smiling. she recommended a restaurant bella's which was down the road from the roosevelt. it was italian and me being italian i was a little nervous b/c it was right on hollywood boulevard, i was thinking tourist trap. but it was really good and the prices were reasonable. so thanks andrea on that call.the lobby and the halls were very dark like other reviewers have stated but it wasn't bad, it just seemed swanky to me. the elevators sucked though, they took forever (but no big deal, we were on vacation). one night all the keys didn't work in the whole hotel but the staff were very helpful and apologetic so it wasn't that big a deal. they had a glitch in their electronic system.rooms were fine, no complaints other then sink leaking in bathroom. beds comfy and rooms were big enough for us. wi-fi fine from where we were in our room (408). not much to talk about, just a normal room, nothing over the top!no ghost stories here, even though i was freaked out before we went from reading other stories. i just was scared a little when i heard any noise. but my son (who we didn't tell that it was haunted) told me that in the middle of the night, on his way back from the bathroom he thought i was standing by the tv but then realized i wasn't standing there. that freaked me out just a bit so who knows!!!bars at the hotel were okay but very expensive---2 drinks $27.00 (and they were not big at all, a couple sips you're done)!!!! we tried to get into teddy's (where the celebs go) and the girl at the door was verrrrrryyyyyyyy mean and just looked at us like we weren't there. the guy said it was for guests and reservations only! we asked about reservations and he said they need to be made 2 weeks in advance which i'm sure is a lie. the fact is if you are not a celeb or millionaire you aren't getting in! tropicana bar was dead, not too many people there but i hear it becomes one of the hot spots during the summer. it was pretty nice there with the pool and some fire pits (i suggest bringing your own drinks in if you could, because atmosphere was cool and no one where you walk in so you can save yourself a buck making the drink in your hotel room first then just hanging out there).

great location! would definitely stay again! great location! would definitely stay again!my husband and i were very pleased with this hotel. the best part about it was definitely the location. itéˆ¥??? right on the hollywood walk of fame. as soon as you walk out the front door you see the stars on the sidewalk. itéˆ¥??? also steps away from the chinese theatre and the kodak theatre, where you can see a great view of the hollywood sign. thereéˆ¥??? a lot of good shopping and restaurants nearby too. if the main point of your trip is to see hollywood, you probably wouldnéˆ¥??› even need a car (and could avoid the steep price for valet). jimmy kimmel live is filmed right down the street and they give away free tickets when you walk by.the hotel itself is obviously very old, but has undergone several renovations. the rooms are decorated very modern with unique artwork. i guess because the hotel was built so long ago the layout was a little strange éˆ¥?you had to walk through the closet to get to the bathroom. the bathroom was very small but was sufficient. there was little furniture in the actual room éˆ¥?you either sat on the bed or on the one desk chair. there were two big windows which made the room look bright and cheery. one small annoyance was that our room faced hollywood high school and the band was practicing on our first night, but it wasnéˆ¥??› too bothersome. the only thing i would say needed improvement in the room was the bed linens or actually lack of linens. it might sound petty to some but there was no top sheet on the bed and the comforter had a couple stains.apparently there are several stories of ghosts at this hotel but luckily (or unluckily depending on your viewpoint) we didnéˆ¥??› run into any! the lobby is extremely dim with candles lit all around giving it a somewhat spooky feeling (especially if you read the ghost stories before you go!). i would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting hollywood who wants to be in the heart of it all! we booked our room on a name your own price website and got a great deal (i was shocked it was accepted!). iéˆ¥??“ not sure the rooms are worth the actual prices iéˆ¥???e seen on other websites ($200-$250) so i would check around for the best price before booking!

ikea meets simulated mahogany our stay was for january 19, 2007 for one night. i booked the hotel through priceline with a accepted bid of $75.00 + tax = $93.41 we arrive just before midnight and used the valet parking $38.00 as there is no self parking. check in was fast. yes, it is a old hotel and updated as their website states however, i found the room to be very depressing. ikea meets simulated mahogany......... and who knew there were so many shades of brown. if i had paid full price for this hotel i would have been more depressed. the hotel served itéˆ¥??? purpose. we had a late flight from boston to la and we needed a hotel in la for one night before continuing on to laguna.

awful celebrity flophouse i arrived at the roosevelt with great anticipation. i was staying there on business and was promised that it was the place to stay in hollywood. i guess if you're a 21-year-old celebrity wannabe, the numerous discomforts wouldn't deter you. in no particular order, here are my complaints:*hard-to-navigate entrance with numerous steps to the reception desk*completely inept posers at the reception desk*waited hours after the normal check-in time for our rooms*common areas so dark you think you're in a cave--even in daytime*run-down room with worn-out, unglued carpeting, sloppily dripped paint on the walls, cheap furnishings, and zero charm*scary back hallway in room (my coworker had this too, and he's a large, generally fearless guy) that made me feel as if i had to check all the hiding places every time i returned to the room*drunk person asleep in front of my door at 1 am

billy bargain we loved this hotel, booked on priceline name your price for only $70, it was everything and more. couldn't have got a better bargain.great location, just opposite mann's. near melrose for shopping.great atmosphere, history, dark lighting, marilyn's mirror, the lobby area's huge leather couches.staff were really helpful, have nothing bad to say at all!!!would recommend to anyone, as long as dark lighting doesn't bother you................
classy hotel, lots of history, prefer the pool-area rooms from three feet in the door (cabana)

cool place the roosevelt los angeles is not your typical american style chain hotel. dark and mysterious. my room on the third floor was a little depressing but i promptly upgraded to a room on the 11th floor with a nice city view. the staff was extremely friendly and attractive. there is a similar, less expensive hotel in downtown los angeles called the figueroa.

pleasantly suprised we stayed at the roosevelt from the 1st jan - 6th jan and were tempted to change our booking based on the number of bad reviews we read. however we are certainly glad we didn't! yes the hotel is dark but it is part of it's ambience, and its unique interior design set it apart from the numerous other hotels were it not for a name would be almost interchangable. from the begining we got a good feeling, the bell boy was friendly, chatty and very informative. our room was clean and reasonably spacious, and when we did have a plumbing issue in the bathroom the staff were polite, helpful and prompt. we had breakfast at dakota most mornings and again found the staff to be great and the food delicious. the location is superb and you are as central as possible most of the must see la. while i could see it would probably not be an ideal choice for people with a younger family, my husband and i both loved our stay there and would most definately stay there again if in la.

great hotel, poor staff checked in on the 30th for 3 nights. we really excited about celebrating the nye here as we had received information from the hotel the party would be massive. anyway, upon check in we had to change room as the twin room was tiny - small enough you could not swing a cat and there was mould in the bathroom. they showed us another room which again was very small and again complained. we later received an upgraded room which was an extra $75.00 a night, and considering the bigger room etc we did not mind paying this. we then thought as we had not booked direct with the hotel and had paid vast cheaper rates that are why they tried to fob us off with a small, dingy dark room. anyway, the staff was very relaxed and like most state on here are only there to help the real celebrities. however, the bar staff at the tropicana bar were lovely and this is where we spent most of our time. drinks are a little over priced, but you are in the middle of hollywood and the view from our room could not be better. as we opened the curtains what do we look at - nothing but the hollywood sign. i had also been advised that the tickets for the nye party were going to be $50.00 we nearly got charged $100 but got that down to $75.00 and since i have sent them the email confirming we would be charged $50.00 and since had the refund. check your bill throughly upon departure.due to the downs there were all the ups too and we did spot a celebrity or 2 here, but don't expect to get near to teddy's - a listers only and you would be lucky even to find the entrance. one last thing, it is true that there are the ghosts of the roosevelt hotel, try standing in the blossom room in the dark on your own - you will soon realise it is true!!!!!!!!!

pool party views are amazing we arrived on a sunday and our room wasnéˆ¥??› ready so we were told to go sit by the pool and have a drink éˆ¥?oh my god éˆ¥?each sunday there is a éˆ¥?¦©ool partyéˆ¥?which basically involves the best looking and richest teenagers / 20 somethings from la getting drunk and throwing each other in the pool éˆ¥?i tell you, some of the ladies looked outstanding in their bikinis éˆ¥?. anyway éˆ¥?i digress éˆ¥?br/>éˆ¥?the hotel was fabulous éˆ¥?very modern, great dèœ…cor, fantastic location .. our room overlooked the hollywood sign and the chinese theatre and we walked out directly on the hollywood walk of fame.la is so big you need to stay in a couple of hotels really éˆ¥? we ate in beverly hills most evenings, which is about a 20 min cab ride away éˆ¥?valet parking was great.pool was great.drinks were éˆ¥?¦—ityéˆ¥?prices, but still greatoverall ..pretty damn good.

embarassingly horrible experience. went to the hollywood roosevelt for new year's at the dakota restaurant. they advertized a spectacular prix fixed dinner on new year's eve and we were told that the price was $100.00 per person. when we arrived, we were warned by the parking valet that 1000 people were expected to show for the huge party and that the night might not be as expected since we were a couple in our fifties. we explained that we had to access our dinner reservations and gave up the car. the spectacular dinner was a tiny appetizer that could easily fit on one forkful. the waitress said it was foie gras but i am very familar with foie gras and the appetizer i ate was only pate'. my date had soup which was the only decent appetizer on the menu. for the main course, the menu said that one choice was a 2 1/2 half pound lobster out of the shell. again, the portion was only 2 or 3 forkfuls with no vegetable or potatoe or salad. my date's dinner was 2 tiny lamb chops undercooked with no sides. we were both very hungry when dinner was over and ate the desert which we normally pass on. we each ordered only one glass of wine during dinner and when the bill was presented, it was $550.00. we questioned the manager on such a gross discrepancy of what we expected and we were told that there must have been a miscommunication as dinner was $200.00 per person and an $85.00 gratuity was included in the total cost. i was so embarrassed for my date who was visibly upset but being the gentleman he is, paid the bill without contest. he did tell the manager that the dinner was certainly not worthy of 200.00 but she just shrugged her shoulders. we then went to the party at the pool. amazingly, the door man let us in but for the dozens of young people in line behind us who paid $100.00 just to get into the party (that offerred a fee for service bar), the dorrman told all of them that the party was filled to capacity and he couldn't allow any more bodies in there. people began to loudly protest, but the doorman just shrugged and said, sue me. the blatant disregard for custormer service, the grossly unacceptable dinner, and the exhorbitant fees connected with this evening should be a warning to anyone who is even considering dining, visiting, or staying at this hotel.

smitten by the roosevelt stayed at the roosevelt in a cabana room for five evenings in late november. generally, a very jolly experience -- our room had a patio which opened onto a lushly landscaped pool area which has (at least for a new yorker) a snazzy hollywood kind of atmosphere. the historic rooms on the main floor are architecturally striking -- and for us, at least, the dark lighting enhanced the hotel's overall

roosevelt, home of the stars and expensive bars we checked into the roosevelt on friday for a little rr. i was excited to be back at the roosevelt as we had stayed there before, and had a great time. i had requested one of the cabana rooms, which are the ones by the pool that allow access to the tropicana bar, one of the la hotspots. we were a little dissapointed to have missed the victoria secret party the night before, but still kept our spirits up with a couple of cocktails from the bar ($26 plus tips for two bloddy marys). our room was super deluxe with a great patio next to the pool, the corner spot was secluded enough that we didn't feel like we were in a fish bowl. rooms service and maid service were prompt and attentive, and for a change they really won't disturb you if you leave the do not disturb sign on your door, a variance from most hotels where maid staff take it to mean knock really softly. the action at the pool bar was less than we could have hoped (we heard that the summer months the place is packed) but it was nice for a couple of drinks before heading out. we ended up staying an extra day we were having so much fun...i would reccomend the roosevelt to anyone visiting la who wants to play movie star for the weekend, just be ready to pay movie star bills as well. the room was about 500 per night with taxes, and drinks were pricey as well.

are you kidding this hotel is so dark and dreary--they should be paying you to stay there. i am a travel agent and recently stayed here for one evening to see the lion king down the street. first, you arrive by the back door because the front door is normally blocked off because something or someone is across the street at the kodak (jay-z) on my trip. you had to walk down into a real dark reception area to get signed in. the employees are okay but not so smart--i was told that sunset blvd was blocked off for the hollywood christmas parade (five days later).the rooms are also dark. sink cracked, no top sheet, and in the honor bar they sell something called the shag bag-contains condoms and wipes--that pretty much sums up this hotel--

going downhill fast stayed here in 2005 and although the pool was closed for renovations, we had a nice room overlooking the theatre and felt the ambiance of hollywood and the price was ok. so we went back again in 2006. we love hollywood. or did.even paid for a cabana room with a garden view thinking it would be even nicer.much higher prices too. what a total disaster. the cabana room was like the black hole of calcutta. drab, dark and musty. and the so called garden had 3 plant pots and a lounger in a 10' x 10' area. the whole place had changed due to new owners. no charlie chaplin sitting at the entrance. the restaurant had changed also. the breakfast ho hum. the only thing we enjoyed was the hospitality of the kiwi girl.i feel sorry for anyone who goes to the roosevelt expecting to feel like a film star. if you want to stroll across the road to the theatre and highland on hollywood then where else can you stay so close. but if you want to enjoy everything about your trip stay somewhere else. we will.

refreshingly different. i loved this hotel!i stayed for business and found the trendy decor and large plush rooms a pleasure to come back to after a long day. this is not your cookie cutter hotel . it offers cosy duvet's on the bed and w style decor but rooms that are double the size.high service touches included gourmet cookies provided with turndown and each morning providing an east coast paper for this east coast resident (the new york times). i was reluctant to stay at the hotel given some negative reviews but had no choice as other hotels were booked out. i'm so glad i stayed and shall definitely return.

don't stay at the roosevelt!!!!!!!! the bell person, elmo, who was the best part of the stay because of his courtesy, assured me that the hotel had spent in excess of $30m on renovations. i could not understand where this money had been spent. i have stayed in better motel 6 rooms. i may have been spoiled after just spending several nights at the westgate in san diego before checking into this hotel. by the way, when in san diego, stay at the westgate--very classy with very courteous and attentive staff. back to the roosevelt--save your money and time. there are numerous other hotels within walking distance that appear to be much better. i was completely disappointed and disillusioned by my stay. stay away!!!! the roosevelt is a dump!!!!!

excellent all round we stayed here for 4 nights as a friend recommended it, we found a great deal on a website and paid for the basic room.on arrival we were upgraded to a cabana room, i can only describe it as fabulous.you are given a typed sheet of instructions to tell you the dress code for the tropicana bar and the admittance policy and the dates during your stay when certain areas of the hotel are closed eg lobby closed for mtv party, that sort of thing. also on returning at night we had to go past about 5 security people to get to our room but such security is commendable in this day and age.the staff are all very pleasant, the pool is beautiful, they serve complimentary coffee there in the mornings.the restaurant and burger bar look great but as we were in hollywood we wanted to eat out and about and particularly in the hamburger hamlet , only a few doors away, which if you sit in the window is the best location for people watching.toiletries in the hotel are by fresh, and the mini bar has great stuff. given the fact it was $28 for 2 glasses of wine in the tropicana bar we tended to use our minibar as a fridge rather than consume its contents. we were erroneously charged for something from the minibar and queried it at checkout but it was immediately removed, no problem at all.plasma tvs, comfortable beds, the location cannot be beaten.i can't see how it could be improved upon.

loved it and would stay again in a heartbeat! we were very hesitant to stay here given the plethora of bad reviews, but we were more than pleased with our stay.we found a booking code on travelzoo for 119 per night. while this got us the cheapest tower room, the check-in clerk upgraded us to a cabana pool room! the desk and concierge were all very nice and helpful to us.the room was huge and clean with a very comfortable bed and great bathroom. the clerk made it clear upon check-in that as a hotel guest we were permitted to bring up to three guests to the tropicana bar. the policy was clearly stated by them and upheld by the tropicana staff. we decided to go have a drink at the bar and we found all of the staff very nice and courteous. we really don't understand all of the bad reviews about the rude service.we also ate at the in-house dakota restaurant and absolutely loved it! we each had a kobe steak and it was one of the tastiest steaks we've ever had in our lives (and we've had kobe steak in kobe). the restaurant staff were also friendly.yes, the lobby of the hotel is dark - but it's massive and moorish architecture. it's true to its past. it is what it is and we felt it would have been a shame to turn the lights up and ruin the atmosphere and architecture.the hotel has two laptops with free internet connections in the check-in area which we thought was a great nice touch.the hotel is also only about a block from the hollywood/highland center and the metro stop there. for all of those who say don't take the metro we disagree! we thought it was great! we took the flyaway bus from lax to union station and the metro the rest of the way to the hotel. it only cost us $4.50! two weeks later we stayed at the hotel mosaic in beverly hills which uniformly receives good reviews on tripadvisor. we agree that it is a great hotel, but we liked the hollywood roosevelt more! all in all we loved it. maybe the management has gotten the message, or maybe everyone who stays there hoping to see a celebrity and doesn't writes bad reviews. whatever the reason, we disagree with the bad reviews.

very trendy! nice hotel but definately aimed at the people with money and young (!). i liked the decor and staff were friendly and nice, the manager incharge of the valet could maybe do with some 'people' skills but all other staff were nice.room was small but nice and very clean. be warned mini-bar charges for everything. location is excellent and the pool area is very very nice. got a bargain of a price so can't complain.
very pleased with the hotel, location, and the room. the hotel is quite pleasant. the rooms are clean and well appointed. will definitely stay there again.

friendly, helpful staff old hollywood, right there on hollywood blvd. my room was small and had a crappy view. but it was clean, decorated in a minimalist style with interesting bw photography and had a lovely bathroom with lots of shelf space. the staff was great. my first room didn't have ac and they moved me almost immediately so i could still make the dodger game at 7:05. the concierge was very helpful with tours, dinner reservations, setting up my pedicure. my experience in the spa was great, too. yes, there was a premiere party when i was there and it made access to the hotel difficult. but la isn't the easiest city to get around anyway. if i'm in la again, i'll try to get into this hotel again, too.

not impressed i agree 100% with the writer from ottowa canada i only wish i had read the review before booking this hotel. the swimming pool is used on sundays for a private party, hotel guests have to wear an armband and it's impossible to get a seat or a bed, the staff are more interested in the party guests than the hotel guests.had to wear earplugs because of the air conditioning noise, reported the excessive noise to 3 seperate members of staff, nothing happened.would not stay again

quite satisfied my husband and i just got back from a two night stay in a garden cabana room. i was a bit hesitant about our accomodations due to prior reviews, but i was pleasantly surprised. yes, the hotel is dark and the layout a bit confusing, but afterall this is a modern hotel. this sort of styling isn't for everyone. our room was clean and had a lovely balcony. housekeeping and room service answered our requests in no time at all. we had a lovely dinner at dakota's and easily gained entrance into the tropicana for after dinner drinks. the drinks are expensive, but it is fun nontheless to peak into the lives of those who want to make it. whatever that means. overall, we'd stay at the roosevelt again. the staff was quite friendly and attentive. plus the location can't be beat if you are coming into the city for some exploration.

absolutely fantastic we stayed only one night here and it was fantastic.the rooms , bed linen , bathroom were spotless.the hotel staff were extremely helpful, chatty and polite.the receptionst helped us plan our trip to san diego and gave us good advice on the drive there.the hotel is centrally located in the centre of the hollywood and very kiddy friendly !

a disappointment was looking forward to staying here. when i checked in the room was very dirty. the bathroom had not been cleaned at all. the carpeting looked 10 years old and had not been vacumed. the drinks at the bar average 8 to 10 dollars plus. my two day stay was over a thousand dollar bill. the computer system for the hotel was down the entire stay. very poorly managed!! the downstairs restaurant and lounge are nice but other than that this hotel is not worth it. you can stay at much nicer hotels for alot less.

crazy experience they authorized my card next day for the restaurant bill of $372, even though we had split the tab by 4. i don't want to talk about the service nor the half baked bouncers at their club, as the only thing thats nice about them is the food and the chef.looks like the whole hotel staff including the restaurant manager needs to be send on training to europe at a michellin 1 star restaurant. it's hollywood blvd, waiters and servers are wannabe actors who don't have passion to serve, but are worried about their next audition.
last 2 reviews got it so right! beautiful lobby bathroom

not as bad as you would think stayed at the roosevelt for 4 nights. although there are good and not so good things about this hotel it was worth the 150.00 a night that i paid. i was satisified with my stay.the good: location. right in the middle of the action.never got refused admittance to the tropicana bar or pool. party going on sat. and sun. nights and we got in even though we stayed in the tower rooms. some b list celebs were there.staff was very nice and never made us feel unwelcome like other reviewers have said. beds were very comfortable. air conditioning worked well in our room. did not hear all the noise everyone else complained about either.our room also did have a tub.the bad: rooms are very small and dark. no room for luggage and we kept banging our legs on the bed frames as we tried to move around.the bathroom is tiny with no room to put your supplies. the shower only had half a door and the water kept soaking the floor. i would stay here again and recommend it to everyone else.

not recommended!! stayed at the roosevelt on business. it was really a grand dissapointment. the room was not clean and the bed noisy and uncomfortable. parking is a real problem since the hotel valets accept anyone. expect to wait an hour or two to park at your own hotel during the early to late evening!! the staff did not provide very good customer service. they charged me for a night i did not stay and never returned repeated calls to solve the problem. the quality of food in the restaurant was very low. there are so many better places to stay and eat in la. will never stay here again!!!

worst hotel in la! a group of us traveling for business were scheduled to stay at the roosevelt for over a week. to put it bluntly, the hotel was completely unacceptable to the entire group. filthy and disgusting rooms. we could not cancel our first night's stay and had to scramble to find another hotel. the overall consensus of the roosevelt was extremely negative. not one redeeming factor. a holiday inn is better then the horrid roosevelt. everyone was relieved to leave the roosevelt the next morning. do not believe the pr hype. this place is a disaster. the best place to stay in la is l'ermitage in beverly hills.
papa can you see me? screaming romantic cult women

place continues to go downhill stayed at the roosevelt a couple of times before the renovation and several times after. the renovation was badly needed and even though the rooms are on the small side and kind of spartan, it was a fun place to stay up until about a 18 months ago when the tropicana (pool bar) got to be the hip place to party. the pool and bar were beutifully renovated, but the majority of the time it's off limits to guests due to various parties and events unless you pay $500-700 for a cabana room. even then you have to go through the security gauntlet to just get to your room. many people at the pool as of late are non guests and many lounge chairs are now reserved. the service has gotten worse and the staff seems to care more about it being a nightclub rather than a hotel. front desk stafff is hit and miss. elevators take forever. parking and entrance is jammed on weekend nights. it's a wannabe w. better bet is the rennaisance for a hollywood stay; good service, nice rooms staff i recently discovered the westood area and now stay regularly at the w there instead. the hollywood w scheduled to open in 2008 will give the roosevelt a serious run for it's money....

horrible atmosphere-great location chose this for its location at the heart of hollywood and that was ideal for us with a short visit and a teenage son keen to do all the walk of fame, kodak theatre and el capitan cinema all on the doorstep. but for all the hype of oscars etc this hotel totally lacks any sense of style or glamour..the main reception area is fascinating in a gloomy gothic sort of way. a most unwelcoming hotel-gloomy airport style lobby in the basement-we had to ask the huge security guy how to find it. reception staff very nice but its not an easy hotel to navigate-not least because its so dark everywhere. confusing layout and anonymous characterless dark grey corridors, with scary unfriendly security men everywhere. a lot of the old character has been refurbished away in a dull grey brown minimalist kind of way. however the bed was gorgeous and the pillows and sheets lovely. the bathroom was horrid-poky and dark with a cracked washbasin and hairdryer handle broken. so over priced and disappointing.

an outstanding hotel the hotel was beautifully decorated. it had great restaurants that served great food at reasonable prices. it was in the heart of hollywood as the stars were right outside the door. the room were lovely and very inviting. the staff were very pleasant and helpful. the pool and the pool bar were also up to a high standard. there is not much more i can say but if you are going to los angeles this is the hotel to stay.

what a dump ! whoever came up with the phrase the customer is always right would be appalled by the service received at this hotel. the staff is rude and uncaring, and they seem to care more about the people who come to their pool bar then the people staying at the hotel itself. imagine advertising that they have a pool and then not being able to take your kids to it because of the mtv beach party that is going on........and that was on one of the few days that they actually allowed us to access the pool. nearly all of their staff who interact with guests need charm school classes, from the front desk staff, one of whom hung up on me when we called to complain that the elevator still hadn't come after 15 minutes of waiting, to the onsite managers who tell you to fill out their customer service survey as a way to voice your concerns. although the common spaces are very nice, catering more to their celebrity visitors then the actual hotel guests, the rooms are small and sparse (a waste paper basket would have been nice), and the air conditioning incredibly loud.......if you are lucky enough to get a room where it actually works which wasn't the case for some of my fellow travelers. we kept hearing we're still getting the kinks out but the problems they have are with their people and the utter lack of concern that they have for their normal paying guests.

do not stay here i am currently staying in the most expensive room at this hotel: a cabana room which is near the famed tropicana pool and costs $500 a night. what did this mean? this meant that it was an ordeal to get to my room every day, as different 'events' were being held every afternoon. i'm talking ny bungalow 8 level of bouncer action - they did everything but frisk me. they prevented my partner bringing her friend in to pick up a present from our room. they made me produce id and my key to walk down the corridor at 2 in the afternoon! remember - i'm only going from reception to my room. this would be understandable if tom cruise and katie holmes were poolside with paris hilton and simon cowell, but these 'events' seemed to be made up of a crowd of wannabes desperately hoping the next person to walk in was famous on any level whatsoever. the cabana rooms are small, pokey and dark, with laughable 'patios' and the level of service (apart from the sparkling car valets) is surly at best. did i mention the rolling hotel power test that meant i had to shower in the dark? a blackout they announced via a note delivered at 5am? and upon my complaint suggested i might like to shave by flashlight? we all know what to expect from hip hotels (poor service, dark rooms, happening bar action), but this place makes the hudson in ny look like the four seasons. and because of its proximity to hollywood's tourist ground zero it never really manages the full conversion to style hotel. i tried it because i had read good things in various style bibles in the uk, and all the good hotels in west hollywood were full. don't make this mistake!unless you're a really desperate hollywood wannabe, or you've got a fetish for being near mann's chinese and the select audience that brings.
had a great time! but everyone is not equal at the roosevelt... the pooside (11am on a weekday)

i quite enjoyed it... despite some shaky reviews here, i booked the hollywood roosevelt because i wanted something fun for a quick 1-night stay and didn't want to spend $400 on one of the 5-star hotels. it definitely served its purpose well. the location is excellent, though quite the mobbed tourist scene on a summer weekend (as expected). the lobby area might be dark, but it has been very attractively renovated and captures the older feel of the building with a contemporary twist. the service throughout was friendly enough, never rude or snobby, though not of four seasons caliber. my room was as expected --- small, rather dark, though clean and nicely renovated. the bathroom was absolutely tiny, which is often the case with hotels in older buildings, and water leaked from a gap between the glass partition at top of the tub and flooded the floor after a brief shower.i had plans all evening and wasn't around to spend time at the tropicana bar, pool ,or restaurants, though they all looked like a lot of fun. the roosevelt isn't the best hotel in l.a., but for the $179 i spent, i thought it represented a relatively good value compared to other options on the westside. i'd definitely go back.

only for the brave! i stayed here for 3 nights in july. i had the previou reviews, so i was prepared for snooty staff and a very basic room.upon arrival the doorman offered to take our cases and we told him it was ok, as we did not have that much and he offered again, and one of his fellow staff told him ' they do not want it' , well that started a shouting match between them, i kid not.very strange, i have never seen anything like it!the check in staff were very friendly, with another check-in counter who was not serving me even asking how i was.maybe cause i am young in my 20's i fit in with the clique!!the rooms are different from a normal hotel but they were perfectly fine. the beds are extra comfortable!!!the bathroom does have a unusual red light but there is a normal light you can use as well.it is true the lobby is very dark but all we did was walk through it to exit so i do not see the big deal!the pool area has been re-done and looks good. the day we checked out and were waiting to go to airport, they were dozens of young hip guys and girls exiting in their swimwear and receiving their cars from valet parking, so i presume that there are many people at the pool area not staying at the hotel. which to me is not right, for as a guest of the hotel you should be able to use the pool when you want and not have it domiated with non-guests.this hotel is definately catered for a younger crowd, as i am 25 i did not mind it. the location is great for hollywood.i would return to roosevelt but as for la, this is my 8th time there and i must say it seems to get dirtier every time. being from sydney which is very clean, it is a shock and something that i do not think you can get used to.

great location - needs a change in management i just returned from a 3 night stay at the hollywood roosevelt. i had read some of the previous reviews before booking - and some of what others said was accurate.the walls are very thin - bring earplugs. we could hear the couple in the next room, and it appeared they were having a normal conversation (i.e. no yelling or loud voices). one of the nights we stayed was a saturday night, other guests were extremely loud when returning to their rooms at 3:00 a.m. éˆ¥?it sounded like they were inside our room. i suspect this is the norm for older hotels éˆ¥?sound-proofing was not the science it is today. the room dèœ…cor is nothing special éˆ¥?dark paint, black white mural over the bed - very minimalist, not what you would expect from a place with such great history. the bed was very comfortable, although i thought housekeeping made a mistake when i noticed there was no top sheet éˆ¥?just a duvet. the air-conditioner was very noisy, we opted to shut it off and sleep with the windows open instead.the pool was a huge disappointment. i always stay in hotels with pools as i like to go for a swim after a long day of sightseeing éˆ¥?i was shocked to return at 4:00 p.m. and find the pool packed with non-paying guests! it appears the pool and the tropicana bar - which is adjacent to the pool, are the éˆ¥?·?néˆ¥?spots for the 20-something crowd of hollywood. many of the hotel staff let their friends in, and one morning i observed one of the pool guys placing reserved placards on 50% of the lounge chairs at 8:00 a.m. in the morning. i spoke to the front desk about this and was told that only hotel guests use the pool éˆ¥?this was a bold face lie, as i had over heard one of the pool staff talking to a group of 8 pool users about driving home and coming back later for drinks - most of the sunbathers at the pool had car keys with their belongings éˆ¥?not hotel cards.if you want to be seen and be in the centre of the action éˆ¥?this is the hotel for you, if you want comfort and luxury - go elsewhere.
loved the atmosphere stayed here on a recent trip to hollywood, the atmosphere was great and soooo hollywood...i like the old style hollywood glam.i felt like a movie queen...

never again what have they done to this hotel with so much history? i have stayed at this hotel twice before and have always had a nice comfortable time. when i had a short business trip recently, it was logical to stay at a place that i knew i could trust. big mistake, the moment i walked in, i could tell something drastically had changed. to start of everything was black, the walls, the floor and the staff dressed in black. felt like i was in a dracula film with all the gothic furniture. this darkness seems to be a growing trend with some hotels across the states. i could not find my card key in my bag the lobby was so poorly lit and people were almost walking into each other, i kid you not. my room was frightening. the room was black, the bathroom light was red and to top of it. a huge photo of a man with bright blonde hair in a black jumper was above my bed looking down at me. my friend had to cover it for me with a towel, so i couldnéˆ¥??› see it. they charge to for coffee and teas in youéˆ¥??™e room too, thatéˆ¥??? the first time for me! the only advantages are the great locations near by; if youéˆ¥??™e tourist itéˆ¥??? all at your doorstep. none of the staff were rude to me, thatéˆ¥??? a plus, but i will never stay here again. itéˆ¥??? a shame because i had a big group of us going next year, but itéˆ¥??? safe to say i will be taking our business somewhere else. it is a shame the hotel has been taken over, it has lost all its glamour and famous history.

dark, dark, dark the lobby and main areas of the hotel are unbelievably dark, i mean you can hardly see - i am not sure what ambience they are going for but it would be ok to have darkened sections without turing the entrance hall into such a dreary place.rooms are very modern and minimalist and quite boring - they are pretty small and don't give you a feeling of comfort. front desk staff were great, the location is good if you want to explore the hollywood area. overall not my type of hotel.

the roosevelt hotel is fabulous! my daughter and i stayed 3 nights in the roosevelt hotel. it was very clean. the beds were incredibly comfortable. we loved the 'look' and style of the hotel and everything about it. the staff was courteous and friendly. the food was incredible. it is right there on the walk of fame. i have nothing negative to say about this hotel.

run!!!! horrible experience from start to finish. the staff was rude, the pool was off limits to those of us who paid too much to stay there in the first place and the banquet food was horrible. service was excruciatingly slow so the food was cold and plates were cleaned away before our members were even finished eating.basically, we were in their way because we were nobody. it's a total shame that such a beautiful, historical hotel has been destroyed by greed and indifference to the customers. can i say something good? well, if i have to, it is in an excellent location and the view out of my window was graumann's and the hollywood sign. but that's where the glamour ends. unless you are somebody you'd better stay away from this one!

not my cup of tea as other posters have stated, the hotel is very dark. our room was a dark brown and with hardly any decorations in the room it seemed depressing. upon arriving, we were told our room wasn't ready and to check back in an hour. we left our luggage with the bell hop and returned an hour later only to be put off again. we waited over 2 hours for our room. while we were standing in the lobby, we overheard another gentlemen tell the desk clerk that he had just checked in, got his key card, and when he went to his room, there were other guests still in it!!! i do not know how his situation turned out.the beds do not have top sheets, but the comforter was nice. there are hardly any plugs, which means tieing up the bathroom while you do your hair. please be aware that if you use the coffee provided in the room, it is charged to you in addition to the regular room rate. the coffee is not included and is considered part of the bar. on one of the nights we stayed, the bet awards after-party was held at the hotel. while that was impressive, it made it impossible for us to leave without breaking through the tight security and standing out like a sore thumb. we tried to leave without walking through the middle of the black-tie event, but they had all the entrances and exits blocked. i even heard someone say, no, this is not going to happen, when she saw our family standing there trying to find a way out. her reference was to the fact that other hotel guests like ourselves were not going to be tolerated walking around when all we wanted to do was leave our room and do some shopping.i would not stay here again.

would not stay at roosevelt again my husband and i frequently stay in hotels for weekend getaways and i must admit this is the first time i have stayed in a room where i just did not want to be in the room. generally i enjoy breakfast in bed, but at the roosevelt i could not wait to get out of the hotel in the morning.to be fair i think whether or not someone likes the roosevelt depends on what you are looking for in a hotel. so i will list the positives and the negatives.positives- 1. the front desk was very nice and we were upgraded to the cabana section of the hotel so we had access to the tropicana during our stay. i'm not sure what is so great about the tropicana, but if you are looking for $14 drinks then i guess this is a perk.2. we had dinner in the restaurant, the food and service were excellent. i ate the veal 2 ways and it was incredible. negaitves-1. the airconditioner did not work properly and our room stayed a consistent 79 even though we set the thermostat lower. we were told engineering was working on this, but during our 3 day stay nothing ever changed.2. the room is very, very, dark. the walls are painted chocolate brown and the lighting is very bad. the unscreened window opens to the street so we did not open the windows. there was not enough light in the room for me to comfortably read a book.3. you can easily hear you neighbors talking, listening to the radio, or watching tv.4. the bathroom more closely resembled a jail cell than a luxury bathroom. the room is concrete, the shower is concrete. there is no tub or any hint of luxury.5. the concierge was not very helpful and insisted that he must make us reservations at restaurants rather than given us some options and letting us make our own decisions.in summary, i would not stay at the roosevelt again. when getting away with my husband i look for a luxury room and amenitities. it appears this hotel is for people who want to be seen at the pool and the tropicana bar. the pool is nice, but it does not make up for the lack of quality in the rooms. i would so say the rooms are lower in quality than the rooms in any lower priced chain hotel.

glorified days inn after reading the reviews posted, i was somewhat skeptical about this hotel. after my stay, i should have listened to my gut instincts. i understand this is considered a botique hotel. painting a few walls black and using minimal lighting does not constitute botique to me. rather, the hotel was a glorified days inn. the attempts to be trendy were silly. a bottle of mms by the bed in a prescription bottle to mimic prescription pills was tacky. the room had no chair, only a bed in it. the ac was loud and didn't work well and the room in general was dirty. the pool was quite nice - if you are 23. overall, the hotel caters to a 20something crowd that does not need/want any comfort during their stay. i would not recommend this hotel.
hollywood roosevelt was perfect more photos

great but expensive this beautiful hotel as i understand it was the venue for the first academy awards. very stately, with beautifully appointed rooms. after a slight hiccup on checkin (they misplaced our reservation) we were appeased with a few drink vouchers redeemable at the tropicana bar. our meal in the restaurant was very expensive with very small portions, something we found very unusual for restaurants in the usa. the location was prime, metro across the road, one stop to universal studios. situated right on the hollywood walk of fame and chinese theatre across the road. the staff were very courteous and our concierge andrea was extremely helpful with tour bookings. our stay was very comfortable and enjoyable

hollywood hotel stayed here for 3 nights in may 2006. initial reception not very good. could not use air conditioner -very noisy. clean but small. good location. first hotel/motel i have stayed in that i had to pay for coffee in room-discovered this at check out at extortion prices. similarly discovered coffee not included in buffet breakfast. minor issues but irritating to say the least. valet parking.

great location, not so great hotel!! i stayed here for 3 nights, the location is fantastic, everything is on your doorstep, couldn't get better. however the hotel is very impersonal, dark (bring a torch for the dining area), the reception staff are distant, not unhelpful but not helpful either!!! the hotel is quiet and really just a place to sleep rather than to relax and people watch.the room was a good size and comfortable but on our last morning we found a cockroach in the bathroom and we were glad we were leaving. the reception sent a member of staff up immediately but were not apologetic, even when we checked out 20 minutes later there was no mention of it even though it was 4.30am when they knew we had rang them about it.i would not stay here again.

excellent stayed here for 3 nights in november. requested a room on a higher floor and after being offered a larger room on the 4th floor, we were eventually found a room on the 11th floor. view was away from the main sights of hollywood blvd but still very nice. room was of a decent size with 2 large beds, tv, cd player, minibar (reasonable prices), tea/coffee making facilities (which you get charged for), safe, plenty of storage space. bathroom was nice and clean. plenty of hot water. only minor complaint was the colours - very dark in the corridor and the lighting did not make it very bright. the room itself was brighter. excellent location on hollywood blvd, close to all the main attractions. could see pool from room and it looked very nice but never had time to investigate. would definately stay here again if we wanted to be close to holywood blvd.

good experience i had to be in los angeles for one night on business (up from san diego). i grew up in la and even went to hollywood high so an opportunity to stay in a great old holloywood landmark was one i could not pass up. i was not disapointed. the hotel has been upgraded nicely. a little too soon to be passed fad modernist for my tastes, but well executed. i was on the sixth floor with a great view of the chinese theatre and the hills. the bathroom was great, the second best hotel bathroom i have ever experienced. it had a huge walk in shower and a seperate tub/shower combo. more than i needed but it would be nice for a couple or family. the staff is big in attractiveness and short on skills. they were helpless when it came to questions about the (poor) internet service. no wifi in my room, which i find unacceptabe at this price point and class of property. also, the tv was particularly bad. it was a little noisy with party-ers on my floor, but i can't fault the hotel for that. this place attracts a wild crowd and i think that is some of the appeal. i would stay here again.

short on good and long on bad.... my husband and i went with another couple to the roosevelt recently. our suite was pretty nice - a large room with some design-junky furniture overlooking the hills. it had a white leather banquette and a spray-lamp and a lot of interesting art. it was quite a nice room. got room service once and it was actually very nice and prompt.but the fun kind of ended there; first of all, the other couple booked and paid for a junior suite on expedia. the roosevelt told them there were no more junior suites and because they went through expedia, they wouldn't be able to get the suite. they were relegated to a standard room - which was about 1/5th the size of our suite. beware - don't let the front-desk people at the roosevelt take advantage of you like that. i think there are several reviewers on this site that had similar experiences. if you pay $150 for what expedia advertises as a junior suite, you should get a junior suite. i've contacted expedia about this. the hotel should quit this consistent and suspect practice. moving on, the ceiling vents in all the rooms on our floor were under a well-lit catwalk under the roof. so maintenance could (and did) get to look into the room, and you could hear whatever was going on in every other room on the floor. when people partied until 4:a.m. then had a fight, my husband and i were privy to every last dramatic detail. when another family ordered room service 3 hours later, we knew what they ordered. the alternative was to turn on the a/c which sounded like a jet engine. the vents in the other couple's room were worse. bathroom was very small, out-dated. the main ventillation was into the bedroom (not good). the toiletries were great - but only *some* rooms got lotion and body-gel while others got shampoo and generic soap. the more i think about that, the angrier i get: just give us all the good stuff! how much could you be saving? the roosevelt's club is evidently the hottest club in the town. but as a guest, you can't go to the club. don't try it, don't think about it, just leave it alone. it's not going to happen unless you book a $400 cabana. i talked to a guy who had a suite and tried to get in the club. a bouncer took him aside and told him he'd let him in if he paid him $350. elevators: mind-boggling. took some people 45 minutes to go down 12 floors. i got acquainted with the fire-well by the 2nd day.ok so the interiors of this place look nice and our room had a lot of style to it. there just wasn't enough good stuff to make up for the snobbery and alienation. i can't remember a time i paid so much to stay at a place denied me full access to its ammenities. bottom line, this place cuts way too many corners because it thinks it can get away with it on unwitting tourists.if you want to get treated better, stay at the le montrose - same price but way more services and seamless luxury. or the renaissance, or the bel age. or the standard, or the w. they're all a similar price and they treat you like a..... guest!

uber trendy this is quite the uber trendy hotel...our second hotel in la and beat the socks off the other one. fantastic lobby for drinks...tori spelling was at the next table!!! drinks are quite expensive...$10 for a bottle of water!! but the room was very cool, although very noisy at night...it sounded like everyone around us was moving furniture. apart from that it was great, right on hollywood blv, across from mann's theatre so location was fab too.

very swanky loved the hotel roosevelt. we arrived early to our surprise our room was ready. the rooms looked like they had been renovated were very nice, with a view out onto the hollywod bvld. our stay in la was made so much more enjoyable due to the fact that the staff were really nice, went beyond there call of duty every single day. they booked resturants for us, gave directions, checked our luggage into storage ordered taxis transportation.the lobby bar is a good place to start of the evening with some refreshments. the pool area is very swanky, the food from the tropicanna bar was to our surprise was beautiful. didn't see any stars our whole time we were in la, but would def stay at this hotel again. the mini bar is quite expensive, as we found out, after comming back to the hotel kicking on till the wee hours of the morning. great location opposite kodak theater hollywood walk of fame. well done to all the staff of the hotel roosevelt!
a great rainy stay rainy view from 212

super!... i took my son on spring break for his great grades and this was our first stop. the hotel was beautiful and the service was wonderful. the front desk was extremely accomodating and even upgraded our room. great location in hollywood. also, the concierge was wonderful. would definitely stay again.

an average hotel my husband and i stayed at this hotel on the last leg of our honeymoon, when we checked in we were given a single room (we may have been on our honeymoon but a single bed really wasn't ideal!), when we complained we were told there were no more rooms... eventually they moved us to a revolting smoke filled room which smelt so awful. the following night we were moved again to a lovely room but this did spoil our trip to la. other than that the hotel is lovely and the pool side bar is a very cool place to hang out.

bring your binoculars my partner and i desperately wanted to stay in this location, but couldn't quite afford the pricetag. i did my research and got a reasonable deal on expedia. ($159 p/n) for a single superior room with double bed. the room was tiny and very basic, however, it did overlook the valet parking and nightclub entrance to the pool area. take your binoculars and you too might spy paris hilton and friends!

great hotel - beware pool drink prices it was a great hotel for young travellers (i stayed with two friends, all around 25 years old). good location, fun people. our room was cute, adequately sized and overlooked the walk of fame. we were a bit nervous driving to our hotel, as we passed some questionable neighborhoods and a friend had warned us that the hollywood area was ghetto. but we were pleasantly surprised to find the strip of hollywood occuped by the roosevelt very nice. the pool is nice, nothing extremely special but cute. but drink prices were a bit insane. we paid $75 for a small pitcher of vodka lemonad that was way too sweet to even drink. we each had one sip and left the rest. overall, a great experience. i would definitely go back, but avoid the drinks at the pool.

loved the roosevelt very nice staff and excellent room. wonderful handicapped accessible bathroom, very clean and stylish. only flaw was no top sheet on beds, comforters only. beds a little low to the floor. great location and will definately will stay again!!!!!
needs more than a botox injection view from tropicana bar

oops! being a movie buff we picked this particular hotel due to its history and p.r. write-ups. we thought the back entrance a bit odd, but persevered. service personel were cordial and helpful. we were toured and shown the room where the academy awards had been presented. when we got to our room we were not surprised as we had looked at the rooms on the net. it had an upscale decor.as we settled down..to unpack i was shocked to realize that there wasn't a bureau. i called the desk and they were a bit flustered; bell boy sent up; flustered; a few phone calls..my last comment was did you expect me to hang up my lingerie in the closet?..when told i could use the closet. when it all settled we were slightly upgraded to a larger room with a bureau..and very accomodating. king bed, nice linens..but, as we settled in we began to notice the tired carpet, the chipped paint, the lack of continuity in the decor; the so-so view; the safe that had to be replaced with a new one; the bathroom that looked like it had been constructed from a used construction site...concrete floors that had streaks on them. there really was nothing that was excitable. the location was superior.we put on the happy face and began to explore.the first shock we got was that guests do not have access to teddy's..the new club. it is advertised and sounds like you can use it..but, the truth is ..it is a private club , with a key..for movie stars to enter and do whatever they please. the pool bar is also excluded on some nights. it almost appears that it is a private playground for the stars. the service elevator was broken and the workmen used the single guest elevator so that getting up and down was dicey.the lobby, front entrance is unappealingly dark. you need a flashlight to see...it hides the gorgeous decor and ceiling. now, thats the negatives..the dining room was splendid for breakfast. that was the only meal we had there. we would not stay there again.
above our expectations! the bar/pool. there's elizabeth shue!

close but no cigar if the accomodations were half as lofty as the attitudes, this would be a fine hotel. the main areas, though dark, are suitably dramatic and set a cool tone. the rooms did not meet expectations. my middle aged husband and i were upgraded to a poolside cabana by a breathlessly excited reservationista who assured us we could bring two friends to the club that night. unfortunately, it is not my idea of luxe to be interrogated by a twenty-something trendster armed with a velvet rope and a rubber stamp to get to my room. the room was clean and the linens were high caliber, but the bed itself was soft and lumpy. the rooms are high concept, mid-century inspired moderne but constructed strictly of cinder block, concrete and cold mirrored surfaces. on balance, it seemed like a stylish means of renovating an old motel without actually upgrading the infrastructure one iota. wear and tear is starting to take a toll too. the concrete flooring in the bathroom was noticeably cracked and broken. endless dark hallways with no elevator and no signage ensured that we roamed lost every time we wanted to leave. it was ok at $159 but would have been an outrage at the aleged standard prices of $500-$600/night.

neat experience! my husband and i stayed here for 2 nights this summer while on a long vacation in california. i was quite suprised by the other comments!! we had a really nice time here--it is definitely a different type of hotel! if you want to experience hollywood--you will get the full effects of it here! definitely go to the pool if you want to see celebs and other crazy hollywood types--we were lucky to actually spot a few!! our room was fine, we dined at the steakhouse there, now called dakota and were very pleased with the food and service. the front desk staff were pleasant with us as well. the only thing negative about the hotel was having to valet park your car and it is a whole process to get your car back out! i recommend just having them park it when you get there and leaving it and just walk places if you can!! i think this hotel might be better suited for younger crowds and couples. not much of a family hotel atmosphere, but overall, we were pleased.

fantastic time!!! my fiance and i drove to hollywood from san diego and decided to stay the night at the roosevelt hotel before our flight home the next day from la back to heathrow.we found a great offer on travelzoo and paid $99 for the kingsize room.when we arrived at the hotel we was greeted by the valet car parking guys who took care of our car and took our cases out of the boot and into the reception area, the car parking charge for the night was $23. we then proceeded to the reception desk and was greeted by a lovely lady who was extremely polite and friendly, she told us that we had been upgraded which we couldnt believe and we had a poolside room all for $99. we was shown to our room by another member of staff who showed us where everything was and if we needed anything who to call etc, and also informed us about the poolside party which would be held later that evening and we could invite 2 friends along who were not staying at the hotel if we wished.the room was fabulous, the decor was second to none, the bed was so comfortable and the bathroom was sparkling clean along with the rest of the room, there was a cd player, and flat screen tv, bath robes, hairdryer, phone, mini bar.the prices of the mini bar were quite pricey so we didnt have anything from there and we ate out rather than in the restaurant as we wanted to see some of hollywood. we had breakfast the next morning in the hotel restaurant which was fantastic the service was excellent and altho a bit pricey $60 with tip for breakfast it was well worth it.the only thing i would complain about is the lighting in the room it was a bit dark altho that it was in line with the decor but the lighting could have been a bit better.the pool was fantastic, and we would definately go back again and wish we had stayed there for a few more days - i would definately reccomend

wonderful service, beautiful hotel i was kind of freaked out by the complaints on this site, especially since i paid a lot more than i usually do for a hotel since i knew i'd be using the hotel to do a little work and would be spending more time in the hotel than i usually do on vacation. however, within moments of arriving at the roosevelt, all my fears were wiped away. the staff was friendly and courteous, the room was lovely and clean. i had a fantastic sandwich from room service, i spent the morning lounging poolside with my free paper and later in the day journaled a bit in the quiet and gorgeous front lobby. i was there during the weekend and it was a bit loud, but i didn't expect it to be country-cottage quiet. it's in the heart of hollywood and there's a club onsite and they had a party in the lobby. i didn't mind it at all, and slept fine, but anyone who would mind it shouldn't stay here, or should bring earplugs.i do agree with other comments that the springs did poke through the mattress and i did mention that to the hotel- and i thought the absence of a top sheet was kind of weird. however all in all- the helpful staff, the nice and relaxing rooms, the gorgeous pool, the historic architecture and the fabulous location made this one of my favorite hotel stays.

don't stay at the hollywood roosevelt there really is no excuse for such mediocrity, when the renaissance around the corner offers every luxury for 10 bucks more.the king standard rooms i had were shabby and small, and i can honestly say that something went wrong every night of my stay. the aircon was broken twice, the bathroom flooded several times - both the impractical bath/shower and then the aging plumbing of the toilet. in fact, despite the hygeine issue, staff there did not offer me another room when the toilet was flooding the floor.other irritations were the lack of mini-bar on floors 3 and 4, the phones which apparently do not always reach a connection downstairs (since everything was going wrong, it would have been nice to be able to report it by phone rather than having to trek down in person every day), and the awful elevators which often take minutes to arrive.i hear that the bar is pretty good, but unfortunately all i saw of it was the poor service and 1930's style rooms and amenities.i hear that the suites are actually renovated to a modern standard. that's great if you have that luxury, but the standard kings are awful - nowhere near the standard of a 2-star chain. my advice - pay the extra 10 bucks and go somewhere good instead.

could be a great hotel just came back from long weekend stay at this hotel. first my complaints:1) front desk needs better people skills. i had confirmed reservations (with a copy of the email) and they still argued about the rate. when we checked out they tried again to overcharge us. 2) the valet parking is a joke. they lost our car several times and took forever to get it when they did find it!3) my friends room had numerous carpet stains and smelled musty.4) we had to ask for the robes and the towels are way too thin- need to be upgraded. our room safe never locked consistently. i would guess all of the above are due to inexperienced management. it is the little things that make a stay enjoyable.however- the concierge (ben) was fabulous. he made us several wonderful and hard to get reservations for dinner, put up with us changing the time constantly and was able to get us in to the tropicana bar. he basically saved our trip for us. we ended up spending alot of time out by the pool, enjoying the private club atmosphere. i will be sending a letter to the management about the problems we encountered along with a letter to the concierge thanking him.like i said- this could be a great hotel.

pretentious and unjustified i went to la to see some friends for the weekend. i booked a cabana room at the roosevelt as i understood it was facing the pool and would provide an excellent location to chill and enjoy the party. prior to arrival i was told i could get 4 guests into the hotel but at check-in i was told only 3 other guests could accompany me to my room. a large group of friends who arrived were forcibly turned away from the bar and could not enter the poolside lounge. it didnt matter that my room rate was $600. an ambience of snobbery and harsh attitude by the staff is their best asset.

worst hotel i've ever stayed in i felt unsafe in this hotel. we were required to go down a dark side street to get back into the hotel because there was a function in the lobby. the corridor to our room felt unsafe as well. we booked a room with 2 beds and got only one. got a fold out bed and they left it standing against the wall because it wouldn't fit on the floor. towel bar in the bathroom fell off the wall every time i dried my hands. room incredibly small and mattress terrible. service was rude and practically nonexistant. i wanted to leave as soon as i checked in. i've lived all over the world-far east, middle east and presently living in europe. i've travelled extensively and have never seen anything like this place. it's as if they want you to get out.
