great location but no pool i took this trip to cheer up my mother you just lost her husband. she has always been intrigued by hollywood. the location of this hotel was great for star watching, as is close to mann's chinese theater, the kodak theatre were they have the oscars and the el capitan were disney holds it's premiers. our room was clean comfortable with a spacious bathroom and a view of the hollywood sign as well as mann's. the front desk staff was courteous and helpful. when our room key was accidentally deactivated, security responded promptly. the room service staff was great. my only complaint is that the pool and tropicana bar that they mentioned frequently on their website is closed from june through aug of 2004 and nobody mentioned that on the website or at the time of booking. if you want to swim or sunbathe pick another hotel this summer. other then the closed pool disappointment , i would stay at this hotel again. the metro station is located within one block of the hotel and is cheap and easy to use . at hollywood and highland roads is a nice shopping and dining complex that is well lit and safe to be in at night.

awful place arrived at this hotel at midnight after a flight from alaska. hoped that what i had read up about this hotel it would be so interesting to see where all the famous people and the oscars were first presented and history.what a disappointment, the staff were non-chalant and uncaring. the first room they showed us was so small we asked for an upgrade which we got. we only stayed a night as we were to carry on with our journey, which was good. the staff were not very helpful at all when we asked for brochures about what to see and places of interest. they gave us a tatty photocopied map and a list of things. other places we stayed had at least a free book of all the attractions. we heard after we had booked here that it was in a dirty area and tried to change but were unfortunately locked in to the itinerary. we placed our luggage in the bell boy's locker when we vacated the room and went to explore. when we got back to the hotel to catch the shuttle back to the airport we could not find the bell boy and it took several minutes to find someone to get our luggage. the shuttle was late to pick us up also and it was a rush to the airport. at the airport it was terrible, with the checking of the luggage as everything had to go through xray machines, unlocked. we booked out luggage in and then had to take it back to this xray machine. we stood at least for half an hour even more to get through this. we had not much time to get onto the plane for our next destination.i think that the hollywood roosevelt hotel is a bit of a dump, even though it is being refurbished. all the things that i had read up on that should have been there had been removed somewhere else. what a disappointment.

great location, great history we enjoyed our stay here in late may very much. the rooms have been remodeled and are very nice, with a sort of funky asian look. the bathrooms are especially neat. the rest of the building has a wonderful retro feel--they have done a nice job restoring the original decor. the location can't be beat if you are a hollywood tourist and the history of the place makes your stay so much more interesting than staying in a chain hotel. my only complaint would be the $18 a day charge for parking, although the valet service was very quick and courteous.

great location this hotel was comfortable and neat without all the frills. i was a little nervous about booking because it was the only hotel left with rooms on a busy la weekend. but, i was pleased to find helpful staff, a clean and stylish room, and a great view of hollywood. the location is perfect if you are looking to walk to dinner or a movie, or just check out the walk of stars.

nonmanaged it is a shame that this potentially great structure has a management that does not do the work needed to run a hotel. we stayed there on a saturday night in may 2004- anticipating that there might be a lot of noise on hollywood blvd we stayed in the cabana (pool) area at the back of the hotel. the pool and surrounding area supposedly closed at 10p.m. a loud group around the pool continued until 4a.m. and kept everyone in that area awake. our call to the desk which should have been unnecessary - especially with the security personnel constantly patrolling - was received politely but the noise continued. we do not recommend this hotel and would not stay here again.

hollywood in the old tradition sure, you could stay at the more exalted beverly hills hotel, but if you want the quintessential hollywood experience, this is the place! i have stayed both in the pool caba?¸½a villa and in the main tower. i much prefer and would recommend the caba?¸½a; as the room is much more spacious and comfortable, not to mention quiet, except for pool noise which might be a problem in summer. the hotel is a historic wonder and is strategically placed in the heart of hollywood blvd. with graumann's chinese theater and other attractions, walk of fame within easy walking distance. the lobby area has the old hollywood flavor coupled with 1920's style architecture and spanish influences throughout; the hotel dates from 1927, the year of the first talking picture. the mezzanine level is a tribute to hollywood history and is worth a look in itself. the famed cinegrill in the blossom room was the site of the first academy awards back in the late 1920's or early '30s. this hotel was literally a clubhouse for the likes of errol flynn who purportedly invented his recipe for gin in the backroom of the ex-barbershop. nearly every star has trysted here, including marilyn monroe and the hotel has attracted famous politicians and literary figures like ernest hemingway. all in all, a fascinating place to stay and good service as well. remember, get a room in the caba?¸½a area; it's the best.

loved this hotel, excellent!! all i can say about this hotel is fantastic! the location is great, right on the walk of fame. the room was spacious and very clean. there was even a premier party there one night! we did have a problem with an overflow in the toilet, but it was cleared up quickly and we had a complimentary breakfast for our trouble. (which was delicious) i recommend this hotel to anyone, it was beautiful, with an excellent view and lovely pool. the staff were helpful and polite and i enjoyed my stay so much, i didn't want to leave.

fantastic i would like to tell people that if it is their first time in hollywood this hotel is excellent. yes i do agree that this area can be quite dangerous at night but during the day what better place to stay. there are so many attractions, you can go acrosss to the chinese theatre, walk the walk of fame, get a tour from outside the chinese theatre(strongly reccommend ask for the tour guide brian i think.) go shopping, and all the other attractions that this area has. at night get a taxi to the places where you would like to eat. as for the hotel we thought it was excellent. we were lucky enough to stay in marlyin monroe's old cabana room, which hasn't changed from she stayed there. yes a lot of the furniture was from the 1950's but if it was good enough for her it was good enough for me???? the staff were excellent they were very helpful when we needed directions and places to go to a night. try this hotel for yourself..

valentines day party i was very nervous about staying at the hotel over valentine's day weekend 2004 after reading the reviews on this site, and although the quality of the room exceeded my expectations the service was just as described. upon arriving, the check-in process was extremely slow. the staff seemed to have no idea what they were doing. our room on the 3rd floor was modern and clean. the bathroom was cool had nice toiletries. however, the private party referred to by an earlier reviewer made our stay very interesting. the sound check started at 3 pm on sat afternoon for the party the noise continued until 5 am. since we were on the 3rd floor, the bass and music were awful. you couldn't even listen to the tv over the noise. we called the front desk several times (3 am, 4am, 5am), and they said the party was out of their control (then don't have people trying to sleep on the floor immediately above a party planned until 5 am that has a dj super bass bumping all night!) finally the next day the manager comped our room for saturday. also, although the hotel was supposedly sold out (it was all star weekend), the bar at the pool was closed. i kind of felt like the hotel was in dire need of new hotel management. in the end, not absolutely awful, but i'm sure there are better places to stay.

an ideal location for your holiday in l.a. i was lucky enough to stay here on my honeymoon and i have to say that i cannot find fault with this hotel. right on the walk of fame- hollywood boulevard and opposite manns theatre and the kodak theatre, its the perfect location for exploring this fantastic city. the staff were excellent - very helpful with advice on tours/sightseeing etc., the outdoor pool and jacuzzi were superb as was the pool bar. we dined in the hotel restaurant and it was perfect. its also a good place for celebrity spotting.as we were on our honeymoon the staff kindly upgraded us to a kabanna room, which was lovely. i would definately stay here again.the nightlife on hollywood boulevard isnt all that fantastic (except fot the knitting factory) but dont miss a night or two on sunset boulevard which is a must. enjoy.....

shame about the staff echo what the other reviewers say - building and rooms are great - staff and service is shocking. it was my second time staying at the hotel (first time was better) and despite a really good deal on the room, the attitude of the staff took the shine off. my tip would be - pay more and stay at le meridien at beverly hills. note also for first timers to la: while the hotel is in hollywood - you'll find not much else is! west hollywood/beverly hills is where all the shops/restaurants are - a 15 min cab ride away.

great location, great room my girlfriend and i stayed at the roosevelt for 4 nights in september 2003. we had a junior suite which was big and really nice. the location is absolutely unbeatable, on the corner of hollywood and highland. it was expensive though. i don't remember the nightly rate, but after a tax for each individual night and a $30-something a night valet fee, our total bill was almost $900. crazy, but i guess it was worth it considering the location and room size. another crazy thing was that our radio would sometimes come on by itself, even though the radio or arlam were not set. the station was always different too then what we had it set to. the roosevelt is supossed to be haunted, and it might just be.

what a waste of what could be a great hotel stayed there feb 14, 2004 (born and raised in la and have tradition of staying in a different local hotel every valentine's day). stayed on 6th floor in a junior suite--had to turn off the air conditioning becuase fan was so loud (not broken, just old and loud) you could not talk over it. the only good thing about the roosevelt is the physical building itself--real 1920's era art deco blended in clsaaic spanish california touches. the bar is awesome--but we and all other guests could not enjoy it since the hotel rents it out to private parties;we wandered too close by mistake as we were trying to find a door to the street and 5 security guards were upon us. to use mini-bar, you have to walk down to front desk to get a key (and give your credit card). front desk gave us a key, but it did not work. did not bother going down again for fear of having security think i was again trying to crash the private rap music party. tried calling room service from our room for dinner--but after 50 or 60 rings and multiple calls they did not answer. called front desk which acted like it happens all the time and they transfereed me to room service (without any apology or even mention of fact room service does not answer phone). when room service came, all the girl wanted to talk about was the private party--the one no one else could get into. called room service again next moring for breakfast (actually had front desk connect me because they would again not answer call from our room) tried ordering coffee, but i was told to just make it myself on the mini-maker in our room. tried, but it was broken. i would not say staff (mostly all in their early 20's) is terrible, but the service is. my feeling is that it's management's fault--they simply give staff no guidance on how guests should be treated at fine hotels, with the result that the roosevelt is a fine physical building but sucks as a hotel.

hollywood roosevelt-an elegant historical treat we stayed at the hollywood roosevelt last weekend and loved it! our junior suite on the 12th floor was not only spacious and clean but had two bathrooms. everyone was exceptionally nice. room service, breakfast in the blossom room, the bellperson--just wonderful. the historical feel of the hotel was elegant. we would highly recommend this hotel when you go to hollywood!
excellent hotel we stayed in april 2003 was fantastic, staff very helpful. rooms were very nice. excellent location across the road from manns chinese theatre. would stay there again, excellent

fantastic fantasitc place to stay, rooms slightly old-fashioned, but they have recently had a renovation. great view of downtown and santa monica, great location right on the walk of fame. meals were delicious, although breakfast was a bit ropey - avoid the pancakes, unless you want to take dioralyte!! getting around is hard, the underground looked dodgy and most of the taxi drivers are direct desendants of dracula and don't keep their eyes on the road. friendly staff, always willing to help out. watch out for elvis doing the rounds of the bar at night!!!!!

this is a very nice hotel my husband and i stayed there last weekend and i do not understand the bad reviews. i had stayed in this hotel back in the 60's and loved it, so i wanted to revisit my youth. i was not disappointed. although it has changed, it still has the ambiance it once had. we stayed on the 11th floor with a large modern room and great bath and a great view of hollywood blvd. they have high speed internet and everything is completely updated. i highly recommend it.

worse than a horror movie- a dump! upon hearing of the old days of grandeur of this hotel, i was reluctant to stay here with some old friends but i thought that perhaps they had invested heavily in the refurbishing of the hotel and made it a top notch place to stay, was i ever wrong. upon arriving around 1 am after a lengthly flight, half starving and dazed, i checked into the basement, where the staff was very rude, they did not even ask me how i was nor if i needed anything, they simply gave me a key and brushed me off. i walked up what seemed a hallway from an insane asylum, as i had been giving a room by the pool by the 'kind staff'. at first glance, i thought, this doesn't look good, considering that there were pools of water from the central ventilating shaft, leaking all over the place, streams of garbage, towels and dirty piles of what seemed like rotted food. i opened the door to the dirty and dingy room, thinking i was in some welfare hotel, upon entering i was disgusted at how bad it truly was. a dirty odor, smelling of foul stench, probably from the old rug which had blood stains upon it, entered my nostrils. this was really horrible and i was the first one to get there, considering my tired friends were still on the plane expecting a comfortable and safe room. i made a quick inspection of the room, from the broken sliding glass door which had no lock upon it to the terrible molded curtain that nearly fell upon my head. the beds had stains upon them, and they weren't even changed as if they had given me an previously used room. i opened the closet up and was startled to notice a 1950's style air conditioner leaking all sorts of water and fluid upon the wood and carpet, that was where the smell was coming from. the bathroom was even worse, to my surprise and horror, there was black mush in the old toilet, the rusted pipes were craclking and the mirror was very scary for it was blemished and aged. there were no towels, no soap, not even any toilet paper! the whole room had not been remodeled since the 1950's, for it was in the cabana style, not even changed, i could not believe i was paying $150 a night for a room that looked like a prison chamber and a dump! when i tried to call the staff, they ignored my requests to get a better room. attempting to use the bathroom, i found out that there was no water at all and the toilet would not flush! this was a complete disaster for me and when i attempted to get to sleep, i was awakened by some noisy generator that sounded as if it was about to explode. that night we looked for a place to eat and the area is dangerous, drug users, prostitutes all hang out there so i wouldn't advise walking around there and there aren't even many places to eat except dirty taco joints and a very expensive mel's dinner. i would not ever stay here again, considering i was gimped out of a forture by the place. be warned, do not stay here at all.

fantastic hotel we visited the hollywood roosevelt in november 2003 for five nights.on arrival we were upgraded to a fantastic suite on the 11th floor.it was very spacious with two kingsize beds,and a huge bathroom which contained a wet room and a bath.the toiletries were plentiful and of excelent quality. we had a view of hollywood blvd,and could see right into the forecourt of manns chinese theatre.we were also very pleased to find that we had a perfect view of the hollywood sign.the hotel was in a brilliant location,taxi to warner bros studios was $10,the tube to universal studios is a minute walk away and whilst on the tube is only a five minute ride.mels diner is a great place to start the day, breakfast is well recomended and not too expensive.next door to mels diner is the max factor museum which contains loads of hollywood costumes and make up worn by the stars for example-marilyn,joan crawford. we were travelling with our 10 year old son who found the outdoor heated pool fantastic,and went for a few moonlit dips.i would reccomend this hotel to anyone.the sheer history of the hotel is overwhelming so dont let other reviews put you off.i would love to go back someday.

used to be nice - what has happened????? myself and my partner stayed at the hollywood roosevelt in october 2002. we had planned on coming back there this year to spend 5 nights of our honeymoon, however, after reading the latest reviews, i think we will be re-considering. when we stayed there, we anticipated to be staying in the cabana rooms, which when we arrived (due to constructions works) we were upgraded to a room on the 11th floor. i had heard some stories before we had arrived about how horrible the cabana rooms were, so i wasn't actually looking forward to going there. when we arrived at our room on the 11th floor, it was amazing, it was everything we could have possibly wanted. it was large with a king-sized bed. we had an excellent view of hollywood blvd too. the room had modern furnishings and was very clean. everything you can imagine is in close proximity and universal is a 10 min drive (at most). everything you need is in this area, which is why this hotel is so appealing. the hotel is now 2 years older, could it really have changed that much? i think i'll just have to keep looking for somewhere new.... shame.

not as nice as it once was we last stayed here two years ago and since that time it has been in the throws of refurbishment. we had four nights there over the new year and into jan 2nd 2004.it felt deserted the night we arrived albeit at a very late hour. however, even during the day it was very quiet. the most number of people we saw in a given night was on new year's eve when the beautiful people arrived in their droves for a new years bash in the ballroom.the reception area in this hotel is now in the basement and not the lobby where it used to be. the lobby now looks completely except for a couple of sofas and a table in the middle of the room. the restaurant on this level is still there though again not many people were using it. the coffee shop place at the front of the hotel is closed.it took them many minutes to sort out a room for us as their computers were slow (overnight processing). once we got keys we were shown to a room on the 4th floor even though we asked for a high floor. we had to ask them again to bring up our bags as they had forgotton to do so. our room keys stopped working on the 2nd day and when the keys were reprogrammed they still did not work necessitating a further trip back to the front desk. they had it transpired misprogrammed the keys to open another room. they were apologetic about this.beds were uncomfortable in the first room we had and it did feel very cold to begin with. it was also very minimalist in tone with also minimal counter space in the bathroom to place toiletries. we had a room change during our stay on new years eve as you could clearly hear all the noise during the soundcheck to the party (our room was above the ballroom). the room change was swiftly dealt by reception with and our bags were efficiently moved to a junior suite on the 8th floor. staff did try overall to make our stay pleasant and the porters were helpful when we checked out. there is a nice restaurant a block away called hamburger hamlet which is well worth calling into. we did not use room service. its main saving grace is its proximity to hollywood and attractions like universal studios (the metro at hollywood and highland costs little and is easy to use) but if and when we return to la we will stay in a different area.

fantastic!! just gives an undescribable feeling. perfect location for all that goes on in the heart of hollywood. walked around the hotel and you could just feel the fabulous history. everywhere you turned was something else to take a picture of. we had my wife, my 18 year old son, my 6 year old twins and everyone enjoyed their stay. i would stay there every time and would recommend it to anyone who likes history or the feeling of being apart of something special.

forget it! my wife and i stayed at the roosevelt hotel on 13/14 september at the start of our two week 'trip of a lifetime', impressed by their website and cabana room advertising. our first impression on check-in did not bode well - lots of furtive looks, comments and glances between receptionists. all became clear when we saw our reserved cabana room, which was not at all close to the pool and overlooked a noisy side room. a dirty and cracked handbasin, rusted bathroom fittings and a filthy carpet completed the room's attractions. our immediate request for a room change was ignored. staff quite unfriendly except for the porter.main entrance to the hotel is locked during private functions leaving guests to wander aimlessly to find a way out. it is hard to see where the much lauded refurbishment has taken place - but certainly not in the cabana rooms. this encounter nearly spoiled our holiday - thank god for the numerous best westerns we stayed at thereafter, the rooms of even the worst one of which was infinitely better than our roosevelt room. its only saving grace is its proximity to hollywood bvld.

ok, but the hotel is located ideally for tourism. if they offer you a room around by the pool, do not take it!! these rooms are not refurbished, noisy surroundings (generartors etc). the staff are very false, behind their smile is a very miserable person. the rooms in the main building are to standard, not the biggest but goog enough.

poolside cabana is no big whoop my family and i stayed at the roosevelt in july 2003 for our big family vacation at universal studios. wanting something cool and art deco, we chose the roosevelt based on its pictures on expedia.....here's the thing - a) only if you stay in the tower room (not the poolside cabanas - which are more $$??) do you even have a chance at the cool art deco room featured in the photo; and b) our poolside room looked (and smelled) like something from motel 6 (or the bates motel). old carpet, old bedspreads, a cranky a/c that leaked all over my clothes in the very small closet, a safe that didn't work 90% of the time, etc., etc... however, the staff was great, the tower room was beautiful, just what i imagined - very art deco/contemporary/zen. would not stay there again.

you people are so wrong if you think the roosevelt's sucks! my goodness. it really surprises me that people feel that a 3 star hotel should be double its rating and also remain the price they paid. the roosevelt is a wonderful place. clean, yes clean, and extremely helpful staff. anytime that i had to speak to the reception, they were very courteous. this was our first experience of valet parking - also very friendly people. the gift shop, although opening/closing at any time, was stocked with what we needed so as not to dip into the minbar so often and the man in charge there was always happy to chat. extremely comfortable beds (we had a tower room) and a more-than adequate bathroom (i have been in 5 stars where the bathroom is smaller). as for the neighborhood - yes it is a bit sleazy but it is hollywood!!!! you get the same street hassle in any major city. the movies are right across the street (including the must-see chinese theatre), the tacky museums are also fun to look at (see hollywood entertainment museum, great people there and good value) and the souvenir shops stock a better quality of junk than anywhere else (unlike venice beach where every souvenir place is identical) with no hassle to buy stuff, the 101 is very close by and a block behind the roosevelt is sunset boulevard (definitely worth a look). furthermore, if you want to leave the car behind, then the metro (across the street) will get you to many places back for a few dollars (downtown la, chinatown, universal city, etc). if you are visiting the hollywood bowl, the shuttle buses are right across the street at the highland shopping centre, so you have no tranport worries (we saw rem during our stay). only irritation we had was the hi-speed internet access required bringing a laptop (not via the tv), although the wonderful internet cafe a block away called cyber java made up for that shortcoming. also met 2 celebs while staying, and experienced the media circus surrounding the deaths of johnny cash and john ritter - their stars on the walk of fame were close by. basically, my sympathies to those who had a bad experience, but to those who expected the high society and high class that comes with the 5 star chains, then you should have booked your holiday 70 years ago and you do not have my sympathy at all. well done all you guys at the hollywood roosevelt from a very satisifed customer!!!!!

roosevelt hotel is the worst ever!!! yuck! my goodness this place was horrible! the neighboorhood at night is disgusting and during the day the hotel's terrible service took the cake. after we checked in they gave us this gross room. i was shocked how nice their rooms looked online but the truth is that their furniture and their decor was cheap and also dirty. i had to demand to change rooms, which took an hour and half even though the so-called manager told us they had plenty of rooms. why? i guess they don't value their guests' time or something.i ordered a grilled sandwich and got full on stomach sickness and had to actually take that immodium ad the rest of the weekend. thank you roosevelt !! yuck!what a horrible place, stay away!

please read this and do not book roosevelt! let me tell you guys what i went through upon my check in. they kept me and my wife waitign fro 2.5 hours with zero explanation. the room was not ready and instead of kindly apologizing and perhaps offering us lunch or something, they kept saying it will be ready in the next 10-15 minutes. well imagine sitting there with a prepaid room for 2.5 hours while they jerked us around. no apologies, nothing complimentary, nothing, just giving us so much attitude, as if we were waiting to get into studio 54. then the rooms, my god the rooms by the pool are like motel 6 (actually worse), and the next night we asked to stay in the tower. we paid for a deluxe large room and got this small room instead. the decorations inside were nice but they refused to refund the difference for no reason. at night i wanted to order from room service but there was no menu in the roo. it took 45 minutes to get through to room service and finally we gave up. the hotel does not even have a full-time concierge. when we asked the front desk about this comedy club they said it was in an area with lots of taxi's and restaurants. when we got there not only was that area dead, the comdey club people laughed at us when we told them what the hotel had told us. there were no restaurants within 8 blocks!whatever you do please do not stay at this hell hole. it was such a ridiculously aweful place i actually took time to write this.
